textual_notes: ובש״ה and ח!דשים contain scribal marks (״ and !) that suggest abbreviation or corruption. ובש״ה likely reads ובששה 'and in the sixth'; ח!דשים likely reads חדשים 'months'. These cannot be confirmed from the consonants alone.
ש״מה contains a scribal mark and likely reads שמה 'its name' but the abbreviation is uncertain.
נצרת has no Strong's entry provided — it is a place name (Nazareth) not found in the standard Hebrew Bible lexicon.

translation_notes: עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with'. A virgin betrothed 'with' a man is the natural reading; 'a people' makes no sense here.
איש (consonants איש): Candidates: H376 'a man', H377 'to act manly'. The context describes a person to whom the virgin is betrothed, so H376 'a man' is correct.
הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/she/it', H1933 'to be'. As a pronoun referring back to Joseph and introducing a clause about his lineage, H1931 'he' fits naturally.
מבית (consonants מ+בית): Candidates: H1004 'house/family', H1006 'Bajith'. With מ (from) + בית + David, this clearly means 'from the house/lineage of David.'
דוד (consonants דוד): Candidates: H1730 'beloved/uncle', H1731 'pot/basket', H1732 'David'. Following 'from the house of,' this is the proper name David, the patriarch — H1732.

שמה (consonants שמה): Candidates: H8047 'ruin', H8048 'Shammah'. In context this is ש + מה or שם + ה meaning 'her name.' H8048 shares the consonants but is a proper name. The reading here is best understood as שם 'name' + ה (her), functioning as 'her name [was].'
textual_notes: ארוסה has no Strong's candidates provided. It appears to be a passive participle from ארס 'to betroth' — a post-biblical Hebrew form not in the standard Strong's lexicon.
ש״מו contains a scribal abbreviation mark; likely reads שמו 'his name.'
שמה could be parsed as שם+ה 'her name' or as H8047 'ruin/desolation.' Context clearly demands 'her name.'

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants ו+כ+אשר): Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness'. With ו+כ prefix, כאשר 'as/when' using H834 is the standard temporal conjunction — the natural reading for introducing a narrative event.
אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. The syntax requires a verb ('the messenger... said to her'), so H559 is correct.

מלאה (consonants מלאה): Candidates: H4395 'something fulfilled/abundance', H4396 'a filling/setting'. Could also be parsed as מ+לאה (H3811 'to tire' or H3812 'Leah'). In context following the greeting, 'full/filled [with] grace' produces a coherent image of blessing; 'from Leah' or 'from weariness' makes no contextual sense.

את (consonants את): Candidates: H852 'portent', H853 'self/object marker', H854 'nearness/with', H855 'hoe'. Here את functions as the second person feminine pronoun 'you' (blessed are you), which is a common function of this form.

בין (consonants בין): Candidates: H995 'to understand', H996 'between/among'. Following 'blessed are you,' the prepositional sense 'among' (H996) is the natural choice — blessed among the rest of the women.

שאר (consonants שאר): Candidates: H7603 'yeast', H7604 'to swell/be redundant', H7605 'a remainder', H7607 'flesh/kindred'. Before 'the women,' H7605 'remainder/rest of' makes the most natural sense — 'among the rest of the women.'
textual_notes: נכנס has no Strong's candidates — it is likely a nif'al form of כנס 'to enter/gather,' a later Hebrew form not in the standard Strong's lexicon.
יושיעך appears to be a hif'il imperfect of ישע 'to save' with 2fs suffix — 'he will save you.' This is a distinctive Hebrew greeting formula not standard in biblical Hebrew angel announcements.
ברוכה has no Strong's candidates provided — it is a passive participle (feminine) of ברך 'to bless' (H1288), meaning 'blessed.'
הנשים has no candidates — it is ה + נשים, the definite article + plural of אשה 'woman' (H802).
את here could be the object marker (H853) or the 2fs pronoun. Context favors the pronoun 'you' as subject complement of ברוכה.

translation_notes: דברי (consonants דברי): The candidate H1704 'Dibri' is a proper name, but the consonants דברי are more naturally the construct plural of דבר 'word/thing' (H1697) — 'words of.' The construct form before 'the messenger' demands this reading.
ההוא (consonants ה+הוא): H1931 'he/she/it' with the article ה forms the demonstrative 'that one' — 'that greeting.'
הוא (consonants הוא): H1931 'he/it' or H1933 'to be.' Following איך 'how,' this reads 'how it is/could be' — either reading produces the same sense.
textual_notes: ואותה could be parsed as ו+אותה 'and her' (object pronoun) or as a demonstrative 'and that one.' Context suggests an emphatic reference — 'and she, the virgin.'
כש״מעה contains a scribal abbreviation — likely כשמעה 'when she heard,' from שמע 'to hear' (H8085) with כ temporal prefix and 3fs suffix.
נבהלה has no candidates provided — it is likely nif'al of בהל 'to be terrified/alarmed' (H926), feminine form.
וחושבת has no candidates — likely a participle of חשב 'to think/reckon' (H2803).
ה״לום contains a scribal mark; likely הלום or השלום — possibly 'the greeting' (from שלום H7965). The abbreviation makes this uncertain.
דברי: The only listed Strong's candidate is H1704 (Dibri, a proper name), but contextually this must be the construct plural of H1697 דבר 'word.' The lexicon gap is noted.

translation_notes: אמר (consonants אמר): H559 'to say' — the messenger is the subject speaking; verb reading is required.

אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'mighty/God', H413 'to/near'. Before תיראי 'you shall fear,' the deprecative negative H408 'do not' is the standard construction — אל תיראי 'do not fear.'
כי (consonants כי): H3588 'for/because' vs H3587 'brand/scar.' As a conjunction introducing the reason not to fear, H3588 is correct.
את (consonants את): H852 'portent', H853 'self/object marker', H854 'with', H855 'hoe.' Here את functions as the 2fs pronoun 'you' — subject of 'have found grace.'
חן (consonants חן): H2580 'grace/favor' vs H2581 'Chen (proper name).' Following the verb 'found,' the abstract noun 'grace/favor' is the natural reading.
textual_notes: תיראי has no candidates provided — it is the 2fs imperfect of ירא 'to fear' (H3372).
מצאת has no candidates — it is the 2fs perfect of מצא 'to find' (H4672).
בעיני has no candidates — it is ב + עיני 'in the eyes of,' construct of עין 'eye' (H5869) with 1cs or construct suffix.

translation_notes: כי (consonants כי): H3588 'that/because' — introduces a content clause after 'know,' so 'that' is the correct function.
את (consonants את): H852 'portent', H853 'self/object marker', H854 'with'. Here את is the 2fs pronoun 'you' — subject of 'will conceive.'
בן (consonants בן): H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'a son.' Following 'will bear,' the common noun 'son' (H1121) is clearly correct.
ישוע (consonants ישוע): H3442 and H3443 both mean 'Jeshua/Yeshua.' H3442 is the primary entry for this name, derived from ישע 'to save.'
textual_notes: תדעי has no candidates — 2fs imperfect of ידע 'to know' (H3045).
תהרי has no candidates — 2fs imperfect of הרה 'to conceive' (H2029).
ותלדי has no candidates — 2fs imperfect of ילד 'to bear/give birth' (H3205) with vav conjunction.
שתקראי has no candidates — ש (relative/that) + תקראי 2fs imperfect of קרא 'to call' (H7121).
שמו has no candidates — שם 'name' (H8034) + ו 3ms suffix 'his name.'

translation_notes: זה (consonants זה): H2088 'this/that' vs H2089 'a sheep'. As the subject of 'will be great,' the demonstrative pronoun 'this one' is the natural reading.

מהאל (consonants מ+ה+אל): The מ is the preposition 'from/of,' ה is the article, and אל — candidates: H408 'not', H410 'mighty/God', H413 'to'. In the phrase 'son of the ____ Most High,' H410 'God/Mighty One' is the only coherent reading.
עליון (consonants עליון): H5945 'Most High/Supreme' vs H5946 'the Supreme.' Both are essentially the same; H5945 as the adjective modifying אל fits: 'son of the Most High God.'
כסא (consonants כסא): H3677 'full moon/festival' vs H3678 'throne.' In context — YHWH giving something to a royal figure — 'throne' (H3678) is the clear choice.
אב (consonants אב): H1 'father' vs H3 'green plant.' Following 'YHWH' and before 'his,' 'father' produces the coherent phrase 'YHWH [the] father of his' or 'YHWH his father.'

שלו (consonants שלו): H7958 'quail', H7959 'security', H7961 'tranquil/careless'. In this context שלו likely functions as the possessive 'his' (של+ו), a later Hebrew construction. None of the biblical Strong's entries fit perfectly, but H7961 shares the consonants and the possessive reading 'of him/his' is the most contextually coherent.
textual_notes: יהיה has no candidates — imperfect 3ms of היה 'to be' (H1961).
נקרא has no candidates — nif'al participle/perfect of קרא 'to call' (H7121), 'be called.'
ואדונינו has no candidates — ו + אדנינו, 'and our Lord,' from אדון 'lord' (H113) with 1cp suffix.
יתן has no candidates — 3ms imperfect of נתן 'to give' (H5414).

שלו is ambiguous: it could be the later Hebrew possessive של+ו 'his/of him' (not in Strong's as such), or one of the biblical entries (H7958-7961). The possessive reading is most natural in context but reflects post-biblical morphology.
The phrase 'כסא יהוה אב שלו' is syntactically ambiguous: it could mean 'the throne of YHWH his father' (i.e., David's throne given by God) or 'the throne of YHWH, [the] father of his [line].'

translation_notes: בבית (consonants ב+בית): H1004 'house/family' vs H1006 'Bajith (place).' Before 'Jacob,' this means 'in the house/household of Jacob' — H1004.

לנצח (consonants ל+נצח): H5329 'to glitter/be eminent', H5331 'a goal/perpetuity/splendor', H5332 'grape juice.' With the preposition ל, 'to perpetuity / forever' (H5331) fits the royal reign context perfectly.
לאין (consonants ל+אין): H369 'non-entity/negative particle' vs H370 'where?' Before קץ 'end,' the phrase לאין קץ 'to no end / without end' uses H369 as the negative.
textual_notes: וימלוך has no candidates — ו + ימלוך, 3ms imperfect of מלך 'to reign' (H4427) with vav consecutive or conjunctive.
ומלכותו has no candidates — ו + מלכות 'kingdom' (H4438) + ו 3ms suffix, 'and his kingdom.'

translation_notes: אמרה (consonants אמרה): H565 'something said.' However, the form אמרה in context is the 3fs perfect of אמר 'to say' (H559) — 'she said.' H565 shares the consonants but is a noun. The verbal reading is required by syntax (Miriam as subject performing speech).

יוכל (consonants יוכל): H3116 'Jukal (proper name).' However, the consonants יוכל are also the 3ms imperfect of יכל 'to be able' (H3201). Context demands the verb 'can/be able' — the proper name makes no sense here.

העשות (consonants ה+עשות): H6219 'shining/polished,' H6220 'Ashvath.' However, this is more naturally ה + infinitive construct of עשה 'to do/make' (H6213) — 'the doing/to be done.' The listed candidates don't fit the context; the infinitive construct reading does.
זה (consonants זה): H2088 'this' vs H2089 'a sheep.' After 'be done,' the demonstrative 'this' is the obvious choice.
שאין (consonants ש+אין): ש (relative 'that/since') + H369 'there is not.' This creates 'since there is not' — Miriam explaining she has no intimate knowledge of a man.
איש (consonants איש): H376 'a man' vs H377 'to act manly.' As the object of 'knowledge of,' the noun 'a man' (H376) is correct.
textual_notes: אמרה: The only listed candidate is H565 (noun, 'something said'), but the form functions as a 3fs perfect verb of H559. This is a lexicon gap in the provided candidates.
יוכל: The only listed candidate is H3116 (Jukal, a name), but contextually this must be the 3ms imperfect of יכל 'to be able' (H3201). Another lexicon gap.
העשות: Listed candidates H6219/H6220 don't fit. This is the hif'il or nif'al infinitive construct of עשה (H6213) with the article, meaning 'the doing / to be done.'
ידיעת has no candidates — it is the construct form of ידיעה 'knowledge/knowing,' from ידע 'to know' (H3045). The phrase 'knowledge of a man' is a euphemism for sexual intimacy.
לי has no candidates — the preposition ל + 1cs suffix 'to me / I have.'

translation_notes: ענה (consonants ענה): Candidates: H6030 'to heed/respond', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6034 'Anah (name).' The messenger is responding to Miriam's question, so H6030 'answered/responded' is the clear choice.
ואמר (consonants ו+אמר): H559 'to say' vs H561 'something said' vs H563 'a lamb.' Following 'answered,' the verb 'and said' (H559) is the standard Hebrew pairing ענה ואמר.
רוח (consonants רוח): H7304 'to breathe freely', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit.' As the subject that 'will come upon you,' the noun 'spirit' (H7307) is required — 'the spirit of holiness.'

הקדש (consonants ה+קדש): H6942 'to be clean/holy (verb)', H6943 'Kedesh (place)', H6944 'a sacred place/thing/sanctity', H6945 'a devotee', H6946 'Kadesh (place).' Following רוח and with the article ה, 'the holiness/sanctity' (H6944) forms the construct phrase 'spirit of the holiness' — i.e., the Holy Spirit.
העליון (consonants ה+עליון): H5945 'Most High/Supreme' — with the article, 'the Most High,' paralleling the spirit of holiness in the first clause.
ומה (consonants ו+מה): H4100 'what?' — functioning as a relative pronoun 'and that which,' introducing what will be born.
קדוש (consonants קדוש): H6918 'sacred/holy' — describing what is born from her.
textual_notes: יבא has no candidates — 3ms imperfect of בוא 'to come' (H935).
עליך has no candidates — על 'upon' (H5921) + ך 2fs suffix, 'upon you.'

יתלונן has no candidates provided. The consonants suggest a hitpolel/hitpael form. It may derive from לון/לין 'to lodge/dwell' (H3885) in a reflexive/intensive stem meaning 'to settle upon/overshadow,' or possibly from צלל 'to shadow' via metathesis. The traditional reading 'overshadow' fits the context of divine power covering her.
שיולד has no candidates — ש (relative) + יולד, nif'al/hof'al of ילד 'to be born' (H3205), 'that which is born.'
ממך has no candidates — מן 'from' + ך 2fs suffix, 'from you.'
ו appears as a standalone conjunction 'and.'
נקרא has no candidates — nif'al of קרא 'to call' (H7121), 'be called.'

The final word בן 'son' stands alone without a genitive — the text may be incomplete or the implied completion is 'son of God' from the earlier context (בן מהאל עליון in section 7). This is a notable textual feature.

translation_notes: והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2009 because the context introduces new information — a revelation about Elisheva's pregnancy — making the exclamatory 'behold' the natural fit.
בן: Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (proper name)', H1123 'a son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 because the context describes conceiving offspring, not naming a specific person called Ben.

החדש: Candidates: H2318 'to be new/rebuild', H2319 'new', H2320 'month/new moon', H2321 'Chodesh (name)'. Chose H2320 because with the definite article and followed by a numeral ('the sixth'), this clearly refers to a month of pregnancy.
א.לישבע: This is the name Elisheva (אלישבע), corresponding to Elizabeth. The dot likely indicates a scribal mark or damaged consonant. No Strong's entry is provided but the name is recognizable.
textual_notes: The word ה11י appears to have corrupted numerals; based on context (month of pregnancy) it is read as 'the sixth' (הששי). The numerals 11 likely represent a scribal notation for שש (six).

לפני תהר בבטנך שתקראו — the syntax is ambiguous: 'before you conceive in your womb, that you shall call [him]' could also be parsed as a separate clause. The sentence appears to continue into the next verse (cut off mid-thought).

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: for/because/that'. Chose H3588 because this is clearly a causal conjunction introducing a theological statement.

שום: Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7761 'to put (Aramaic)', H7762 'garlic'. In later Hebrew שום דבר functions as 'any thing' (lit. 'a placed thing'). Chose H7760 because in context it means 'any' modifying דבר.
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because שום דבר = 'any thing/matter'.
לפני: H3942 'anterior/before' — used as a preposition meaning 'before the face of' YHWH.
יהוה: Candidates: H3068, H3069 — both YHWH. Chose H3068 as the standard divine name.
textual_notes: אינינו is a later Hebrew form (אינננו) meaning 'there is not' or 'is not for us/him'. The suffix may be third person or first person plural — context favors impersonal 'there is not'.
איפשרי is a post-biblical Hebrew word meaning 'possible', formed from the root א-פ-ש-ר. It has no Strong's number as it is not found in biblical Hebrew. The combination בלתי איפשרי = 'impossible'.
The double negation structure (אינינו שלא יהיה בלתי איפשרי) is emphatic: literally 'there is not that it will be impossible' = 'nothing will be impossible'.

translation_notes: הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2009 because Miriam is making a declarative statement presenting herself.
פה: Candidates: H6310 'mouth', H6311 'here/this place'. Chose H6311 because 'behold here [is] the maidservant' is the natural reading — she is presenting herself as present and available.
שפחת: The provided candidate H6354 (פחת 'a pit') does not fit. The word is שפחת, construct form of שפחה (H8198, maidservant/female servant). The ש is integral to the root שפח, not a prefix.
textual_notes: שפחת — the candidates list only provides פחת H6354 'a pit', but the actual word is the construct form of שפחה 'maidservant'. This is clearly שפחת יהוה = 'the maidservant of YHWH'.
יהיה לי עשוי could be parsed as 'let it be done to me' (jussive) or 'it will be done to me' (future). The jussive sense fits the context of willing submission.

translation_notes: מהרה: Candidates: H4120 'a hurry/promptly', H2029 'to be pregnant', H2030 'pregnant'. Chose H4120 because the context describes travel — she went quickly — not a statement about pregnancy. 'She went in haste into the hills' is coherent; 'she went pregnant into the hills' is forced here.

בעיר: Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'a city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'a watcher/angel', H5895 'a young ass'. Chose H5892 because 'to a city of Judah' is the natural geographic reference for a destination of travel.
וקמה: The candidate H7054 'stalk of grain' does not fit. This is the verb קום (H6965 'to rise/stand up') in the feminine form with vav-consecutive: 'and she rose up'.
textual_notes: מ&ם appears to be משם ('from there') with a corrupted or damaged consonant represented by &. This is the standard word for 'from there'.
בהרים — this could be 'in the mountains/hills' (plural of הר, H2022) or 'in Harim' (a place name). Context of traveling to the Judean hill country favors 'in the hills/mountains'.

translation_notes: בבית: Candidates: H1004 'a house', H1005 'house (Aramaic)', H1006 'Bajith (place)', H3487 'sign of object'. Chose H1004 because 'the house of Zechariah' is the clear intended meaning — she entered a household.

שלום: Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare/greeting', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. Chose H7965 because giving שלום is the standard Hebrew greeting, meaning she greeted Elisheva with peace.
textual_notes: לאץלישבע — the form is unusual with the צ prefix. This appears to be a variant or scribal form of לאלישבע ('to Elisheva/Elizabeth'). The צ may represent a dialectal or scribal convention in this manuscript.
ונתנה לה שלום — literally 'she gave to her peace'. This is the Hebrew idiom for greeting someone, equivalent to 'she greeted her'.

translation_notes: נער: Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy/child', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the context describes a child in the womb who responds to a greeting — 'the child of Elisheva' is the natural reading.

שמח: Candidates: H8055 'to brighten up/be glad/rejoice', H8056 'blithe/gleeful', H4220 'fat/rich', H4221 'marrow'. Chose H8055 because the child responding with joy in the womb is the coherent image — a child leaping with gladness.

מרוח: Candidates: H4790 'bruised/emasculated', H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room/interval', H7306 'to blow/smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 'spirit (Aramaic)'. Chose H7307 because 'filled from/with spirit of holiness' describes a divine infilling, consistent with the theological context.

הקדש: Candidates: H6942 'to be clean/holy', H6943 'Kedesh (place)', H6944 'a sacred place or thing/sanctity', H6945 'sacred person/devotee', H6946 'Kadesh (place)'. Chose H6944 because רוח הקדש ('spirit of the holiness') is the standard Hebrew expression for the Holy Spirit.
textual_notes: ש&מעה and ה&לום contain damaged or marked consonants (represented by &). ש&מעה is clearly ששמעה ('when she heard', with the relative ש + שמעה). ה&לום appears to be השלום ('the greeting/peace'), with the ש partially damaged.
ומיד — literally 'and from hand' but in later Hebrew this is the standard idiom for 'immediately'. The connection to H3027 (יד 'hand') is etymological; the functional meaning is 'at once'.

translation_notes: את: Candidates: H852 'a portent', H853 'self/object marker', H854 'nearness/with', H855 'a hoe'. Chose H853 because here את functions as the second person feminine pronoun 'you' — 'blessed are you among the women'. In context this is a direct address.

בין: Candidates: H995 'to distinguish/understand', H996 'between/among', H997 'between'. Chose H996 because 'blessed you among the women' is the natural reading — comparing her status relative to other women.

וברוך: The candidate H1263 'Baruk (name)' does not fit. This is the passive participle of ברך (H1288 'to bless'), masculine form: 'and blessed [is]'. Masculine because it modifies פרי (fruit), which is masculine.
textual_notes: וצע3קה — contains a numeral 3, likely representing a damaged or uncertain consonant. The word is clearly וצעקה ('and she cried out'), from צעק (H6817). The 3 may represent a gimel or simply scribal damage.
את could be the object marker (H853) or the pronoun 'you' (feminine). In this context it functions as 'you' — the subject of the blessing.

translation_notes: קרה: Candidates: H7135 'coolness', H7136 'to light upon/happen/come about', H7137 'an occurrence/accident'. Chose H7136 because 'how has this happened' expresses wonder at an event occurring — the arrival of the mother of her lord.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this (demonstrative)', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'this' as a demonstrative pronoun is the natural reading: 'how has this happened'.

שאם: Candidates: H517 'a mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H517 because 'that the mother of my lord has come to me' produces the coherent image of a woman expressing amazement at being visited by someone of higher status. 'If my lord' would make the clause conditional and incomplete.
באה: H872 'an entrance' as a noun, but here באה functions as the feminine perfect of בוא (H935 'to come/enter'): 'she has come'. The form is verbal, not nominal.
textual_notes: א3דוני — contains a numeral 3, likely representing a damaged consonant. The word is clearly אדוני ('my lord/my master'), from אדון (H113). The 3 may represent the letter gimel or scribal damage.

שאם — the ש prefix functions as a relative particle ('that/who') in later Hebrew, + אם 'mother'. Could theoretically be read as ש + אם 'that if', but 'that the mother' is far more coherent in context.

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction'. Chose H3588 because this introduces a causal/explanatory clause.

הנער: Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy/child', H5289 'wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the context describes the unborn child responding to the greeting — 'the child rejoiced'.

שמח: Candidates: H8055 'to rejoice/be glad', H8056 'blithe/gleeful', H4220 'fat', H4221 'marrow'. Chose H8055 because the child rejoicing with great joy is the natural image — consistent with the preceding section's description of the child leaping.

בגיל: Candidates: H1523 'to spin round/rejoice', H1524 'joy/a revolution of time'. Chose H1524 because 'with joy' (בגיל) paired with 'great' produces 'with great joy/exultation' — a coherent description of the child's response.

אזני: The only candidate H244 is 'Ozni, an Israelite'. However, the word is clearly אזני 'my ears', from אזן (H241 'ear') with first person singular suffix. The listing of H244 is misleading — this is not a proper name here.
textual_notes: כא3שר contains a numeral 3 representing a damaged consonant — this is clearly כאשר ('when/as'), a standard temporal conjunction.
שלומך — 'your peace/greeting'. This is שלום with second person feminine suffix, referring to Miriam's greeting of peace.
שמעו אזני — literally 'my ears heard'. The subject-verb agreement (plural ears, plural verb) is standard.

translation_notes: ולא כי: This phrase is syntactically ambiguous. Option 1: 'and [did] not [doubt], for...' — meaning she believed and did not waver, because the words will be fulfilled. Option 2: 'and not because...' which would mean her blessedness is not because of the words but for some other reason — this is incoherent in context. Chose option 1: ולא = 'and [she did] not [doubt]', כי = 'for/because' introducing the reason.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction'. Chose H3588 because this introduces the explanatory clause about why she is blessed.
יהוה: Candidates: H3068, H3069. Chose H3068 as the standard divine name.
textual_notes: שהאץמנת — this appears to be ש + האמנת ('who believed/trusted'), from אמן (H539 'to believe/trust'), with an extraneous צ possibly representing a scribal convention or dialectal spelling in this manuscript. The root is clearly אמן in the hiphil: 'she believed'.

ולא כי — the most challenging phrase in this section. It could mean: (a) 'and [she did] not [doubt], because...' (b) 'and not, for...' as a corrective statement. Option (a) produces the most coherent reading: 'blessed are you who believed and did not [doubt], for those words spoken to you from YHWH will be fulfilled in you.'
נשלמים — passive participle plural of שלם, meaning 'being completed/fulfilled/perfected'. This could also carry the sense of 'being made whole' or 'being brought to peace'.

translation_notes: ומעלה (מעלה/עלה): Candidates: H4608 'elevation/acclivity', H4609 'elevation/journey upward', H5927 'to ascend/mount', H5928 'holocaust', H5929 'leaf', H5930 'step/holocaust', H5931 'pretext'. Chose H5927 as a Hiphil participle (מַעֲלָה) meaning 'causes to ascend, exalts' — parallel to 'praises' and producing a coherent image of active worship.

האל (אל): Candidates: H408/H409 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411/H412 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. With the definite article ה and as the object of praise and exaltation, H410 'God' is the only coherent reading.
textual_notes: נשמתי has no Strong's candidates listed but consonants match H5397 (נְשָׁמָה) 'breath, spirit, soul' with 1cs suffix. This is the only plausible reading from the consonants.
משבחת has no candidates listed but consonants match H7623 (שׁבח) 'to praise' in a feminine participle form, agreeing with נשמתי as its subject.

translation_notes: שמחה: Candidates: H8057 'blithesomeness/glee', H4229 (מחה) 'to stroke/erase'. In context of spirit praising God, H8057 'joy' is the coherent reading — spirit being in a state of joy.
באל: Candidates: H408/409 'not', H410 'God', H411/412 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. With prefix ב (in) and parallel to section 1's praise of God, H410 'in God' is the natural reading.
שהוא: The ש is a relative particle ('who/that'), followed by הוא. Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. H1931 as pronoun 'who he [is]' fits the relative clause structure.
textual_notes: שלומי: No candidates listed. Consonants match H7965 (שָׁלוֹם) 'peace, completeness, welfare, soundness' with 1cs suffix. Could also be parsed as the proper name Shelomi (H8015), but in context of describing God, 'my peace/salvation' is far more coherent.

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. As a conjunction opening a causal clause, H3588 is the clear reading.
הוא: H1931 'he' as the subject pronoun referring back to God from sections 1-2.

שפלות: H8220 'remissness' — but in context of a maidservant before God, the consonants שפלות more naturally read as the abstract noun from שפל (H8217) meaning 'lowliness, humble state'. H8220 is listed but its meaning 'remissness/slackness' is less fitting than the broader sense of lowliness/humility.
ובעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Causal conjunction fits perfectly here.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. H2088 as demonstrative pronoun 'this' following ובעבור forms the natural phrase 'on account of this'.
textual_notes: הבריות: No candidates listed. The consonants suggest בריות from ברא (H1254 'to create') — 'creatures/creations'. This is a post-biblical Hebrew formation but fits the consonantal text.

ה%יות: The % symbol suggests a damaged or uncertain letter. The consonants suggest היות from H1961 (היה 'to be') as an infinitive construct 'being'. The phrase אנכי היות מאורת would mean 'I am being illuminated/radiant'.

מאו(רת: The ( suggests a damaged letter. The consonants suggest מאורת from H3974 (מָאוֹר) 'luminary/light-source' or the feminine form meaning 'illuminated/blessed'. This could also relate to H835 (אשר) via a different parsing, but the consonants most naturally read as from אור 'light'. The phrase 'all creatures will call me illuminated/blessed' fits the song of praise context.
שפחתו: No candidates listed. Consonants match H8198 (שִׁפְחָה) 'maidservant/female slave' with 3ms possessive suffix — 'his maidservant'.

translation_notes: כי: H3588 as causal conjunction 'for/because'.
שהוא: ש as relative particle + הוא H1931 'he' — 'who he [is]'.
הוא: H1931 as emphatic pronoun 'he' — subject of עשה.

בי: H994 is listed as 'oh that!/with leave' but the consonants ב + י (preposition ב + 1cs suffix) simply mean 'in me/for me'. The Strong's entry H994 reflects a specific interjection use, but here it functions as the common prepositional phrase.
textual_notes: אותו: No candidates listed. Could be the direct object marker את (H853) with 3ms suffix 'him', or could be אות (H226) 'sign' with 3ms suffix 'his sign'. In context, it appears to function as a pronoun referring to God: 'for him, who is wholly able' — i.e., the direct object marker used pronominally or as emphasis.
כולו: No candidates listed. Consonants match כל (H3605) 'all/whole' with 3ms suffix — 'all of him, entirely, wholly'.
יכול: No candidates listed. Consonants match H3201 (יכל) 'to be able, to prevail' — here as an adjective/participle 'able, capable'.
שמו: No candidates listed. Consonants match H8034 (שם) 'name' with 3ms suffix — 'his name'.
דברים: No candidates listed. Consonants match H1697 (דבר) 'word, thing, matter' in masculine plural — 'things/words'.
גדולים: No candidates listed. Consonants match H1419 (גדול) 'great' in masculine plural — 'great ones/great things'.

translation_notes: חסד: Candidates: H2616 'to bow/be kind', H2617 'kindness/piety/lovingkindness', H2618 'Chesed (proper name)'. As a noun opening a statement about God's enduring quality, H2617 'lovingkindness' is the clear choice.

שלו: Candidates: H7958 'quail', H7959 'security', H7960 'fault', H7961 'tranquil/security'. However, in context שלו most naturally parses as the relative particle ש + ל (to/of) + ו (him) = 'that is of him / his'. This produces the coherent phrase 'His lovingkindness'. The dictionary entries treat שלו as a standalone word, but the consonants here function as a compound particle+preposition+suffix.

מדור: Candidates: H4070 'dwelling', H1752 'to remain', H1753 'to reside', H1754 'circle', H1755 'generation', H1756 'Dor (place)'. With prefix מ (from) and paired with לדור, H1755 'generation' creates the classic phrase 'from generation to generation'.
לדור: Same candidates as דור above. H1755 with prefix ל (to) completes 'from generation to generation'.
textual_notes: ליריאיו: No candidates listed. The consonants suggest ל + ירא (H3373 'fearing, one who fears') + י (plural construct) + ו (3ms suffix) = 'to those who fear him'. The י before ראי could also be parsed differently, but 'to his fearers/those who revere him' is the most natural reading.

שלו could theoretically be read as a standalone word (H7958 'quail', H7961 'tranquil') but this produces incoherent results in context. The compound reading ש+ל+ו ('that of him' = 'his') is far more natural.

translation_notes: כי: H3588, causal conjunction.
הוא: H1931, pronoun 'he' as subject.

מבזה: Candidates: H959 'to disesteem/despise', H960 'scorned', H961 'booty', H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep'. With prefix מ as participial marker and in context of God acting against the proud, H959 'despising/scorning' in participle form produces the coherent image.
והוא: H1931 with conjunction ו, 'and he'.
textual_notes: עושה: No candidates listed. Consonants match H6213 (עשה) 'to do/make' as a masculine singular participle — 'doing/making'.
דברים: H1697 'things/words/deeds' in plural.
חזקים: No candidates listed. Consonants match H2389 (חזק) 'strong/mighty' in masculine plural.
בזרועו: No candidates listed. Consonants match ב + זרוע (H2220 'arm') + ו (3ms suffix) = 'with his arm'.
הגאים: No candidates listed. Consonants match ה + גאה/גא (H1343 גֵּאֶה 'proud/haughty') in plural with article = 'the proud ones'.
במחשבת: No candidates listed. Consonants match ב + מחשבת (H4284 'thought/device/plan') in construct = 'in the thought/scheming of'.

לבו: No candidates listed but the consonants suggest an anomalous form. Expected for 'their heart' would be לבם. However, לבו (H3820 לב 'heart' + ו 3ms suffix) could be 'his heart' referring collectively to each proud person, or the ו suffix may be used loosely for the plural referent.

translation_notes: והוא: H1931 with conjunction, 'and he'.
textual_notes: משפיל: No candidates listed. Consonants match H8213 (שפל) 'to be low/humble' in Hiphil participle = 'one who brings low/humbles'.
החזקים: H2389 'strong/mighty' with article, masculine plural.
והגבוהים: No candidates listed. Consonants match ו + ה + גבוה (H1364 'high, lofty, exalted') in masculine plural = 'and the exalted/lofty ones'.

מאריותם: No candidates listed. This is a difficult form. The consonants suggest מ (from) + אריות + ם (3mp suffix). The most likely root is related to a word for 'throne/seat' — possibly a variant or late Hebrew form. The Aramaic/late Hebrew כורסיא or the Hebrew כסא would be expected for 'throne', but אריות from ארי (H738 'lion') would give 'from their lions' which is incoherent. Another possibility: if this is a scribal rendering of a word for 'seats/places of honor', it may be an unusual form. Given the context of deposing the mighty, 'from their thrones/seats' is the contextually demanded meaning, though the exact etymology is uncertain.
ומגביה: No candidates listed. Consonants match ו + מגביה from גבה (H1361 'to be high') in Hiphil participle = 'and one who raises up/lifts high'.

ה(פלים: The ( indicates a damaged/uncertain letter. In context of being contrasted with 'the strong and exalted', the lowly/humble is expected. Consonants likely reconstruct as השפלים from שפל (H8217 'low, humble') = 'the lowly ones'. The missing letter is likely שׁ, giving השפלים.

translation_notes: ממלא: Candidates: H4390 'to fill', H4391 'to fill (Aramaic)', H4392 'full', H4393 'fullness', H4394 'consecration', H3808 'not'. As a participle with prefix מ describing God's action toward the hungry, H4390 'filling' is the clear reading.
כל: H3605 'all/every' as quantifier before טוב.

טוב: Candidates: H2895 'to be good', H2896 'good (adj/noun)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness/the best'. As a noun following כל, H2896 'good' or H2898 'goodness' both work; H2896 as the broader adjective/noun 'good things' fits naturally.
textual_notes: הרעבים: No candidates listed. Consonants match ה + רעב (H7457 רָעֵב 'hungry') in masculine plural = 'the hungry ones'.
ועוזב: No candidates listed. Consonants match ו + עוזב from עזב (H5800 'to leave, forsake, abandon') as participle = 'and forsaking/leaving/sending away'.
העשירים: No candidates listed. Consonants match ה + עשיר (H6223 'rich, wealthy') in masculine plural = 'the rich/wealthy ones'.
רקים: No candidates listed. Consonants match H7386 (רֵק/רֵיק 'empty, vain') in masculine plural = 'empty/empty-handed'.
The apostrophe at the end likely marks a section break or paragraph marker in the manuscript.

translation_notes: ישראל: H3478 'Israel' as the object of redemption.
textual_notes: פודה: No candidates listed. Consonants match H6299 (פדה) 'to ransom, redeem' as a masculine singular participle = 'redeeming/one who redeems'.

בנו: No candidates listed. Consonants match H1121 (בן) 'son/child' with 3ms suffix = 'his son'. Could alternatively be parsed as H1129 (בנה) 'to build' with 3ms suffix, but 'his son' referring to Israel as God's child is the contextually coherent reading.
זוכר: No candidates listed. Consonants match H2142 (זכר) 'to remember' as a masculine singular participle = 'remembering'.

מחסדיו: No candidates listed. Consonants match מ (from/of) + חסד (H2617 'kindness/lovingkindness') in plural with 3ms suffix = 'from/of his kindnesses/mercies'. The מ prefix could indicate 'from/out of his mercies' (source/motivation) or be partitive.

translation_notes: כמו: H3644 'as, thus, so' — comparative particle introducing the comparison with past promises.
שנדר: Candidates: H5087 'to promise/vow (to God)', H5088 'a promise/vow'. With ש as relative particle and the verbal form, H5087 'that he vowed/promised' fits as a verb: 'as that he promised'.
textual_notes: לאבותינו: No candidates listed. Consonants match ל + אבות (H1 אָב 'father' in feminine plural construct form, used for 'fathers/ancestors') + ינו (1cp suffix) = 'to our fathers/ancestors'.
ולזרעו: No candidates listed. Consonants match ו + ל + זרע (H2233 'seed, offspring, descendants') + ו (3ms suffix) = 'and to his seed/descendants'.

לעולמים: No candidates listed. Consonants match ל + עולם (H5769 'long duration, antiquity, futurity, forever') with ים suffix functioning as intensifier = 'for ages, forever, in perpetuity'. The ים here amplifies the sense of eternity rather than indicating a numerical plural.

translation_notes: עמדה (consonants עמד+ה): H5979 'a station, domicile' — she stationed/settled herself. This fits the context of a prolonged stay with Elisheba.
עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with (preposition)'. Chose H5973 because the preposition 'with' fits — she dwelt with Elisheba.

כמעט (כ+מעט): Candidates: H4591 'to lessen', H4592 'a little/few', H4593 'sharp', H5842 'stylus'. The כ prefix + H4592 yields 'nearly/almost', which fits naturally before a number — nearly three months.

שלשה: Candidates: H8030 'Shilshah (name)', H8031 'Shalishah (place)', H7716 'sheep'. None match 'three' directly in Strong's, but שלשה is the standard Hebrew word for 'three' (feminine form). The consonants ש-ל-ש-ה clearly spell the numeral three, which fits before 'months'.

שבה (consonants שבה): H7617 'to transport into captivity' — however the consonants ש-ב-ה also support the root שוב 'to return' (H7725) in a 3fs perfect form. In context, 'she returned' is the only coherent reading. The captivity meaning produces a bizarre image.
במקדש: Candidates: H4720 'sanctuary/consecrated place', H6944 'sacred place'. Chose H4720 — she returned to her house which was in/at the sanctuary.
textual_notes: חףדשים appears to be חדשים (months) with an anomalous ף — possibly a scribal error or variant spelling. Read as חדשים 'months'.
בביתה lacks a Strong's candidate entry — it is בבית+ה 'to/in her house', standard Hebrew prepositional construction.
שבה could theoretically be H7617 'captivity' but in context must be from שוב 'to return' (H7725), which was not provided as a candidate. The consonants support both roots.

The final phrase 'to her house in the sanctuary' is ambiguous: does it mean her house was located at/in the sanctuary complex, or that she returned first to her house and then to the sanctuary? The Hebrew בביתה במקדש most naturally reads as her home being in/at the sanctuary.

translation_notes: והיה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist, be, become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 — 'and there was/came to be' fits the narrative progression: she gave birth and there was for her a son.
בן: Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'a son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 — the context clearly calls for the common noun 'son'.
ללדת: The root ילד 'to bear/give birth' with ל prefix (infinitive construct) — 'to give birth'. The candidate listing shows דת 'edict' but the full consonantal form ללדת is clearly ל+לדת from ילד.
textual_notes: ותלד has no Strong's candidate listed but is clearly ו+תלד, wayyiqtol 3fs of ילד 'to give birth'.

translation_notes: עמה: Candidates: H5980 'conjunction, near, beside, with', H5981 'Ummah (place)'. Chose H5980 — 'with her' fits perfectly in the clause 'they rejoiced with her together'.
יחד: Candidates: H3161 'to be/become one', H3162 'unitedly, together (adverb)'. Chose H3162 — the adverb 'together' modifies 'they rejoiced with her', producing a natural image.
ה<כנים: The < appears to be a textual corruption or uncertain letter. The context (neighbors hearing news) suggests השכנים 'the neighbors' — from שכן 'neighbor/dwelling'.
]חסדיה: The ] bracket indicates textual damage. Reading חסדיה 'her loving-kindness/grace' from חסד (H2617).
המעולה: From root עלה, meaning 'the exalted/supreme' — describes the greatness of the חסד shown to her.
textual_notes: ה<כנים has a damaged/uncertain character marked by <. Most likely השכנים 'the neighbors' based on context.
]חסדיה has a bracket indicating textual damage at the beginning. Reading as חסדיה 'her loving-kindness'.
מאותה could be parsed as מ+אותה 'from/of that [feminine]' — a demonstrative construction pointing to the exalted grace.

translation_notes: בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of, in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 — 'in order that they would circumcise' makes perfect narrative sense.
הבן: Candidates: H1894 'ebony', H1121 'son'. Chose H1121 with the definite article ה — 'the son'. Circumcising ebony is absurd.
שם: Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name/appellation', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name (Aramaic)'. Chose H8034 — 'they called him [the] name of his father' is the coherent reading.
ונאספו[: The bracket suggests textual damage. Reading as ונאספו from root אסף 'to gather' — 'and they gathered'.
שימולו: Reading as ש+ימולו — 'that they would circumcise', from מול 'to circumcise' (H4135). The ש prefix functions as the relative/purpose particle.
textual_notes: ונאספו[ has a bracket indicating possible textual damage at the end.
בשמונת הימים literally reads 'in the eight of the days' — an unusual construction for 'on the eighth day', but the meaning is clear from context.

translation_notes: כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/right', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 — 'it will not be so' is the natural reading in a naming dispute.

אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay, truly, yet (adversative)'. Chose H61 — 'but/rather' serves as the adversative conjunction needed here: 'not so, but rather his name shall be Yochanan'.
ואמרה: H565 'something said' — but here functioning as the verb 'and she said', from root אמר.
textual_notes: וענתה lacks a listed candidate — clearly from root ענה 'to answer' (H6030) in 3fs wayyiqtol form with 3fs suffix or simply feminine ending.
שיהיה is ש+יהיה 'that it will be' — the ש functioning as relative particle 'that'.

translation_notes: אין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 — 'there is not' introduces the objection: no one in your family has such a name.
כזה: כ+זה. Candidates for זה: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'like this' (כ = 'like' + זה = 'this'), meaning 'such as this name'.
textual_notes: ראוי lacks a Strong's candidate — it appears to be a later Hebrew/Rabbinic form meaning 'fitting, worthy, proper' (from root ראה 'to see/regard').
ה ם appear as separated fragments — likely השם 'the name' with textual damage or spacing issue. The ש is missing or illegible between ה and ם.
במשפחתך is ב+משפחת+ך 'in your family/clan' from משפחה (H4940).

translation_notes: ועשו: The candidate listed is H6215 'Esau', but the consonants ו+עשו clearly parse as waw-consecutive + 3mp perfect of עשה 'to do/make' (H6213). Choosing 'they made' because the context demands a verb — they made a sign to his father. 'Esau' as a proper noun here is nonsensical.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 — 'he' as the subject pronoun: 'how he desires'.

חפץ: Candidates: H2654 'to incline, be pleased, desire', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire'. Chose H2654 as the verb — 'he desires/wishes [that] his name would be'. This produces the natural question: how does the father want the child named?
textual_notes: סימן has no Strong's entry provided — it is a post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew word meaning 'sign, signal, gesture'.
The apostrophe ' at the end may indicate a textual break, lacuna, or section marker.
ועשו consonants match both עשה 'to make' (3mp) and עשו 'Esau' — context decisively favors the verb.

translation_notes: שאל: Candidates: H7592 'to inquire/request/demand', H7593 'to inquire (Aramaic)', H7594 'Sheal (name)'. Chose H7592 — 'he requested/asked for' a tablet. The narrative context is that he is mute and needs a writing surface.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 — 'one tablet' / 'a single tablet'.
אשר (first): Candidates include H834 'who/which/that' and others. Chose H834 — relative pronoun 'which' introducing 'on which he wrote'.

כתב: Candidates: H3789 'to write/inscribe', H3790 'to write (Aramaic)', H3791 'a writing', H3792 'a writing (Aramaic)'. Chose H3789 — the verb 'he wrote', fitting the action of inscribing on the tablet.
שם (second occurrence): Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name'. Chose H8033 — 'all who were there' is the natural adverbial use, distinct from שמו 'his name' which appears earlier.

מזה: Candidates: H4198 'exhausted', H4199 'Mizzah (name)', H2088 'this/that'. Chose מ+זה = 'from this / at this' (preposition מן + demonstrative H2088). They were astonished at this — a coherent concluding image.
אשר (second): Same analysis — H834 'who/that', connecting 'all who were there'.
textual_notes: תמהו has no Strong's candidate listed — it is from root תמה 'to be astonished/amazed' (H8539) in 3mp perfect.
הוא שמו could be read as a nominal clause 'he is his name' (i.e., 'that is his name') or as an emphatic identification. Both yield essentially the same meaning.

translation_notes: ומיד: The candidate is H3027 'hand'. ומיד = 'and from [the] hand', idiomatically meaning 'immediately/at once'. This is standard Hebrew usage.
האב: Candidates: H1 'father', H2 'father (Aramaic)', H3 'green plant', H4 'green plant (Aramaic)'. Chose H1 — 'the father'. The narrative is about Zechariah the father whose mouth is opened.

דברה: Candidates: H1700 'a reason/suit/manner', H1701 same, H1702 'a raft', H1703 'a word'. The consonants also support the verb דבר 'to speak' (H1696) in 3fs perfect — 'his tongue spoke'. Chose this verbal reading because 'his tongue spoke' produces a coherent image of speech being restored. The listed noun candidates don't fit syntactically.

ובירך: The candidate listed is H3409 'thigh'. However ו+בירך clearly parses as waw + piel perfect 3ms of ברך 'to bless' (H1288). The ב is part of the root, not a preposition. 'And he blessed YHWH' is the only coherent reading.
textual_notes: נפתח has no listed candidate — from root פתח 'to open' (H6605) in niphal perfect 3ms, 'was opened'.
פי has no listed candidate — construct form of פה 'mouth' (H6310).
ולשונו has no listed candidate — ו+לשון+ו 'and his tongue' from לשון (H3956).
ובירך: The only listed candidate is H3409 'thigh' (ירך), but the word must be parsed as ברך 'to bless' in piel, which was not provided as a candidate.

translation_notes: והיה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/become/come to pass', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 — 'and there was/came to be' introduces the resulting state of fear.
פחד: Candidates: H6342 'to be startled/fear', H6343 'alarm/fear (noun)', H6344 'testicle'. Chose H6343 — the noun 'fear/dread', which serves as the subject: 'there was fear upon all their neighbors'.
בכל (both): H3605 'the whole/all' — 'in all' or 'upon all'. Standard usage.

הרי: The candidate listed is H7377 'irrigation/shower' for רי, but הרי is clearly the construct plural of הר 'mountain' (H2022) — 'the mountains/hills of'. 'The hill country of Judah' is a well-known geographic designation and produces a coherent image.

אלה: Candidates: H421 'bewail', H422 'adjure', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. However, the consonants אלה also represent the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (H428). In context, 'these words/matters' is the only reading that makes sense — it serves as the demonstrative modifying הדברים.
textual_notes: נתפ טו appears to be a single word split by textual damage — likely נתפרסמו or נתפשטו 'were spread/published'. The exact root is uncertain due to the break. The context demands a verb meaning 'were spread/reported/published'.
שכיניהם has no listed candidate — from שכן 'neighbor' (H7934) with 3mp possessive suffix: 'their neighbors'.
הדברים has no listed candidate — from דבר (H1697) 'word/matter/thing' with definite article and masculine plural: 'the words/matters'.

אלה is identified as the demonstrative 'these' (H428), though this entry was not among the provided candidates. The candidates listed all point to other roots, but the consonants אלה unambiguously also spell the common demonstrative pronoun.

translation_notes: אשר (H834 vs H833/H835/H836/H837/H838): Candidates: H834 'who/which/that', H833 'to be straight', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because this is a relative pronoun introducing 'all who heard' — the standard relative clause construction.

אי (H335 vs H336/H337/H338/H339): Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 because it forms an interrogative phrase 'what will this be?' — a question about the child's destiny.

זה first occurrence (H2088 vs H2089/H2090): H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 as the demonstrative pronoun; 'a sheep' makes no sense in an interrogative about a child's future.

הנער (H5288 vs H5286/H5287/H5289/H5290): H5288 'boy/child', H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble', H5289 'wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 with the article ה — 'the boy/child' fits perfectly as the subject of the question about the child's destiny.
שמוהו: Parsed as שמ + והו — root שים (H7760, to put/place) with 3mp suffix + 3ms object suffix. They placed them (the things heard) regarding him, i.e., stored these things in their hearts.
textual_notes: אי זה could be parsed as a single interrogative phrase 'what sort' or as two separate words 'where/what' + 'this'. The combination אי זה functions idiomatically as 'what kind of' or 'what'.
שמוהו is morphologically complex — it could theoretically be from שם (H8034 'name') as a denominative, but the context of placing things in the heart strongly supports שים (H7760 'to put/place').

translation_notes: היה (H1961 vs H1962): H1961 'to be/become', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 — 'was full' is coherent; 'ruin full of spirit' is nonsensical.

מלא (H4390/H4391/H4392/H4393/H4394 vs H3808/H3809): The consonants מלא clearly support the root meaning 'full/filled'. H4392 (adjective 'full') fits best with היה — 'was full'. The alternative reading מ + לא ('from not') is contextually absurd.

רוח (H7304/H7305/H7306/H7307/H7308): H7307 'spirit/wind/breath' is the noun reading that fits with 'full of spirit'. The verbal readings (H7304 'breathe freely', H7306 'to smell') don't fit the adjectival construction.

הקדש (H6942/H6943/H6944/H6945/H6946): H6944 'a sacred thing/sanctity' with the article — 'the holiness'. This forms the construct 'spirit of the holiness'. H6943 'Kedesh' (place) and H6946 'Kadesh' (place) don't fit; H6945 'cult prostitute' is contextually impossible.
ואמר (H559 vs H560-H564): H559 'to say' is the obvious choice in this narrative context. H563 'a lamb' and H564 'Immer' (proper noun) don't fit.
textual_notes: וניבא: No candidates were provided. Parsed as ו + נבא (root נבא, H5012, 'to prophesy') in a reflexive/passive stem. This is the standard form for 'and he prophesied'.

translation_notes: ברוך: The only candidate listed is H1263 (Baruk, proper name). However, the consonants ברוך are the passive participle of ברך (H1288 'to bless'), yielding 'blessed'. In a doxological opening ('Blessed be the Lord...') this is clearly the passive participle, not the proper name. I assign the gloss 'blessed' from the root ברך.
אדון (H113 vs H114): H113 'sovereign/lord' vs H114 'Addon' (proper name). Chose H113 — 'Lord God of Israel' is a standard divine epithet.
כי (H3588 vs H3587): H3588 'for/because' vs H3587 'brand/scar'. Chose H3588 — conjunction introducing the reason for blessing.
הוא (H1931 vs H1932/H1933/H1934): H1931 'he' (pronoun) fits as subject of 'visited'. The other candidates are Aramaic or verbal forms less suited here.
ישראל (H3478 vs H3479): Both refer to Israel. H3478 is the standard Hebrew form.
textual_notes: א3להי: The consonants appear to contain a textual marker or corruption (the '3'). Read as אלהי — construct form of אלהים (H430), 'God of'. The numeral in the manuscript may indicate a scribal note or variant.
פדיון: No candidates were provided. Parsed as from root פדה (H6299 'to ransom'), noun form פדיון (H6306 'ransom/redemption').
עמו: Could be עם + ו (H5971 'his people') or the preposition עם + ו (H5973 'with him'). Context strongly favors 'his people' — he made redemption for 'his people'.

translation_notes: ומהר (H4116 vs H4117/H4118/H4119 vs H2022/H2023): H4116 'to hurry/hasten', H4117 'to bargain for a wife', H4118 'in a hurry', H4119 'bride-price', H2022 'mountain'. Chose H4116 — 'hastened to give' is contextually coherent in a narrative about God's swift redemption. 'Mountain of giving' or 'bride-price of giving' are forced.
שלום (H7965 vs H7966/H7967): H7965 'peace/welfare/wholeness', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum' (name). Chose H7965 — deliverance/peace fits the theme of salvation from the house of David.
בית (H1004 vs H1005/H1006): H1004 'house/household/dynasty'. Chose H1004 — 'house of David' is the dynastic reference.
דוד (H1730 vs H1731/H1732): H1732 'David' (proper name), H1730 'beloved/uncle', H1731 'pot/basket'. Chose H1732 — 'house of David' is a well-known dynastic designation.
textual_notes: והיישיר: No candidates provided. Parsed as hiphil (causative) of ישר (H3474 'to be straight'), meaning 'he made straight/directed'. The ו prefix is conjunctive, and the יי may reflect a double-yod spelling of the hiphil.
תת: No candidates provided. Parsed as the infinitive construct of נתן (H5414 'to give').

נערו: Could be from נער (H5288 'boy/servant') with 3ms suffix — 'his servant/boy', or from נער (H5287 'to shake off') as a verb. Context of the house of David suggests 'his servant' — referring to David as God's servant.
The apostrophe ' between שלום and בית may represent a divine name abbreviation or a textual separator. Its exact function is unclear.
בית דוד נערו could also be read as 'the house of David his youth' (from H5290 נער 'boyhood'), but 'his servant' fits better with David as YHWH's servant.

translation_notes: כאשר: The כ prefix + אשר. H834 'who/which/that/as' — with כ prefix yields 'as/just as'. The other candidates (H833 'to be straight', H835 'happiness', etc.) don't form meaningful prepositional compounds here.

הגיד: The listed candidate H1517 (גיד 'tendon/thong') doesn't fit. The consonants הגיד match the hiphil perfect of נגד (H5046 'to tell/declare'). The ה prefix is the hiphil marker, not the article. 'He declared' fits the context of prophetic proclamation.

שהם (H7718 'beryl' vs H1992 'they'): The consonants ש + הם. ש functions as the relative particle (= אשר) + הם (H1992 'they'). Reading 'who they [are]' — i.e., 'who are from the beginning of the age'. H7718 'beryl/gem' produces nonsense in this context.
textual_notes: הגיד: The provided candidate (H1517 'tendon') doesn't match the context. I identify this as hiphil of נגד (H5046), which shares the consonants גד in the root but produces הגיד in the hiphil. This is the standard form for 'he declared/told'.
שהם could theoretically be the relative ש + הם ('who they are') or the gemstone שהם (H7718). Context decisively favors the relative construction.

translation_notes: שלום (H7965 vs H7966/H7967): H7965 'peace/welfare/safety' fits as the object of deliverance — salvation from enemies. H7966 'requital' is possible but less natural. H7967 'Shallum' (name) doesn't fit.
ומיד: ו + מ + יד. H3027 'hand' vs H3028 (Aramaic 'hand'). Chose H3027 — 'from the hand of' meaning 'from the power/grip of'.
כל (H3605 vs H3606): H3605 Hebrew 'all' vs H3606 Aramaic 'all'. Chose H3605 for Hebrew context.
textual_notes: משונאינו: No candidates provided. Parsed as מ + שונאינו — from the root שנא (H8130 'to hate'), participle with 1cp suffix: 'from those hating us / from our enemies'.

אותן: No candidates provided. This appears to be a demonstrative/pronoun 'those' (possibly related to את sign of the accusative, or אותו with plural ending). It functions as 'those' referring to the people described in the following relative clause.

שהקציפונו: No candidates provided. Parsed as ש (relative) + הקציפו (hiphil of קצף H7107 'to be wrathful', causative: 'provoked to anger') + נו (1cp suffix 'us'). 'Who provoked us to anger' or 'who enraged us'.

translation_notes: לעשות: The candidates H6219 'shining/polished' and H6220 'Ashvath' (name) don't fit. The consonants עשות are the infinitive construct of עשה (H6213 'to do/make') with ל prefix. 'To do kindness' is a standard Hebrew expression.
חסד (H2616 vs H2617 vs H2618): H2617 'kindness/covenant loyalty' (noun) fits as the object of 'to do'. H2616 (verb 'to be kind') would need different syntax. H2618 'Chesed' (name) doesn't fit.
עם (H5971 vs H5973): H5973 'with' (preposition) vs H5971 'people'. 'To do kindness with our fathers' uses the preposition. 'To do kindness [the] people of our fathers' is awkward.

ולזכור: The candidate H2138 'male' and H2139 'Zakkur' don't fit. The consonants זכור are the infinitive construct of זכר (H2142 'to remember') with ל + ו prefix. 'And to remember' fits the context of recalling the covenant.
textual_notes: קדו<ת: Contains a textual corruption or scribal mark (<). Read as קדושת — construct form of קדושה (from H6944 'holiness'). 'The holiness of his command' or 'his holy [covenant]'.

צואתו: No candidates provided. Parsed as צוא/צוה + תו. Most likely from צוה (H6680 'to command'), noun form צואה (H6673 'command/charge') with 3ms suffix: 'his command/charge'. Alternatively could relate to H6675 צואה 'filth/excrement', but this is contextually impossible in a passage about God's holy covenant.

translation_notes: לאברהם (H85): Only one candidate — Abraham, the patriarch. Fits perfectly in context of the oath sworn to the ancestor.
textual_notes: וה<בועה: Contains a textual corruption or scribal mark (<). Read as והשבועה — from שבועה (H7621 'oath') with the article and conjunctive ו. 'And the oath'.
שנשבע: No candidates provided. Parsed as ש (relative 'that') + נשבע (niphal of שבע H7650 'to swear'): 'that he swore'.

נתון: No candidates provided. Parsed as the passive participle (qal passive / infinitive absolute) of נתן (H5414 'to give'): 'given/granted'. With יהיה this forms a periphrastic construction: 'will be given'.

translation_notes: בעבור (H5668 vs H5669): H5668 'on account of / in order that' vs H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 — purpose clause 'in order that he deliver us' fits the context of divine rescue.

פחד (H6342 vs H6343 vs H6344): H6343 'fear/dread' (noun) vs H6342 'to fear' (verb) vs H6344 'testicle'. Chose H6343 — the noun 'without fear' following בלי. The verb form would require different syntax, and H6344 is contextually absurd.
textual_notes: שיצילנו: No candidates provided. Parsed as ש (relative/purpose) + יציל (hiphil imperfect of נצל H5337 'to deliver/rescue') + נו (1cp suffix 'us'): 'that he will deliver us'.
מאויבינו: No candidates provided. Parsed as מ + אויבינו — from אויב (H341 'enemy') with 1cp suffix: 'from our enemies'.
נעבוד: No candidates provided. Parsed as 1cp imperfect of עבד (H5647 'to serve/worship'): 'we will serve'.

translation_notes: כל (H3605 vs H3606): H3605 Hebrew 'all' vs H3606 Aramaic 'all'. Chose H3605 for Hebrew context.
textual_notes: בקדו<ה: Contains a textual corruption or scribal mark (<). Read as בקדושה — 'in holiness', from the root קדש (H6944).
ובטהףרה: Contains a textual corruption or scribal mark (ף). Read as ובטהרה — 'and in purity', from the root טהר (H2893 'purification/purity').

ימינו could be parsed as ימי + נו ('our days', from יום H3117) or as ימין + ו ('his right hand', from ימין H3225). The context of 'all our days' — describing the duration of service — strongly favors 'our days'. Singular 'his right hand' doesn't fit with כל in this context.

translation_notes: ואתה (אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'thou/you'. Chose H859 because the sentence addresses someone directly ('and you, child'), fitting a second-person address.

נער: Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'boy/child', H5289 'wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the text addresses a young person who will be called a prophet — 'child' fits naturally as a vocative.
נביא: Candidates: H5029 'a prophet', H5030 'a prophet/inspired man'. Chose H5030 as the more common biblical term for prophet.

]מהמאד[: This word appears bracketed/damaged in the manuscript. The consonants suggest מן + המאד, 'of the most/exceedingly'. Read as 'of the Most [High]' connecting to נעלה (exalted) — together: 'prophet of the Most High Exalted.'
שלום (first): Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum'. Chose H7965 because the passage concerns directing paths toward peace/wholeness.

האל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these/those', H413 'near/to'. Chose H410 because with the article ה it reads 'the God/the Mighty One', completing 'in the way of God' as a parallel to 'in the way of peace.'
textual_notes: The bracketed word ]מהמאד[ appears to be a scribal correction or damaged text. The consonants suggest 'of the most' but the exact reading is uncertain. It may be a compound: מן + המאד (from/of the exceedingly) modifying נעלה (exalted), yielding 'prophet of the Most High/Exalted.'
מיו<רים contains a damaged character (<). The likely reading is מיושרים from ישר (to be straight/directed), meaning 'straightened/directed,' but this is uncertain.
תשלום could be parsed as 'you will complete/fulfill' (from שלם, to be complete) or as a noun 'recompense/completion.' The verbal reading fits better with the preceding clauses of purpose.

The final clauses 'שלום תשלום עבדו ושלום בדרך שלום ובדרך האל' have ambiguous phrase boundaries. It could read: 'peace you-will-complete his-service, and-peace in-way-of peace and-in-way-of God' or alternatively segment differently.
רפואה (healing/remedy) is not in the provided Strong's candidates but is a standard Hebrew noun from רפא (H7495, to heal). The form is clear from context.
שלימה (complete/whole) derives from שלם and means 'complete, whole, perfect.' It modifies רפואה — 'complete healing.'
למחילת (for the forgiveness of) derives from מחילה (forgiveness/pardon), a post-biblical Hebrew form. No Strong's number is standard for this noun, though the root מחל relates to pardoning.
עונותיהם (their iniquities) is the plural of עון (H5771) with third-person masculine plural suffix.

translation_notes: בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because the context speaks of a reason (his mercies) for the visitation.

שבהן: The ש is a relative particle ('that/which'), ב is 'in', הן is the pronoun 'them' (H2004). Together: 'in which' or 'by which.' The candidates H931 'thumb' and H932 'Bohan' are irrelevant here — the ב+הן parsing as preposition + pronoun makes clear contextual sense referring back to חסדיו (his mercies).
שהוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as the pronoun 'he [is]' in a relative clause 'who he [is]' — describing the one from on high.
מרום: Candidates: H4791 'altitude/elevated place', H4792 'Merom (lake)'. Chose H4791 because the text describes a divine figure visiting from on high, not a geographic location.
textual_notes: חסד]יו[ has a partially damaged/bracketed suffix. The likely reading is חסדיו 'his mercies/lovingkindnesses' (חסד H2617 with 3ms suffix), but the brackets indicate manuscript uncertainty.
מי שהוא מרום could be read as 'he who is [from] on high' (identifying a divine visitor) or 'whoever is exalted' (a more generic statement). The former fits the context of a divine visitation.

translation_notes: ובצלמות: H6757 'shade of death/the grave/calamity.' This is the only candidate and fits perfectly with the parallel בערפליות (in thick darkness).
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 — purpose clause: 'in order that our feet will be illuminated.'
בדרך: Candidates: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'a road/way'. Chose H1870 as the noun 'way/path' — 'in the way of peace.'
שלום: Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare', H7966 'requital', H7967 'Shallum'. Chose H7965 — 'peace' completes the image of walking in the path of wholeness.
textual_notes: מאו+רות contains a marked character (+). The likely reading is מאורות from אור (light, H216), meaning 'illuminated/given light.' The + may indicate a scribal insertion or uncertain letter.
תהיו is plural ('will be'), agreeing with רגלינו ('our feet'). This confirms the subject is the feet being guided/illuminated.

שיושבין uses the participial form with a final ן (-in), a later Hebrew/Aramaic plural ending rather than classical Hebrew ים (-im). This suggests the manuscript may reflect a later Hebrew dialect or Aramaic influence.

translation_notes: והנער: Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'boy/child', H5289 'wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the narrative follows a child growing up — the article ה indicates a specific, previously mentioned child.
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/become', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because this is a narrative auxiliary 'was' used with participles (growing, strengthening).

גדל: Candidates: H1431 'to be/make large, grow', H1432 'large', H1433 'magnitude', H1434 'thread/tassel', H1435 'Giddel'. Chose H1431 as the verbal form 'growing' — participial use with היה for continuous past action.
וחזק: Candidates: H2388 'to be strong/strengthen', H2389 'strong', H2390 'powerful', H2391 'help', H2392 'power'. Chose H2388 as the verb 'becoming strong' parallel to גדל (growing).

ברוח: Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room', H7306 'to smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 'wind/spirit (Aramaic)'. Chose H7307 because 'spirit' paired with הקדש (holiness) yields 'spirit of holiness' — the domain in which the child was strengthened.

הקדש: Candidates: H6942 'to be clean/holy', H6943 'Kedesh', H6944 'sacred place/thing/sanctity', H6945 'devotee', H6946 'Kadesh'. Chose H6944 because with the article it reads 'the holiness' or 'the holy,' completing 'spirit of the holiness' = 'the Holy Spirit.'
עד: Candidates: H5703 'terminus/duration', H5704 'as far as/until', H5707 'witness'. Chose H5704 as the temporal preposition 'until' — 'until the time.'
שהראה: The ש is a relative particle, ה is the hiphil prefix, ראה (H7200) is 'to see.' In hiphil: 'to cause to see/show.' Chose H7200 in causative stem meaning 'he showed/revealed.'
לישראל: Candidates: H3478 'Israel', H3479 'Israel (Aramaic)'. Chose H3478 as the standard Hebrew form.
textual_notes: עומד (standing/dwelling) could imply either temporary standing or sustained residence. In context with במדברות (in the wilderness places), it likely means 'dwelling/remaining' rather than merely standing upright.
במדברות is the plural of מדבר (wilderness, H4057) with a feminine plural ending -ות, meaning 'wilderness places' or 'desert regions.' This is a less common plural form.

עצמו (himself) could theoretically derive from עצם (H6106 'bone' or H6105 'to be strong'), but in post-biblical Hebrew עצמו functions as a reflexive pronoun 'himself,' which fits the context of 'he showed himself.'

translation_notes: עוד (consonants עוד): Candidates: H5749 'to testify, repeat', H5750 'again, furthermore', H5751 (same as H5750). Chose H5750 because it functions adverbially here introducing a new narrative event — 'again' or 'furthermore' fits the opening of a passage.
היה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist, be, become, come to pass', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because the context requires a copulative/narrative verb 'it came to pass'.

שכל (consonants שכל): This is parsed as the relative particle ש + כל (H3605 'all, the whole'). The context 'that all the world' demands this compound reading rather than H7919 'to be intelligent' or H7921 'to miscarry'.
כן (consonants כן): Candidates: H3651 'so, thus', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. Chose H3651 because paired with כמו it forms the idiom 'like so / likewise'.
textual_notes: נוגש has no Strong's candidates listed but shares consonants with נגש (H5065 'to drive, exact, oppress, tax'). The context of a census/registration decree suggests 'taxed' or 'registered' — the word carries overtones of exacting or pressing for tribute.
ציווי appears to be a post-biblical Hebrew nominal form from צוה (H6680 'to command'); no exact Strong's match. It means 'a command, decree'.
מקיסר and גושט are transliterations of the Latin 'Caesar Augustus' — no Strong's entries exist for these foreign proper nouns.

translation_notes: האדון (consonants אדון): Candidates: H113 'sovereign, controller', H114 'Addon (proper noun)'. Chose H113 because the text describes a ruling authority — 'the lord/governor king of Syria'.
מלך (consonants מלך): Candidates: H4427 'to reign', H4428 'a king', H4430 'a king (Aramaic)', H4432 'Molek'. Chose H4428 because the word is positioned as a noun title following 'the lord'.
במרום (consonants מרום): Candidates: H4791 'altitude, height', H4792 'Merom (a lake)'. Chose H4791 because 'the fathers on high/in the height' fits a liturgical or theological context.

חסד (consonants חסד): Candidates: H2616 'to be kind', H2617 'kindness, lovingkindness', H2618 'Chesed (proper noun)'. Chose H2617 because the noun 'kindness' fits the surrounding phrase about peace and blessing.
textual_notes: This section appears severely corrupted or is a composite of the narrative text with liturgical fragments. The sequence תהיו יהיו תהיו ת תהיינה appears to be scribal repetition or practice marks — multiple verb forms ('you will be', 'they will be', 'they (f.) will be') with no clear syntactic function.
אנור״ל appears to be an abbreviation (marked with ״) whose expansion is unknown. It may be a scribal gloss or reference mark.
דרךשלום appears written as one word, likely 'way of peace' (דרך + שלום). This phrase, along with what follows, may be a liturgical insertion or marginal note that was incorporated into the text.
הנגישה is a nominal/participial form derived from נגש — 'the taxing/registration', corresponding to the נוגש in section 1.

The phrase בעד האדון מלך של שיריאה is ambiguous: it could mean 'while [the] lord [was] king of Syria' (temporal) or 'on behalf of the lord king of Syria' (agential). The context of a first census under a specific governor suggests a temporal reading.

translation_notes: אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify, collect thoughts', H259 'one, united, first'. Chose H259 because כל אחד is 'each one' — a standard distributive expression.

לעירו (consonants עירו): The listed candidate H5900 is 'Iru' (proper noun). However, the ל prefix + עיר + ו suffix clearly gives 'to his city' (from עיר H5892). The proper noun reading makes no contextual sense.
בעבור (consonants עבור): Candidates: H5668 'on account of, in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because a purpose clause fits — they were going in order to comply.
של (consonants של): Candidates: H7944 'a fault', H7945 'on account of, which'. Chose H7945 because it serves as a genitive particle 'of' connecting 'his command' to 'the lord'.
האדון (consonants אדון): Candidates: H113 'sovereign', H114 'Addon'. Chose H113 — referring to the ruling authority who issued the decree.
textual_notes: שישמעו could mean 'that they would hear' or 'that they would obey' — שמע carries both senses. In context of a decree, 'obey/comply with' is the likely force.
האדון could refer to the earthly sovereign (Caesar/governor) or could carry a theological double meaning. The immediate narrative context points to the earthly ruler.

translation_notes: עלה (consonants עלה): Candidates: H5927 'to ascend', H5928 'a holocaust', H5929 'a leaf', H5930 'stairs/holocaust', H5931 'a pretext'. Chose H5927 because the verb 'to go up' fits traveling from Galilee (lower elevation) to Judah (higher elevation).

בעיר (consonants בעיר/עיר): Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'a city', H5893 'Ir (proper noun)', H5894 'a watcher', H5895 'a young donkey'. Chose H5892 because 'to the city of David' is the clear sense in a travel narrative.
דוד (consonants דוד): Candidates: H1730 'beloved, uncle', H1731 'a pot/basket', H1732 'David'. Chose H1732 — the proper name David, as this refers to the ancestral city and lineage.

בית + לחם: בית — H1004 'house'; לחם — Candidates: H3898 'to consume/battle', H3899 'bread/food', H3900 'bread', H3901 'battle'. Together they form the place name Bethlehem ('House of Bread'). H3899 chosen for לחם.
ומעם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people, tribe', H5973 'with'. Chose H5971 because 'from the people/lineage of David' parallels 'from the house of David'.
textual_notes: מנצרת has no Strong's listing — it is a transliteration of the place name Nazareth with the preposition מן (from).

בעבור שיהיה could mean 'in order that he would be [registered there]' (purpose) or 'because he was' (causal). Both are grammatically possible; the causal reading ('because he was from the house of David') explains why he specifically went to Bethlehem.

translation_notes: עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5973 because 'with Miriam' indicates accompaniment — Joseph went to obey the decree together with Miriam.
הרה (consonants הרה): Candidates: H2029 'to become pregnant, conceive', H2030 'pregnant'. Chose H2030 because the adjective 'pregnant' describes Miriam's state at the time.
המצוה (consonants מצוה): Candidate H4687 'a command' fits perfectly; H6680 'to command' is the verbal root. The ה prefix makes this 'the command', pointing to the decree of section 1.
textual_notes: ארוסתו is a post-biblical Hebrew term for 'his betrothed' (from ארוס), with no classical Strong's entry. It clearly denotes a woman pledged in marriage.

The juxtaposition of ארוסתו ואשתו ('his betrothed and his wife') is notable — it may indicate that the text preserves two traditions about her status, or that she was both betrothed and considered his wife.

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who, which, when, where', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כ + אשר forms the conjunction 'when/as', introducing a temporal clause.
שם (consonants שם): Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'a name', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'a name'. Chose H8033 because the context indicates location — 'while they were there [in Bethlehem]'.

מלאו: Root מלא (H4390 'to fill, be full, complete'). No Strong's candidate was listed but this is clearly the 3rd person plural completed form 'were filled/completed'. The days of her pregnancy reached their fullness.
ללדת: ל (infinitive prefix) + ילד (H3205 'to bear, give birth') + ת (infinitive construct ending). 'To give birth.'
שם (consonants שם): Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name'. Chose H8033 — 'she gave birth there' indicates location.
כי (consonants כי): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'because, for, that'. Chose H3588 — introduces the causal clause explaining why the manger was used.
לא (consonants לא): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Chose H3808 — standard Hebrew negation.
מקום (consonants מקום): Candidates: H4725 'a place, standing spot', H6965 'to rise'. Chose H4725 — 'there was no place' requires the noun.
אחר (consonants אחר): Candidates: H309 'to delay', H310 'after', H311 'after', H312 'other, another', H313 'Acher'. Chose H312 because 'another place' fits — no other place was available.
מן (consonants מן): Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from, out of', H4481 'from (Aramaic)', H4482 'a musical chord'. Chose H4480 — 'from the wall' describes the projection.
הקיר (consonants קיר): Candidates: H7023 'a wall', H7024 'Kir (a place)'. Chose H7023 — the physical wall from which the ledge projects.

הבהמות (consonants בהמות): H930 is listed as 'behemoth/hippopotamus', but the consonants are identical to the common plural of בהמה (H929 'beast, animal, cattle'). In context of a manger, domestic animals are meant.
textual_notes: וילדה is parsed as ו + ילדה (she gave birth), not as H3207 'a lass'. The vav-consecutive plus 3fs verb fits the narrative flow.
בנו: The suffix ו could be 'his' or 'her' depending on vocalization. Context (she gave birth to her son) suggests 'her son' though the consonants alone are ambiguous.

קרוי appears to be a passive participle ('that which is called/named') but in this context seems to refer to a physical structure — possibly a protruding shelf or niche in the wall. The word may function both as 'called' and as a noun for the structure itself.

פורשי is a foreign loanword or technical term — possibly from Old French 'porche' or similar Romance language term for a projecting structure/porch. No Hebrew Strong's entry exists. This suggests the manuscript was produced in a Romance-language environment.

The extended explanation about the wall-shelf called 'porshi' appears to be a scribal gloss explaining what kind of structure the manger was in — unusual for a narrative text and suggests a translator adding cultural context.

translation_notes: הדור (consonants דור): Candidates: H1752 'to gyrate, remain', H1753 'to reside', H1754 'a circle/ball', H1755 'a generation, age; also a dwelling', H1756 'Dor (a place)'. Chose H1755. This could mean 'generation' (time period) or 'region/dwelling'. In context, 'in that region' makes good geographic sense (the area around Bethlehem), though 'generation' (era) is also possible.

על (consonants על): Candidates: H5920 'the top, aloft', H5921 'over, upon, against', H5922 (Aramaic same), H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 — 'over their livestock' indicates the shepherds' responsibility.
