שעות: No Strong's candidates directly listed. The consonants match שעה (H8160 Aramaic 'an hour' or post-biblical Hebrew 'hours'). The listed candidates עות (H5790 'to hasten', H5791 'to wrest') would require reading ש as a prefix, giving 'that they twisted/hastened', which makes no sense here. 'Hours/watches' fits — the watches of the night.
textual_notes: הדור could be 'the generation' (temporal — in that era) or could relate to 'dwelling/region' (H1755 secondary meaning). The narrative context allows either, but since באותו הדור parallels באותן הימים in section 1, the temporal reading 'in that period/generation' seems primary.
שעות as 'hours/watches' reflects post-biblical Hebrew usage. Classical Hebrew would use אשמרות for 'night watches'. This further suggests a medieval Hebrew composition or translation.

translation_notes: והנה (consonants הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo! behold!'. Chose H2009 — the interjection 'behold!' introduces a sudden dramatic event.
מלאך (consonants מלאך): Candidates: H4397 'a messenger, angel', H4398 'an angel (Aramaic)'. Chose H4397 — the Hebrew form for a divine messenger.
נצב (consonants נצב): Candidates: H5324 'to station, stand', H5325 'a handle'. Chose H5324 — the angel 'stood/was stationed' near them.

להם: The listed candidate H3859 'to burn in, rankle' requires reading להם as a verb, which makes no sense here. Reading as ל + הם (H1992 'them') gives 'to them', which is the obvious prepositional phrase.
ואור (consonants אור): Candidates: H215 'to make luminous', H216 'illumination, light', H217 'flame', H218 'Ur (a place)'. Chose H216 — 'the light/radiance of YHWH' as a noun subject.
והיה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to be, come to pass', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 — 'and there was to them' (i.e., they had/experienced).
פחד (consonants פחד): Candidates: H6342 'to fear', H6343 'dread, alarm', H6344 'a testicle'. Chose H6343 — the noun 'dread/fear' pairs with the adjective 'great'.

אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — the standard Hebrew verb 'said' in narrative.
אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative negation)', H410 'God, mighty', H413 'to, near'. Chose H408 because אל + imperfect verb (תפחדו) forms a negative command 'do not fear'.
הנה (consonants הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'behold!'. Chose H2009 — introducing the announcement with dramatic emphasis.

מגיד: This is a hifil participle from נגד (H5046 'to declare, announce, tell'). The listed candidate H1517 'a tendon/sinew' (גיד) shares consonants but makes no sense. The מ prefix + גיד consonants as a hifil participle of נגד is the clear reading: 'one who declares/is declaring'.
שמחה (consonants שמחה): Candidates: H8057 'joy, gladness', H4229 'to wipe, erase'. Chose H8057 — 'great joy' is the natural reading after an angelic announcement.
העם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5971 — 'all the people' as the recipients of the joyful news.
textual_notes: תפחדו has no separate Strong's listing but is clearly the 2nd person masculine plural imperfect of פחד (H6342 'to fear') — 'you shall fear / you will fear', here negated as a command: 'do not fear'.

translation_notes: בעיר (consonants ב+עיר): Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'young ass'. Chose H5892 because 'in the city of David' is a coherent place reference that fits a birth announcement, whereas 'in the cattle of David' or 'in the donkey of David' produces no real-world image.

דוד (consonants דוד): Candidates: H1730 'beloved/uncle', H1731 'pot/basket', H1732 'David'. Chose H1732 because paired with 'city of' it identifies a specific place (the city of David), producing a coherent geographical reference.

משיח (consonants משיח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed one/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder/converse', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'a shoot/shrubbery'. Chose H4899 because the mem-prefix + שיח as 'anointed' fits the parallel with 'lord/sovereign' and the birth announcement context.
ואדון (consonants ו+אדון): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon (a name)'. Chose H113 because paired with 'anointed one' it forms a natural title pair in a birth proclamation.
textual_notes: העולם could mean 'the world' (spatial sense) or 'the age/eternity' (temporal sense). Both readings of H5769 are plausible. The spatial reading ('deliverer of the world') fits the grandeur of the announcement; the temporal reading ('deliverer of the age') is also coherent.

translation_notes: האות (consonants ה+אות): Candidates: H225 'to come/assent', H226 'a signal/sign/evidence'. Chose H226 because 'this is the sign' introduces identifying evidence for locating the child, which is the contextual function here.

הנער (consonants ה+נער): Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy/child', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the context describes finding a specific infant who has been born.

בבגד (consonants ב+בגד): Candidates: H898 'to cover/act covertly', H899 'a covering/clothing'. Chose H899 because 'wrapped in a garment' produces a coherent image of a swaddled infant, and the preposition ב + noun is the natural parsing.
textual_notes: באיבוס has no Strong's candidates provided. The consonants א-י-ב-ו-ס correspond to a feeding-trough or manger (a loanword or late Hebrew term). No alternative reading is available from the provided data.
מעוטף could be parsed as a pual participle of עטף (to wrap/cover) or potentially from a related root. The wrapping/swaddling reading is most natural for a newborn child.

translation_notes: עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with (preposition)'. Chose H5973 because 'appeared with the angel' makes sense—the host appeared alongside the messenger. 'A people the angel' would be grammatically awkward.
המלאך (consonants ה+מלאך): Candidates: H4397 'messenger/angel', H4398 'angel (Aramaic)'. Chose H4397 as the Hebrew form, since this text uses Hebrew syntax throughout this section.

חיל (consonants חיל): Candidates: H2426 'army/intrenchment', H2427 'a throe', H2428 'force/army/strength', H2429 'army (Aramaic)'. Chose H2428 because 'multitude of heavenly host/army' is the coherent image—a heavenly military force appearing with the angel.

הודאה (consonants הודאה): The provided candidates under דאה (H1675 'to fly', H1676 'kite') do not fit. The consonants הודאה naturally parse as a noun from the root ידה (to give thanks/praise), meaning 'thanksgiving/praise.' The Strong's candidates listed relate only to the final three consonants דאה, but the full form הודאה is a standard Hebrew noun for 'thanksgiving.' I read it as such.
textual_notes: ומיד literally means 'and from hand' but functions idiomatically as 'immediately/at once.' This is a post-biblical Hebrew usage.

הודאה: The Strong's candidates provided (H1675, H1676 under דאה) do not match the word. The form הודאה is a well-known noun meaning 'thanksgiving/acknowledgment' from ידה. No Strong's number is provided for this reading.
שממיי has no Strong's candidates provided. It appears to be an adjective 'heavenly' derived from שמים (sky/heaven). The doubled מ and yod ending suggest an adjectival form.

translation_notes: לאל (consonants ל+אל): Candidates: H3815 'Lael (name)', H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because 'to God most high' forms a coherent phrase of divine praise. 'To Lael most high' or 'to not most high' make no sense.
עליון (consonants עליון): Candidates: H5945 'the Supreme/lofty', H5946 'the Supreme (Aramaic)'. Chose H5945 as the Hebrew form, modifying 'God.'

שלום (consonants שלום): Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare/prosperity', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. Chose H7965 because 'peace on the earth' is coherent in a proclamation of divine blessing.

טוב (consonants טוב): Candidates: H2895 'to be good (verb)', H2896 'good (adjective/noun)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness/the best'. Chose H2896 as an adjective modifying 'favor'—'good favor/goodwill' toward people.
textual_notes: עלוי has no Strong's candidates provided. It could be a noun meaning 'exaltation/elevation' from the root עלה, or potentially an Aramaic-influenced form. It functions here as the subject: 'Exaltation [will be] to God most high.'
לאנשים has no Strong's candidates provided. Standard plural of איש (man/person) with preposition ל. It could also be parsed as אנשים from אנוש (mortal human).

The phrase מרצון טוב could be read as 'of good favor' (God's goodwill toward people) or 'of [people of] good will' (people who have good will). The Hebrew word order suggests 'favor good' as an attributive phrase modifying the kind of favor.

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants ו+כ+אשר): Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כאשר ('as/when') is a standard temporal conjunction that fits: 'and when the angels departed.'
מהם (consonants מ+הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because מ + הם = 'from them,' the natural prepositional reading.

בבית לחם: For בית: H1004 'house', H1005 'house (Aramaic)', H1006 'Bajith (place)'. For לחם: H3898 'to eat/battle', H3899 'bread/food', H3900 'bread (Aramaic)', H3901 'battle'. Together בית לחם = 'Bethlehem' (House of Bread), the well-known place name. This is confirmed by section 1's reference to 'the city of David.'
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'this thing/matter' is the natural demonstrative before הדבר.

הדבר (consonants ה+דבר): Candidates: H1907 'vizier', H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'this matter/thing which God is doing' produces a coherent request to go verify an event.
אשר: Same as above, chose H834 as relative pronoun 'which.'
האל (consonants ה+אל): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to'. Chose H410 because 'which God is doing' fits the context of a divine action being reported.
textual_notes: ל<מים appears to have a damaged or missing letter (indicated by <). The most likely reconstruction is לשמים ('to the heavens/skies'), as the context describes angels ascending and descending.

והראתה: The ה ending could indicate 3fs perfect ('she showed') or could be a paragogic he on a 3ms form. Given that the subject could be 'God' (masculine) or the implied event/revelation, I read it as hiphil perfect meaning 'has shown/revealed.' The feminine ending is unusual if the subject is האל; it may agree with an implied feminine subject like 'the matter' or 'the sign.'

עולים ויורדים ('ascending and descending') describes the manner of the angels' departure, creating an image of movement between heaven and earth. This could describe their going upward, or a sustained vision of angels going up and down.

translation_notes: מהר (consonants מהר): Candidates: H4116 'to hurry', H4117 'to wed', H4118 'hurrying/in a hurry', H4119 'a price for a wife', H2022 'mountain', H2023 'Hor'. Chose H4118 because 'they went quickly' produces the most natural image of shepherds hurrying to see the child. 'They went [to] a mountain' is possible but doesn't fit the established context of going to Bethlehem.
והנער (consonants ו+ה+נער): Same as section 2 analysis. Chose H5288 'boy/child' because the context is finding the newborn.

מונח: The provided candidate H5146 'Noah (the patriarch)' for נח does not fit. The form מונח is a hophal participle from נוח (to rest/place), meaning 'placed/laid.' This matches the description in section 2.

הבהמות (consonants ה+בהמות): H930 'a water-ox/hippopotamus.' However, בהמות is also simply the plural of בהמה (H929, beast/animal/cattle). In context, 'the animals were around them' describes livestock in a stable setting, which is far more coherent than hippopotami. I read it as the common plural 'beasts/animals.'
היה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to be/exist', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 because 'the beasts were around them' produces a natural descriptive clause.
textual_notes: הבהמות: The only Strong's candidate provided is H930 (hippopotamus/water-ox), but the consonants are identical to the common plural of בהמה (H929, domestic animal/beast). In a stable/manger setting, domestic animals are the obvious reading.
באיבוס again has no Strong's entry. Same feeding-trough/manger reading as section 2.

translation_notes: והנה (consonants ו+הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'and behold, they recognized' introduces a dramatic observation naturally.
הם (consonants הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 as the emphatic pronoun 'they' serving as the subject of 'recognized.'
להם (consonants ל+הם): Same analysis—H1992 with preposition ל = 'to them.' The candidate H3859 'to rankle' does not fit the context.
נער (consonants נער): Same as previous sections. Chose H5288 'boy/child' as the object of recognition.
textual_notes: שאמרו could be parsed as 'that they said' (active: the angels said) or 'that was said' (passive). Both are plausible; the context of recognizing what was told to them suggests 'what was said/told to them.'
הכירו from נכר in hiphil means 'to recognize/acknowledge/identify.' This confirms the shepherds verified what they had been told.

translation_notes: וכל (consonants ו+כל): H3605 'the whole/all' vs H3606 (Aramaic). Chose H3605 as the Hebrew form.
להם: Chose prepositional reading ל + הם (H1992 'them') over H3859 'to rankle,' as 'said to them' is coherent.

בעד (consonants בעד): Candidates: H1157 'in up to/over against/for/behind/through', and various readings of עד. Chose H1157 because 'through/by the shepherds' indicates the means by which the words were communicated.
textual_notes: ש<מעו has a damaged/missing letter (indicated by <). The reconstruction שמעו ('they heard') from שמע is virtually certain given the context.
אותן and מאותן appear to be feminine plural demonstratives ('those'). This is a later Hebrew form. The feminine could agree with an implied feminine antecedent (people, souls) or be used generically.
בעד could mean 'through/by means of' or 'on behalf of' or 'behind.' I chose 'through/by' as it indicates the shepherds as the agents of communication.

translation_notes: שמה (consonants שמה): Candidates: H8047 'ruin/consternation', H8048 'Shammah (name)', H4100 'what?'. However, שמה can also be parsed as the qal perfect 3fs of שים (to put/place/set). In context, 'Miriam placed all these words in her heart' produces a coherent image of treasuring/pondering, whereas 'Miriam [was] ruin' or 'Miriam, what?' does not. Chose the verbal reading from שים.

אלה (consonants אלה): Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to imprecate', H423 'an imprecation', H424 'an oak', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. However, אלה is also the common demonstrative pronoun 'these' (cf. H428). In context, 'all these words' is natural. The Strong's number H428 (אלה = 'these') is not listed among candidates but the consonants match perfectly. I will use H411 which covers 'these/those.'
בלבה (consonants ב+לבה): Candidates: H3826 'the heart', H3827 'flame'. Chose H3826 because 'in her heart' completes the image of inward treasuring. 'In her flame' makes no contextual sense.
textual_notes: שמה is genuinely ambiguous between the verb שים 'to place/put' (3fs perfect) and the noun שמה 'ruin/desolation' (H8047). Context strongly favors the verbal reading.
אלה: The provided Strong's candidates do not include the common demonstrative 'these' (typically H428). I assigned H411 ('these/those') as the closest match among provided options.

translation_notes: והעם (consonants ו+ה+עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people/tribe', H5973 'with (preposition)'. Chose H5971 because with the definite article ה, 'the people' serves as the subject of 'returned.' A preposition 'with' would not take the article in this way.

שבו (consonants שבו): Candidate: H7618 'agate (gem)'. However, שבו is naturally parsed as qal perfect 3cp of שוב (to return). 'The people returned' is coherent; 'the people [were] an agate' is not. Chose the verbal reading from שוב.

כן (consonants כן): Candidates: H3651 'thus/so/just', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'thus/just as' connects to the following כאשר clause naturally.
כאשר (consonants כ+אשר): Chose H834 (relative 'which/that/as') because כאשר = 'as/just as' functions as a comparative conjunction here.

למעלה (consonants ל+מעלה): Candidates: H4608 'elevation/platform/above', H4609 'elevation/journey upward', and various readings of עלה. Chose H4608 because 'above/from above' or 'previously' (as in 'said above/earlier') fits the context—referring back to what was announced earlier.
להם: Prepositional ל + הם (H1992) = 'to them.' Chose over H3859 'to rankle.'
textual_notes: שבו: The provided Strong's candidate H7618 ('agate') shares these consonants, but the verbal reading from שוב ('to return') is far more natural and is the standard parsing.

למעלה could mean 'above' (spatially, i.e., from heaven) or 'previously/before' (temporally, i.e., what was told earlier). Both work: the angels spoke from above, and they also spoke earlier. The ambiguity may be intentional.
והעם ('the people') likely refers back to the shepherds mentioned throughout the narrative, though the term 'people' is broader. Context confirms these are the same group.
אמור appears to be a qal passive participle ('having been said/told'). It could also be parsed as an infinitive absolute. The passive participle reading fits: 'just as was told to them.'

translation_notes: ואחר (אחר): Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'after', H311 'after (Aramaic)', H312 'another', H313 'Acher'. Chose H310 because the conjunction ו + אחר followed by a completed action naturally reads 'and after [something was] completed.'

שמנה: Candidates: H8083 'eight', H4487 'to weigh out', H4488 'a mina', H4489 'a measured portion', H4490 'a division', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H8083 because 'eight days' is a coherent phrase in context of circumcision timing.

הנער (נער): Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy/child', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the article ה + נער in context of circumcision and naming clearly refers to an infant boy.
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 because the verb 'was' functions as the copula connecting 'the child' to 'circumcised.'
בבטן (בטן): Candidates: H990 'belly/womb', H991 'Beten (place)', H992 'pistachio-nut'. Chose H990 because 'in the womb of his mother' is the only coherent reading in context of prenatal events.
textual_notes: ה<ם appears to have a damaged or uncertain letter (marked with <). The reading 'השם' (the name) fits the context — 'that name which was called by the angel' — but the original consonants are uncertain.
שאותו is a compound: ש (that/which) + אותו (him/it). It could refer back to the name or to the child. Context favors 'which' referring to the name Yeshua.

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because וכאשר (and-as-which) functions as a temporal conjunction 'and when.'

משה: Candidates: H4871 'to pull out', H4872 'Moshe the lawgiver', H4873 same, H4874 'a debt', H7716 'a sheep'. Chose H4872 because 'the statute of Moshe' is the coherent reading in legal/ritual context.
הנער: Chose H5288 'a boy/child' for the same contextual reasons as section 1.
בעבור (עבור): Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because 'in order that they would present' is coherent purposive usage.
textual_notes: טהףרת appears to have a damaged or inserted letter (ף). The expected reading is טהרת (purification), from the root טהר. The ף may be a scribal error or variant spelling.

שידרו is parsed as ש + ידרו. The root could be נדר (to vow) or דרר (another root). In context of bringing a child to the Temple 'to YHWH,' the sense of presenting/dedicating or vowing fits. The form suggests a hiphil or similar causative — 'they would present/dedicate.'

translation_notes: שכל: The consonants שכל could be parsed as ש + כל (that + every, H3605) or as the root שכל (H7919 'to be circumspect', H7921 'to miscarry', H7922 'intelligence'). Chose ש + כל because 'that every male' produces a coherent legal formula, while 'intelligence' or 'miscarry' make no sense here.
זכר: Candidates: H2142 'to remember', H2143 'a memorial', H2144 'Zeker', H2145 'a male'. Chose H2145 because 'every male opening the womb' is a well-known legal formula about firstborn males.

פטר: Candidates: H6362 'to cleave/burst through', H6363 'a firstling/opening of the matrix'. Chose H6363 because the noun 'opening [of the] womb' pairs directly with רחם to form the standard phrase for firstborn.

רחם: Candidates: H7355 'to have compassion', H7356 'compassion/womb', H7357 'Racham', H7358 'the womb', H7359 'pity', H7360 'a vulture'. Chose H7358 because פטר רחם (opening of the womb) is a fixed phrase referring to the firstborn.
<כתוב: The < mark suggests damage. The expected reading is שכתוב or הכתוב (that which is written / the written). The root כתב (to write) is clear from context.
textual_notes: <כתוב has a damaged initial letter. Most likely reading is שכתוב (that [which is] written) or הכתוב (the written [thing]).

translation_notes: אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'one pair' is the natural reading.
שני: Candidates: H8144 'crimson', H8145 'two/second', H5204 'lamentation'. Chose H8145 because 'two young doves' parallels the pair of turtledoves as an offering alternative.

בני: Candidates: H1137 'Bani (name)', H1138 'Bunni (name)', H5204 'lamentation'. Actually parsed as בני from בן (H1121 'son'), construct plural 'sons of.' Chose H1121 because 'sons of dove' (young doves) is the standard Hebrew idiom for young pigeons.
יונה: Candidates: H3123 'a dove', H3124 'Jonah'. Chose H3123 because 'sons of dove' = young doves, an offering item.
שעל: Candidates: H8168 'the palm/handful', or ש + על (H5921 'concerning/upon'). Chose ש + על because 'that concerning that child' makes contextual sense introducing a new clause about the child.
נער: Chose H5288 'a boy/child' as in previous sections.

שמעה: Candidates: H8093 'Shimah (name)', H8094 'Shemaah (name)', or from root שמע 'hearing/report'. The form שמעה can be the feminine noun 'a report/hearing.' Chose the common noun sense because 'a report to YHWH' fits the context of what the shepherds communicated.
textual_notes: This section appears textually disrupted. The flow from the offering of doves to the angels speaking about the child, then to the shepherds and circumcision, is disjointed. It may represent a conflation of multiple verses or a scribal rearrangement.
שמעה could be a proper name (H8093/H8094) or a noun from שמע meaning 'a report/hearing.' Context is ambiguous but the common noun reading is slightly more coherent.
לה׳ ליהוה appears redundant — 'to the Lord, to YHWH.' This may be a scribal gloss or duplication, or לה׳ abbreviates a different word.
The final clause שנשלמו נמול הנער is syntactically awkward. It could mean 'that [when] the circumcision of the child was completed' or 'that they completed circumcising the child.'

translation_notes: והנה (הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold!', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'and behold, a man' is the natural presentative usage introducing a new character.

אדם: Candidates: H119 'to flush/turn rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'a red gem'. Chose H120 because 'a man one was in Jerusalem' describes a person being introduced.
אחד: Chose H259 'one' — 'a certain man.'
שמעון: Candidates: H8095 'Shimon', H4583 'an abode', H4584 'Maon', H5770 'to watch', H5771 'perversity'. Chose H8095 because it is clearly a personal name following 'his name [was].'
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'this man was righteous' is the natural demonstrative usage.
וירא (ירא): Candidates: H3372 'to fear/revere', H3373 'fearing/reverent'. Chose H3373 because the adjective 'fearing God' pairs with 'righteous' as a character description.

הנחת (נחת): Candidates: H5181 'to descend/press down', H5182 'to descend (Aramaic)', H5183 'descent/rest/comfort', H5184 'Nachath (name)', H5185 'descending'. Chose H5183 because 'the comfort/consolation of Israel' describes the messianic hope Shimon awaited.

ורוח (רוח): Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room/deliverance', H7306 'to blow/smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 same (Aramaic). Chose H7307 because 'spirit of holiness' is the expected phrase.

הקדש (קדש): Candidates: H6942 'to make clean', H6943 'Kedesh', H6944 'a sacred thing/sanctity', H6945 'a devotee', H6946 'Kadesh'. Chose H6944 because 'the holiness' with the article forms 'the spirit of the holiness' = the Holy Spirit.
textual_notes: ש<מו has a damaged letter (marked <). Expected reading is שמו (his name). The ש could be a relative pronoun ש or part of the word שמו. Most likely: 'his name [was].'
ממתין is not a standard biblical Hebrew form. It appears to be a later Hebrew participle from the root מתן or המתין (to wait). This suggests the text may contain post-biblical Hebrew vocabulary.

translation_notes: וקבל (קבל): Candidates: H6901 'to admit/take/receive', H6902 'to acquire', H6903 'on account of', H6904 'battering-ram', H6905 'the presence'. Chose H6901 because 'he received an answer' is the coherent narrative action.

מענה: Candidates: H4617 'a reply/response', H4618 'a furrow', or verbal roots H6030-H6034. Chose H4617 because 'he received a reply from the Spirit of Holiness' produces a clear image of divine communication.
מרוח: Candidates: H4790 'bruised/emasculated', or מ + רוח (from + spirit). Chose the prepositional reading מ + H7307 because 'from the spirit of holiness' is the natural source of the divine answer.

ראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'a vulture', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'a seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 because 'see death' and 'see Yeshua' both use the basic verb of perception.
מות: Candidates: H4191 'to die', H4192 title of a song, H4193 'death (Aramaic)', H4194 'death'. Chose H4194 because the noun 'death' is the object of 'see.'

עד: Candidates: H5703 'perpetuity', H5704 'until', H5705 same (Aramaic), H5706 'booty', H5707 'a witness', H5708 'menstrual flux'. Chose H5704 because 'until he would see' is the temporal conjunction needed.

שיראה: The candidates list H3374 'fear/reverence' for יראה. However, in context the form is clearly ש + יראה from ראה (H7200 'to see') in imperfect 3ms — 'that he would see.' The consonants ירא and יראה overlap between ירא (fear) and ראה (see), but the preceding עד ש ('until that') demands a visual perception verb, not 'fear.'
אל: Candidates: H408 'not', H409 same, H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these/those', H412 same, H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because 'son of God living' is coherent as a title following 'Messiah.'
חי: Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 same (Aramaic). Chose H2416 because 'the living God' is a standard epithet.
textual_notes: י before ראה appears to be a fragment — possibly the imperfect prefix י of the verb יראה (he will see), with ראה written separately. The combined reading is יראה = 'he would see.'
שיראה: The consonants could theoretically support ש + יראה from ירא 'to fear' (H3374), yielding 'until he fears.' But the parallel with 'see death' earlier strongly favors 'until he sees Yeshua.'

translation_notes: ברוח (רוח): Chose H7307 'spirit' because 'he came by the Spirit to the sanctuary' continues the theme of the Holy Spirit guiding Shimon.
אל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Chose H413 because 'to the sanctuary' indicates direction of movement.
המקדש: Candidates: H4720 'sanctuary/consecrated place', or root קדש readings. Chose H4720 because 'the sanctuary' (Temple) is the clear destination in Jerusalem.
וכאשר: Chose H834 as temporal conjunction 'and when,' same reasoning as section 2.
שיעשו: Listed candidate H3299 'Jaasu (name)' is not relevant. The form is ש + יעשו, imperfect 3mp of עשה 'to do/make.' Reading: 'that they would do.'

מנהג: Candidates: H4491 'the driving (of a chariot)', H5090 'to drive/lead'. Chose H4491 but with the extended post-biblical meaning of 'custom/practice,' which developed from the sense of 'manner of conduct/driving.' The context of ritual observance supports this.
בעבור: Chose H5668 'in order that' for purposive sense.
textual_notes: דתו — 'his law': the possessive suffix ו (his) could refer to the child's law (the Torah applicable to him as a firstborn) or to the law of Moshe mentioned earlier. The referent is ambiguous.

מנהג in biblical Hebrew strictly means 'the driving of a chariot' (H4491), but here it clearly functions in its later Hebrew sense of 'custom/practice.' This is another indicator of post-biblical vocabulary in this text.

translation_notes: ושמעון: Candidates: H8095 'Shimon', H4583 'abode', H4584 'Maon'. Chose H8095 because the named character Shimon is the subject continuing from section 5.

ובירך: The candidates list H3409 'thigh' for ירך, but the form ובירך is clearly ו + בירך from ברך (to bless) in piel perfect 3ms. The consonants ב-ר-ך are the root here, not י-ר-ך. The candidate listing is misleading — the root is ברך not ירך. Reading: 'and he blessed.'
האל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to'. Chose H410 because 'he blessed the God' is the natural object of blessing in a temple scene.
ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same (Aramaic), H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because 'and said' introduces the speech that follows.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord', H114 'Addon (name)'. Chose H113 because Shimon is addressing God as 'Lord/Sovereign.'
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 same, H859 'you'. Chose H859 because 'Lord, now you release' addresses God in second person.
בשלום: Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare/wholeness', H7966 'a requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. Chose H7965 because 'in peace' describes the manner of the servant's release.
textual_notes: עזוב — from root עזב (to leave, abandon, release). The form could be an imperative ('release!'), a participle ('releasing'), or an infinitive absolute. Context of address to God ('Lord, now you...') suggests either imperative or participle. The lack of explicit verb morphology markers makes this ambiguous.

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Chose H3588 because 'for my eyes saw' provides the causal explanation for being released in peace.
textual_notes: שלומך — 'your peace/salvation/welfare': from שלום (H7965). In this context, referring to what Shimon's eyes have seen, this likely refers to the divine salvation/deliverance embodied in the child Yeshua. The word שלום encompasses peace, wholeness, welfare, and salvation — all may be in view here. This is notably not the word ישועה (salvation) but שלום, suggesting the emphasis is on wholeness/completeness of God's redemptive act.

translation_notes: שהכינות: No Strong's candidates provided. Parsing as ש (relative particle 'that') + הכינות (Hiphil 2ms/2fs perfect of כון 'to establish/prepare'). The form means 'that you prepared/established.'
העם: Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5972 (Aramaic), H5973 'with', H5974 (Aramaic 'with'). With the definite article ה, this is clearly 'the people' (H5971), not the preposition 'with.'
שיהיו: No candidates provided. Parsing as ש (relative 'that') + יהיו (Qal imperfect 3mp of היה 'to be'): 'that they will be.'

באור: Candidates: H215 'to be luminous', H216 'illumination/luminary', H217 'flame/the East', H218 'Ur'. With prefix ב ('in/as'), H216 'illumination/light' fits naturally: 'as a light' or 'in light.' The context of revelation to peoples supports this.
והגדת: No candidates provided. Parsing as ו + הגדת, from root נגד (Hiphil noun form), meaning 'declaration/telling.' This is a nominal form meaning 'and a declaration.'
לעמים: No candidates provided separately but עם has H5971 'people.' With ל prefix and ים plural: 'to the peoples.'
ואזרת: No candidates provided. Parsing as ו + אזרת, from root עזר 'to help' or אזר 'to gird.' In context of strengthening Israel, both work. Choosing 'help/girding' as the meaning.
עמך: Parsing as עם + ך (2ms possessive suffix): 'your people.'
textual_notes: ואזרת could derive from אזר 'to gird/strengthen' or עזר 'to help.' Both produce coherent readings in context of Israel. The consonants favor אזר 'girding/strengthening.'

translation_notes: ואביו: ו + אב + יו: 'and his father.'
ואמו: ו + אם + ו: 'and his mother.'
תמהים: Plural participle from תמה 'to be amazed/astonished.' Meaning 'marveling/astonished.'
מאותן: מ (from) + אותן (those, feminine demonstrative pronoun in later Hebrew): 'from those.'
הדברים: ה + דברים, plural of דבר 'word/thing': 'the words/things.'
ש: Relative particle: 'that/which.'
נאמרו: Niphal perfect 3mp of אמר 'to say': 'were spoken.'
ממנו: מ + מנו 'from him/about him.'
והיה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah.' H1961 fits as the narrative verb 'and he was/it was.'
textual_notes: The words ירושלים, בירושלים, ירושלם appear to be scribal repetitions or marginal variants of 'Jerusalem/in Jerusalem' that were incorporated into the text. Similarly ושמו ('and his name') appears to be a fragmentary note or displaced text. These likely represent scribal glosses or textual corruption rather than continuous narrative.

translation_notes: ושמעון: Candidates: H8095 'Shimon/Simeon', H4583 'abode', H4584 'Maon.' In a narrative where someone blesses and speaks, a personal name is required. H8095 Shimon fits.

בירך: The only candidate offered is H3409 'thigh.' However, the consonants ברך clearly correspond to the root ברך 'to bless' (H1288). The form בירך is a Piel perfect 3ms 'he blessed.' The H3409 candidate shares only ירך consonants. Choosing ברך 'blessed.'
ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 (Aramaic), H561 'something said', H562, H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer.' With ו prefix and narrative context 'and said,' H559 is the clear choice.
שזה: ש + זה. Candidates for זה: H2088 'this/that' (demonstrative), H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that.' A sheep makes no sense; H2088 demonstrative pronoun fits: 'that this one.'
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 (Aramaic), H1933 'to be', H1934 (Aramaic). As pronoun in nominal clause: H1931 'he [is].'
מונח: The only candidate H5146 is נח 'Noah.' However מונח is clearly a Hophal participle of נוח 'to rest/lay/place' — meaning 'laid, placed, appointed.' The מו prefix is the Hophal participle marker.
ולאות: Candidates: H225 'to come/assent', H226 'a signal/sign/omen.' Context of something set as a portent clearly points to H226 'sign.'
למושיע: Hiphil participle of ישע 'to save' with ל prefix: 'for a savior/deliverer.'
ולפדיון: ו + ל + פדיון from פדה 'to ransom/redeem': 'and for a redemption.'
textual_notes: נגדו at the end could be parsed as 'against him' (נגד + ו suffix) or as a verb from נגד 'to declare.' In context following נאמרו ('were spoken'), 'against him' as a prepositional phrase complements the verb: 'were spoken against him.' The ובו earlier may be a doublet or intensifier — 'and in/against him... were spoken against him.'

translation_notes: ובסכין: ו + ב + סכין 'knife/blade.' No candidates provided. Standard Hebrew word for cutting instrument.
יחצו: From חצה 'to divide/pierce' — imperfect 3mp: 'they will divide/pierce.'
ויעברו: ו + יעברו, imperfect 3mp of עבר 'to pass through/cross over.'
נפשו: נפש + ו. The suffix could be masculine 'his' or (in later Hebrew convention) feminine 'her.' Given the context pointing to the mother addressed in the prior section, reading as 'her soul.'
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain.' Context demands the conjunction: H5668.
לבבות: The candidate H956 (בות 'to lodge') doesn't account for the full word. לבבות is the plural of לבב 'heart' (H3824). Reading as 'hearts.'
מפורסמות: Later Hebrew form, Pual participle feminine plural of פרסם 'to publicize/make known.' No Strong's entry — this is a post-biblical Hebrew word meaning 'made known/revealed.'
textual_notes: נפשו — the suffix ו is typically masculine ('his soul'), but in this textual tradition it may serve for feminine ('her soul'), referring to the mother. Context from the preceding section (addressed to 'his mother') suggests 'her soul.'
ובסכין is unusual — traditional renderings of this passage-type use 'sword' (חרב). סכין specifically means 'knife.' This may be a translator's lexical choice.

translation_notes: ובת: Candidates: H1323 'daughter', H1324 'bath measure', H1325 (Aramaic bath). Context of a named person's lineage: H1323 'daughter.'
אשר: Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/that', H836 'Asher (tribe)', H835 'happiness', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step.' Following מ<בט (tribe), this is the tribal name Asher: H836.
באה: Candidate H872 'an entrance.' However באה is also the Qal perfect 3fs of בוא 'to come/enter.' In the phrase באה בימים 'come in days' = 'advanced in age,' the verbal reading fits perfectly.
עם: Candidates: H5971 'people', H5973 'with.' Before אישה 'her husband,' H5973 'with' is correct.
שבע: Candidates: H7646-7651. Before שנים 'years,' the numeral H7651 'seven' is the natural choice.
שנים: Candidate H8147 'two/twofold.' However שנים also represents the plural of שנה 'year.' Given it follows the number seven, 'years' is the correct reading.
ע ם: These appear to be the word עם 'with' split by a scribal break. Combined they read עם 'with' — connecting to בתוליה 'her virginity': 'from her virginity' or 'with her virginity.'
textual_notes: מ<מואל and מ<בט appear to contain damaged or unclear characters (marked with <). מ<מואל likely represents פנואל (Phanuel), and מ<בט likely represents משבט or שבט ('from the tribe of').
ע ם split across two tokens is likely a single word עם 'with.' The phrase עם בתוליה means 'from/since her virginity.'
שנים could be 'years' (plural of שנה) or 'two' (H8147). After 'seven,' 'years' is the clear reading.

translation_notes: אלמנה: H490 'a widow/desolate place.' In context of a woman: 'widow.'
עד: Candidates: H5703 'perpetuity', H5704 'as far as/until', H5705 (Aramaic), H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'menstrual flux.' Before a number of years, H5704 'until/up to' fits.
ארבע: Candidates: H702 'four', H703 'four', H704 'Arba (a person).' Before ושלשים 'and thirty,' the numeral H702 'four' is correct. The phrase 'four and thirty' = thirty-four.
שנה: Candidates: H8138 'to fold/duplicate', H8139 'sleep', H8140 'year (Aramaic)', H8141 'year', H8142 'sleep', H5089 'lamentation.' After a number, H8141 'year' is correct.
textual_notes: ארבע ושלשים שנה — literally 'four and thirty years.' This could mean thirty-four years as a widow, or the Hebrew translator may have been rendering 'eighty-four' (the age) with a textual confusion. The literal consonantal text says 'four and thirty.'

translation_notes: שעה: Candidates: H8159 'to gaze/inspect', H8160 'a look, a moment.' After באותה 'in that,' H8160 'moment/hour' fits as a noun: 'in that moment.'
מתודה: Based on H8426 תודה 'thanksgiving/confession.' מתודה is a Hitpael participle feminine of ידה: 'confessing/giving thanks.'
ליהוה: H3068 'YHWH' with ל prefix: 'to YHWH.'
מדברת: The candidate H1705 'Daberath (a place)' doesn't fit. מדברת is the Piel participle feminine of דבר 'to speak': 'speaking.'
לכל: H3605 'all' with ל prefix: 'to all.'
למרים: H4813 'Miriam.' With ל prefix: 'to Miriam.'
textual_notes: The sequence תהיו יהיו תהיו ת תהיינה יהיו appears to be extensive scribal repetition/corruption. Multiple variant forms of 'they will be' (feminine, masculine, 2nd person, 3rd person) are listed, suggesting a copyist was working through alternatives. Only one instance is needed for coherent text.

The passage from לפדיון ובו יעברו בסכין ויחצו נפשו שמחשבות appears to be a repetition or gloss from section 5 (Simeon's prophecy about the sword piercing the soul), incorporated into the Anna narrative. This may be a marginal comment that entered the main text.
ותקרבו תבטחו at the end appear to be displaced text or scribal additions — 'and you will draw near, you will trust' — not clearly connected to the preceding narrative.

translation_notes: וכאשר: Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'step.' With כ prefix and ו conjunction, כאשר = 'when/as': H834.
דברי: Candidate H1704 'Dibri (a person).' However דברי is the construct plural of דבר 'word/matter' (H1697). Reading as 'matters/words of.'
דת: H1881 'a royal edict/statute' or H1882 (Aramaic). In the phrase 'matters of the law of Moses,' H1881 'law/statute' fits.
משה: Candidates: H4871 'to pull out', H4872 'Moses', H4873 (Aramaic Moses), H4874 'debt', H7716 'sheep.' After 'law of,' the personal name Moses (H4872) is clear.
בעיר: Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir (person)', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'young ass.' Before נצרת (Nazareth, a place), H5892 'city' is correct.

והנער: Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy/youth', H5289 'wanderer', H5290 'boyhood.' With definite article ה and followed by a proper name, H5288 'boy/youth' is correct.
ישוע: H3442 or H3443, both 'Yeshua.' H3442 chosen as the standard entry.

גדל: Candidates: H1431 'to be/make large/grow', H1432 'large', H1433 'magnitude', H1434 'thread/tassel', H1435 'Giddel (person).' In a sequence describing a child's development, H1431 'grew' (Qal perfect) is correct.
וחזק: Candidates: H2388 'to fasten/be strong', H2389 'strong', H2390 'powerful', H2391 'help', H2392 'power.' Parallel with 'grew,' H2388 verbal sense 'became strong' fits.

ומלא: Candidates: H4390 'to fill/be full', H4391 (Aramaic), H4392 'full', H4393 'fullness', H4394 'consecration', H3808 'not', H3809 (Aramaic 'not'). Before חכמה 'wisdom,' H4392 'full' or H4390 'was filled' both work. Choosing H4392 as adjective 'full [of].'
חכמה: H2451 'wisdom' vs H2452 'wisdom' (Aramaic). Hebrew context: H2451.
וחן: H2580 'grace/favor/beauty' vs H2581 'Chen (a name).' In the phrase 'grace of YHWH,' H2580 is correct.
יהוה: H3068 vs H3069. H3068 as the standard divine name.

שנה (consonants שנה): Candidates: H8138 'to fold/duplicate', H8139 'sleep', H8140 'year (Aramaic)', H8141 'year', H8142 'sleep'. Chose H8141 because 'every year' is the coherent temporal expression with בכל preceding it.
של (consonants של): Candidates: H7944 'a fault', H7945 'on account of/of'. Chose H7945 because it functions as a genitive particle connecting 'the honored day' to 'Passover'.

פסח (consonants פסח): Candidates: H6452 'to hop/skip over', H6453 'Passover (the festival)', H6454 'Paseach (name)', H6455 'lame'. Chose H6453 because the context is a pilgrimage festival in Jerusalem.

וכאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כאשר is a temporal conjunction 'when' introducing the circumstantial clause.

הנער (consonants נער): Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the definite article + noun referring to a named person (Yeshua) fits 'the boy'.
שנה (consonants שנה): Chose H8141 'year' because it follows the numeral 'twelve' and denotes age.
textual_notes: עולים is a participle without explicit subject; context implies the family (his father and mother) were going up, continuing from section 1.

translation_notes: הנער (consonants נער): Chose H5288 'boy' as in section 2, referring to the same youth Yeshua.
ולא (consonants לא): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation.
textual_notes: כש<בין appears to have a damaged/corrupt consonant (<). Reading as כשבין or כששבין — likely כש + שבין (when they returned), from שוב (to return). The < may represent a damaged shin or other letter. The reading 'when they returned' fits the narrative context of departing Jerusalem after the festival.

הכירוהו — literally 'they recognized him' with negation: 'they did not recognize/notice [that he was missing]'. This could also mean 'they did not know [where he was]' — the verb נכר can mean to recognize or to notice.

translation_notes: עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people/tribe', H5972 'a people (Aramaic)', H5973 'with (preposition)', H5974 'with (Aramaic)'. Chose H5973 because the preposition 'with' fits: 'he would be with the others'.
וכן (consonants כן): Candidates: H3651 'so/thus', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'and so/thus' connects the assumption to the action of traveling.
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'one day' is a standard temporal expression.
בין (consonants בין): Candidates: H995 'to understand', H996 'between/among', H997 'between (Aramaic)'. Chose H996 because 'among the rest of the relatives' describes where they searched.

שאר (consonants שאר): Candidates: H7603 'leaven', H7604 'to remain', H7605 'a remainder', H7606 'a remainder (Aramaic)', H7607 'flesh/kindred'. Chose H7605 'remainder/rest' because 'the rest of the relatives' is the natural reading for searching among their wider circle. H7607 'kindred/flesh' would also work contextually but שאר + הקרובים reads better as 'the rest of the close ones'.
textual_notes: הנוכרים — could be read from נכר 'to recognize/be acquainted' (i.e., 'acquaintances, known ones') or from נכרי 'foreigner, stranger'. In context, searching among 'foreigners' after already searching among relatives makes less narrative sense. More likely this means 'acquaintances' — people known to them but not family. However, the consonants נכר more commonly yield 'foreign/strange' in biblical Hebrew. This text may use a later Hebrew sense where הנוכרים = 'the recognized/known ones'.
הלכו — the candidates list shows כו H3551 'window' but this is clearly the verb הלך (to go/walk) in 3rd person plural perfect, not a separate word. The system parsed the suffix incorrectly.

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants אשר): Chose H834 'when' as temporal conjunction, same usage as section 2.
לא (consonants לא): Chose H3808 standard Hebrew negation particle.
במקדש (consonants מקדש): H4720 'a consecrated place, sanctuary, palace'. The context of Jerusalem pilgrimage and teachers makes 'the Temple/sanctuary' the clear reading.
textual_notes: ה<לישי — the < appears to be a damaged or uncertain consonant. Reading as השלישי (the third), which fits the narrative of finding him after a period of searching. The damaged letter is likely a shin (ש).
ושואלן — the suffix ן- (rather than ם-) for 'them' reflects a later/dialectal Hebrew form. This is a notable linguistic feature of the manuscript.

translation_notes: וכל (consonants כל): Chose H3605 'the whole, all' as it introduces the collective subject 'all who were hearing him'.
textual_notes: ה<ומעין — the < again appears to be a damaged consonant. Reading as השומעין (the ones hearing), with the Aramaic/late Hebrew participial plural suffix ין-. The damaged letter is likely a shin (ש).
מתמיהין — hitpael or causative participial form with ין- suffix, from תמה (to be astonished). The ין- ending again reflects later Hebrew or Aramaic influence.

ומענהו — could be parsed as 'and his answer' (from ענה, to answer → מענה, an answer) or potentially 'and his response/testimony'. The singular construct 'his answer' fits the pairing with 'his wisdom'.

translation_notes: האב (consonants אב): Candidates: H1 'father', H2 'father (Aramaic)', H3 'a green plant', H4 'a green plant (Aramaic)'. Chose H1 because the narrative context is parents finding their child.
והאם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H517 because paired with 'the father' — 'the father and the mother'.
למה (consonants מה): Candidates: H4100 'what/why/how', H4101 'what (Aramaic)'. Chose H4100 because ל + מה = 'for what' = 'why', a standard Hebrew interrogative.
כי (consonants כי): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Chose H3588 as the causal conjunction introducing the reason for their distress.
אני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the mother is speaking in first person.
ומאד (consonants מאד): H3966 'vehemently, greatly, exceedingly'. This is the only strong candidate; H108 'fog' does not fit.
textual_notes: כואבים — from כאב (to be in pain, to grieve). The candidates list shows H38 'Abijam' for אבים which is clearly wrong for this word. The full form כואבים is a participle meaning 'are aching/grieving/in pain'. This is the mother speaking of both parents' distress.
חפשנוך — 'we searched for you' with the archaic/emphatic 2ms suffix ך-. The verb חפש means to search thoroughly.

translation_notes: והוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 as the independent pronoun 'he' introducing the speaker.

אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said (Aramaic)', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the verb 'said' fits the narrative of direct speech.
להם (consonants הם): The preposition ל + H1992 'them' = 'to them'.
מה (consonants מה): Chose H4100 as the interrogative 'what'.
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 as the demonstrative pronoun paired with מה = 'what is this'.
לא (consonants לא): Chose H3808 as the negation in a rhetorical question: 'did you not know?'
שאני (consonants אני): Chose H589 'I' with relative prefix ש = 'that I'.

שהן (consonants הן): Candidates: H2004 'they (feminine)', H2005 'lo!/behold', H2006 'lo/unless/whether'. Chose H2004 because 'that they are' (referring to הדברים) fits the clause 'the things that are of my father'.
מאבי: The candidates show H21 'Abi (a name)' for אבי, but this is clearly מ + אבי 'from/of my father', using the common noun אב (H1) with 1st person singular suffix.
textual_notes: שחוייב — this appears to be a passive participle from חיב (to be obligated/required), a form more common in Mishnaic/later Hebrew. It means 'it is obligated/necessary/required'.

באותן הדברים שהן מאבי — 'in those things/matters that are of my Father.' This could mean 'in the affairs of my Father' (i.e., in my Father's house/business/concerns). The phrase is ambiguous between 'in my Father's house' and 'about my Father's affairs/matters'. The Hebrew הדברים can mean both 'words/matters/things/affairs'.
מאבי — the מ prefix could be partitive ('from my father') or possessive ('of/belonging to my father'). In context, 'that belong to my Father' or 'that are of my Father' is the natural reading.

translation_notes: והם (consonants הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because 'and they' is the subject of the clause.

הדבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1907 'a vizier', H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'a pestilence', H1699 'a pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'the word/matter' that he spoke to them is the object of understanding.

שאמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said (Aramaic)', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 as the verb 'said' in the relative clause.
להם: Preposition ל + H1992 'them' = 'to them'.

וירד (ירד): Candidates: H3381 'to descend', H3382 'Jered (proper name)'. The waw-consecutive prefix and the context of traveling to a destination clearly indicate the verb 'to descend/go down.' Chose H3381.

והיה (היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah (sacred name)'. The waw-prefix with the surrounding narrative context of describing his ongoing state ('was subjected') clearly points to the verb 'to be.' Chose H1961.

להם (ל + הם): Candidates: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they/them'. The preposition ל + pronoun הם giving 'to them' fits perfectly as the complement of 'subjected.' Chose H1992.

אלה: Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak/strong tree', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. None of these fit. In context, 'all ___ the words' demands a demonstrative pronoun 'these' (אלה as demonstrative, commonly listed under H428). The consonants אלה serve as the demonstrative 'these' in Hebrew, which is the only reading that produces coherent syntax here.
בלבה (לבה): Candidates: H3826 'the heart', H3827 'flame'. 'In her heart' is the natural reading for preserving words/matters internally. 'In her flame' would be bizarre. Chose H3826.
textual_notes: משועבד is a Mishnaic/late Hebrew passive participle from the root שעבד (to enslave, subject, obligate). It does not appear in the Strong's biblical lexicon. The form clearly means 'subjected/made subordinate/obedient.'
מקיימת is a late Hebrew participle from קיים (to uphold, preserve, fulfill). It also does not appear in the classical Strong's lexicon. The form means 'preserving/maintaining/keeping.'
אלה as demonstrative 'these' (H428) was not listed among the candidates but is the only consonantally and syntactically viable reading in 'all these the words.'

translation_notes: מרבה: Candidates: H4766 'increasing/greatness', H4767 'abundance/great quantity', H7235 'to increase', H7236 'to increase (Aramaic)', H7237 'Rabbah (place)'. The participial form מרבה describing Yeshua's progressive growth fits H4766 'increasing' as an active participle/adjective. H4767 as a noun 'abundance' is possible but less natural as a predicate here. Chose H4766.

ובשנים (שנים): Candidate: H8147 'two/twofold'. However, the consonants שנים also correspond to שנים from שנה (H8141 'year'), meaning 'years.' In context of growing in wisdom and years and favor, 'years' (indicating age/maturity) is the coherent reading. H8147 'two/twofold' makes no sense here.

ובחן: Candidates: H974 'to test/investigate', H975 'watch-tower', H976 'trial', H2580 'graciousness/favor/beauty', H2581 'Chen (name)'. The preposition ב + חן: growing 'in favor/grace' alongside wisdom and years produces a coherent image of a maturing person gaining approval. 'In testing' or 'in a watch-tower' would be incongruous. Chose H2580.
textual_notes: ובשנים: The only Strong's candidate listed (H8147 'two/twofold') does not fit the context. The consonants שנים clearly correspond to the plural of שנה (H8141 'year'), meaning 'years,' which is the standard reading for growth over time. The candidate list appears incomplete.
The syntax of 'favor God and men' could be parsed as 'favor before God and men' or 'favor of God and of men' — the preposition governing the relationship is implicit.

3.summary: Phase 1 consonantal translation — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided. Literal and amplified readings produced independently from consonantal Hebrew.

translation_notes: חמש (consonants חמש): Candidates: H2567 'to tax a fifth', H2568 'five', H2569 'a fifth tax', H2570 'abdomen', H2571 'able-bodied soldiers'. Chose H2568 'five' because context is a numerical date ('year of five ten' = fifteenth year).
מורשה (consonants מורשה): Only candidate H4181 'a possession'. In context of a Roman governor appointed over Judea, the sense is 'one who holds possession/authority' — functioning as 'governor'.
אח (consonants אח): Candidates: H251 'brother', H252 'brother', H253 'Oh!', H254 'fire-pot', H255 'howler'. Chose H251 because Philip is identified as the brother of Herod, a familial relationship.
ממלכות (consonants ממלכות): Candidates: H4468 'dominion/realm', H4438 'a rule/dominion'. Chose H4468 because the context describes a territorial domain (Ituraea and Trachonitis).
textual_notes: The word מורשה (H4181 'possession') is used here to render the concept of a Roman governor/procurator — an unusual Hebrew rendering suggesting 'one who holds authority/possession' over a province.
Several words are transliterations of Latin/Greek names (קיסר, טברי, פילאט, הורדוס, טטרקא, פליף, איטוראה, טרכנה, לישניאה, אבילינה) with no Strong's numbers.
The consonants ש נת could be parsed as שנת (construct of שנה 'year') or as separate particles ש + נת. The year-of construction fits the dating formula.

translation_notes: תחת (consonants תחת): Candidates: H8478 'underneath/under', H8479 same, H8480 'Tachath' (proper noun). Chose H8478 because context describes a hierarchical authority — 'under the chief priests.'

שרי (consonants שרי): Candidates: H8297 'Sarai', H8298 'Sharay', or שר (H8269) 'chief/prince' in construct plural. Chose שרי as construct plural of שר 'chiefs/princes' because it modifies הכהנים 'the priests' — yielding 'chiefs of the priests' (high priestly authority).
מאל (consonants מ+אל): Candidates for אל: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 'God' because the context describes a divine commission/word coming from God.

במדבר (consonants ב+מדבר): Candidates: H4057 'wilderness/pasture/desert', or ב+דבר H1697 'in [the] word/matter'. Chose H4057 'wilderness' because the physical location of Yochanan's activity is being specified.
textual_notes: The separation 'נ ע&שת המילה' is puzzling. It could be read as נעשת 'was done/made' (nifal of עשה) with 'the word' — i.e., 'the word was made/established.' The נ may be a nifal prefix separated in the manuscript.
הולך בקיפא could mean 'walking in Caiaphas' (i.e. Caiaphas was the one officiating/serving) or 'going to Caiaphas.' The participial form suggests an ongoing state — Caiaphas was the one presiding.
המילה could be read as 'the word' (from מלה) or 'the circumcision' (from מילה). In context of a divine commission, 'the word' is more coherent.

translation_notes: בכל (consonants ב+כל): H3605 'the whole/all' with prefix ב 'in'. Straightforward: 'in all.'
ממלכות (consonants ממלכות): Candidates: H4468 'dominion/realm', H4438 'rule/dominion'. Chose H4468 — the concrete sense 'country/realm' fits describing the geographic region of Judah.
תשובה (consonants תשובה): H8666 'a recurrence/return/reply'. Here used in the moral sense of 'returning' (repentance), which is the standard later Hebrew usage of this root.
textual_notes: דורש could be from דרש 'to seek/inquire/demand' — here functioning as a participle meaning 'proclaiming' or 'advocating.' No Strong's candidates were provided but the root דרש (H1875) fits.
טבילת and מחילת are construct forms of post-biblical Hebrew words (טבילה 'immersion' and מחילה 'forgiveness') not found in the Strong's Hebrew lexicon, suggesting a later Hebrew composition.
החוטאים 'the sinners' — this could modify עונות ('iniquities of the sinners') or stand independently. The construct chain suggests 'iniquities of the sinners.'

translation_notes: בספר (consonants ב+ספר): Candidates: H5608 'to inscribe', H5609 'a book', H5612 'writing/book', H5613 'scribe'. Chose H5612 'a book/scroll' because the preposition ב + noun 'book' yields 'in the book,' matching the context of a written prophetic text.
דרך (consonants דרך): Candidates: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'a road/way'. Chose H1870 'way/road' because it is the object of פנו 'clear' — 'clear the way.'

האל (consonants ה+אל): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to'. Chose H410 'God' with definite article ה — 'the God/the Mighty One.' This fits the prophetic quotation about preparing God's way.
עשר (consonants עשר): Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6236 'ten', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6240 'ten in combination (-teen)'. Chose H6240 because combined with חמשה it yields 'fifteen.'
תרשתא (consonants תרשתא): H8660 'Tirshatha — title of a Persian governor.' Used here as a Hebrew gloss for 'governor,' explaining the foreign term 'tetrarch.'
textual_notes: The latter portion of this section (from ט״ו onward) appears to be marginal glosses or scribal annotations, not continuous text. Multiple variant spellings of Tiberius (טיברי/טברי) and Caesar (שיזאר/שיסאר) suggest a scribe working through transliteration options.
קורא could be the proper name Kore (H6981) or a participle of קרא 'to call/cry out.' The prophetic context ('a voice calling in the wilderness') strongly favors the verbal participle.
The relationship between תרשתא and טטררך suggests the scribe glossed the foreign word 'tetrarch' with the known Hebrew term for a foreign governor (Tirshatha).
דברי could be the proper name Dibri (H1704) or the construct plural of דבר 'word.' Context ('book of the words of Isaiah') demands the latter.

translation_notes: כל (consonants כל): H3605 and H3606 are identical in meaning ('the whole/all'). H3605 is the standard Hebrew form; H3606 is Aramaic. Chose H3605 for Hebrew context.
textual_notes: מיו<רים contains an unclear character (<). It likely represents מיושרים 'made straight/directed' (from ישר via pual/hophal participle), with the < possibly being a damaged or uncertain letter in the manuscript.

רעים could be from רע 'bad/evil' (describing crooked paths) or from רעע 'to break/shatter' (describing rough terrain). Both produce coherent images in this leveling-landscape context; 'bad/crooked' fits the parallel with ישרים 'straight.'

translation_notes: בשר (consonants בשר): Candidates: H1319 'to announce glad news', H1320 'flesh/body/person', H1321 same. Also שר H8269 'chief' with prefix ב. Chose H1320 'flesh' because 'all flesh' is a standard Hebrew idiom for all humanity, and it is the subject of 'will see.'

שלום (consonants שלום): Candidates: H7965 'safe/welfare/health/prosperity/peace', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum' (name). Chose H7965 'peace/welfare/salvation' because the context is a prophetic promise of God's saving action visible to all humanity.
האל (consonants ה+אל): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God', H411 'these', H413 'to'. Chose H410 'God' with definite article — 'the God.' The salvation/peace belongs to God.
textual_notes: שלום here could mean 'peace,' 'welfare,' 'wholeness,' or 'salvation.' The Hebrew word carries a broader semantic range than any single English equivalent. The prophetic context (Isaiah quotation) typically carries the sense of God's saving deliverance, but the Hebrew consonants support the full range of שלום — peace, completeness, wholeness, prosperity.

translation_notes: אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same (Aramaic), H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 'to say' — the verb form fits 'then he said.'

בעבור (consonants ב+עבור): Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain.' Chose H5668 because the context describes the purpose for which the crowds came — so that he would immerse them.

למד (consonants למד): Candidates: H3925 'to teach/goad'. Also מד H4055 'a measure/garment.' Chose H3925 'taught' because the question 'who taught you to flee' makes coherent sense as a rhetorical challenge.

ברוח (consonants ב+רוח): Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room', H7306 'to smell/blow', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit'. This could mean 'to flee' (reading ברוח as infinitive of ברח 'to flee' with different vocalization) or 'in/by spirit/wind.' Given the question 'who taught you to flee from the coming wrath,' reading ברוח as לברוח 'to flee' produces the most coherent image.
textual_notes: ברוח is highly ambiguous: it could be (1) from ברח 'to flee' (infinitive with ב prefix), (2) ב + רוח 'in/by wind/spirit' (H7307), or (3) related to ריח 'smell/perceive.' The flee reading produces the most natural sentence: 'who taught you to flee from the coming wrath?'

מאפינו is difficult. It could be מ + אף + ינו 'from our nostrils/anger' (אף = nose/anger + 1cp suffix), yielding 'from our wrath.' Alternatively it could be a form related to 'baking' (אפה). The wrath/anger reading fits the context of fleeing from coming judgment.
תולדות could mean 'generations/descendants' or 'offspring' — both work for describing those born of vipers.
פתנים — likely plural of פתן 'viper/asp' (cf. H6620). No Strong's candidate was provided but the consonants match the known Hebrew word for venomous serpent.

translation_notes: עשו (consonants עשו): H6215 'Esau' (proper name). However, in context this is clearly an imperative plural of עשה 'to do/make' — 'do/produce [fruits].' The consonants match Esau's name coincidentally but the grammatical function is verbal imperative.
הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/she/it', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist.' Chose H1931 as the emphatic pronoun 'he [is]' — identifying Abraham as father.
אני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship.' Chose H589 'I' because the speaker is making a first-person declaration.
שהאל (consonants ש+ה+אל): ש is relative particle 'that' + ה definite article + אל. Candidates for אל: H408 'not', H410 'God'. Chose H410 'God' — 'that the God [is able].'

החזיר (consonants החזיר): Candidates: H2386 'hog/pig', H2387 'Chezir' (name). However, this is almost certainly the hifil infinitive/verb of חזר 'to return/restore' — 'to cause to return/restore.' The hog reading would produce: 'the pig alive son of Abraham' which is incoherent. The causative 'to restore/bring back' fits perfectly.
חי (consonants חי): Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 same (Aramaic). Chose H2416 — 'alive/living' modifying 'son.'

אלו (consonants אלו): Candidates: H431 'lo!/behold', H432 'if.' Context suggests 'these' (demonstrative pronoun, a common later Hebrew form). H431 'lo!' can function demonstratively. Chose H431 as 'these.'
לאמר (consonants ל+אמר): H559 'to say' with prefix ל (infinitive construct). Standard Hebrew construction meaning 'to say/saying.'
textual_notes: החזיר is the most significant ambiguity: the consonants match both חזיר 'pig/hog' (H2386) and the hifil of חזר 'to return/restore.' The verbal reading ('to restore alive') produces a coherent theological statement; the noun reading ('the pig alive') does not.
א בינו — the א could be an abbreviation for אב 'father' with בינו meaning 'our father,' or א could be a separate particle. The combined reading 'our father' fits the declaration about Abraham.
עשו matches both the imperative of עשה and the proper name Esau (H6215). Context demands the verb.

translation_notes: כי (consonants כי): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that.' Chose H3588 because this introduces a causal explanation — 'for the axe already...'

כבר (consonants כבר): Candidates: H3527 'to augment/multiply', H3528 'long ago/already/formerly', H3529 'Kebar river.' Also בר candidates. Chose H3528 'already' because it modifies the verb — the axe has already been laid to the root.

עברה (consonants עברה): Candidates: H5678 'an outburst of passion/wrath', H5679 'a crossing-place.' However this is most likely the 3fs perfect of עבר 'to cross/pass over' — 'has passed/been laid.' The axe has crossed over to the root. Neither noun candidate fits as well as the verbal reading.
טוב (consonants טוב): Candidates: H2895 'to be/do good', H2896 'good (adj)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness (noun).' Chose H2896 adjective 'good' modifying fruit.

באש (consonants ב+אש): Candidates for באש: H887 'to smell bad', H889 'stench.' Candidates for אש: H784 'fire', H787 'foundation.' Chose ב + אש H784 'in fire' — trees cast into fire is the coherent image. 'In a stench' would be bizarre here.
לכן (consonants ל+כן): H3651 'so/thus' with prefix ל yielding 'therefore.' Standard Hebrew conjunction.
textual_notes: עברה could be parsed as a noun (H5678 'wrath' or H5679 'crossing-place') or as a 3fs perfect verb from עבר 'to pass/cross.' The verbal reading ('has passed/been set') is most natural with 'the axe' as subject.

translation_notes: אם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether/although.' Chose H518 'if' because the phrase אם כן 'if so' is a standard Hebrew conditional expression introducing a question.
כן (consonants כן): Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/upright', H3652 'so', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat.' Chose H3651 'so/thus' — paired with אם to form 'if so.'
מה (consonants מה): Candidates: H4100 'what?/how?/why?', H4101 same (Aramaic). Chose H4100 — interrogative 'what?'

יעשו (consonants יעשו): H3299 'Jaasu' (proper name). However, this is clearly the 3mp imperfect of עשה 'to do/make' — 'shall they do?' or 'shall we do?' The proper name reading is contextually impossible.
textual_notes: יעשו could be 3mp 'shall they do' or understood as 1cp in sense ('what shall we do') given that the crowds are asking about themselves. The 3mp form is literal but the intent is self-referential.

translation_notes: ענה (ע-נ-ה): Candidates: H6030 'to respond', H6031 'to depress', H6034 'Anah (name)'. Chose H6030 because the context is a dialogue — he is responding to a question or situation.

שיש (ש-י-ש): Candidates: H7893 'marble', H3426 (יש) 'there is'. The ש is a relative prefix ('who/that'), and יש means 'there is', yielding 'who has' — this fits the context of possessing garments perfectly.

שני (ש-נ-י): Candidates: H8144 'crimson', H8145 'two/second'. Chose H8145 'two' because the sentence is about sharing garments — 'two garments' makes perfect sense while 'crimson garments' would be oddly specific.
אחד (א-ח-ד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one'. Chose H259 'one' — the person who lacks even one garment.
זה (ז-ה): Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 'this' as the demonstrative pronoun pointing to the same action of giving.
כן (כ-נ): Candidates: H3651 'so/likewise', H3653 'a stand', H3654 'a gnat'. Chose H3651 'likewise/so' as an adverb completing 'also likewise'.
textual_notes: The sequence תתמלאו יתמלאו תתמלאו ת תתמלאנה יתמלאו appears to be a scribal difficulty — possibly multiple attempts at copying a single verb form, or a textual corruption. The repeated forms alternate between 2mp and 3mp/3fp, which is unusual. The isolated ת may be an abbreviation or a fragment. This entire sequence is highly uncertain.
חלופי העושרים: 'portions/exchanges of the riches' — חלופי derives from ח-ל-ף (to exchange/change). It could mean 'surplus provisions' or 'exchangeable wealth'. The exact nuance is ambiguous.
The word אומר is listed only as H201 'Omar' (a proper name), but in context it clearly functions as a participle of אמר (H559) 'saying'. The lexicon entry provided is incomplete.

translation_notes: מה (מ-ה): Candidates: H4100, H4101 — both mean 'what?'. Chose H4100 as the standard interrogative.
יעשו: Listed only as H3299 'Jaasu' (a name), but contextually this is clearly a 3mp imperfect of עשה (H6213) 'to do'. The provided lexicon entry is a name sharing the same consonants.
textual_notes: העולמיים — 'the worldly ones': This is not a standard biblical Hebrew term. It appears to be a later Hebrew formation from עולם (world/age) with a gentilic/adjectival suffix. It likely refers to people involved in worldly affairs — possibly tax collectors or secular officials. The exact referent is uncertain.

translation_notes: ענה (ע-נ-ה): Chose H6030 'to respond' — he is answering their question.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', H1992 (הם) 'them'. With ל prefix, this is 'to them' — standard indirect object. Chose H1992.
לא (ל-א): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 (Aramaic 'not'). Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation.
עוד (ע-ו-ד): Candidates: H5749 'to testify', H5750 'more/again', H5751 (same as 5750). Chose H5750 'more' — 'do not do more' fits the instruction to restrain their actions.
לבד (ב-ד with ל prefix): H905 'separation/alone/only'. 'Only' works perfectly — 'do not do more, only what...'
כמה: Candidates: H3642 'to pine after', or כ + מה (H4100) 'as/how much'. Chose the compound reading כ + מה = 'as much as', which fits the instruction about limits of authority.
שנתן: ש (relative 'that') + נתן H5414 'was given'. Passive sense from context — 'that was given to you.'
textual_notes: רשות is a post-biblical Hebrew term meaning 'authority/permission', not found in the Strong's biblical lexicon. It confirms the later Hebrew provenance of this text.

translation_notes: אמר (א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — Yochanan is speaking.
אל: Candidates: H408 'do not (deprecative)', H410 'strength/God', H413 'to/near'. Chose H408 — this is a negative imperative 'do not desire'.

רע (ר-ע): Candidates: H7451 'evil', H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate/friend', H7454 'thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 'evil' — 'do not desire evil to any person' is a coherent moral instruction.
לשום: ל + שום. Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7762 'garlic'. H7760 in the sense of 'any' (as in לשום אדם = 'to any person') fits perfectly.
אדם (א-ד-מ): Candidates: H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H123 'Edom'. Chose H120 — 'any person'.
נזק (נ-ז-ק): Candidates: H5142 'to suffer/inflict loss', H5143 'loss/damage'. Chose H5143 as the noun 'harm/damage'.
textual_notes: וה]פרשים[ — The brackets in the source indicate editorial uncertainty. פרשים could be 'horsemen/cavalry' (from פרש H6571) or possibly a corruption of פרושים 'Pharisees'. Given that the context parallels a scene where soldiers ask what to do, 'horsemen/soldiers' is more fitting.

משכיר0 יותיהם — This phrase is difficult. משכיר appears related to שכר (wages), and the 0 may indicate a scribal mark or corruption. יותיהם is unclear — possibly a possessive suffix construction. The overall sense appears to be 'from their wages' but the exact morphology is uncertain.
תחפצו — from חפץ 'to delight in, desire'. Not listed in candidates but clearly the verb root from context.

translation_notes: העם (ע-מ): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with'. With the definite article ה, this is clearly 'the people' — H5971.
ישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua', H3443 (same). This is the proper name Yeshua/Jeshua.

משיח (מ-ש-י-ח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', or root שיח H7878 'to ponder/converse'. Chose H4899 — 'anointed one/Messiah' fits the context of people wondering if Yochanan is the expected anointed figure.
textual_notes: סבורים is a post-biblical Hebrew term (from Aramaic סבר) meaning 'thinking/supposing'. It is not in the biblical Strong's lexicon, confirming later Hebrew composition.

The syntax ישוע משיח could be read as a title 'Yeshua the Messiah' or as two separate concepts 'the salvation [that is] the anointed one'. Given the narrative context — people wondering about identity — 'Yeshua the Messiah' as a title/name is most natural.

translation_notes: ענה (ע-נ-ה): Chose H6030 'to respond' — Yochanan is answering the people's speculation.
ואמר: Chose H559 'to say' — standard speech introduction.
במים (מ-י-מ): Candidates: H4325 'water', or ב + ים H3220 'sea'. 'In water' (H4325) makes perfect sense for immersion; 'in the sea' would be oddly specific.
חזק (ח-ז-ק): Candidates: H2388 'to fasten/be strong', H2389 'strong/powerful', H2390 'powerful', H2391 'help', H2392 'power'. Chose H2389 as the adjective 'strong/mighty' — describing the coming one.
ממני: The מן prefix ('from/than') + ני ('me'). Listed candidates H4507 'Fate idol' and H5204 'lamentation' are irrelevant. This is simply 'than me' — a comparative construction.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 — emphatic pronoun 'he' as subject of 'will immerse'.
ברוח (ר-ו-ח): Candidates: H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7304 'to breathe freely'. Chose H7307 'spirit/breath' — paired with 'the holy' to form 'the spirit of holiness'.
הקדש (ק-ד-ש): Candidates: H6944 'a sacred thing/holiness', H6942 'to be clean', H6943 'Kedesh'. Chose H6944 — 'the holiness' forming 'spirit of the holy'.
ובאש: ו + ב + אש. Candidates for אש: H784 'fire', or באש H887 'to stink'. 'And in fire' (H784) is the coherent reading — paired with 'spirit' as the two elements of immersion.
textual_notes: ח!גורת נע!לו — 'strap of his sandal': The exclamation marks in the source indicate scribal difficulty. חגורת typically means 'belt/girdle', but here it seems to mean 'strap/thong' of a sandal. This may be a translation choice in this Hebrew text rendering an original concept of 'sandal strap'.
ראוי is a post-biblical Hebrew term meaning 'worthy/fitting', not in the Strong's biblical lexicon.

translation_notes: מזרה (מ-ז-ר-ה): Candidates: H4214 'winnowing shovel', H4215 'north wind', H4216 'constellation/zodiac', or root זרה H2219 'to winnow'. Chose H4214 — a winnowing shovel is the tool used to winnow a threshing floor, producing a perfectly coherent agricultural image.
דבר (ד-ב-ר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. In this marginal context it appears to be a noun 'word' — H1697.
באש: Candidates: H887 'to stink', or ב + אש H784 'in fire'. Chose H784 — 'burn the chaff in fire' is the coherent image.
שלא: ש (relative 'that') + לא H3808 'not' = 'that will not'.
textual_notes: This section contains what appears to be a main text (the winnowing/burning passage) interspersed with marginal glosses or scribal notes. The words שתי ב׳ אחת א׳ חלופים עושרים כך העולמים העולמים ר׳ נעשה אמר דבר אלא נ0תן ניתן פרושים פרשים appear to be catchwords or abbreviations referencing earlier passages — possibly a scribe's index of key terms from the preceding sections. The abbreviations ב׳, א׳, and ר׳ likely stand for fuller words.
The 8 in ויא8סוף and the 0 in נ0תן appear to be scribal marks or damage indicators, not part of the Hebrew text.

פרושים vs פרשים — these two words appear side by side and may represent variant readings: פרושים 'Pharisees' (those who separate themselves) and פרשים 'horsemen/cavalry'. This likely reflects a scribal notation of two possible readings for the same word in an earlier passage.

translation_notes: לעם (ע-מ): Candidates: H5971 'people', H5973 'with'. With ל prefix, 'to the people' (H5971) fits — he is proclaiming to the people.

ומגיד: The listed candidate H1517 (גיד 'tendon/thong') shares consonants but ומגיד is clearly a hiphil participle of נגד 'to declare/tell', meaning 'proclaiming/declaring'. The lexicon entry provided is misleading.
כאשר: כ + אשר. Candidates for אשר: H834 'who/which/when'. Chose H834 — 'when' as a temporal conjunction.
אחיו: Listed as H283 'Achio (a name)', but contextually this is clearly אח 'brother' + יו (3ms possessive suffix) = 'his brother'.

הרעות (ר-ע-ו-ת): Candidates: H7468 'female associate', H7469 'grasping after', H7470 'desire'. However, with the definite article, this is most naturally the feminine plural of רע/רעה (H7451) meaning 'evil deeds/evils'. The listed candidates share consonants but do not fit the context of wrongdoing.
ומכל: ו + מן + כל H3605 = 'and from/concerning all'.
textual_notes: This section appears to be an incomplete sentence — it sets up the situation (Herod being rebuked) without completing the main clause. The completion follows in section 10.
מאשת — 'concerning the wife of': the מ prefix here carries the sense 'on account of / concerning'.

translation_notes: קבץ (ק-ב-ץ): H6908 'to grasp/collect'. Here meaning 'he gathered/heaped up' — Herod added to his evils by seizing Yochanan.
