הרעות: Same as section 9 — feminine plural of רע/רעה meaning 'evil deeds'. The listed candidates H7468-7470 do not fit.
תפש (ת-פ-ש): H8610 'to seize/capture'. Perfectly fits — Herod seized Yochanan.
בבור (ב-ו-ר): Candidates: H952 'to bore/examine', H953 'a pit/cistern/prison'. Chose H953 — 'in the pit/prison' as the place of imprisonment.
textual_notes: ושמו could be parsed as 'and placed him' (וישם + אותו contracted) or 'and his name'. Context strongly favors 'and placed him' — continuing the narrative of Herod seizing and imprisoning Yochanan.

קבץ הרעות שעשה — 'He gathered the evils that he did': This phrase is syntactically ambiguous. It could mean (a) Herod added this to the collection of evils he had done, or (b) having accumulated all these evils, he then seized Yochanan. Reading (a) seems more natural — imprisoning Yochanan was yet another evil added to the pile.

translation_notes: היה (first): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/become/come to pass', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 because the verb 'came to pass' fits the narrative opening formula.
כאשר: The כ is a prefix and אשר H834 'when/that/which' fits as a temporal conjunction introducing the circumstance.
העם: Candidates: H5971 'people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5971 because the article ה + עם as 'the people' makes sense as the subject of 'were immersed'.
היה (second): H1961 again, functioning as auxiliary 'was' with the participle טובל.

ה<מים: The angle bracket suggests a damaged or uncertain letter. Given the context of heavens opening (a cosmic event following prayer), this most likely reads השמים 'the heavens/skies.' The שׁ may have been lost or marked as damaged.
textual_notes: ה<מים: The damaged consonant (marked with <) makes this word uncertain. It could be השמים (the heavens) or המים (the waters). Context of 'opened' strongly favors 'the heavens' since 'the heavens were opened' is a coherent cosmic image, while 'the waters were opened' is less natural in this immersion context.
נטבל: No Strong's entry provided. This appears to be a nifal form of טבל (to dip/immerse), a post-biblical Hebrew usage for ritual immersion.
The initial נ is ambiguous — it could be a truncated word or a scribal mark. I treat it as part of a conjunction or verbal prefix.

translation_notes: ורוח: Candidates: H7304 'breathe freely', H7305 'room', H7306 'smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 (Aramaic equivalent). Chose H7307 because 'spirit' descending upon someone is a coherent image, whereas 'wind/room/smell' don't fit with 'the holy' + 'descended upon him.'

הקדש: Candidates: H6942 'to make clean', H6943 'Kedesh (place)', H6944 'sacred place/thing/sanctity', H6945 'male devotee', H6946 'Kadesh (place)'. Chose H6944 because 'the holiness' paired with 'spirit' produces 'spirit of holiness' — a natural Hebrew construct.
ירד: Candidates: H3381 'to descend', H3382 'Jered (name)'. Chose H3381 because a verb of descent fits the subject (spirit) and the prepositional phrase (upon him).

בעצם: Candidates: H6105 'to be powerful', H6106 'bone/body/substance/selfsame', H6107 'Etsem (place)', H6108 'power/body'. Chose H6106 because 'in substance/body' pairs naturally with 'bodily' (גופני) to describe the physical manifestation.
יונה: Candidates: H3123 'a dove', H3124 'Jonah (name)'. Chose H3123 because כמו ('like') introduces a simile — 'like a dove' is a coherent image of descent, whereas 'like Jonah' is forced.

ובאה: H872 'entrance' — but the ו prefix and the form suggest this is actually the feminine qal perfect of בוא 'to come/enter' (ובאה = 'and she came'), fitting with בת קול as the feminine subject. H872 itself derives from the same root.
בת: Candidates: H1323 'daughter', H1324 'bath (measure)', H1325 (same). Chose H1323 because 'daughter of voice' (בת קול) is a known Hebrew expression for a heavenly echo/voice.

בני: Candidates: H1137 'Bani (name)', H1138 'Bunni (name)', H5204 'lamentation'. None fit perfectly. In context, this is בן + pronominal suffix י = 'my son.' The candidates listed are proper names, but the consonants בני with suffix clearly read 'my son' from בן H1121.
מ<מים: Same damaged-letter issue as section 1. Context of a voice coming 'from' somewhere — 'from the heavens' (מן השמים) is the coherent reading.
textual_notes: מ<מים: Same damage as section 1. Could be מהשמים (from the heavens) or מהמים (from the waters). A voice coming 'from the heavens' is far more coherent than 'from the waters.'

אתהו: No Strong's candidates provided. This appears to be אתה + הוא = 'you [are] he' — a compound pronoun construction. Could alternatively be parsed as את + הוא with a direct object marker, but 'you are he' fits the declarative context of a heavenly voice.
ואומרת: Feminine participle of אמר 'to say' — the feminine form agrees with בת קול (daughter of voice) as the speaker.
גופני: No Strong's candidates provided. This is post-biblical Hebrew for 'bodily/physical,' derived from גוף 'body.'

translation_notes: היה (first): H1961 'to be/become' — 'Yeshua was at the beginning of thirty years' describes his age.
שנה: Candidates: H8138 'to fold/duplicate', H8139 'sleep', H8140 'year (Aramaic)', H8141 'year', H8142 'sleep'. Chose H8141 because 'thirty year(s)' is a coherent age statement.
שהוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 (Aramaic 'he'), H1933 'to be', H1934 (Aramaic 'to exist'). Chose H1931 because ש + הוא = 'that he' functions as a relative conjunction + pronoun.
בן: H1121 'son' — in a genealogical context, 'son of Yosef' is the natural reading.
שם: Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name', H8035 'Shem', H8036 (Aramaic 'name'). Chose H8034 'name' because 'whose name was Eli' introduces the genealogical chain.
עלי: Candidates: H5940 'pestle', H5941 'Eli (high priest)', H5942 'high', H5943 'supreme/God'. Chose H5941 because this is a proper name in a genealogical list — Eli as a personal name.
textual_notes: סבורים: No Strong's candidates provided. This is a post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew participle meaning 'supposing/thinking.'
בהתחלת: No Strong's candidates provided. Post-biblical Hebrew, 'at the beginning of,' from the root חלל/תחלה.

שם היה עלי: This could be parsed as 'whose name was Eli' (introducing the father of Yosef in the genealogy) or 'there was Eli' (listing a genealogical ancestor). The former is more natural as a transition from the narrative into the genealogy.

translation_notes: שם: In the genealogical formula 'שם היה X', שם as H8034 'name' produces 'whose name was X' — a standard genealogical tracing formula. H8033 'there' would give 'there was X' which is also possible but less natural for a lineage list.
היה: H1961 'was' — auxiliary in genealogical formula.
textual_notes: The trailing apostrophe (') may be a scribal mark, section divider, or abbreviation marker. Its function is unclear.
יודא: No Strong's candidates provided. This is an alternate spelling of Judah (יהודה), possibly reflecting an Aramaic or late Hebrew orthography (cf. Yehuda → Yuda).
]יוחנן[: The brackets in the source text suggest this name is a scribal insertion, correction, or restoration. The consonants יוחנן correspond to Yochanan (cf. H3110).
]ר[יסא: The bracket around ר suggests damage or uncertainty about the first letter. The name could be ריסא (Risa/Rhesa).
זרובבל: No Strong's candidates provided but this is the well-known name Zerubbabel (cf. H2216).
שלתיאל: No Strong's candidates provided. This is Shealtiel (cf. H7597).
נרי: No Strong's candidates provided. This is Neri, a personal name in the genealogical line.

translation_notes: מלאכי: H4401 'Malaki/Malachi, a prophet.' In the genealogical context this is a proper name. The consonants also support H4397-related 'my messenger,' but a proper name fits the genealogical list.
אנו: H580 'we.' However, in a genealogical list this must be a proper name. The consonants אנו likely represent a personal name (perhaps a Hebraized form). H580 does not fit context.
textual_notes: אטדי: No Strong's candidates provided. The root אטד appears in H329 (a thorn/bramble), and the ־י suffix could be a gentilic or patronymic. This appears to be a proper name, possibly Addi.
קושן: No Strong's candidates provided. Could relate to H3572 (Cushan), but here it appears to be a personal name in the genealogy, possibly representing Cosam.
מודאן: No Strong's candidates provided. This appears to be a personal name, possibly Moadi or a Hebraized form.
אנו: Listed as H580 'we,' but context demands a proper name. This may represent a Hebraized form of a name.

translation_notes: לוי: Candidates: H3878 'Levi, a son of Jacob', H3879 'wreath'. Chose H3878 because a personal name fits the genealogical list.
שמעון: Candidates: H8095 'Shimon/Simeon', H4583 'abode', H4584 'Maon (place)', H5770 'to watch', H5771 'perversity'. Chose H8095 because a proper name fits the genealogical list.
יונה: Candidates: H3123 'a dove', H3124 'Jonah'. Chose H3124 because in a genealogical list, this is a personal name, not the common noun 'dove.'
textual_notes: אלי: No Strong's candidates provided for this entry, but cf. section 3 where עלי was listed. Here the consonants are אלי which could be a personal name meaning 'my God' or could correspond to Eli (H5941). In the genealogical context it is a proper name.
אלים: No Strong's candidates provided. The consonants could represent a personal name Elim, or could be a shortened form of אליקים (Eliakim). In the genealogical list, it functions as a proper name.
אקים: No Strong's candidates provided. This appears to be a proper name, possibly a shortened form of a theophoric name.

translation_notes: מליה: Candidates: H3914 'wreath' (from ליה), H3050 'Jah' (from יה). Neither fits perfectly. In the genealogical context this is a proper name, likely Melea/Melyah. The consonants מ + ליה could mean 'from Yah' or be a Hebraized personal name.

מכנה: Candidates: H4368 'Mekonah (place)', H4369 'a spot', H3655 'to eulogize', H3656 'Canneh', H3657 'a plant', H5089 'lamentation'. In a genealogical list, this is a proper name. H4368 is a place name, but the consonants here serve as a personal name, possibly representing Menna.
מתת: H4991 'a present/gift'. In the genealogy this functions as a proper name Mattat, meaning 'gift.'
נתן: Candidates: H5414 'to give', H5415 'give (Aramaic)', H5416 'Nathan (name)'. Chose H5416 because a proper name fits the genealogical context.
דוד: Candidates: H1730 'beloved/uncle', H1731 'pot/basket', H1732 'David'. Chose H1732 because David the king is the expected terminal ancestor in this genealogical line.
textual_notes: מליה: The consonants are genuinely ambiguous between a proper name and 'wreath of Yah.' Context as genealogy dictates a proper name reading.
מכנה: Could be a place name (Mekonah H4368) or a personal name. In a genealogy, it must be a personal name. The exact identity is uncertain — possibly Menna or Menan.

translation_notes: שם (consonants שם): Candidates: H8033 'there/then', H8034 'name/appellation', H8035 'Shem (proper noun)', H8036 'name (Aramaic)'. This is a genealogical list where each entry follows the pattern 'name was [person]'; H8034 'name' fits perfectly as the subject of the existential verb followed by a proper noun. H8035 'Shem' would make no sense repeated five times before different names.

היה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin'. In the pattern 'name was X,' the verb 'was' (H1961) is the natural copula linking the subject to the predicate noun. 'Ruin' produces no coherent image here.
textual_notes: בועז has no Strong's entry for the full consonantal form as a proper noun in the provided candidates; only עז root forms are given. The name Boaz is well attested as a person in Israelite genealogy and is read here as the proper noun despite the absence of a specific Strong's entry for the complete form.

translation_notes: שם: Same reasoning as section 1 — H8034 'name' fits the genealogical pattern.
היה: Same reasoning as section 1 — H1961 'was' serves as the copula.

פרץ (consonants פרץ): Candidates: H6555 'to break out (verb)', H6556 'a break (noun)', H6557 'Perez (proper noun)'. In a genealogical list of proper names following the pattern 'name was X,' only the proper noun H6557 makes sense.

יודה: No Strong's candidates were provided for this form. The consonants ידה with a vav (יודה) appear to be a variant spelling of Judah (cf. יהודה H3063). In a genealogical list tracing back from Perez, Judah is the expected ancestor.
textual_notes: יודה has no Strong's candidates provided. It appears to be a variant or defective spelling of יהודה (Judah, H3063). The genealogical context (Perez's father) strongly supports reading this as Judah.

translation_notes: שם and היה: Same genealogical pattern as previous sections — H8034 'name' and H1961 'was'.

פלג (consonants פלג): Candidates: H6385 'to split (verb)', H6386 'to split (Aramaic)', H6387 'a half', H6388 'a rill/channel', H6389 'Peleg (proper noun)'. In the genealogical list pattern 'name was X,' only the proper noun H6389 is coherent. The genealogical sequence Eber > Peleg > Reu > Serug matches known patriarchal lineage.

עבר (consonants עבר): Candidates: H5674 'to cross over (verb)', H5675 'region across (Aramaic)', H5676 'region across', H5677 'Eber (proper noun)'. In the genealogical pattern, H5677 the proper noun Eber is the only coherent reading, and he is the expected father of Peleg.

]שם[ (in brackets in the source text): The brackets indicate an editorial insertion or restoration. In a genealogical line going Arpachshad > [Shem] > Noah, the consonants שם here clearly refer to the proper noun Shem (H8035), son of Noah and father of Arpachshad.
שם preceding היה throughout: H8034 'name' as established by the genealogical pattern.

אנו (consonants אנו): The only candidate is H580 'we,' but in a genealogical list this appears to be a proper name — possibly a variant of Enosh or another ancestral name. The context demands a personal name, not a pronoun.
עלי (consonants עלי): Candidates: H5940 'pestle', H5941 'Eli (high priest)', H5942 'high/upper', H5943 'supreme/God'. In a genealogical name list, the proper noun Eli (H5941) is most coherent.
textual_notes: The second half of this section (from אנו onward) breaks from the established שם היה pattern and appears to be a list of names without the formulaic introduction. Several names (מתתא, אליא, אלייה, אליי׳, אלים, מליא, מליאה, מנאנא, יודא, יודה) have no Strong's candidates provided, suggesting they may be variant spellings, Aramaic forms, or names not in the standard Hebrew lexicon.
אנו could be the pronoun 'we' (H580) or a proper name (possibly Enosh in a variant form). The genealogical context strongly favors a proper name.

The repetition of יודא/יהודה and יודה/יהודה may represent variant spellings of Judah being catalogued, or different individuals named Judah in the genealogy, or scribal annotations showing alternate forms.

This section appears to be a transition zone in the manuscript where the structured genealogical formula gives way to a less structured name list, possibly indicating a different source or scribal hand.

translation_notes: ירד (consonants ירד): Candidates: H3381 'to descend (verb)', H3382 'Jared (proper noun)'. In the genealogical pattern 'name was X,' only the proper noun Jared (H3382) is coherent. The genealogical sequence Mahalalel > Jared > Enoch > Methuselah matches known antediluvian lineage.
textual_notes: The final entry ]שם היה קינן[ is marked with brackets in the source text, indicating the scribe or a later editor considered this a restoration or uncertain reading. Kenan (H7018) also appeared in section 5, which may indicate overlapping genealogical segments or a textual join.

translation_notes: אנוש (consonants אנוש): Candidates: H582 'a man/mankind', H583 'Enosh (son of Seth)'. In the genealogical sequence Adam > Seth > Enosh, the proper noun H583 is clearly indicated. Reading H582 'mankind' would break the genealogical pattern.
שת (consonants שת): Candidates: H8351 'tumult', H8352 'Seth (third son of Adam)', H8353 'six'. In the genealogical list between Adam and Enosh, only Seth (H8352) fits.

אדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to flush/turn rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam (first man)', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. In the genealogical line tracing back from Seth to the origin, Adam (H121) the first man is the clear reading. The sequence then moves to 'the name of God,' indicating Adam's origin from God.

האל (ה + אל): The ה is the definite article 'the.' Candidates for אל: H408 'not', H409 'not', H410 'strength/mighty/the Almighty/deity', H411 'these/those', H412 'these/those', H413 'near/to/among'. The genealogy has traced from Jesse back through the patriarchs to Adam; the final entry 'the name of the Mighty One' (H410 with the article) indicates Adam bore the name/identity of God — i.e., Adam [was of] God. H410 'the Almighty' produces the coherent climactic conclusion to the genealogy: humanity's origin in God.
textual_notes: The final phrase שם האל breaks from the pattern שם היה [name] by dropping the verb היה. This could mean: (1) '[the] name [of] the Mighty One' — indicating Adam was [of] God, a possessive construction; (2) '[the] name [was] the Mighty One' — with the verb implied; (3) a title: 'the Name of God' as a theological capstone to the genealogy. The absence of the verb היה distinguishes this final entry from all others, suggesting intentional structural emphasis marking the terminus of the lineage at God himself.

one_way_hebrew: Uses נסע (nasa', H5265) meaning 'to pull up tent-pins, depart on a journey' — this specific Hebrew term for departure carries the nomadic sense of breaking camp and beginning a journey, connecting to Israel's wilderness wanderings. Greek ὑπέστρεψεν means 'returned,' but Hebrew emphasizes departure/beginning.
greek_deviations: Hebrew emphasizes departure (נסע 'departed') from the Jordan, while Greek emphasizes return (ὑπέστρεψεν 'returned') from the Jordan.
translation_notes: 'The Anointed' for משיח preserves the Hebrew messianic terminology.
'Departed' for נסע captures the sense of setting out on a journey.

one_way_hebrew: CRITICAL: Uses יהוה (YHWH, H3068) — the divine name. Greek has τοῦ διαβόλου ('the devil'). This is a major theological difference: Hebrew attributes the testing to YHWH directly, while Greek attributes it to the devil. This reflects the Hebrew understanding that YHWH tests his servants (as with Abraham, Job), following OT precedent.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: 'tested by YHWH' (ונתנסה בעד יהוה). Greek: 'tested by the devil' (πειραζόμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου). Completely different theological framing of who conducts the test.
translation_notes: YHWH preserved as the Hebrew divine name rather than translating as 'the LORD'.
The Hebrew presents YHWH as the one conducting the test, consistent with OT theology where God tests his servants.
textual_notes: The phrase א רְבּעים appears to be a scribal error or variant spelling for ארבעים (forty).

one_way_hebrew: Uses השטן (ha-satan, H7854) with the definite article — 'the Satan' as a title/office, consistent with Job 1-2 and Zechariah 3:1-2. The Hebrew presents Satan as a specific adversary figure, not merely 'the devil.'

Uses אל חי (El Chai) — 'God the Living' (H410 + H2416). This is the classical Hebrew designation for the living God as opposed to dead idols, found throughout the OT (Deut 5:26, Josh 3:10, 1 Sam 17:26, Ps 42:2). Greek θεοῦ lacks this specific 'Living' emphasis.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: 'God the Living' (אל חי). Greek: simply 'God' (τοῦ Θεοῦ) without the 'Living' qualifier.
Hebrew: 'stones' (plural אבנַים). Greek: 'stone' (singular λίθῳ).
translation_notes: 'The Satan' preserves the Hebrew title with definite article.
'God the Living' captures the Hebrew emphasis on the living God versus dead idols.

one_way_hebrew: Uses יהוה (YHWH, H3068) — the divine name, not found in the Greek text. Greek has simply θεοῦ ('God'), but Hebrew specifically invokes the covenant name of Israel's God, connecting this to Deuteronomy 8:3 which also uses יהוה.

אדון (ʾ-D-W-N): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord', H114 'Addon (name)'. Chose H113 because Shimon is addressing someone with reverence.
הפרד (H-P-R-D): Candidates: H6504 'to separate/spread apart', H6505 'a mule'. Chose H6504 because 'separate yourself from me' is the coherent plea in this context.
נא (N-ʾ): Candidates: H4994 'please/I pray', H4995 'raw flesh', H4996 'Thebes'. Chose H4994 because it is an interjection added to an imperative.
כי: H3588 'for/because' — introducing the reason for his plea.
textual_notes: וכיפא has no Strong's candidates — it is an Aramaic proper name (Kepha/Cephas, meaning 'rock'), used as a surname for Shimon.
]ראה[, ]נפל[, ]ואמר[ are all bracketed in the source, indicating they are editorial restorations or uncertain readings. The narrative logic strongly supports 'saw', 'fell', and 'said'.

מעלי — מ (from) + על (upon) + י (me). The candidates listed are for עלי; H5941 'Eli' (name) and H5940 'pestle' don't fit. The reading is simply the prepositional phrase 'from upon me' = 'away from me'.
חוטא has no candidates listed; it is a qal active participle of חטא ('to sin'), meaning 'sinner / one who sins'.

translation_notes: כי: H3588 'for/because' — causal conjunction explaining why Shimon said what he said.

חרד (Ch-R-D): Candidates: H2729 'to shudder with terror/fear', H2730 'fearful/reverential'. Chose H2729 because the verbal/adjectival sense of 'trembling/shuddering' better captures the active state described.
הוא (first): H1931 'he' — subject pronoun. The trembling was upon him.
הוא (second): H1931 'he/it' — this second הוא may be emphatic or resumptive, reinforcing that the trembling 'it' was surrounding 'him'.
textual_notes: מסובב has no candidates; root סבב ('to surround/encompass'). The form is pual or polel participle: 'surrounding/encompassing'. The syntax 'trembling he surrounding he' is awkward — likely means 'trembling was surrounding him' with הוא used both for subject (trembling) and object reference.
The double הוא is syntactically unusual. One reading: 'For trembling — it was surrounding him.' Another: 'For trembling he was, surrounded, he and all those...' The first reading seems more natural.
בלקיחת — no candidates; ב + לקיחה + ת (construct): 'at/in the catching of'. From root לקח ('to take/catch').

translation_notes: בני (B-N-Y): Candidates: H1137 'Bani (name)', H1138 'Bunni (name)'. Neither fits; the consonants are clearly the construct plural of בן ('son'): 'sons of'. This is a standard construct form without its own Strong's number.
זבדי: H2067 'Zabdi' — proper name, father of Yaakov and Yochanan (Zebedee in other traditions).
אמר: H559 'to say' — introduces direct speech.
לשמעון: H8095 'Shimon' — the addressee.
אל (ʾ-L): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/toward'. Chose H408 because אל + imperfect (תפחד) forms a negative command: 'do not fear'.
כי: H3588 'for/because' — introduces the reason not to fear.
בעבור: H5668 'on account of / in order that' — Chose H5668 over H5669 'stored grain' because it introduces purpose/cause.
זה: H2088 'this' — demonstrative pronoun referring to the miraculous catch.
textual_notes: חבירו — no candidates; חבר means 'companion/associate/partner'. The singular suffix ו ('his') with what appears to be a reference to multiple people (Yaakov and Yochanan) suggests 'his companions' with the suffix distributive or the noun understood as collective.
עומדין — no candidates; participle plural of עמד with Aramaic-influenced ין- ending: 'standing'.

שוממין — no candidates; could be from שמם ('to be desolate/astonished/stunned'). The ין- ending again suggests Aramaic influence. In context, 'astonished/stunned' fits the reaction to the miraculous catch.
תפחד — no candidates; root פחד ('to fear/dread'). 2ms imperfect: 'you will fear' → with אל: 'do not fear'.
תהיה — no candidates; root היה, 2ms imperfect: 'you will be'.
לוקח — no candidates; active participle of לקח ('to take/catch'). 'One who catches/takes' — here 'a catcher of men'.

במשמעתך — no candidates; ב + משמעת + ך. The noun משמעת from root שמע ('to hear/obey') means 'obedience/discipline/charge/following'. The suffix is 2ms 'your'. The phrase could mean 'in your following/discipleship' or 'under your authority/charge'. This is an unusual addition suggesting that the people will follow under Shimon's leadership.

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. With prefixed ו+כ, this forms 'and when/as' — chose H834 because כאשר is a temporal conjunction meaning 'when'.
משיח: Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'shrubbery'. Following the proper name Yeshua, 'anointed one' is the coherent reading as a title.

והלאה: Candidates: H1973 'to the distance/onward', H3811 'to tire/be disgusted', H3812 'Leah'. In context of a transitional phrase between narrative sections, 'onward/further' (H1973) makes sense as a narrative marker.
textual_notes: אחרי is listed only as H317 'other' in candidates, but the consonants אחרי more naturally read as the preposition 'after/behind' (H310). The context of following a person strongly supports 'after' rather than 'other'.
האףניות appears to be a later Hebrew or loan word for 'boats/ships' not in the standard Strong's lexicon. The consonants suggest אניות (ships) with an inserted ף possibly as a scribal artifact.
והלאה ראו — unclear whether this means 'and further, behold' (transitioning to next section) or 'and from there on, they saw.' The section break suggests a transitional use.

translation_notes: וזה: Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this or that'. With ו prefix, 'and this' makes contextual sense as the opening of a narrative section. H2089 'sheep' would be nonsensical here.
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. 'Was' (H1961) is the obvious choice as a copula verb describing Yeshua's location.

בעיר: Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'a city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'donkey colt'. 'In a city' (H5892) fits — a person full of leprosy coming to someone in a city is coherent; 'in cattle' or 'in a donkey colt' is not.

אדם: Candidates: H119 'flush/rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. H120 'a human being/man' is the natural reading in a narrative about someone approaching Yeshua.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. H259 'one/a certain' — standard usage as an indefinite article.

מלא: Candidates: H4390 'to fill', H4391 'to fill', H4392 'full', H4393 'fullness', H4394 'consecration', H3808 'not'. H4392 'full' as an adjective describing the man's state with leprosy produces the clearest image.
ראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. H7200 'he saw' — a verb in context of 'when he saw Yeshua he fell'.
נפל: Candidates: H5307 'to fall', H5308 'to fall', H5309 'abortion'. H5307 'he fell' — falling at someone's feet is a coherent physical image of supplication.
ואומר: Listed only as H201 'Omar (proper name)'. However, the consonants אמר are clearly the verb 'to say' (H559) in participial form with ו prefix. The participial form 'saying' fits the narrative.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon (name)'. H113 'Lord/Master' — a form of address to Yeshua in a plea.
אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. H518 'if' — introduces a conditional clause in the plea.
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you'. H859 'you' — the subject pronoun in 'you are able'.

ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. H559 'and he said' — standard narrative verb in context of speech following an action.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. H589 'I' — the speaker is responding to the leper's plea, so the first-person pronoun is coherent.
לטהר: Candidates: H2891 'to be pure/cleanse', H2892 'brightness/purification'. H2891 as an infinitive 'to cleanse' — directly parallels the leper's request.
ומיד: The candidates list יד H3027 'hand'. With prefix ו+מ, this reads 'and from hand' i.e. 'immediately' — a common idiomatic use.

ברחה: Listed candidate is H7347 'millstone' (רחה). However, the consonants ברח more naturally parse as ברח (H1272 'to flee/run away') with feminine suffix ה for agreement with צרעת (feminine noun). 'The leprosy fled' is a vivid, coherent image; 'the leprosy millstoned' is not.
textual_notes: ברחה — the candidate listed is רחה H7347 'millstone', but the consonants far more naturally read as the verb ברח 'to flee' (H1272) with 3fs suffix. I read it as the latter based on contextual coherence.

translation_notes: אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. H61 'but/yet' — an adversative conjunction between the negative command and the positive instruction.
אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. H559 'he said' — narrative speech verb.
אדם: H120 'a human being' — 'to any person' is the natural reading after 'that not they tell it'.

לשום: Candidates: H7760 'to put/set', H7761 'to put', H7762 'garlic'. Here לשום functions as 'to any' — a later Hebrew usage meaning 'any' (from שום 'to set/place' used idiomatically). This fits the prohibition context.

שמשה: Candidates under משה: H4871 'to pull out', H4872 'Moses', H4873 'Moses', H4874 'a debt'; under שה: H7716 'a sheep/goat'. With prefix ש (relative 'that/which'), שמשה = 'that Moses' — H4872 is the coherent reading as 'as Moses commands'.

מצוה: Candidates: H4687 'a command/the Law', H6680 'to command/enjoin'. Could be noun 'command' or verb 'commands'. In context 'as Moses commands' (verb), H6680 as a participle makes the sentence flow naturally.
בעד: H1157 'on behalf of/for' — used with 'your purification' to indicate the purpose of the offering.
בעדות: H5715 'testimony' — with prefix ב, 'for a testimony'.
שלהם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they/them'. With prefix ש+ל, this is 'that of them' / 'theirs' — H1992 'them' with prefix ש+ל gives 'of them / for them'.
textual_notes: ותדור could be parsed as from נדר (to vow/make a vow) or דור (to dwell/go around). In context of priestly cleansing ritual, 'vow/offer' makes more sense than 'dwell'.
טהףרתך contains an unexpected ף; likely a scribal variant or error for טהרתך (your purification, H2893).
מצוה could be the noun 'commandment' (H4687) or the verb 'commands' (H6680 participle). Both produce coherent readings: 'as Moses commands' or 'as [is the] commandment of Moses'.

translation_notes: עוד: Candidates: H5749 'to repeat/testify', H5750 'again/still/more', H5751 'again/still'. H5750 'more/still' — adverbial use indicating the report continued to spread further.

באים: Listed candidate H366 'frightful' (אים). However, the consonants באים naturally parse as the participle of בוא (H935 'to come') — 'coming'. 'Many peoples coming to Yeshua' is coherent; 'many peoples frightful' is not.
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of / in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. H5668 — purpose clause introducing why the crowds came.
textual_notes: ישמעשהו appears to be a compound or corrupted form. It likely contains שמע (to hear, H8085) with a 3ms suffix הו and possibly a relative ש prefix or a yod prefix for imperfect. Reading: 'that they might hear him'.
מחףלייהם contains an unexpected ף; likely a scribal variant for מחלייהם 'from their sicknesses' (from חלי H2483). The dual/plural suffix יהם indicates 'their'.
ושיתרפאו — a hitpael form of רפא with ש prefix (relative/purpose) and ו conjunction: 'and that they would be healed'. The reflexive/passive stem fits the medical context.

translation_notes: משיח: Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'shrubbery'. Following the name Yeshua as a consistent title throughout this text, H4899 'Anointed One' is the clear reading.
נסע: H5265 'to pull up tent-pins / start a journey' — a departure verb, coherent with withdrawing from crowds to the wilderness.

במדבר: Candidates: H4057 'wilderness/pasture/desert', H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. With prefix ב, 'in the wilderness' (H4057) fits the image of withdrawal for prayer.
ליהוה: Candidates: H3068 'YHWH', H3069 'YHWH'. H3068 — the divine name as the object of prayer.
textual_notes: מ<ם contains a damaged or unclear character (<). Context suggests מהם or ממם 'from them', referring to the crowds mentioned in the previous section.

translation_notes: היה (first): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. H1961 'it was/came to pass' — standard narrative opening formula.
באחד: H259 'one/first' with prefix ב — 'in one of' the days.

ומלמד: Candidates: H4451 'an ox-goad', H3925 'to teach/goad'. H3925 — in the piel/mD participle form 'teaching' makes perfect sense; Yeshua sitting and teaching is a coherent image. An 'ox-goad' does not fit.
הדת: Candidates: H1881 'a royal edict/statute', H1882 'statute'. H1881 'the law' — 'wise men of the law' describes legal scholars.

באו: Listed candidate H176 'or/desire' (או). However, באו naturally parses as the 3mp perfect of בוא (H935 'to come') — 'they came'. 'Who came from all' is coherent; 'or from all' is not in this context.
גלילה: H1552 'a circuit/region' — the name Galilee derives from this word.
היה (second): H1961 'was' — 'the power of YHWH was in him'.
לרפא: Candidates: H7495 'to cure/heal', H7496 'ghost', H7497 'giant', H7498 'Rapha'. H7495 — infinitive 'to heal' is the only coherent reading with 'the power of YHWH was in him to ___'.
textual_notes: ש<ם contains a damaged character. Likely reads שם ('there' H8033) or שהם ('who they/that they'). Context suggests a relative clause: 'who came from all the great [regions of] Galilee...'

גדולי could modify the places ('great [regions of] Galilee') or the people ('the great ones/notables of Galilee'). Both produce coherent readings. I chose a dual reading acknowledging both possibilities.
The apostrophe (') between וירושלם and וכח may be a scribal section marker or paragraph divider.

translation_notes: והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. H2009 'and behold' — a narrative attention marker introducing a new scene element.
איש: Candidates: H376 'a man/individual', H377 'to act manly'. H376 'a man' — the object being carried.
אחד: H259 'one/a certain' — indefinite article usage.
לפנים: H6440 'face/front' — with ל prefix, 'to the interior/inside'. This indicates they wanted to bring the man into the space where Yeshua was.
לפני: H3942 'anterior/before' — 'before Yeshua', indicating spatial position.

שער: Candidates: H8175 'to storm/fear', H8176 'to act as gatekeeper/estimate', H8177 'hair', H8178 'tempest/terror', H8179 'gate/door', H8180 'a measure', H6144 'Ar', H6145 'foe', H6146 'foe', H6147 'Er'. H8179 'gate/door' — they could not find an entrance due to the crowd. This is the only reading that produces a coherent physical scene.
בעד (first): Candidates: H1157 'through/on account of', H5703-H5708 various. H1157 'because of / on account of' — they couldn't enter because of the crowd.
העם: Candidates: H5971 'a people/crowd', H5972 'people', H5973 'with', H5974 'with'. H5971 'the people/crowd' — with definite article ה, refers to the crowd blocking entry.
שהיה: H1961 'that was' — relative clause 'the crowd that was there great'.
שם (first): Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name'. H8033 'there' — locative adverb describing where the crowd was.

הלבנים: Listed candidate H1143 'double interval/space between armies'. However, the consonants לבנים more naturally read as לבנה (H3843 'brick/tile') in plural with definite article. Removing bricks/tiles from a roof to lower someone through is a coherent physical action.
ובעד: H1157 'through' — they lowered the bed through the roof opening.

המטה: Candidates: H4294 'branch/rod/tribe', H4295 'downward', H4296 'a bed/litter', H4297 'distortion', H4298 'expansion'. H4296 'the bed' — consistent with the bed/litter mentioned in the previous section.
שם (second): H8033 'there' — adverb of place.
עם: Candidates: H5971 'people', H5973 'with'. H5973 'with' — 'the bed there with the sick one'.

כשלם: Candidates: H7999 'to be complete/safe', H8000 'to complete/restore', H8001 'prosperity', H8002 'sacrifice of thanks', H8003 'complete/whole', H8004 'Shalem'. With prefix כ, H8003 'completely/wholly' — describing how they placed him fully/completely before Yeshua. Alternatively could mean 'in wholeness/peace'.
משיח: H4899 'Anointed/Messiah' — consistent title throughout the text.
textual_notes: בעד appears twice. First occurrence likely means 'because of/on account of' (the crowd); second occurrence means 'through' (the roof). Both uses are attested for H1157.
הלבנים — the provided candidate H1143 does not fit. The consonants more naturally read as the plural of לבנה (brick/tile, H3843). This is a known word for building material used in roofing.

כשלם — could be כ+שלם 'as/like complete' (wholly/completely, H8003), or כ+שלם 'like Shalem' (H8004, an early name for Jerusalem), or even 'as peace/safely'. The adverbial sense 'completely' best fits the context of lowering someone into position.
הגגות — plural of גג 'roof'. Could indicate the roof structure had multiple layers or sections, or this is simply a variant reference to the same roof.

translation_notes: וכאשר: H834 'when' with prefix ו+כ — temporal conjunction 'and when'.
ראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'experiencing', H7203 'seer', H7204 'Roeh'. H7200 'saw' — Yeshua perceiving their faith.
אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer'. H559 'he said' — introducing direct speech.
איש: H376 'man' — addressing the sick man directly.
אמונה: H530 'firmness/fidelity/faith' — used as a descriptor: 'man of faith'.
textual_notes: נמחלו — not in the provided candidates. The root מחל (to forgive/pardon) is post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew, which may indicate the late linguistic register of this manuscript. Alternatively it could relate to מחה (H4229 'to wipe/blot out'), which in niphal would give a similar meaning of sins being blotted out/erased. The semantic result is similar either way.
איש אמונה — could be a vocative ('O man of faith!') or a descriptive statement ('a faithful man'). The vocative reading fits the direct address pattern where Yeshua speaks to the paralyzed man.

translation_notes: הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/she/it', H1932 (Aramaic 'he'), H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because this is a pronoun in the question 'who is he this' — a standard Hebrew identificatory clause.

זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'who is he this' is a natural demonstrative question; 'who is he a sheep' makes no sense here.
מדבר (consonants מדבר): Could be H4057 'desert/speech' (noun) or from H1696 'to speak' (participle). Chose H1696 as a participle 'speaks' because the context requires a verb: 'who speaks curses.'
לבד (consonants לבד): Candidates: H905 'separation/alone', H906 'linen', H907 'a lie'. Chose H905 because 'alone the God' = 'God alone' fits the theological context of exclusive divine prerogative.

האל (consonants האל): Candidates: H408/409 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411/412 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 with the article: 'the God' — the statement is about who alone can forgive sins.
textual_notes: לחשוב: The only Strong's candidate given is H2815 (a proper name Chashshub), but the consonants חשב clearly function here as the infinitive 'to think/reason.' This is a common verb (H2803 חשב 'to think, plan, reckon') not listed among the candidates. I read it as the infinitive of חשב 'to think.'
יוכל: The only candidate given is H3116 (Jukal, a proper name), but the consonants clearly represent the imperfect of יכל (H3201) 'to be able.' The verb form is standard.

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because וכאשר = 'and when/as' — a temporal conjunction introducing the clause.

ענה (consonants ענה): Candidates: H6030 'to heed/respond', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 (Aramaic respond), H6033 (Aramaic afflict), H6034 'Anah'. Chose H6030 because 'he responded and said' is a standard narrative formula.

ואמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 (Aramaic 'to say'), H561 'something said', H562 (Aramaic), H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because this is a standard verb 'and he said.'
להם (consonants להם/הם): H3859 'to burn/rankle' vs. H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 with preposition ל = 'to them,' the natural indirect object after 'said.'

רע (consonants רע): Candidates: H7451 'evil', H7452 'a crash/noise', H7453 'an associate/friend', H7454 'a thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 because 'why have you thought evil in your hearts' produces a coherent moral rebuke; 'why have you thought a friend' or 'a noise' does not.
textual_notes: הכיר: The only candidate given is H3600 כיר 'a cooking range,' which makes no sense. The consonants נכר (H5234) 'to recognize/discern' in the Hiphil הכיר = 'he recognized/perceived' is the obvious reading, though not listed among candidates.

translation_notes: אי (consonants אי): Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 because אי זה together = 'which?' — a standard Hebrew interrogative compound asking 'which thing is easier.'
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because אי זה is a compound meaning 'which' — demonstrative function.
דבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 'thing/matter' because 'which thing is easy' is the natural reading.
הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. Either works; chose H1931 as copula 'it [is]' in a nominal sentence.
קום (consonants קום): H6965 and H6966 both mean 'to rise.' Chose H6965 (Hebrew) as the standard imperative 'rise!'
textual_notes: נקל: Not listed in candidates but clearly from קלל (H7043) or קל — meaning 'easy/light.' The Niphal נקל = 'it is easy/light.'
אי זה could be read as two separate words ('where? this?') or as the compound interrogative 'which?' — context strongly favors the compound reading.

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 because 'but/yet' is the adversative conjunction needed to introduce a counter-statement to the scribes' challenge.
בעבור (consonants עבור): Candidates: H5668 'on account of / in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because 'in order that you will know' is purposive — stored grain makes no sense.
כי (consonants כי): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'that/because/for'. Chose H3588 because 'that the son of God has power' is the content clause.
בן (consonants בן): Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 (Aramaic 'son'). Chose H1121 because 'son of God' is the meaningful phrase in context.
אמר (consonants אמר): Chose H559 'to say' — the narrative verb introducing direct speech.
אני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because 'I say to you' is coherent speech; 'a ship says to you' is not.
אומר: The only candidate is H201 'Omar (name)'. However, the consonants אמר clearly represent the participle of H559 'saying/I say.' Context demands the verbal reading.
textual_notes: לעזוב: Not explicitly listed but from עזב (H5800) 'to leave/forsake.' In this context it means 'to release/forgive' sins — an extended sense of 'leaving behind.'
The double לך could be parsed as 'to you' (preposition + pronoun) and then 'go' (imperative of הלך), or both as 'go.' Context favors the first as 'to you' and the second as the imperative 'go.'

translation_notes: כשלם (consonants כ + שלם): Candidates: H7999 'to be safe/complete', H8000 'to restore', H8001 'prosperity', H8002 'peace offering', H8003 'complete/whole', H8004 'Shalem'. Chose H8003 because כשלם = 'as complete/whole (ones)' — meaning 'in full view of all of them.' This produces a coherent image: he rose before them in their completeness/entirety.

והלך (consonants הלך): Candidates: H1980 'to walk', H1981 'to walk', H1982 'journey', H1983 'toll/journey'. Chose H1980 as the standard verb 'and he walked.'
מהלל (consonants מהלל/הלל): Candidates: H4110 'fame', H1984 'to shine/praise/boast', H1985 'Hillel'. Chose H1984 because the participle מהלל = 'praising/glorifying' — parallel to 'and blessing God.'
ומברך (consonants ברך): Candidates: H1288 'to bless/kneel', H1289 (Aramaic), H1290 'a knee', H1291 (Aramaic knee). Chose H1288 because 'blessing God' parallels 'praising God.'

textual_notes: שבה: The candidate H7617 'to take captive' doesn't fit. I read שבה as the relative particle ש + the preposition בה = 'that on which [he was lying].' This is common in later Hebrew.
ומיד: Literally 'and from hand' — an idiom meaning 'immediately.' Could also be parsed as 'and from [his] hand' but the idiomatic sense is far more natural in narrative.

translation_notes: אשר (consonants אשר): Chose H834 'who/which/that' — relative pronoun introducing 'who were there.'
שם (consonants שם): Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name', H8035 'Shem', H8036 (Aramaic name). Chose H8033 because 'all who were there' is a natural locative expression.
וכשלם (consonants כ + שלם): Same analysis as section 5. Chose H8003 'complete/whole' — meaning 'altogether/as a whole' they were filled with awe.
מלאים: The only candidate given is H366 אים 'frightful.' However, the word is clearly מלאים from מלא (H4392/H4390) 'full/filled.' The ים suffix is the plural/intensive adjective 'full.'
יראה (consonants יראה): H3374 'fear/reverence/awe.' This fits perfectly: 'they were full of awe.'
היום (consonants יום): Candidates: H3117 'a day', H3118 (Aramaic 'day'). Chose H3117 with the article: 'the day' = 'today.'

נפלאות גדולות ראינו: Word order could be 'great wonders we have seen' or 'wonders — great [things] — we have seen.' I read נפלאות גדולות as a single phrase 'great wonders.'

translation_notes: ואחר (consonants אחר): Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'after', H311 'after', H312 'other/next', H313 'Acher'. Chose H310 because 'and after these things' is a standard temporal transition.

אלה (consonants אלה): Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. None of these fit 'these.' The common demonstrative pronoun אלה 'these' (H428) is the obvious reading. Chose accordingly despite H428 not being listed.
מקום (consonants מקום): Candidates: H4725 'a place/standing', H6965/6966 'to rise'. Chose H4725 because 'from that place' is a natural locative phrase.

וראה (consonants ראה): Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 because 'and he saw a man' is a standard narrative verb.
אדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'he saw a person/man' is the natural reading.
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'a certain man' uses 'one' as an indefinite article.
לוי (consonants לוי): Candidates: H3878 'Levi', H3879 'a wreath'. Chose H3878 because this is clearly a personal name in context.
ואמר: Chose H559 'to say.'

שלו (consonants שלו): Candidates: H7958 'quail', H7959 'security', H7960 'a fault', H7961 'tranquil/his own'. Chose H7961 in the sense of 'his own' — 'in his business/occupation' with the possessive שלו = 'of his.'
אחרי: The candidate H317 'other' is listed, but the consonants אחרי clearly function as the preposition 'after me' (from H310 אחר + first person suffix). Context demands 'go after me.'
textual_notes: שלו could be the possessive 'his' (later Hebrew usage) or from H7961 'tranquil/at ease' — meaning he was sitting calmly/comfortably at his business. Both produce coherent images; I favor the possessive reading as simpler.

The phrase ואמר לו יושב בעסק שלו could be parsed as 'and said to him sitting in his business' (circumstantial clause) or 'and said to him: Sit in your business.' Context strongly favors the circumstantial reading, as the command that follows is 'go after me,' not 'sit.'

translation_notes: והאיש (consonants איש): Candidates: H376 'a man/individual', H377 'to act manly'. Chose H376 because 'and the man rose' is straightforward narrative.
כל (consonants כל): H3605 and H3606 are Hebrew and Aramaic respectively for 'all/every.' Chose H3605.
והלך (consonants הלך): Candidates: H1980 'to walk', H1981 'to walk', H1982 'journey', H1983 'toll'. Chose H1980 — the standard verb 'and he walked.'

משתה (consonants משתה): Candidates: H4960 'a banquet/feast', H4961 'a banquet', or from שתה H8354 'to drink'. Chose H4960 because 'he made a feast' is the natural construction — עשה משתה is a standard Hebrew idiom.
שם (consonants שם): Chose H8033 'there' — locative adverb.

ושאר (consonants שאר): Candidates: H7603 'yeast', H7604 'to swell/be redundant', H7605 'a remainder', H7606 (Aramaic remainder), H7607 'flesh/kindred'. Chose H7605 'remainder/rest' because 'many worldly ones and the rest/others' describes the mixed crowd at the feast.
textual_notes: עולמיים: This term (from עולם 'world/age') in this context appears to designate 'worldly people' or 'people of the world' — those outside the religious establishment. This is a later Hebrew coinage not in classical biblical Hebrew.
The subject of ואוכלים is ambiguous — it could be the worldly ones and others eating with Yeshua's group, or Yeshua and disciples eating with the worldly ones. Context suggests mutual dining.

translation_notes: משיח (consonants משיח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', or from שיח H7878 'to ponder/converse', H7879 'utterance', H7880 'shrub'. Chose H4899 because 'Yeshua the Anointed One' is a title following the proper name — 'Yeshua the shrub' or 'Yeshua the utterance' produce incoherent images.
למה (consonants ל + מה): Candidates: H4100 'what/why/how', H4101 (Aramaic). Chose H4100 — the interrogative 'why?' introducing the accusatory question.

עם (first occurrence, consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people/tribe', H5972 (Aramaic), H5973 'with', H5974 (Aramaic 'with'). Chose H5973 because 'eating and drinking with the worldly ones' requires the preposition 'with.'
ועם (consonants עם): Same analysis — H5973 'and with' as preposition before 'the sinners.'
textual_notes: אתם: The only candidate given is H864 'Etham (a place).' However, the consonants clearly represent the second person plural pronoun אתם 'you' — standard Hebrew. No Strong's number is typically assigned for basic pronouns in some systems.
העולמיים and החוטאים appear as two distinct groups — 'the worldly ones' and 'the sinners.' Whether these are truly distinct categories or overlapping descriptions is unclear from context alone.

translation_notes: ענה (consonants ע-נ-ה): Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 Aramaic 'to respond', H6034 proper name. Chose H6030 because the immediate context 'answered... and said' is a standard response formula.
ואמר (consonants א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 because this is clearly a speaking verb coordinated with 'answered.'
להם: Could be H3859 'to rankle' or ל + הם H1992 'to them'. Chose ל + H1992 because the context requires a dative recipient of speech.
שהוא (consonants ה-ו-א): Candidates: H1931 pronoun 'he', H1933 'to be/exist'. Chose H1931 as the relative clause 'who he [is] healthy' uses the pronoun as copula.
textual_notes: אינו, צריך, and רופא have no Strong's candidates listed. These appear to be post-biblical Hebrew forms: אינו = 'he is not' (אין + pronominal suffix), צריך = 'needing/requiring', רופא = active participle of רפא 'to heal' (cf. H7495). They function clearly in context.

translation_notes: אבל (consonants א-ב-ל): Candidates: H56 'bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 because the adversative 'but/rather' logically contrasts the healthy not needing a physician with the sick who do.
כי (consonants כ-י): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 conjunction. Chose H3588 because this introduces a causal clause explaining the preceding statement.
אני (consonants א-נ-י): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the speaker is identifying himself as the subject of 'came.'
רק (consonants ר-ק): Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because 'only/merely' creates the logical restriction: not the righteous, only sinners.
לתשובה (consonants ת-ש-ו-ב-ה): H8666 'recurrence/reply/return'. In context, 'returning' (i.e., repentance — turning back) fits the call to sinners.
textual_notes: באתי has no Strong's match listed. The consonants ב-א-ת-י correspond to the first-person perfect of בוא (H935 'to come/go in'). The candidate H863 'Ittai' is a proper name and does not fit.

החולים, צריכים, רופא, לקרוא, הצדיקים, לחוטאים have no Strong's candidates listed. These are standard Hebrew forms: חולים = sick ones (from חלה H2470), צריכים = needing, רופא = healer (from רפא H7495), לקרוא = to call (from קרא H7121), הצדיקים = the righteous (from צדיק H6662), לחוטאים = to sinners (from חטא H2398).

translation_notes: והם (consonants ה-ם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because the context requires a pronoun subject for 'said.'
למה (consonants מ-ה): H4100 'what/why'. The prefix ל makes this 'for what?' = 'why?'
וכן (consonants כ-ן): Candidates: H3651 'so/thus', H3652 'so' (Aramaic), H3653 'stand/pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'and so/likewise' connects the Pharisees' disciples to Yochanan's.
אבל (consonants א-ב-ל): Chose H61 'but/yet' because the adversative introduces the contrast with 'yours eat and drink.'
שלך (consonants ש-ל-ך): Candidates: H7993 'to throw', H7994 'pelican'. Neither fits. In post-biblical Hebrew, שלך = 'yours' (possessive pronoun). Context demands 'yours [i.e., your disciples].'

מלחמות: The listed candidate H2545 'mother-in-law' (חמות) does not fit. The word מלחמות could derive from לחם, but in this context — paired with כובד (weight/heaviness) and describing pious activity alongside fasting — this likely represents 'prayers' (a Hebraized form reflecting supplication/intercession). The standard biblical meaning 'battles/wars' would create a bizarre image when combined with 'making weight of wars' in a context about fasting and piety. 'Heavy prayers' is coherent.
כובד: No Strong's candidates listed directly. The consonants כ-ב-ד relate to כבד (H3515 'heavy/weighty'). The noun form means 'weight/heaviness.'
textual_notes: מלחמות is ambiguous. Biblical Hebrew מלחמות means 'wars/battles' (from לחם H3898). However, in this context of fasting and devotional practice, 'battles' makes little sense alongside 'making weight of.' This Hebrew manuscript text may use מלחמות to render a concept of 'prayers/supplications' — possibly a Hebraization of a term for prayer. Alternatively, כובד מלחמות could mean 'heavy struggles/wrestlings' as a metaphor for intense prayer. The reading 'earnest prayers' fits the context best but is uncertain.
תלמידי and מהפרושים have no Strong's candidates. תלמידי = 'disciples of' (post-biblical Hebrew), מהפרושים = 'from the Pharisees' (מן + הפרושים).
שלך as 'yours' is a post-biblical Hebrew possessive, not matching either Strong's candidate (H7993/H7994).

translation_notes: ולהם: ו + ל + הם. Chose H1992 'them' with preposition ל 'to'. H3859 'to rankle' does not fit the discourse context.
אמר (consonants א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'lamb'. Chose H559 because the subject is speaking in response.

שבני: ש + בני. The ש is the relative particle 'that.' בני candidates: H1137/H1138 proper names, or בני as construct plural of בן (H1121 'son'). Context requires 'sons of' the bridegroom.
בעוד (consonants ע-ו-ד): Candidates: H5749 'to testify', H5750 'continuance/still/while', H5751 same. Chose H5750 because ב + עוד = 'while still' describing the temporal condition.

הארוס has no Strong's entry. This is a post-biblical Hebrew term for 'bridegroom/betrothed one' (from ארס 'to betroth').
יצומו and יכולים have no Strong's entries listed. יצומו = 'they will fast' from צום (H6684), יכולים = 'able' from יכל (H3201).

translation_notes: אבל (consonants א-ב-ל): Chose H61 'but/yet' as it introduces the contrasting future scenario.

כאשר (consonants א-ש-ר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'step'. Chose H834 with כ prefix = 'as/when', introducing the temporal clause.
מהם (consonants ה-ם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 with מן prefix = 'from them', as the bridegroom is separated from the companions.

translation_notes: ואומר: The candidate H201 'Omar' (proper name) does not fit. This is the active participle of אמר (H559) with ו prefix = 'and [I am] saying/telling.'

אדם (consonants א-ד-ם): Candidates: H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H123 'Edom'. Chose H120 because the context describes any person generically.

מלבוש (consonants מ-ל-ב-ו-ש): H4403 'garment/clothing'. The alternative readings H3830 (לבוש 'garment') or H954 (בוש 'to be ashamed') — chose H4403 as the full form including the מ prefix fits 'garment.'
חדש (consonants ח-ד-ש): Candidates: H2318 'to be new/rebuild', H2319 'new', H2320 'new moon/month'. Chose H2319 'new' as adjective modifying garment.
ישן (consonants י-ש-ן): Candidates: H3462 'to sleep', H3463 'sleepy', H3465 'old'. Chose H3465 'old' because it describes the garment's age, contrasting with 'new.'
כי אם: H3588 + H518 = 'for if' — a conditional causal clause.

textual_notes: יחליף has no Strong's candidates listed. From חלף (H2498 'to pass on, change, exchange'). The hiphil form means 'to exchange/replace.'
נשבר has no candidates listed. From שבר (H7665 'to break/burst'). The niphal 'is broken/torn.'
מתיחד has no candidates listed. This appears to be a hitpael form from יחד (H3161 'to be united'). 'Does not unite itself / does not match.'

The parable's logic: putting a new garment patch on an old one ruins the old and the new doesn't match. The verb יחליף could mean 'patch' rather than simply 'exchange' — both are possible from the consonants.

translation_notes: ושום (consonants ש-ו-ם): H7760 'to put/set'. Here as indefinite 'any' (ושום אדם אין = 'and no person').
אדם: Chose H120 'human being' — generic person in a parable.

לשום: ל + שום. H7760 'to put' with ל infinitive marker = 'to put.'
חדש: H2319 'new' — adjective for wine.
בנאד: ב + נאד H4997 'in a skin bag.'
ישן: H3465 'old' — describing the wineskin.

משבר (consonants מ-ש-ב-ר): Candidates: H4866 'orifice of womb', H4867 'breaker of the sea', or from שבר H7665 'to burst/break'. Chose H7665 in participial/causative form because the new wine 'breaks/bursts' the old skins — a coherent physical image of fermentation pressure.
כי אם: H3588 + H518 = 'for if.'
textual_notes: משבר: Could be read as the noun H4867 'breaker' or as a verbal form from שבר H7665 'to break.' The participial reading 'breaking/bursting' fits the active image of wine breaking skins.
אובדין has no Strong's entry. This is a post-biblical/Aramaic-influenced plural participle from אבד (H6 'to perish/be destroyed').
נשפך has no candidates listed. From שפך (H8210 'to pour out'). Niphal = 'is poured out/spilled.'
הנאדות, והנאדות: Plural of נאד (H4997) with feminine plural ending = 'the wineskins.'

translation_notes: אבל: Chose H61 'but/rather' as it contrasts the right method with the wrong one described previously.
חדש: H2319 'new' — adjective for both wine and skin.
לשים: ל + שים. The candidates for ים include H3220 'sea' etc., but this is clearly the infinitive of שים/שום (H7760 'to put') with ל prefix. The ים is part of the verb root, not the suffix.
בנאד: ב + H4997 'in a skin bag.'

מתקיימין has no Strong's entry. This is a hitpael participle with Aramaic-influenced plural ending from קום (H6965 'to stand/arise'). The meaning is 'are sustained/preserved/endure.'

אדם: H120 'human being' — generic person.
ישן (consonants י-ש-ן): H3465 'old' — describing the wine.
מיד (consonants מ-י-ד): From מן + יד H3027 'hand'. The idiomatic meaning 'from the hand' = 'immediately/at once.'
חדש: H2319 'new' — adjective for wine.
כי: H3588 conjunction 'for/because.'
אומר: The candidate H201 'Omar' (proper name) does not fit. This is the participle of אמר H559 'saying/says.'
הישן: H3465 'the old' — with article, referring to old wine.
הוא (consonants ה-ו-א): Candidates: H1931 pronoun 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as the copular pronoun: 'the old — it [is] good.'
טוב (consonants ט-ו-ב): Candidates: H2895 'to be good', H2896 'good (adj/noun)', H2897 place name, H2898 'goodness'. Chose H2896 as the predicate adjective 'good.'
textual_notes: ש)ותה appears to have a scribal mark or parenthetical in the consonantal text. The consonants ש-ו-ת-ה likely represent ש (relative particle) + שותה (active participle of שתה H8354 'to drink'). The parenthesis may indicate a textual corruption or editorial note in the manuscript.
רוצה has no Strong's entry listed. From רצה (H7521 'to be pleased with/accept') — the participle means 'wanting/desiring.'
שתות has no Strong's entry listed. This is the infinitive construct of שתה (H8354 'to drink').

translation_notes: זה (consonants ז-ה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because the demonstrative 'this' fits the narrative introduction pointing to the event described.
כאשר (כ + אשר): The כ prefix + H834 'which/when' yields 'when/as', which fits the temporal clause introducing the scene.
ישוע: H3442 and H3443 are the same name Yeshua; chose H3442 as the primary entry for this proper name.
textual_notes: The word עשוי lacks Strong's candidates in the provided list. It appears to be a passive participle from עשה (to do/make), here functioning as 'it was done / it happened.' This is post-biblical Mishnaic Hebrew narrative style.
ב)בת appears to be בשבת (on Shabbat) with a scribal marker or damage obscuring the shin. The context of Sabbath controversy confirms this reading.
Several words (תלמידיו, לוקטין, ומוללין, ואוכלין, הגרעינים) are post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew forms not covered by Strong's biblical lexicon.

translation_notes: ומקצת: H7117/H7118 both mean 'a portion/end'. With the prefix ו (and) + מ (from), this yields 'and some of', which fits the partitive sense here.
להם: The preposition ל + הם H1992 'them' = 'to them'. H3859 'to rankle' makes no contextual sense in a dialogue introduction.
למה: ל + מה H4100 'what' = 'for what' i.e. 'why', standard interrogative usage.

עשות: The provided candidates H6219 'shining/polished' and H6220 'Ashvath' do not fit. This is clearly the infinitive construct of עשה (to do/make), a standard biblical form not needing a separate Strong's entry from the root.
textual_notes: אתם is listed only as H864 'Etham, a place', but in context this is clearly the second person plural pronoun 'you' (אַתֶּם), a common word that may not have matched the consonantal lookup properly.
