translation_notes: ענה: Candidates include H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6034 'Anah (name)'. Chose H6030 because the pattern 'answered and said' is a standard dialogue formula.
ואמר: H559 'to say' fits the narrative formula perfectly. H563 'a lamb' and H564 'Immer (name)' produce incoherent images here.
דוד: H1732 'David' fits as the historical figure being referenced. H1730 'uncle/lover' and H1731 'pot/basket' do not fit the narrative about reading Scripture.
כשהיה: כש + היה H1961 'when it was/existed' — temporal clause 'when there was'. H1962 'ruin' does not fit.
רעב: H7456 'to hunger', H7457 'hungry', H7458 'hunger (noun)'. With לו ('to him'), the noun H7458 'hunger' fits: 'when hunger was to him' = 'when he was hungry'.
הוא: H1931 'he' as emphatic pronoun fits the appositive construction 'he and those with him'.
החדש: H2319 'new' fits as an adjective describing a patch or garment. H2320 'new moon/month' is possible but less coherent with the tearing/breaking imagery.
משבר: H7665 'to burst/break' as a participle 'breaking' fits the image of new fabric tearing away from old. H4866 'womb opening' and H4867 'sea-breaker' do not fit.
הישן: H3465 'old' fits perfectly as 'the old [garment]'. H3462 'to sleep' and H3463 'sleepy' produce incoherent images.
textual_notes: The final clause 'משללכם יחבר החדש משבר הישן' appears to be a separate saying about patching garments — joining new to old causes tearing. The word משללכם is puzzling: it could be מ + שלל + כם 'from your spoils/garments' (שלל can mean 'plunder' or 'stripped garments'). This clause seems to be a parable about not mixing new and old, which may be contextually displaced or part of a composite teaching.
The transition from the David narrative to the garment saying is abrupt, suggesting either a textual compression or a different verse division than expected.

translation_notes: לבית: H1004 'house' with preposition ל 'to' = 'to the house of'. H1006 'Bajith (place)' does not fit the narrative about entering God's dwelling.
האל: H410 'God/mighty one' with the article ה = 'the God'. H408/H413 (negation/preposition) make no sense after 'house of'. This is 'the house of God'.
ולקח: H3947 'to take' fits perfectly — David took the bread. H3948 'instruction' does not fit as a verb here.
לחם: H3899 'bread/food' fits as the object of 'took'. H3898 'to battle' and H3901 'battle' produce incoherent images with 'the face/presence'.
שהוא: H1931 'he' as the relative clause subject 'that he [was]' fits. The שׁ prefix is the Mishnaic relative pronoun.
ואין: H369 'non-entity / not' = 'there is not / it is not', fitting the prohibition statement. H370/H371 do not fit.
לשום: H7760 'to put/set' is possible but here לשום functions as 'for any' (ל + שום in post-biblical Hebrew = 'for any'). H7762 'garlic' is absurd in context.
אדם: H120 'human being/person' fits perfectly. H121 'Adam (name)', H123 'Edom' do not fit the generic usage here.
רק: H7535 'only/merely' fits the restrictive clause. H7534 'emaciated' and H7536 'spittle' are contextually impossible.
textual_notes: הכה!נים appears to have a scribal mark (!) within the word, likely הכהנים 'the priests' with some notation or damage at the he/nun junction.

translation_notes: אדון: H113 'sovereign/controller/lord' fits perfectly — declaring authority. H114 'Addon (name)' does not fit a declarative statement about lordship.
הוא: H1931 'he' as emphatic pronoun in a nominal clause 'he is'. H1933/H1934 'to exist' would be redundant with the copular function.
בן: H1121 'a son' in construct with האדם = 'son of the man/human'. H1122 'Ben (name)' does not fit this title.
האדם: H120 'human being' with article = 'the man/the human'. This is the title 'Son of Man'. H121 'Adam' or H123 'Edom' are less fitting for the title.
ועוד: H5750 'again/also/furthermore' fits as an additive — 'and also [lord] of the Shabbat'. H5749 'to testify' does not fit syntactically.
מה: H4100 'what/how' — here functioning as an exclamatory 'how [great] a lord he is'.
textual_notes: מה&בת appears to be מהשבת 'of the Shabbat' with the & symbol marking a scribal issue at the shin. Combined with ועוד, the meaning is 'and also of the Shabbat' — i.e., the Son of Man is lord also of the Sabbath.
ואומר: The Strong's candidate H201 'Omar (grandson of Esau)' is clearly wrong for this context. This is a participial form of אמר (to say) = 'and saying / and I say'.
The syntax 'מה אדון הוא' could be parsed either as exclamatory ('what a lord he is!') or interrogative ('what lord is he?'). The exclamatory reading fits a proclamation of authority better.

translation_notes: היה: H1961 'to exist/become/come to pass' fits the narrative frame. H1962 'ruin' does not fit.
עוד: H5750 'again/yet/another' — indicating another Sabbath occasion. H5749 'to testify' does not fit.
בבית: ב + H1004 'house' = 'in the house of'. The construct with הכנסת gives 'house of assembly' = synagogue.
ומלמד: H3925 'to teach/goad to learn' as a participle 'and teaching' fits the scene. H4451 'a goad for oxen' is the noun form — less fitting since the context requires a verbal participle.
והיה: H1961 'and it was / and there was' continues the narrative.
שם: H8033 'there' fits the locative sense. H8034 'name' does not fit 'and there was ___ a person'.
אדם: H120 'human being/person' fits. Used generically for 'a certain man'.
אחד: H259 'one/a certain' fits as an indefinite article equivalent. H258 'to unify/collect thoughts' does not fit as an adjective here.
שהיה: ש (relative) + H1961 'was' = 'who was / that had'.
יד: H3027 'hand' fits the body part being described. H3028 is the Aramaic equivalent.
יבשה: H3004 'dry ground' — the same consonants serve as the feminine adjective 'dry/withered' describing the hand.
textual_notes: ונע!שה has a scribal mark (!) that likely indicates ונעשה 'and it was done / and it happened', a niphal form of עשה.
מ&בת again has the & marker, likely representing משבת / שבת 'Shabbat'.
יבשה (H3004) is listed as 'dry ground' but the same consonants form the feminine adjective 'dry/withered' modifying יד (hand). The adjectival reading is required by context.

translation_notes: אם: H518 'whether/if' fits the indirect question of whether he would heal. H517 'mother' is contextually impossible.
מקום: H4725 'a standing/place/spot' here used figuratively as 'grounds/basis/occasion' for accusation. H6965 'to rise' is the verbal root and does not fit the noun needed here.
textual_notes: שילשינוהו is a post-biblical Hebrew form meaning 'that they would inform against him / accuse him / denounce him' (from the root לשן, related to לשון 'tongue', i.e., to use the tongue against someone). Not in Strong's biblical lexicon.
בע!בור has a scribal mark, likely בעבור 'for the sake of / in order that'.
ב&בת again = בשבת 'on the Shabbat'.

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say' is the clear choice for the dialogue verb. H563 'lamb' and H564 'Immer' are contextually impossible.
לאיש: H376 'a man/individual' with preposition ל = 'to the man'. H377 'to act manly' does not fit a prepositional target.
שידו: Listed candidate H3035 'Jiddo (name)' does not apply. This is ש (relative) + יד (hand) + ו (his) = 'whose hand / that his hand'. The consonants ידו here are יד + pronominal suffix.
קום: H6965 'to rise' as imperative 'rise!' fits the command. H6966 is the Aramaic equivalent.
ועמד: H5975 'to stand' fits perfectly as the narrative completion of the command. H5976 'to shake', H5977 'a fixed spot', H5978 'along with' do not fit.
על: H5921 'upon/on' fits 'stood on his feet'. H5923 'a yoke' is contextually impossible.
textual_notes: וע!מוד has a scribal mark, likely ועמוד 'and stand' — imperative of עמד.
יבשה again functions as the feminine adjective 'withered/dry' rather than H3004's nominal gloss 'dry ground'.

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say' — dialogue introduction, as before.
להם: ל + הם H1992 'them' = 'to them'.
אם: H518 'whether/if' introduces the question. H517 'mother' does not fit.
טוב: H2896 'good (adjective)' fits as the object-concept of doing. H2895 'to do good (verb)' is possible but the infinitive ע!שות already provides the verbal element, so the adjective/noun is needed.
רע: H7451 'bad/evil' fits as the contrasting pair with 'good'. H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate/friend', H7454 'thought' do not fit the moral contrast.
הנפש: H5315 'a breathing creature / soul / life' fits the question about saving life. H5314 'to breathe/be refreshed' is the verb form and does not fit with the article ה.
textual_notes: א!ני has a scribal mark, likely אני 'I'.
ע!שות has scribal marks, likely עשות 'to do' — infinitive construct of עשה.
ב&בת again = בשבת 'on the Shabbat'.

שואל: The provided consonantal candidates only list אל forms (H408–H413), but this is clearly שׁ-ו-א-ל from the root שאל 'to ask/inquire' (H7592), in participial form 'asking'. The shin was apparently not parsed in the candidate list.

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say' for the dialogue verb, as consistently throughout.
לאיש: H376 'a man' with ל = 'to the man'. Same as section 8.

שלח (first): H7971 'to send away/out' = 'stretch out / extend'. This is the imperative command. H7973 'spear/branch', H7974 'Shelach (name)', H7975 'Shiloach (fountain)' do not fit a command to extend one's hand. H3892 'fresh/unused' (from לח) does not fit either.
שלח (second): Same as above, H7971 in completed action — 'he stretched out'.
והאיש: H376 'the man' with conjunctive ו and article ה.
ידו: H3035 'Jiddo (name)' is the only listed candidate, but this is clearly יד 'hand' (H3027) + ו (his) = 'his hand'. The pronominal suffix created a consonantal match with the name.

ומיד: ו + מ + יד. H3027 'hand' forms the basis, but ומיד in post-biblical Hebrew is an adverb meaning 'immediately / at once' (literally 'from the hand' = 'on the spot'). Both the literal and idiomatic meanings work.
textual_notes: וכא!שר has a scribal mark, likely וכאשר 'and when/as'.

ומיד is ambiguous between the literal 'and from [his] hand' and the post-biblical adverbial usage 'immediately'. The adverbial reading is more natural: the healing happened instantly upon stretching out the hand.
נתרפאה is a hitpael/nitpael form of רפא 'to heal' — 'it was healed / it healed itself', with feminine agreement matching יד 'hand' (feminine in Hebrew).

translation_notes: מלאים (מלא + ים): The root מלא means 'full/filled'; the ים suffix here functions as a plural adjective — 'filled.' The candidate H366 אים 'frightful' shares only the suffix. The context of rage/fury fits 'filled with fury' perfectly.
מה: Candidates H4100 and H4101 are essentially the same interrogative 'what?' — fits the context of deliberation: 'what shall we do?'
מישוע (מ + ישוע): The prefix מ means 'from/about'; ישוע is the proper name Yeshua (H3442/H3443). Context of discussing what to do 'about Yeshua' is coherent.
textual_notes: The text appears to have a scribal repetition or dittography: 'כשנכנס כ שנכנס' — 'when he entered as when he entered.' This may be a copying error, or it may be an emphatic construction. The nw in נע!שה appears to have a scribal mark (!) which may indicate damage or uncertainty in the manuscript.

translation_notes: ההם: H1992 'they/those' — as a demonstrative adjective modifying 'the days,' yielding 'those days.' H1990 'Ham' (a place) and H1991 'abundance' do not fit.

עלה: H5927 'to ascend' produces a coherent image of going up a mountain. H5928/H5930 'holocaust/offering' would be a noun and doesn't fit the narrative verb slot. H5929 'leaf/foliage' is nonsensical here.
בהר: H2022 'a mountain' — with prefix ב 'on/in.' H2023 'Hor' is a specific peak; context says 'one mountain' generically, so H2022 is better.
אחד: H259 'one/a certain' — fits 'a certain mountain.' H258 'to unify/collect thoughts' is a verb and doesn't fit the adjective slot.

האל: H410 'God/the Mighty One' — with the definite article ה, 'the God.' In context of 'prayer of God,' this is the most coherent. H408/409 'not' makes no sense. H411 'these/those' would be odd after 'prayer of.'
היה: H1961 'to be/was' — standard narrative verb. H1962 'ruin' is a noun and doesn't fit.

ער: H6145 'a foe (as watchful)' — but the root ער fundamentally means 'watchful/awake.' In context of all-night prayer, 'he was awake/vigilant' is the natural reading. H6144 'Ar' (a place) and H6147 'Er' (a name) produce nonsense in this sentence.
textual_notes: ער could be read as 'awake/watchful' (from the root meaning wakefulness underlying H6145) or as the proper noun Er (H6147). The narrative context of prayer through the night strongly favors 'awake/watchful.' The word ונעשה at the beginning could also be parsed as 'and we shall do' (1cp imperfect of עשה), but contextually 'and it came to pass' fits the narrative frame better.

translation_notes: וכאשר: ו + כ + אשר — H834 'who/which/when' with כ 'as/when' and ו 'and' — yields 'and when.' H833 'to be happy,' H835 'happiness,' H836 'Asher,' H838 'a step' — none fit the temporal conjunction needed here.
היה: H1961 'was/came to be' — with בקר following, 'it was morning.' H1962 'ruin' is nonsensical.
בקר: H1242 'morning/dawn' — 'it was morning' is the most natural continuation. H1241 'cattle' would produce 'it was cattle,' which is bizarre. H1239 'to inspect' doesn't fit after היה.
קרא: H7121 'to call/summon' — the standard meaning for summoning disciples. H7122 'to encounter' is possible but less specific. H7124 'partridge' is a noun and doesn't fit.
ובחר: H977 'to select/choose' — perfect fit for choosing disciples. H2715 'noble/pure' is an adjective and doesn't parse as a verb here.
עשר: H6235 'ten' — combined with שנים 'two' yields 'twelve.' H6238 'to grow rich' and H6239 'wealth' produce nonsense.
שקרא: ש + קרא — H7121 'whom he called' — relative pronoun + verb, naming them as sent-ones.
textual_notes: שלוחים is not in the provided Strong's candidates — it is derived from the root שלח (to send), meaning 'sent-ones/emissaries.' This is the Hebrew equivalent of the concept of apostles.

translation_notes: שמעון: H8095 'Shimon' — the proper name, one of Jacob's sons. The other candidates (H4583 'abode,' H5771 'perversity') are component roots but the full form שמעון is clearly the personal name in this list of disciples.
שקרא: H7121 'whom he called' — relative ש + קרא 'called.' Same usage as in the previous section. He gave Shimon the name Kepha.

אחיו: H283 'Achio' is listed as a proper name, but in context this is אח + יו 'his brother' — Andrei is identified as Shimon's brother. The possessive suffix makes this a common noun, not the proper name Achio.
textual_notes: אחיו could technically be the proper name Achio (H283), but in context — immediately following Andrei and preceding a list of other names — it clearly means 'his brother,' identifying Andrei as Shimon's brother. כיפא, ואנדרי, פיליף, and ברתלמי are transliterated foreign/Aramaic names without Strong's numbers.

translation_notes: ושמעון: H8095 'Shimon' with prefix ו 'and.' H4583/H4584 'abode/Maon' are component roots but the full form is clearly the personal name in this name list.
textual_notes: The word ]קני[ appears in brackets in the source text, suggesting manuscript damage or editorial uncertainty. It likely represents קנאי 'zealot/zealous one' from the root קנא (to be zealous). חלפי appears to be a patronymic (Aramaic/Hebrew form of Alphaeus) identifying which Yaaqov this is.

translation_notes: איש: H376 'a man' — in construct with קריות produces 'man of Qeriyot,' the Hebrew equivalent of 'Iscariot.' H377 'to act manly' is a verb and doesn't fit the nominal slot.
שהיה: ש + היה — H1961 'who was/existed.' H1962 'ruin' or H3050 'Yah' do not fit this relative clause construction.

בוגד: The root בגד means 'to deal treacherously/betray.' The candidates listed under גד (H1407-H1410) are for the sub-root only. The full form בוגד is a participial form of בגד (Strong's H898), meaning 'betrayer/traitor.'
textual_notes: The two occurrences of יהודה likely refer to two different persons: the first is Judah (Jude, son of James or Thaddaeus) and the second is Judah of Qeriyot (Judas Iscariot). The text lists them sequentially without a conjunction between them, which is slightly unusual but the identifying phrase 'man of Qeriyot' disambiguates.

translation_notes: וירד: H3381 'to descend' — he came down from the mountain. H3382 'Jered' is a proper name and doesn't fit the verb slot with ו-consecutive.

ההר: H2022 'mountain' with definite article — 'the mountain' previously mentioned. H2023 'Hor' is a specific named peak; the definite article pointing back to the previously mentioned mountain favors H2022.
ועמד: H5975 'to stand' — 'and he stood.' This is the most natural reading. H5976 'to shake' produces an odd image. H5977 'a spot' is a noun. H5978 'along with' is a preposition.
במקום: H4725 'a standing place/location' with prefix ב — 'in a place.' H6965 'to rise' is a verb root that doesn't fit the nominal construction here.

חרב: H2720 'parched/dry/level' — describing the terrain of the place. In context of descending from a mountain to stand on flat ground, 'level/flat' (a dry plain as opposed to a mountainous area) makes the most sense. H2719 'sword' would produce 'a place of sword' — possible but forced. H2722 'Choreb/Horeb' would mean he stood at Mount Sinai, which contradicts just descending from a different mountain. H2717 'to desolate' is a verb.
עם: H5971 'a people/nation' — 'a multitude of people.' H5973 'with' is a preposition and doesn't fit after רוב 'multitude of.'
מכל: מ + כל — H3605 'all/every' with prefix מ 'from' — 'from all of.'

ומעבר: H4569 'a crossing-place/beyond' — 'from beyond.' The other candidates (H5674 'to cross,' H5676 'the opposite side') overlap semantically; H4569 as a noun 'the crossing/beyond' with prefix ומ fits best.

לים: ל + ים — H3220 'sea' with prefix ל — could mean 'to the sea' or in construct 'of the sea.' Combined with ומעבר: 'from beyond the sea.' H3222 'warm spring' is implausible in this geographic listing.

וצור: H6697 'rock/cliff' is the common noun, but in context of a geographic list alongside Tsidon, this is clearly the city Tyre (Tsor). H6696 'to cramp/besiege' is a verb. H6698 'Tsur' as a personal name doesn't fit.
textual_notes: חרב is a significant ambiguity: it could mean 'dry/level ground' (H2720), 'desolate' (H2717/H2721), 'sword' (H2719), or even 'Horeb' (H2722). The narrative context — descending a mountain and standing on flat ground to teach a multitude — strongly favors 'flat/level/open place.' The separation of מ and ן (from the mountain) suggests מן was split across a word boundary in the manuscript, which is unusual.
וצור could be the common noun 'rock' (H6697) or the city Tyre; the pairing with Tsidon (Sidon) makes the city identification virtually certain.

translation_notes: בעבור: H5668 'on account of / in order that' — fits the purpose clause 'in order that they might hear.' H5669 'stored grain' is completely out of context.
בעד: H1157 'on account of / by reason of' — 'on account of an evil spirit.' The other candidates under עד (H5703-H5708) could yield 'until' or 'witness' but don't fit as naturally.
רוח: H7307 'wind/breath/spirit' — in the phrase 'evil spirit,' this is clearly 'spirit.' H7304 'to breathe freely' and H7306 'to smell' are verbs and don't fit the nominal slot.

רעה: H7465 'breakage/evil/badness' — modifying רוח as 'evil spirit.' H7462 'to tend/shepherd' would produce 'spirit of shepherding,' which is incoherent in context of affliction and healing. H7463 'companion' would yield 'companion spirit,' which is less natural. H7464 'female associate' is forced.
textual_notes: מצטערין appears to be a Mishnaic/Late Hebrew hitpael participial form with Aramaic-style plural suffix ין rather than biblical ים, suggesting this text is from a later Hebrew period. The root צער means 'to suffer/be distressed.'

translation_notes: העם: H5971 'a people' with definite article — 'the people.' H5973 'with' is a preposition and doesn't work with the definite article in this way.
כי: H3588 'because/for' — introduces the causal clause explaining why they wanted to touch him. H3587 'a brand/scar' is a noun and doesn't fit.

ומרפא: H4832 'curative/healing' — as a participle 'and healing.' Could also be parsed as מ + רפא (H7495 'to cure') with prefix, but H4832 as the participial/nominal form 'healing' fits the sentence structure where power goes out and heals.
textual_notes: ומרפא could be the noun 'a cure/healing' (H4832) or parsed as a participial form of רפא (H7495) 'and curing/healing.' Both yield essentially the same meaning in context.

translation_notes: והוא: H1931 'he' — emphatic pronoun 'and he.' H1933/H1934 'to be/exist' are verbs that don't fit with the following participle as naturally.

אומר: Listed candidate H201 'Omar' is a proper name (grandson of Esau). However, אומר is clearly the qal active participle of אמר (H559, 'to say') — 'saying.' The Strong's candidate provided doesn't match the actual usage; this is a participle of אמר.
של: H7945 'on account of / which / of' — functioning as a possessive particle 'of' (common in later Hebrew) — 'of the poor.' H7944 'a fault' doesn't fit.
שמהם: ש + מ + הם — H1992 'they/them' with ש (relative/because) and מ (from) — 'for from them / for theirs.' H1990 'Ham' and H1991 'abundance' don't fit.
מלכות: H4438 'a kingdom/dominion' — 'kingdom of God.' H3575 'Cuth' is a place in Assyria and produces nonsense.

האל: H410 'God/the Mighty One' with definite article — 'God.' H408/409 'not' would produce 'kingdom of not.' H411/412 'these/those' would produce 'kingdom of those,' which is incomplete. H413 'to/near' doesn't fit as a noun.
textual_notes: אומר: The only Strong's candidate provided (H201 'Omar') is clearly wrong for this context. This is the participle of אמר (H559) 'saying.' I have assigned no Strong's number from the provided candidates since none match.

עניים has no Strong's candidates provided. The root ענה/עני means 'poor, afflicted, humble.' This could be H6041 (poor/afflicted) with the ים suffix. The ים could be intensifying ('the utterly poor') or simply plural ('the poor ones'). Context of a blessing suggests a class of people, hence plural.

translation_notes: של (consonants שׁל): Candidates: H7944 'a fault', H7945 'on account of, whatsoever, whichsoever'. Chose H7945 because this is functioning as a relative particle 'of' connecting 'blessed are they' to 'hungry ones.'

כי (both occurrences): Candidates: H3587 'a brand or scar', H3588 'conjunction for/because'. Chose H3588 because this clearly functions as a causal conjunction 'for/because' introducing the reason for the blessing.

שבעים: The candidate H7657 'seventy' shares these consonants, but the root שׂבע meaning 'satisfied/full/sated' is the natural reading here — hungry ones will be satisfied. The lexicon only lists H7657 but the root שׂבע (H7646-7649) fits perfectly in context with 'hungry.'
שהם: Candidates: H7718 'beryl', H7719 'Shoham', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. The word is שׁ + הם, the relative particle plus the pronoun 'they,' yielding 'that they [are].' Chose H1992.
textual_notes: שבעים: The only Strong's candidate provided is H7657 'seventy,' but the consonants שׂבעים clearly derive from the root שׂבע 'to be satisfied/full' (H7646-7649). In context with 'hungry' the meaning 'satisfied' is certain, but the provided lexicon candidates do not include the correct entry.

translation_notes: אתם: The candidate H864 'Etham, a place' makes no sense here. This is clearly the 2mp pronoun 'you' (אַתֶּם), which is so common it may not have a Strong's entry in the provided list.
מהם: Prefix מ 'from' + הם. Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. Chose H1992 — 'from them' fits the context of being separated from people.

הרע: Candidates: H7451 'bad/evil', H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate', H7454 'thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 because 'cast out your name as evil' produces the most coherent image — your reputation is slandered.
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of, in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 — 'on account of' introduces the reason for persecution.

טעם: Candidates: H2938 'to taste', H2939 'to feed', H2940 'perception/intelligence/reason', H2941 'judicial sentence', H2942 'flavor/judgment/account'. Chose H2940 'reason/sake' — 'on account of the reason/sake of the Son of Man.'
בן: Candidates: H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 — 'son of the human' is the natural reading.
האדם: Candidates: H119 'flush/rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 — 'the human' forming the phrase 'son of the human.'
textual_notes: טעם בן האדם: The phrase is unusual. טעם could mean 'reason/sake' or 'judgment/decree' or even 'taste/perception.' The phrase 'on account of the reason of the Son of Man' could also be read 'on account of the decree/judgment of the Son of Man.' The translation 'for the sake of' is the most natural reading in context.

translation_notes: היום: Candidates: H3117 'a day', H3118 'a day (Aramaic)'. Chose H3117 as the standard Hebrew form.
כי: H3588 conjunction 'for/because' — introduces the reason to rejoice.
מאד: Candidates: H3966 'vehemently/exceedingly', H108 (from אד) 'a fog'. Chose H3966 — 'exceedingly' modifies the reward naturally.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 'he/it (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 — the pronoun 'it' serving as copula 'it is.'
מושפע: From root שפע H8228 'resources/abundance.' The מו- prefix indicates a hophal/passive participle: 'poured out' or 'made abundant.'
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'like this' = 'in the same way.'
textual_notes: ב<מים: The text contains a damaged/uncertain character (<). The consonants suggest בשמים (in the heavens/skies) with the שׁ partially damaged, which fits the context of heavenly reward.

שכרכם: While the candidate H3750 'crocus' is listed for כרכם, the word is clearly שׂכר + כם (your reward), from root שׂכר (H7939). The lexicon listing is misleading as it parsed the consonants differently.
ובאבות: Could mean 'and to the fathers/ancestors' or 'and to the patriarchs.' The context of persecution of prophets and forefathers is coherent either way.

translation_notes: רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'merely/only/but', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 — functions as a contrastive particle 'but/however' transitioning from blessings to woes.
אוי: Candidates: H188 'woe/lamentation', H189 'Evi (a name)'. Chose H188 — 'woe' fits the exclamatory warning context.
כי: H3588 conjunction 'for/because.'
הוא: H1931 pronoun 'it [is]' serving as copula.

נח: The only candidate is H5146 'Noah (the patriarch).' However, the consonants נח naturally read as the root נוח meaning 'rest/settled/at ease' (H5117-5118). In context, 'your mind is at rest' = 'you have already received your consolation.' The provided lexicon is incomplete here.
textual_notes: נח דעתכם: This phrase 'rest of your mind/knowledge' is a Rabbinic Hebrew idiom (נחת דעת or נח דעתו) meaning 'satisfaction/contentment of mind.' It implies the rich have already received their comfort — their mind is at ease with what they have, and nothing further awaits them.

translation_notes: אוי: H188 'woe/lamentation' — same pattern as section 4.
כי: H3588 conjunction 'for/because.'
אוי: H188 'woe' — consistent with the woe-sayings pattern.
כי: H3588 — here functioning as 'when/for' introducing the circumstance.

כשלם: The כ prefix means 'when/as.' The root שלם candidates: H7999 'to be complete', H8000 'to complete/restore', H8001 'prosperity', H8002 'sacrifice', H8003 'complete/whole', H8004 'Shalem (Jerusalem)'. Read as כ + שלם = 'when all of them' or 'when they completely.' Chose H8003 'complete' — meaning 'when everyone/all of them' bless you.

אלה: Candidates: H421 'bewail', H422 'imprecate', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. However, אלה also serves as the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (H411/H428). Chose the demonstrative reading — 'these things.'
של: H7945 'of/on account of' — relative particle connecting 'their fathers' to 'those.'
אלו: Candidates: H431 'lo!/behold', H432 'if'. In Mishnaic Hebrew, אלו commonly means 'those/these.' Chose H431 loosely, but functionally this is the demonstrative 'those.'
textual_notes: ה<קר: The text has a damaged/uncertain character (<). The consonants suggest השקר 'the falsehood/lie' (from שקר H8267), yielding 'prophets of the falsehood' = 'false prophets.' The שׁ appears partially damaged.

כשלם: Could be parsed as כ + שׁלם 'when complete/all' or as כשל + ם 'they stumble.' The former produces a coherent reading ('when everyone blesses you') while the latter ('they stumble you will bless') does not. Chose the former.

The syntax of this verse is somewhat compressed. 'According to these things their fathers were doing to the false prophets' — the word order suggests the fathers' behavior toward false prophets is the comparison point.

translation_notes: אבל: Candidates: H56 'bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 — 'but/yet' functions as a contrastive conjunction transitioning from woes to positive instruction.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 — 'I' is the speaker's self-reference.

אומר: Candidate H201 'Omar (name)'. The consonants א-מ-ר are the root of 'to say' (H559 אמר). The participle form אומר means 'saying.' The provided candidate is a proper noun that happens to share consonants.
שזה: ש + זה. Candidates for זה: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'that which' or 'this [that].'
טוב: Candidates: H2895 'to be/make good', H2896 'good (adj/noun)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness'. Chose H2896 — 'good' as a noun/adjective: 'do good.'
ועשו: The candidate H6215 'Esau' shares these consonants, but this is clearly the imperative plural of עשׂה 'to do/make' with vav conjunction: 'and do.'
textual_notes: ואוהביכם: This word is ambiguous. It could mean 'and your lovers' (those who love you) or, in context with enemies, it might be expected to say 'and those who hate you' (שׂונאיכם). The consonants clearly read 'and your lovers/those loving you.' This may be a scribal feature, a deliberate pairing (love your enemies AND your friends), or an unusual textual tradition. Translated as written.

translation_notes: רע: Candidates: H7451 'bad/evil', H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate', H7454 'thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 — 'says evil to you' = speaks evil/curses against you.
בעד: Candidate H1157 'on behalf of, for, behind.' Also עד candidates include H5703-5708 with various meanings. Chose H1157 — 'pray on behalf of' is the natural reading.

שמכבדין: The root כבד can mean 'to honor/glorify' (H3513) or 'to be heavy/burden' (H3515). The Aramaic-style suffix -ין suggests a participial form. In context of praying for persecutors, 'those who burden/oppress you' fits better than 'those who honor you,' though the ironic reading 'those who [claim to] honor you' is also possible.
textual_notes: שמכבדין: This is genuinely ambiguous. The root כבד means both 'to honor' and 'to make heavy/burden/oppress.' In context with blessing those who curse and praying for persecutors, 'those who oppress/mistreat you' fits the pattern. However, some traditions read this as an ironic or sarcastic honoring. The -ין ending is an Aramaic/late Hebrew plural participle suffix.

translation_notes: בלחי: Candidates: H3895 'cheek/jaw-bone', H3896 'Lechi (place)', H2416 'alive', H2417 'alive (Aramaic)'. The ב prefix means 'on/in.' Chose H3895 — 'on the cheek' is the coherent physical image of being struck.
לא: Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Chose H3808 — standard Hebrew negation.
תרצה: Candidate H8656 'Tirtsah (place/name).' However, the consonants are clearly the 2ms imperfect of רצה 'to desire/want/be pleased' (H7521). 'You shall not want to prevent him.'
ועוד: Candidates: H5749 'to testify/protest', H5750 'again/still/also', H5751 same as H5750. Chose H5750 — 'and also/furthermore.'
אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 — 'if he desires' introduces a conditional clause.
textual_notes: הגונילא: This word does not correspond to any standard biblical Hebrew root. It appears to be a loanword, possibly from Latin 'gaunacum' or similar, referring to an outer cloak or mantle. The ה prefix is the definite article 'the.'
שיכך: This appears to be שׁ + יכך where the root may be נכה 'to strike' (H5221) with a 2ms suffix. The form is unusual but the meaning 'strikes you' fits the context of being hit on the cheek.

translation_notes: אבל: Candidates: H56 'bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel', H60 'lamentation', H61 'truly/yet/but'. Chose H61 — contrastive 'but' transitioning to a new instruction.
אדם: Candidates: H119 'flush/rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 — 'every human/person' is the natural reading.

תן: Candidate H8565 'a monster/sea-serpent/jackal.' However, the consonants תן are unmistakably the masculine singular imperative of נתן 'to give' (H5414). The provided lexicon candidate is irrelevant here.
את: Candidates: H852 'portent', H853 'object marker', H854 'with/near', H855 'hoe'. Chose H853 — the definite object marker before 'yours.'

שלך: Candidates: H7993 'to throw out/cast away', H7994 'pelican'. However, שלך here is שׁ + ל + ך, the relative particle + preposition + 2ms suffix = 'that which [belongs] to you / yours.' The provided candidates reflect a different parsing.

אל: Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative negation)', H409 same, H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these/those', H412 same, H413 'to/near'. Chose H408 — 'do not' as a prohibitive particle before the imperfect verb 'seek.'
textual_notes: שלך: Could be parsed as the verb 'to cast/throw' (H7993) or as the possessive construction שׁ + לך 'that which is yours.' The latter is clearly correct in context — 'that which is yours' is being robbed.
תבקשם: The suffix -ם 'them' could refer to the stolen goods or to the person. In context, 'do not seek them back' refers to the possessions that were taken.

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. With prefix כ (as/like) this forms 'and as/when' — H834 is the conjunction that fits the comparative clause structure.

להם (להם/הם): Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they/them'. The ל prefix + הם as 3mp pronoun 'to them' fits perfectly as the indirect object mirroring לכם. Chose H1992.

עשו: The Strong's only lists H6215 'Esau' for this form, but the consonants ע-ש-ו are clearly the imperative 2mp of עשה (H6213 'to do/make'). The dictionary listing is incomplete; this is plainly the verb.
textual_notes: אתם has no Strong's entry for the 2mp pronoun 'you' in the provided candidates (only H864 'Etham'). This is clearly the 2mp independent pronoun, a standard Hebrew form not requiring a Strong's number.

חפצים and שהאנשים have no candidates listed; חפצים is the masculine plural participle of חפץ (H2654 'to delight/desire'), and שהאנשים is the relative particle ש + definite article ה + אנשים (plural of איש H376 'man').

translation_notes: אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. The clause structure is conditional ('if you love...'), so H518 is clearly correct.

אי: Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Combined with זו ('this'), אי זו forms 'which/what kind of' — an interrogative construction. H335 'where/how' best captures this interrogative function.
זו: Candidates: H2097 'this/that', H2098 'this/that', H2099 'Ziv (a month)'. In the phrase אי זו, this is the demonstrative 'this/that' forming an interrogative. H2098 chosen.
חן: Candidates: H2580 'graciousness/favor/beauty', H2581 'Chen (proper name)'. The context asks what kind of favor is deserved — H2580 is the common noun.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 'he/it', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Functions as copula 'it is' — H1931.
כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus', H3652 'so', H3653 'stand/pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Adverbial 'so/likewise' fits the sentence conclusion — H3651.
textual_notes: ראויה has no candidates listed; it appears to be a later Hebrew form meaning 'fitting/worthy/deserving', not found in the classical Strong's lexicon.
תאהבו and אוהביכם lack listed candidates but are clearly forms of אהב (H157 'to love') — 2mp imperfect and participle with 2mp suffix respectively.
שהחוטאים and עושים lack listed candidates; שהחוטאים = ש + ה + חוטאים (participle of חטא H2398 'to sin'); עושים = participle of עשה (H6213 'to do').

translation_notes: שכר: Candidates: H7936 'to hire', H7937 'to become tipsy', H7938 'wages', H7939 'payment/salary/compensation', H7940 'Sakar (name)', H7941 'intoxicant', H3733 'ram/meadow', H3734 'cor (measure)'. The context discusses giving to those from whom one expects something back — 'reward/payment' (H7939) fits perfectly.
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. The clause introduces purpose ('so that they receive') — H5668.
גמול: Candidates: H1576 'treatment/recompense/requital', H1577 'Gamul (name)'. The context describes receiving something in return — H1576 'recompense'.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: for/because/that'. Introduces a causal clause — H3588.
אי: H335 'where/how' — interrogative with זו forming 'what kind of', same as section 2.
זו: H2098 'this/that' — demonstrative in interrogative phrase, same as section 2.
textual_notes: שירות has no candidates listed; it appears to be a noun meaning 'service/ministry', likely derived from שרת (H8334 'to minister/serve').
מקוים has no candidates listed; it is the plural participle of קוה (H6960 'to wait/hope/expect').
שיקבלו has no candidates listed; it is ש + imperfect 3mp of קבל (H6901 'to receive/accept').
ראוי has no candidates, same later Hebrew form as ראויה in section 2, meaning 'fitting/worthy'.

translation_notes: אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. This word introduces a contrast with the preceding conditional statements — 'but/rather/truly' (H61) fits as an adversative conjunction.
טוב (first): Candidates: H2895 'to do good', H2896 'good (adj/noun)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness'. As the object/complement of 'do to them' — 'good' as noun/adjective (H2896).

דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. After 'not expecting' — 'a thing/matter' (H1697) makes the most natural sense: expecting nothing in return.

ושכרכם: The candidates list only H3750 'crocus' for כרכם. However, the full word is ו+שכר+כם = 'and your reward'. שכר maps to H7939 'payment/wages'. The כרכם entry is a false match from splitting the consonants differently.
הרבה: Candidates: H7235 'to increase', H7236 same, H7237 'Rabbah (place)'. Adverbial use meaning 'much/greatly' — H7235.
מאד: Candidates: H3966 'vehemently/very', H108 'fog'. Intensifier 'very/exceedingly' — H3966.

בנים: The only candidate listed is H1143 'space between armies'. However, these consonants בנים are the standard plural of בן (H1121 'son'). The dictionary listing is incomplete. Context demands 'sons/children of God Most High'.
מאל: Candidates for אל: H408 'not', H409 'not', H410 'strength/mighty/God', H411 'these', H412 'these', H413 'to/toward'. With prefix מ (from/of), מאל = 'from/of God' — H410.
עליון: Candidates: H5945 'the Supreme/lofty', H5946 'the Supreme'. Both fit; H5945 is the standard Hebrew form for 'Most High'.
שהוא: H1931 'he' with relative prefix ש — 'that he [is]'.
טוב (second): H2896 'good' — adjective describing God's nature.
על (both): Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'upon/over/toward', H5922 same, H5923 'yoke'. Preposition 'upon/toward' — H5921.
להם: H1992 'them' with ל prefix — 'to them', same reasoning as section 1.
textual_notes: רגוזי הרצון is a difficult phrase. רגוזי appears to be a construct form related to רגז (H7264 'to tremble/be agitated/provoke'). הרצון is 'the goodwill/favor' (H7522). Together 'those who provoke goodwill' likely means 'the ungrateful' — those who spurn favor. This is an unusual construction and may be a Hebrew rendering of a concept like 'ungrateful.'
הרעים lacks listed candidates but is clearly the plural of רע (H7451 'evil/bad') with the definite article — 'the evil/wicked ones'.
מתנות lacks listed candidates; it is the plural of מתנה (H4979 'a gift/present').
אויביכם lacks listed candidates; it is the plural of אויב (H341 'enemy') with 2mp suffix.

translation_notes: לכן (כן): Candidates: H3651 'thus/so/therefore', H3652 'so', H3653 'stand', H3654 'gnat'. With prefix ל, לכן = 'therefore' — H3651.

בעלי: Candidates: H1180 'Baali (symbolic name)', also עלי candidates H5940-H5943. However, בעלי is the construct plural of בעל (H1167 'owner/master/possessor'). 'Possessors of graciousness' is a natural Hebrew idiom for 'compassionate people'. The H1180 entry is for a specific proper noun use, not the common noun.
כאשר (אשר): H834 'who/which/when/as' — comparative conjunction 'just as'. Same reasoning as section 1.
הוא: H1931 'he' — emphatic pronoun functioning as copula.
חנון: Candidates: H2586 'Chanun (name)', H2587 'gracious'. The adjective describing the father — H2587 'gracious'.
textual_notes: בעלי could theoretically be parsed as ב + עלי (H5942 'high' or H5941 'Eli'), but 'in the high ones of graciousness' makes no sense. בעלי as construct of בעל 'possessor' is standard Hebrew idiom.

translation_notes: אל (both): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H409 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H412 'these', H413 'to/toward'. Before an imperfect verb (תחפצו), אל functions as the negative particle of prohibition — H408.
ולא (both): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not'. Simple negation before imperfect verb — H3808.
textual_notes: תחפצו, לדון, נדונים, לענוש, תענשו, תעזבו, ותעזב all lack listed candidates. תחפצו = 2mp imperfect of חפץ (H2654 'to desire/delight'). לדון = infinitive of דין (H1777 'to judge'). נדונים = passive participle of דין. לענוש = infinitive of ענש (H6064 'to fine/punish'). תענשו = 2mp imperfect passive of ענש. תעזבו = 2mp imperative of עזב (H5800 'to leave/release/forsake'). ותעזב = 3fs imperfect passive of עזב.

עזב (H5800) can mean 'to leave, forsake, abandon, let go, release.' In this context of reciprocal action ('release and it will be released to you'), the sense of 'release/forgive/let go' is most fitting.

translation_notes: אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. The speaker says 'I will give' — H589 'I'.
מדה (both): Candidates: H4060 'measure/extension', H4061 'tribute in money'. The imagery of measuring out and receiving back demands 'measure' — H4060.
יותר: H3148 'redundant/over and above/more' — comparative adverb modifying עליונה, meaning 'even more exalted'.

בסוף (סוף): Candidates: H5486 'to terminate', H5487 'to come to an end', H5488 'reed/papyrus', H5489 'Reed Sea', H5490 'termination', H5491 'termination'. With prefix ב, 'in the end/at the termination' — H5490.
כי: H3588 causal conjunction 'for/because' — introduces the explanation of the measuring principle.
textual_notes: ובחונה lacks listed candidates; it appears to be a feminine passive participle of בחן (H974 'to test/examine/prove') with conjunction ו — 'and tested/proven'.
ומצודקת lacks listed candidates; it appears to be a feminine passive participle (or pu'al/hofal form) related to צדק (H6663 'to be just/righteous') — 'and justified/made righteous'.
באותה lacks candidates; it is ב + אותה = 'in that (same)' — a demonstrative construction.
שתמדדו and תמדד lack candidates; both are forms of מדד (H4058 'to measure') — שתמדדו = relative + 2mp imperfect 'that you measure'; תמדד = 3fs imperfect passive 'it will be measured'.
כדמותה lacks candidates for the full form; כ + דמות + ה = 'according to its likeness'. דמות (H1823) means 'likeness/resemblance'.
The phrase structure 'give and I will give to you' with first person is unusual. It could be divine speech, or אני could be emphatic. The first-person voice is noteworthy.

translation_notes: עור (both): Candidates: H5782 'to wake', H5783 'to be bare', H5784 'chaff', H5785 'skin/hide', H5786 'to blind', H5787 'blind'. The sentence describes one leading another and both falling into a pit — the image of a blind person leading a blind person is coherent and proverbial. H5787 'blind (adj)' fits both instances.
אחר: Candidates: H309 'to procrastinate', H310 'after/behind', H311 'after', H312 'other/another', H313 'Acher (name)'. Modifying the second עור — 'another blind one' — H312.
הוא: H1931 'he/it' — copula in nominal sentence 'it is a necessity'.
בבור (בור): Candidates: H952 'to examine', H953 'a pit/cistern/prison'. The destination of falling — H953 'pit'.
textual_notes: אינינו and איפשרי lack listed candidates. אינינו appears to be אין + suffix = 'it is not' (a negation of existence). איפשרי appears to be a later Hebrew word meaning 'possible' (from the root אפשר), not found in the classical Strong's lexicon.
הכרח lacks listed candidates; it appears to be a later Hebrew noun meaning 'necessity/compulsion', not in Strong's.
ש<ניהם has a textual marker < suggesting damage or uncertainty in the manuscript. The reading שניהם = 'both of them' (from שנים H8147 'two') fits perfectly.
ימשוך lacks listed candidates; it is 3ms imperfect of משך (H4900 'to draw/drag/lead').
יפלו lacks listed candidates; it is 3mp imperfect of נפל (H5307 'to fall').

translation_notes: על: Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'above/over/upon', H5922 same, H5923 'yoke'. The spatial/hierarchical relationship between pupil and master — 'above' — H5921.

הרב (רב): Candidates: H7227 'abundant/great (also: master/teacher)', H7228 'archer', H7229 'abundant', H7230 'abundance'. In the context of pupil-and-teacher, רב means 'master/great one/teacher' — H7227.

שלם: Candidates: H7999 'to be safe/complete', H8000 'to restore', H8001 'prosperity', H8002 'sacrifice of thanks', H8003 'complete/whole/friendly', H8004 'Shalem (place)'. Describing the state a pupil achieves — 'complete/perfected' (H8003).
כאשר (אשר): H834 comparative conjunction 'as/when'.
הוא (both): H1931 'he' — pronoun/copula.

כרבו (רבו): Candidates listed: H7238 'increase of dignity', H7239 'myriad', H7240 'myriad'. However, כ + רב + ו = 'like his master/great one'. The consonants רבו with suffix match רב (H7227) + 3ms possessive. The listed candidates for רבו as a standalone word don't fit the context of pupil-teacher relationship.
כל: H3605 'all/every' — universal quantifier.
textual_notes: כרבו could be parsed as כ (like) + רבו where רבו is 'his master' (from רב H7227 with 3ms suffix), or as כ + a form from H7238-7240. The teacher-student context strongly favors 'like his master'.

translation_notes: איך: H349 'how/how!' — introduces a rhetorical question of astonishment.
בעין (עין): Candidates: H5869 'eye/fountain', H5870 'eye', H5871 'Ajin (place)'. Body part in context of seeing/splinter — H5869 'eye'.
שאתה (אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you (singular)'. Subject of 'carry' — H859 'you'.

בשלך (שלך): Candidates: H7993 'to throw out/away', H7994 'pelican'. With prefix ב and 2ms suffix, בשלך = 'in yours/in your own [eye]'. The root שלך here is used as a possessive pronoun form (ב + של + ך = 'in that which is yours'). However, H7993 is the only root listed. The form functions as 'in yours'.

בריח: Candidates from בריח: H1280 'bolt/bar', H1281 'fugitive/serpent', H1282 'Bariach (name)'. Also from ריח: H7381 'odor', H7382 'odor'. Contrasted with a tiny splinter, a large solid object is needed — 'bolt/bar/beam' (H1280) creates the most coherent contrasting image. An 'odor' in the eye makes no sense. A 'fugitive serpent' is forced. A 'beam/bolt' as something large lodged in one's own eye provides the perfect hyperbolic contrast to the splinter.
גדול: H1419 'great/large' — modifies בריח, emphasizing the contrast.
textual_notes: קיסם lacks listed candidates. It appears to be a later Hebrew word meaning 'splinter/sliver/chip' (related to קסם or a loan form), not found in the classical Strong's lexicon. The context of something small in an eye confirms this meaning.
תראה lacks listed candidates; it is 2ms imperfect of ראה (H7200 'to see').
אחיך lacks listed candidates; it is אח (H251 'brother') with 2ms suffix.
ואינך lacks candidates; it is ו + אין + ך = 'and you are not' (negation of existence with 2ms suffix).
חושב lacks candidates; it is the active participle of חשב (H2803 'to think/consider/reckon').
נושא lacks candidates; it is the active participle of נשא (H5375 'to carry/bear/lift').

בשלך is genuinely ambiguous: it could be ב + של + ך ('in yours', later Hebrew possessive construction) or ב + שלך from H7993. The possessive reading 'in yours [i.e., your own eye]' is required by the context of comparing what's in your brother's eye vs. your own.

translation_notes: לאמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 (Aramaic 'to say'), H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because 'to say' fits the infinitive construct introducing speech.
ואני (אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because 'and I will remove' is coherent; 'and a ship will remove the splinter' is nonsensical.

גרש: Candidates: H1643 'grain/kernel', H1644 'to drive out/expel', H1645 'produce'. Chose H1644 because the imperative 'drive out the beam' fits the context of removing something from one's eye; 'grain' or 'produce' would be incoherent here.

הבריח (בריח): Candidates: H1280 'a bolt/bar', H1281 'a fugitive/serpent constellation', H1282 'Bariach (name)'; also ריח H7381 'odor'. translation_notes: וכאשר: The conjunction וכ + אשר. Candidates include H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness'. In narrative context introducing a temporal clause ('and when...'), H834 is the clear choice.

קרב: Candidates: H7126 'to approach', H7128 'hostile encounter', H7130 'the center/midst', H7131 'near'. The subject is Yeshua moving toward the gate; H7126 'to approach' produces the most natural image.
בשער: Candidates: H8175 'to storm', H8179 'a gate/door', H8177 'hair', etc. Combined with 'the city,' H8179 'gate' is the only coherent reading — cities have gates.
העיר: H5892 'city' vs H5894 'watcher' vs H5895 'young ass'. Following 'the gate of the ___,' H5892 'city' is the natural reading.
הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. As a narrative interjection introducing a dramatic scene (a funeral procession), H2009 'behold' fits perfectly.
מת (H4962): Only candidate 'an adult/man' but the consonants מת in context clearly mean 'dead [person]' (from the root מות). H4962 is the nominal form used here to mean a dead man.
אחד: H258 'to unify' vs H259 'one/first'. As an adjective modifying the dead man, H259 'one' fits — indicating a sole/only [son].
שהיה: H1961 'to be/exist' vs H1962 'ruin'. Relative clause 'who was a son' requires a copulative verb; H1961.
עוד: H5749 'to testify' vs H5750 'again/more/still'. After 'there was not to her,' H5750 'any more' is the natural adverbial reading.
ורב: H7227 'abundant/great' vs H7228 'archer'. Describing a crowd, H7227 is clearly correct.
עם (first): H5971 'people' vs H5973 'with'. After 'ורב' (a multitude of), it must be the noun 'people' (H5971).
מן: H4478 'manna' vs H4480 'from/out of'. Preceding 'the city,' H4480 'from' is the only coherent reading.
עם (second): H5971 'people' vs H5973 'with'. Before 'that woman,' this must be the preposition 'with' (H5973).
textual_notes: הא<ה appears to have a damaged/missing consonant (indicated by <). The context strongly suggests אשה (woman), referring to the widow. The reading 'the woman' is contextually certain but the text is physically damaged.
ההיא is a feminine demonstrative 'that one' — here modifying the woman. No Strong's candidates were provided.

translation_notes: וכאשר: H834 'when' — temporal conjunction introducing the scene, same as section 2.
היה: H1961 'to be/exist' vs H1962 'ruin'. Auxiliary verb describing Yeshua's state: 'he was moved'; H1961.

בחסד: H2616 'to be kind/bow', H2617 'kindness/lovingkindness/compassion', H2618 'Chesed (name)'. The preposition ב + noun describing the emotional quality; H2617 'compassion/kindness' produces the coherent image of being moved with tender mercy.
אמר: H559 'to say' vs H561 'something said' vs H563 'a lamb'. As a verb with Yeshua as subject and speech following, H559 'to say' is the clear reading.
אל: H408 'not (deprecative)' vs H410 'God/mighty' vs H413 'to/toward'. Before the imperfect תבכי, H408 is the standard negative particle for prohibitions: 'do not.'

עליה: H5944 'something lofty/upper room'. However, the consonants על + יה naturally parse as the preposition 'upon/over' + 3fs suffix 'her.' The Strong's entry H5944 is for the noun עליה, but here the context demands the prepositional reading 'upon her / over her.'
textual_notes: ראתה could be parsed as 'she saw' (3fs perfect of ראה with paragogic ה) or as 'he saw her' (3ms perfect of ראה + 3fs object suffix). The narrative flow suggests Yeshua is the one seeing the widow and being moved to compassion, so 'he saw her' is more likely. However, the form ראתה is morphologically more natural as 3fs 'she saw.' The subsequent clause makes Yeshua the subject of the emotional response, which works with either parsing.

נע has no Strong's candidates provided. The consonants נע could derive from נוע (H5128 'to waver, move, shake') or be related to a Mishnaic usage meaning 'moved/stirred.' In context — 'he was moved in compassion' — it describes an emotional stirring.

translation_notes: קרב: H7126 'to approach' vs H7128 'hostile encounter' vs H7130 'center'. Yeshua is physically moving toward the bier; H7126 'to approach' fits.
ונגע: H5060 'to touch/lay the hand upon' vs H5061 'a blow/affliction'. The action is physical contact with the bier; H5060 'to touch' is the natural reading.

המטה: Candidates: H4294 'rod/staff/tribe', H4295 'downward/below', H4296 'a bed/bier/litter', H4297 'distortion', H4298 'expansion'. In the context of a funeral procession where bearers are carrying a dead man, H4296 'bier/litter' produces the only coherent image.
נער: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble', H5288 'a boy/young man', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Yeshua is addressing the dead son directly; H5288 'young man' is the natural vocative.
אני: H589 'I' vs H590 'a ship/fleet'. The speaker is identifying himself as the one commanding; H589 'I' is obvious.
מצוה: H4687 'a command (noun)' vs H6680 'to command/constitute (verb)'. After 'I,' a verb is expected; H6680 as a participle 'commanding' — 'I [am] commanding' — fits the syntax.
דבר: H1696 'to speak' vs H1697 'a word/matter/thing' vs H1698 'pestilence'. In context describing 'this ___ like this,' the noun H1697 'matter/thing' is the coherent choice.
משם: H8033 'there' (with prefix מ = 'from there') vs H8034 'a name'. The prepositional reading 'from there' fits the concluding clause.
textual_notes: The final clause 'זו דבר כזאת אותם שנשלחו שנרפא משם' is syntactically difficult. It may be a summary or narrator's comment rather than part of Yeshua's direct speech. One possible reading: 'This [is] a matter like this [regarding] those who were sent out — that [one who] was healed from there.' Another parsing: it could describe the report being sent out about the healing. The text is genuinely ambiguous at this point.

שנרפא could be parsed as 'that he was healed' (nifal perfect of רפא) or 'that he healed' (with the ש as a relative pronoun). The nifal (passive) reading 'was healed' seems more natural given the dead man being raised.
שנשלחו — 'who were sent out' — the referent is unclear. It could refer to messengers, or to the words/reports being sent out about the miracle.

translation_notes: שהיה (היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist, be, become', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because the relative clause 'who was dead' requires a copulative verb, not 'ruin'.

לדבר (דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1696 because the lamed prefix indicates an infinitive 'to speak', fitting the context of someone rising and beginning to talk.
textual_notes: מת: Only H4962 is listed ('an adult, a man'), but the consonants מת clearly also function as the adjective/participle 'dead' in Hebrew. The context demands 'dead' — one who was dead rose and spoke. The Strong's listing appears incomplete for this form.

translation_notes: רי או: The consonants רי (H7377 'irrigation/shower') and או (H176 'or') standing alone make no contextual sense. These consonants likely represent ראו — 'they saw' — with a scribal separation. The full phrase 'all the peoples saw a great fear' is coherent.

האל (אל): Candidates: H408/H409 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411/H412 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because the article ה + אל = 'the God', and the context is praising and blessing, which requires a divine object.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Chose H3588 because the clause introduces a reason for praise.
נביא: Candidates: H5029 'a prophet', H5030 'a prophet/inspired man'. Both are essentially identical; chose H5030 as the more common form.
textual_notes: רי או appears to be a scribal splitting of ראו ('they saw'). The word division in the consonantal text is ambiguous here.
The [] marker appears to indicate a lacuna or editorial insertion point in the manuscript, likely where 'saying' or 'lēmor' would appear.

translation_notes: וזה (זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because the demonstrative pronoun 'this' fits as a modifier of 'the word/report'.

הדבר (דבר): Candidates: H1907 'a vizier', H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'the word/report was scattered' describes the spreading of news.

אלה: Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'an imprecation', H424 'an oak', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. None of these match the obvious demonstrative pronoun אלה ('these'), which is extremely common in Hebrew but apparently not listed among the candidates. The context 'all these the words' clearly requires the demonstrative pronoun.
textual_notes: אלה: The demonstrative pronoun 'these' is not among the Strong's candidates provided, yet the context unmistakably requires it. This is likely an omission in the candidate list.

translation_notes: קרא: Candidates: H7121 'to call out to/address/summon', H7122 'to encounter', H7123 'to call (Aramaic)', H7124 'a partridge'. Chose H7121 because the action of summoning disciples fits perfectly.
ושלחם: The root is שלח 'to send' with suffix ם 'them'. The candidates listed under לחם are irrelevant; the word parses as ו+שלח+ם.
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive (Aramaic)', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because the sentence structure 'you he [are] the one' requires a pronoun.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/the same', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 because it functions as a copulative pronoun identifying the subject.
שעתיד: Candidates: H6263 'prepared', H6264 'prepared/future/treasure'. Chose H6264 because 'the one prepared/destined to come' fits the messianic expectation context.

אחר: Candidates: H309 'to delay', H310 'after', H311 'after (Aramaic)', H312 'another/other', H313 'Acher (name)'. Chose H312 because 'hoping for another' makes contextual sense as the alternative to the expected one.

וענה (ענה): Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 'to respond (Aramaic)', H6033 'to afflict (Aramaic)', H6034 'Anah (name)'. Chose H6030 because 'answered and said' is a standard Hebrew narrative formula.

ואמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said (Aramaic)', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because it is the standard verb 'and he said'.
להם: Listed candidate H3859 'to burn/rankle' is irrelevant; this is the preposition ל + pronoun הם (H1992) 'to them'.
החרשים: H2798 'mechanics/craftsmen (valley name)' is listed, but the consonants חרש also yield 'deaf' (from חרש meaning deaf/silent). Context of healing miracles demands 'the deaf'.
ץראיתם: Appears to be a scribal variant of ראיתם ('you have seen') with a prefixed ץ possibly a scribal artifact or abbreviation.
textual_notes: ץראיתם: The initial ץ is anomalous. It may be a scribal error, abbreviation, or damaged text. The core form ראיתם ('you saw/have seen') is clear from context.

מוגדים: This form is unusual. It appears to be a passive participle from a root related to נגד (to tell, announce) in a causative/passive form — 'being told/announced to'. The exact morphological derivation is uncertain.
החרשים: The Strong's candidate offered (H2798 'mechanics/valley name') does not fit. The consonants חרש also mean 'deaf' in Hebrew, which the healing-list context requires.

translation_notes: בי: The candidate H994 'oh that!/if it please' does not fit. The consonants ב+י simply mean 'in me' (preposition ב + first person suffix). Context of denying/rejecting requires 'in me'.
textual_notes: כופרים: From root כפר which can mean 'to cover/atone' (H3722) or 'to deny/disbelieve'. In this context the meaning is clearly 'denying/disbelieving' — those who reject or refuse to believe.

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כ+אשר = 'as/when', a standard temporal conjunction.
לאמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562-H564. Chose H559 because ל+אמר is the standard infinitive 'to say/saying'.

במדבר: H4057 'wilderness/desert/open field' fits perfectly as the location one goes out to see something. The sub-candidates for דבר are irrelevant when the full form מדבר is recognized as 'wilderness'.

מושבים: This could derive from שוב ('to return') in a passive/causative form, or from ישב ('to sit/dwell'). Given the context — the messengers of Yochanan departing — 'returning' fits better than 'seated'.
textual_notes: מושבים: Could be parsed as from שוב ('returning') or ישב ('seated/dwelling'). The narrative context of messengers leaving favors 'returning', but 'departing/going back' is also possible.

הץוקים: The ץ prefix is anomalous (as in section 7). This likely represents קנים or a similar word for 'reeds'. The exact form is uncertain — possibly a scribal convention in this manuscript for representing a tsade-initial or qoph-initial word.
שנועות: Appears to be a participle from נוע ('to shake/sway/wander'). The ש prefix is the relative particle. The feminine plural form matches 'reeds' (which are grammatically feminine).

translation_notes: אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 because the adversative conjunction 'but/yet' introduces a contrasting question after the previous one about reeds.
אי: Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 because combined with זה it forms the interrogative 'what kind/which sort'.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because אי זה together means 'what kind of' — an interrogative phrase.
הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2009 because 'behold those who dress in costly clothing' is a natural presentative exclamation.
הנם: H2011 'Hinnom (a Jebusite)' does not fit. This is הנ+ם = 'behold them' (הנה with 3mp suffix). The context of pointing to kings in their houses requires a demonstrative.
textual_notes: הנם: The only Strong's candidate (H2011 'Hinnom') is a place name that does not fit. This form is best parsed as הנה + ם (behold them), a suffixed presentative particle.
והעמיםכלם appears to be a run-together scribal form of והעמים כלם ('and the peoples all of them').

The syntax of this verse is complex. It could be read as two questions ('What did you go out to see? A man clothed in many garments?') followed by a declarative contrast ('Behold, those in costly clothes — they are kings in their houses').

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 because the context is a rhetorical address transitioning to a question — an adversative conjunction 'but/yet' fits naturally.

אי (consonants אי): Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 because combined with זה דבר it forms a question 'where is this thing' or 'what is this thing', fitting the rhetorical questioning pattern.

דבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'thing/matter' fits naturally as the object of 'where is this' in a rhetorical question about purpose.

אומר (consonants אומר): The only Strong's candidate is H201 'Omar' (a proper name), but contextually this is clearly a participle from אמר (to say), functioning as 'saying/I say'. The lexicon listing is incomplete for this verbal form.
textual_notes: אי זה דבר could be parsed as 'where [is] this thing' (interrogative) or as a compound 'what kind of thing.' The phrase אי זה together commonly functions as 'which/what' in later Hebrew.

אומר is listed only as H201 (Omar, proper name) in the candidates, but in context it is unmistakably a qal participle of אמר 'to say.' No Strong's number for the verb form was provided among candidates.

translation_notes: הנה (consonants הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because this introduces a proclamation formula — 'Behold, I am sending' is a coherent announcement.

מלאכי (consonants מלאכי): The candidate H4401 is 'Malachi' the prophet name, but the consonants מלאכי literally mean 'my messenger' (from מלאך + 1cs suffix). In context, 'I am sending my messenger' is the coherent reading. The Strong's number H4401 covers both the proper name and the possessive form.
הדרך (consonants דרך): Candidates: H1869 'to tread/walk', H1870 'road/way/path'. Chose H1870 because with the article ה it functions as a noun 'the way,' which fits as the object of 'prepare.'
textual_notes: שולח has no verb root candidates listed (only לח 'fresh'), but it is clearly a qal participle of שלח 'to send.' The lexicon candidates are incomplete here.

שיכין is listed only with H3199 'Jakin' (proper name), but in context it is a hiphil imperfect of כון 'to establish/prepare' with the relative prefix ש-. No appropriate Strong's for the verb was provided.
מלאכי simultaneously evokes the prophet Malachi (H4401) and the literal meaning 'my messenger' — both are valid and may be intentionally dual.

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Chose H61 'but/yet' because it introduces a contrast between the greatness of Yochanan and the status of the least in the kingdom.

קטן (consonants קטן): Candidates: H6994 'to diminish', H6995 'little finger', H6996 'small/diminutive', H6997 'Katan (name)'. Chose H6996 because 'small/least' as an adjective fits the contrast with 'greater.'
שהוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because 'whoever he [is]' uses the pronoun as a copula.

טבול (consonants טבול): H2871 'dyed/turban'. The consonants טבל relate to 'dipping/immersing' (cf. H2881 טבל 'to dip'). Here טבול appears to function as an epithet 'the Immerser/Baptizer,' derived from the root טבל. H2871 is the closest match though its primary gloss is 'turban (dyed)' — the root meaning of immersion/dyeing is shared.
שמים (consonants שמים): Candidates: H8064 'sky/heaven', H4325 'water', H3220 'sea'. Chose H8064 because 'kingdom of heaven' is a coherent and well-attested phrase.
textual_notes: מא<ה appears to contain a corrupted or damaged consonant (<). It likely reads מאשה 'from a woman' (אשה H802), describing those born of women.
טבול is glossed as 'turban/dyed' (H2871) but functions here as an epithet from the root טבל 'to dip/immerse.' This is a denominative use not fully captured by the single Strong's entry provided.

translation_notes: העם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'people/tribe', H5972 'people (Aramaic)', H5973 'with', H5974 'with (Aramaic)'. Chose H5971 because 'all the people' with the article makes natural sense as a collective noun.
הם (consonants הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because 'they were immersed' is the coherent subject-verb pairing.
שזה (consonants זה): H2088 'this'. With the relative prefix ש-, it reads 'that this' or 'who this,' functioning as a relative clause marker.
textual_notes: והעולמיים is a later Hebrew formation not found in biblical Strong's. It derives from עולם (H5769) with an adjectival suffix, meaning 'worldly ones' or 'people of the world' — likely referring to common people or those engaged with worldly affairs (possibly tax collectors or similar).
נטבלים and בטבילת are derived from the root טבל 'to dip/immerse' in a nithpael/hitpael form. No Strong's numbers are provided but the root is H2881.

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Chose H61 'but/yet' again as it introduces a contrast between the people who accepted immersion and the Pharisees who rejected it.

הדת (consonants דת): Candidates: H1881 'royal edict/statute', H1882 same. Chose H1881 because 'wise ones of the law/statute' describes legal experts, fitting the context of religious authority figures.
textual_notes: מבזים is a piel participle from בזה 'to despise/scorn' — not listed in candidates but the root is H959. The form indicates ongoing or characteristic action of despising.
עצת is the construct form of עצה 'counsel/plan' (H6098), not listed in candidates. 'The counsel of YHWH' refers to God's purpose or plan.
מיוחנן with the מ prefix could mean 'from Yochanan' or 'by Yochanan' — both are valid. 'By Yochanan' (agent) fits the passive verb נטבלים better.

translation_notes: לכן (consonants כן): Candidates: H3651 'thus/therefore', H3652 'so', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 because ל + כן forms the standard conjunction 'therefore,' which logically connects the preceding rejection to the following parable.

הדור (consonants דור): Candidates: H1752 'to gyrate', H1753 'to reside', H1754 'circle/ball', H1755 'generation/age', H1756 'Dor (place)'. Chose H1755 because 'this generation' is the coherent reading with the demonstrative זה.
textual_notes: נאמר could be parsed as 1cp imperfect 'shall we say' or as niphal 'shall it be said.' Both work; the 1cp reading is slightly more natural as a rhetorical self-address.
נמשלים is a niphal participle from משל 'to compare/liken' (H4911), meaning 'are compared/likened.'

translation_notes: הם (consonants הם): Chose H1992 'they' as the subject of the comparison.

ערב (consonants ערב): Candidates: H6148 'to intermix/barter/pledge', H6149 'to be agreeable/pleasing', H6150 'to grow dusky', H6151 'to commingle', H6152 'Arabia', H6153 'dusk'. Chose H6149 because 'it was not pleasing to you' perfectly describes the children's complaint that their companions did not respond to the music — a natural, coherent image of unresponsiveness.
ואתם (consonants אתם): H864 'Etham (place)' is the only candidate listed, but contextually this is clearly the 2mp pronoun 'you' (אתם). The lexicon candidates are incomplete.
textual_notes: ב<וק appears to have a damaged/uncertain consonant. It likely reads בשוק 'in the market/marketplace' (שוק H7784).
ניגון is not listed in Strong's candidates but derives from the root נגן 'to play music' (H5059). It means 'melody/music/playing.'
שרנו could be from שיר 'to sing' (H7891) — 'we sang' — which fits the context of children playing music and singing.
The phrase ולא ערב לכם is unusual. Instead of the expected 'you did not dance,' this text reads 'it was not pleasing to you,' which may represent a different textual tradition.

translation_notes: כאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'step'. Chose H834 because כ + אשר forms 'as when/just as,' introducing a temporal clause.

לחם (consonants לחם): Candidates: H3898 'to consume/battle', H3899 'bread/food', H3900 'bread (Aramaic)', H3901 'battle'. Chose H3899 because 'not eating bread' describes abstinence from food, a coherent image of asceticism.
שהוא (consonants הוא): Chose H1931 'he' because 'that he [is] demonized' provides the subject for the accusation.
textual_notes: משוטן is a later Hebrew form meaning 'demonized/possessed by Satan/a demon,' derived from שטן (H7854 'adversary/Satan'). The מ- prefix with the passive/reflexive pattern indicates a state: 'one who has been made subject to a שטן.' No Strong's number was provided in candidates.
טבול as 'Immerser' — see note in section 3 about this epithet.

translation_notes: בן (consonants בן): Candidates: H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 because 'son of the human' is the well-known Hebraic idiom for a human being or the specific title 'Son of Man.'

האדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to flush/turn rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/gem'. Chose H120 for both occurrences — first as 'the human' in 'son of the human,' second as 'the man/this person' in the accusation.
הנה (consonants הנה): Chose H2009 'lo/behold' as it introduces the accusatory exclamation.
textual_notes: מחריב derives from the root חרב which can mean 'to destroy/lay waste' (H2717) or 'to dry up.' In context, as an accusation paired with eating and drinking, it likely means 'glutton/one who destroys (food)' — i.e., a voracious eater. This is an unusual word choice compared to expected forms.
ו]אוהב[ has brackets in the source text, indicating the scribe marked this as uncertain or a correction. It appears to be from אהב 'to love' (H157) — 'and a lover/friend of.'
העולמיים — same later Hebrew formation as in section 4, meaning 'worldly people' or 'people of the world,' likely parallel to 'sinners' in the following word.

translation_notes: והצדקה (consonants צדקה): Candidates: H6665 'beneficence', H6666 'rightness/righteousness/justice/virtue'. Chose H6666 because 'righteousness/justice' being 'justified by its children' produces a coherent proverbial statement about vindication through results.

בעד (consonants בעד): Candidates: H1157 'on behalf of/for/by', plus עד candidates H5703-H5708. Chose H1157 because 'justified on behalf of / by means of its children' makes sense — righteousness is proved right through its children/outcomes.
textual_notes: נצטדקה is a hitpael/nitpael form of צדק 'to be righteous/justified' — a reflexive-passive meaning 'was justified/vindicated itself.' This rare intensive form emphasizes the self-evident nature of the vindication.

בניו has a masculine 3rd person suffix ('his/its sons'), but צדקה is grammatically feminine. This may indicate that the suffix refers loosely to the concept ('its children') or reflects a scribal convention. Some traditions read 'her children' for wisdom/righteousness personified as female.
צדקה here may be functioning as a stand-in for 'wisdom' (חכמה), as parallel traditions of this saying use 'wisdom' in this position. However, the consonants clearly read צדקה 'righteousness.'

translation_notes: אחד (H258 vs H259): H258 = 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 = 'one/first'. In context 'one from the Pharisees' is a natural count, so H259 'one'.

חלה (H2470 vs H2471): H2470 in piel = 'to entreat, beseech (the face of someone)', H2471 = 'a cake'. With פניו 'his face' following, the idiom חלה פני = 'entreated his face' is coherent. A cake doesn't fit the syntax. Chose H2470.
וכאשר: אשר candidates — H834 'when/that' forms the conjunction כאשר 'when'. All other candidates (happiness, step, proper nouns) don't form this conjunction. Chose H834.
בבית: H1004 'house' fits perfectly in 'in the house of the Pharisee'. H1006 is a place name, H3487 is an Aramaic object marker. Chose H1004.
והנה: H2009 'lo!/behold' fits as a narrative interjection introducing a new character. H2007 'themselves' and H2008 'hither' don't fit the syntax. H5089 'lamentation' doesn't match. Chose H2009.
בעיר: H5892 'city' vs H1165 'cattle' vs others. 'Was in the city' is coherent. 'Was in cattle' is not. Chose H5892.
משיח: H4899 'anointed/Messiah' vs H7878-H7880 (ponder/shrub). As a title following the name Yeshua, 'the Anointed' is the natural reading. Chose H4899.
לשם: H8033 'there' with ל prefix = 'to there'. H3958 'a gem' and H3959 'Leshem (place)' don't fit narratively — she came to the location. Chose H8033.

ממשיחה: The candidates H7881 'devotion/reflection' and H7882 'pitfall' don't fit a physical object being carried in a flask. The consonants מ+משיחה suggest 'of ointment/anointing-oil' (from root משח, to anoint). The lexicon candidates don't perfectly match but the root meaning 'anointing substance' is the only coherent reading for what's inside a flask.
textual_notes: קאפסא appears to be a loanword (possibly from Greek kapsa or Latin capsa, meaning a box/flask/vessel). No Strong's number available.
ממשיחה: The provided candidates (H7881, H7882) don't match well. The word likely derives from the root משח (to anoint), meaning 'anointing-oil/ointment'. The מ prefix here is 'of/from'.

translation_notes: משיח (both occurrences): H4899 'Anointed/Messiah' vs H7878-H7880. As a title following 'Yeshua', the anointed one is the clear reading. Chose H4899.
עם (all three occurrences): H5973 'with' vs H5971 'a people'. The preposition 'with' fits all three contexts: 'with tears', 'with hair', 'with ointment'. Chose H5973.
ואחר: H310 'after' vs H312 'other/next' vs H309 'to loiter'. As a temporal transition 'and after [that]', H310 is the natural reading. Chose H310.
שער: H8177 'hair' vs H8179 'gate' vs others. Following עם and preceding ראשה 'her head', 'hair of her head' produces a perfectly coherent image of drying feet with hair. Chose H8177.
ראשה: H7222 'the head' vs H7221 'a beginning'. With possessive suffix, 'her head' is the natural reading alongside 'hair of'. Chose H7222.
הרגלים: H7274 is listed as 'Rogelim' (a place name), but the consonants רגלים are clearly the plural of רגל 'foot'. The article ה confirms 'the feet'. Using as common noun 'the feet'.
textual_notes: רגלי (H7273) is listed as 'footman/soldier' but the consonants רגלי are the construct plural of רגל (foot), meaning 'feet of'. The Strong's number doesn't perfectly match the usage here.
משיחה: Provided candidates H7881/H7882 don't match. This word likely derives from root משח (anoint), meaning 'ointment/anointing-oil'.
מרגליית: No Strong's candidates provided. Likely from מרגלית (pearl/precious thing), a loanword. The word modifies the ointment as 'precious' or 'pearl-quality'.

translation_notes: ראה: H7200 'to see' fits perfectly — the Pharisee 'saw this'. Other candidates (vulture, seer as noun) don't fit as the main verb. Chose H7200.
זה (first): H2088 'this' as demonstrative pronoun, object of ראה. A sheep (H2089) makes no sense here. Chose H2088.
