רוח (second occurrence): Same candidates as above. Here used as 'spirit' in the sense of disposition or animating force — H7307.
textual_notes: ש״ appears to be an abbreviation (with gershayim) for the relative particle ש 'that'. ל״א+כול appears to be an abbreviated/scribal form for לאכול 'to eat'.
חזר is not among provided candidates — it is a post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew verb meaning 'returned'. This may indicate the manuscript's late linguistic register.

אתם: The only candidate H864 'Etham (place name)' does not fit; this is clearly the 2nd person plural pronoun 'you' (standard Hebrew אתם), which should map to a pronoun entry not provided in the candidate list.
ומיד could be parsed as ו + מיד 'and immediately' (adverbial use of 'from hand') or ו + מ + יד 'and from [the] hand'. The adverbial sense is standard in later Hebrew and fits the narrative flow.

translation_notes: ואמה (consonants א-מ-ה): Candidates: H519 'maidservant', H520 'cubit/mother-unit', H522 'Ammah (place)'. Following 'and her father' — the parallel demands 'and her mother'. The consonants אמה with possessive suffix ה can be read as אמה 'her mother' (from אם with feminine suffix). H519 'maidservant' would be awkward after 'her father'; the natural pairing is father and mother.

וצום: The candidate list offers H6684 'to fast' and H6685 'a fast' for צום. However, in context this reads as ו + צו + ם = 'and commanded them' (from צוה with 3mp suffix). The form ויצום would be more standard, but this manuscript appears to use abbreviated/later forms. The fasting reading makes no contextual sense here — Yeshua is giving them an instruction.
אדם (consonants א-ד-ם): Candidates include H119-H124. As 'any man/person' — H120 'human being' fits.
בן (consonants ב-ן): Candidates: H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'son'. In 'son of the man' — H1121.
האדם (consonants א-ד-ם with ה): H120 'human being' with definite article. 'The man/humanity' — forming the title 'Son of Man'.
לא (consonants ל-א): H3808 'not' — standard negation before 'came'.
לאבד (consonants א-ב-ד): Candidates: H6 'to perish/destroy', H7 (Aramaic same), H8 'destruction'. With ל prefix as infinitive 'to destroy' — H6.

אלא: H414 'Ela (name)' is the only candidate, but contextually this is clearly the conjunction אלא 'but rather' — a standard Mishnaic/post-biblical Hebrew conjunction not in the Strong's biblical lexicon.

במגדול: Candidates: H4024 'Migdol (place in Egypt)', H1419 'great'. The word מגדול can also mean 'tower/fortified place' and by extension 'village/town'. With ב prefix and אחר 'another' following, 'in another village/town' is the natural reading.
אחר (consonants א-ח-ר): Candidates: H309 'to delay', H310 'after', H312 'other/another'. Modifying 'village' — H312 'another' is correct.
textual_notes: ואביה: The candidate H29 'Abijah (proper name)' shares these consonants, but in context (paired with 'and her mother'), this is clearly אב + י + ה 'her father' with conjunction ו.
וצום is ambiguous between 'and commanded them' (from צוה) and 'and fasted' (from צום H6684). The following clause 'that they not tell' requires a verb of commanding, not fasting.
ש״לא, א״ת, ה״עשוי all contain abbreviation marks (gershayim ״), indicating scribal shorthand. ש״לא = שלא 'that not'; א״ת = את (object marker); ה״עשוי = העשוי 'what was done'.
לשץ ם is unclear — possibly a damaged or abbreviated form. It likely represents לשום אדם 'to any man' or a similar phrase. The ץ may be a scribal error or abbreviation.
The brackets ] [ in the text appear to indicate a lacuna or editorial gap in the manuscript.
מ<ם has a damaged consonant (<); likely משם 'from there'.

במגדול could be read as 'in Migdol' (the Egyptian place name H4024) or as 'in a tower/village'. Given the narrative of traveling to 'another' location, a generic 'village/town' reading is more coherent than a specific Egyptian location.

translation_notes: קרא (QR'): Candidates: H7121 'to call out/summon', H7122 'to encounter', H7124 'partridge'. Context is summoning disciples, so H7121 'called/summoned' fits perfectly.
משיח (MSHYCH): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder/utter', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'shrub'. Following the proper name Yeshua, this is clearly a title — H4899 'Anointed One'.
עשר ('SR): Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6240 '-teen (in combination)'. Preceded by 'the two' (ה2נים), this forms 'twelve' — H6240 is the combining form.
ה2נים: The 2 likely represents שנ (two), reading השנים — 'the two'. Combined with עשר = twelve.
ה2דים: The 2 likely represents שד (demon), reading השדים — 'the demons'. Context of power over spiritual forces and healing supports this.
textual_notes: ה2נים and ה2דים use a numeral abbreviation (2) whose expansion is inferred from context. ה2נים likely = השנים (the two), and ה2דים likely = השדים (the demons). The use of '2' as an abbreviation for שנ/שד is unusual and could theoretically represent other words.
יכול״ת (with abbreviation marks) appears to be יכולת 'ability/capability' — a noun form from the root יכל. This is not a standard Strong's entry but is well-attested in later Hebrew.

translation_notes: ושלחם: Root שלח 'to send' with vav-consecutive and 3ms suffix on the object (them). The candidate לחם (H3898 'to fight', H3899 'bread') shares some consonants but the leading ו+ש clearly marks this as ושלחם from שלח 'and he sent them'.
מלכות: Candidates: H4438 'kingdom/dominion', H3575 'Cuth/Cuthah'. In context of preaching a divine reign, H4438 is the natural reading.
textual_notes: לדרוש: Root דרש 'to seek, inquire, expound'. No Strong's candidates were provided but the root is unambiguous — H1875. The infinitive construct with ל prefix means 'to seek/proclaim'.

translation_notes: ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. With vav-consecutive and context of giving instructions, H559 'and he said' is clear.
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. After 'you shall not carry' — an object is expected, so H1697 'a thing' fits.

מעות: The consonants מעות could derive from עות (H5790 'to hasten', H5791 'to wrest') but in context of items not to carry, this is the well-known post-biblical Hebrew word for 'coins/money' (from the root מעה). No exact Strong's match; closest contextual meaning is 'money/coins'.
ואם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Following ואב 'and father', H517 'and mother' creates the natural pair.
הנערה: Candidates: H5291 'a girl', H5292 'Naarah (proper name)'. Context suggests a narrative about a girl, H5291.
ישנה: H3466 'Jeshanah' (a place). But the consonants also support ישנה from ישן 'old/existing/sleeping'. Context is unclear; possibly 'there is [already there]' or 'sleeping'.
textual_notes: This section appears to contain two distinct passages merged or a textual corruption. The first part (instructions about not carrying items) is coherent. The second part beginning with 'and father and mother the girl...' followed by fragmentary elements (ה ־ ה תה ־ א) and repeated verb forms (קראה/קראתה, יצאה/יצאתה) is extremely difficult. The repeated pairs of verb forms (3fs perfect with and without ה suffix) suggest a grammatical paradigm or gloss rather than narrative text.

ל״ח״ם and א״ב״ן use abbreviation marks (geresh/double-geresh) suggesting these are treated as abbreviations or marked words. ל״ח״ם = לחם 'bread' (H3899), א״ב״ן = אבן 'stone' — in context 'stone' likely means money/coins (as small stones were used as weights/currency markers).
The fragment ה ־ ה תה ־ א is extremely obscure. It may represent a damaged portion, a marginal notation, or abbreviations. No confident translation is possible for this fragment.

The section from ואב onward may be a different text entirely (possibly a narrative about a girl being called/going out, perhaps related to the raising of Jairus's daughter or another account). The verb paradigm pairs (קראה/קראתה and יצאה/יצאתה) could be scribal notes showing alternative conjugation forms.

translation_notes: ובאי: Candidates include H335 'where?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. With the prefix ו + ב, and followed by זה בית, the reading 'and in which(ever)' using H335 ('where? / which?') produces the coherent instruction: 'and in whichever house you enter'.
זה: H2088 'this/that' vs H2089 'a sheep' vs H2090 'this/that'. As a demonstrative modifying בית, H2088 is the clear choice.
בית: H1004 'house' vs H1006 'Bajith (place)' vs H3487 'object marker'. As the object entered and dwelt in, 'house' is obvious.
שם: H8033 'there' vs H8034 'name' vs H8035 'Shem' vs H8036 'name'. Following 'that you enter' and preceding 'you shall remain', 'there' (H8033) is the coherent adverb.
textual_notes: ומ<ם contains a damaged character (marked '<'). The likely reading is ומשם 'and from there'.

translation_notes: העיר: Candidates H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'young donkey'. After 'go out from that the ___', 'city' is the only coherent reading — one exits a city, not a donkey or angel.
ועפר: Candidates H6080 'to be dust', H6081 'Epher (name)', H6082 'fawn', H6083 'dust/earth'. Before 'your feet', 'dust' (H6083) produces the coherent image of shaking dust off one's feet.
לעדות: H5715 'testimony'. With ל- prefix = 'for testimony'. Straightforward.
בכל: H3605 'the whole / all / every' vs H3606 (Aramaic equivalent). Hebrew context favors H3605.
מקום: H4725 'a place/standing' vs H6965 'to rise'. With the prefix ב- and preceded by כל, 'in every place' (H4725) is the natural reading.
textual_notes: מ<ם contains a damaged character. Likely reads משם 'from there'.
The apostrophe character (') between תחפשו and הבתים indicates damaged or missing text. There may be a missing preposition or particle.
תחפשו could mean 'you shall search/seek out' or 'you shall disguise yourselves'. In context of going through houses preaching and healing, 'search through' is the more coherent reading.

translation_notes: אדון: H113 'sovereign/controller' vs H114 'Addon (name)'. Describing Herod's title alongside 'tetrarch', H113 'lord/ruler' is the coherent reading.
שמע: H8085 'to hear' vs H8086 (Aramaic 'to hear') vs H8087-8090 (names/nouns). As a verb ('Herod heard all the things'), H8085 is correct.
והיה: H1961 'to exist/be/become' vs H1962 'ruin' vs H3050 'Yah'. 'And it was to him in doubt' — H1961 is the clear verbal reading.

בספק: H5606 'to clap hands/chastisement' vs H5607 'chastisement; also satiety'. The word ספק in later Hebrew means 'doubt'. In context ('it was to him in doubt because people were saying...'), doubt/perplexity is the coherent image. Neither 'clapping' nor 'satiety' fits.
שיש: H7893 'marble' vs H3426 'there is/are'. The reading ש + יש = 'that there are (those saying)' produces the coherent clause. 'That marble saying' is nonsensical.
הוא: H1931 'he/it' as an emphatic pronoun. 'Yochanan — he [is the one] who returned alive.' Clear usage.
חי: H2416 'alive' vs H2417 (Aramaic 'alive'). Hebrew context, H2416.
textual_notes: בספק: The Strong's candidates (H5606/H5607) do not directly offer 'doubt', but ספק in post-biblical Hebrew means 'doubt/uncertainty'. This may reflect a later Hebrew stratum in the manuscript.
טטרקא is a transliteration of the Greek/Latin 'tetrarch' and has no Strong's entry.

translation_notes: אליהו: H453 is listed as 'Elihu', but the consonants אליהו equally support the prophet Elijah (אֵלִיָּהוּ). In context — speculation about who a miracle-worker might be — Elijah the prophet is the coherent identification, not Job's friend Elihu.
שאחד: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts' vs H259 'one/united/first'. After ש ('that'), 'that one of' (H259) produces the coherent clause.

מישישי: H3454 'Jeshishai, an Israelite'. However, the consonants can also be parsed as מ + ישישי = 'from the old/aged ones of', from ישיש (an aged person). Context ('one of the ancient prophets') demands the common noun reading, not a proper name.
הוא (both occurrences): H1931 emphatic pronoun 'he' — functioning as a copula in both clauses.
textual_notes: אליהו: The Strong's entry provided (H453) is for Elihu (Job's friend and other Israelites), but these same consonants represent the prophet Elijah. The context (speculation about prophetic figures returning) strongly points to Elijah.

מישישי: Could be parsed as the proper name Jeshishai (H3454) or as 'from the elders/ancient ones of'. The latter reading produces the coherent phrase 'one of the ancient prophets' and is clearly preferable.

translation_notes: ואמר: H559 'to say' vs H560 (Aramaic), H561-562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. As a verb opening reported speech ('And Herod said'), H559 is the clear choice.
אני: H589 'I' vs H590 'a ship/fleet'. Herod speaking about himself: 'I am the one who commanded' — H589.

לשחוט: The candidates listed under חוט are H2338 'to string together' and H2339 'a string/measuring tape'. However, the consonants לשחוט clearly represent the infinitive of שחט (H7819, 'to slaughter/kill'). The ש is part of the root, not a prefix. 'To slaughter Yochanan' is the only coherent reading.
זה: H2088 'this/that' vs H2089 'a sheep'. In the question 'who is he this?', H2088 demonstrative pronoun is correct.
אלו: H431 'lo!/these' vs H432 'if/nay'. Modifying דברים ('things'), 'these' (H431, functioning as a demonstrative) is the natural reading.
ורצה: H7521 'to be pleased with / to desire / to satisfy a debt'. 'He desired to see Yeshua' — the meaning 'desired/wished' fits perfectly.
משיח: H4899 'anointed/Messiah' vs H7878-7880 (ponder/shrub). As a title following Yeshua, 'Messiah/Anointed One' (H4899) is the clear reading.
textual_notes: לשחוט: The Strong's candidates provided (H2338/H2339 for חוט) do not match. The word is the infinitive of שחט 'to slaughter' (H7819), where the ש belongs to the root. This is unambiguous in context.
אלו as 'these' is post-biblical Hebrew usage. In biblical Hebrew, אלה would be expected. This suggests a later Hebrew stratum.
The placement of משיח ('Messiah') after ישוע could be the narrator's title for Yeshua rather than part of Herod's speech.

translation_notes: להגיד: The candidate H1517 (גיד = 'tendon') shares consonants but this is clearly the hiphil infinitive of נגד 'to tell/declare'. 'To declare to Yeshua all the things' is coherent; 'to tendon to Yeshua' is not.
שעשו: H6215 'Esav/Esau'. However, this is clearly the relative pronoun ש + the verb עשו (3mp perfect of עשה, 'they did'). 'All the things that they did' is the coherent reading, not 'that Esau'.
לקח: H3947 'to take' vs H3948 'instruction/something received'. As a verb with 'them' as object, 'took' (H3947) is correct.
במקום: H4725 'a place' vs H6965 'to rise'. With ב- prefix and followed by 'one called Beit Tzaidah', 'in a place' is the clear reading.
אחד: H258 'to unify' vs H259 'one/a certain'. Modifying מקום ('place'), 'one/a certain place' uses H259.
משיח: H4899 'Messiah/Anointed One' vs H7878-7880 (shrub/pondering). As a title following Yeshua, H4899 is unambiguous.
בית: H1004 'house' vs H1006 'Bajith' vs H3487 'object marker'. As the first element of a place name (Beit Tzaidah), H1004 'house' is correct.
צידה: H6720 'food/provision'. The place name Beit Tzaidah means 'House of Provision/Food' (= Bethsaida).
textual_notes: שעשו: The only Strong's candidate listed is H6215 (Esau), but the consonants are identical to the 3mp perfect of עשה 'to do/make'. Context decisively favors the verb.
צידה could also be related to ציד 'hunting/fishing', which would give 'House of Fishing' — an equally attested etymology for Bethsaida.

translation_notes: והדבר (דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture', H1907 'vizier'. With the article ה and demonstrative ההוא following, this is a noun — 'the matter/word that.' Chose H1697.
ההוא (הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/that', H1932 same Aramaic, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. With the article prefix ה, this is the demonstrative 'that.' Chose H1931.

כאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. With prefix כ, כאשר = 'as/when' — standard relative conjunction. Chose H834.

ומדבר (דבר/מדבר): Candidates: H4057 'desert/speech', H1696 'to speak'. In context 'and-speaking with-them about the kingdom,' the participle form of H1696 (speaking) fits perfectly. H4057 'desert' would be incoherent here. Chose H1696 as participial form.

ומרפא (רפא): Candidates: H4832 'curative/medicine', H7495 'to cure/heal', H7496 'ghost', H7497 'giant'. In context of healing the sick, the participial form of H7495 'healing' is the natural reading. Chose H7495.
עיר: Candidates: H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'young ass'. In context of receiving/not receiving from a place, 'city' is the coherent reading. Chose H5892.

עפר: Candidates: H6080 'to be dust', H6081 'Epher (name)', H6082 'a fawn', H6083 'dust'. In the context of shaking off from a city, 'dust' produces the clearest image — shaking dust off one's feet. Chose H6083.
לבוש: Candidates: H3830 'garment', H3831 same, H954 'to be ashamed'. In context alongside לבושים (garments), clothing is the coherent reading. Chose H3830.
textual_notes: This section appears to be a composite or fragmentary passage — multiple phrases seem to be variant readings or editorial notes stacked together (שלאיקבלו / שיקבלו / שלא יקבלו appear to be three attempts at the same phrase: 'that they do not receive'). The words יהיה / יהיו / לבוש ם / לבושים / תעמדו similarly seem like marginal variants or scribal alternatives rather than continuous prose.

תחפצו could be from חפץ H2654 'to delight/desire' or potentially a form meaning 'to shake off.' The context of dust from a city suggests a shaking-off gesture, but the consonants most naturally map to חפץ 'desire.' This remains genuinely ambiguous.
ידעשהו appears to be a compound: ידע (to know) + שהו (that-him/it), possibly 'knew it' or 'made it known.' No Strong's entry was provided; parsed as ידע (H3045) + pronominal suffix.

translation_notes: עשר: Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6236 'ten (Aramaic)', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth', H6240 'teen (in combination)'. With ה<נים preceding (likely שנים = two), this forms 'twelve' — שנים עשר. Chose H6240 for the combinatory '-teen' sense, though H6235 also works.
זה (first): Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Following העם, 'this people' is the coherent reading. H2089 'sheep' would be bizarre after 'the people.' Chose H2088.
למקום: Candidates: H4725 'a place/standing', H6965 'to rise'. With prefix ל and following demonstrative זה, 'to [this] place' is clear. Chose H4725.
הזה: Candidates: H1957 'to dream', H2088 'this'. Following המקום, 'this place' is the standard demonstrative construction. 'To dream' makes no sense here. Chose H2088.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 same Aramaic, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Functions as copula: 'it [is] desolate.' Chose H1931.

חרב: Candidates: H2717 'to parch/desolate', H2718 'to demolish', H2719 'sword', H2720 'parched/ruined', H2721 'drought/desolation', H2722 'Horeb'. As predicate adjective after הוא, H2720 'desolate/ruined' fits perfectly — describing a barren place with no food. Chose H2720.
textual_notes: ה<נים — the text has a damaged/unclear character marked with <. In context of 'the ___ ten emissaries,' this is almost certainly שנים (two), yielding 'the twelve emissaries.' The damaged letter is likely ש.
<יאכלו — also has a damaged character. Most likely שיאכלו ('that they will eat') or simply יאכלו ('they will eat'). The ש prefix would be the relative 'that.'
למגדליהם — could be from מגדל (H4026) 'tower' but in later Hebrew usage מגדל could refer to a village/hamlet. The pairing with 'their cities' suggests smaller settlements.

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same Aramaic, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. As a verb preceding direct speech, H559 'said' is the clear choice. Chose H559.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'them'. As preposition ל + pronoun הם = 'to them,' this is standard. Chose H1992.
אין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/not', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. In context 'there is not to us except,' H369 is the natural negative existential. Chose H369.
לבד: Candidates from בד: H905 'separation/alone', H906 'linen', H907 'a lie'. With prefix ל, לבד = 'alone/only/except' — standard usage. Chose H905.
ושני: Candidates: H2059 'Vashni (name)', H8145 'second/two', H5204 'lamentation'. Before דגים (fish), 'two' is the only coherent reading. Chose H8145.
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Before מאכל (food), 'thing of food' = something to eat. Chose H1697.
מאכל: Candidates: H3978 'food/eatable', H398 'to eat', H400 'food'. As a noun following דבר, H3978 'food' is the direct reading. Chose H3978.
הזה: Candidates: H1957 'to dream', H2088 'this'. After העם, 'this people' is standard. Chose H2088.
textual_notes: חמ<ה — damaged character. In context before לחמים (loaves) and with ושני דגים (and two fish), this is almost certainly חמשה (five), matching the well-known narrative of five loaves and two fish.

translation_notes: והם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. As subject pronoun opening a clause about quantity, 'they' is the only coherent reading. Chose H1992.
כמו: H3644 'as/about/thus'. Before a number (five thousand), 'about' fits perfectly — an approximation. Chose H3644.

עשו: Candidate listed: H6215 'Esau'. However, in context 'Yeshua said to his disciples _____ that they sit,' this must be the imperative plural of עשה (H6213) 'do/make.' The consonants עשו can be the imperative of עשה. The listing of H6215 'Esau' is clearly wrong for this context. Chose H6213.
העם: Candidates: H5971 'people', H5973 'with'. As direct object of 'make sit,' 'the people' is correct. Chose H5971.
textual_notes: חמ<ים and לחמ<ים — both have damaged characters. Given the context of organizing groups, these are almost certainly חמשים (fifties). The ל prefix on the second instance creates a distributive: 'fifties by fifties' = in groups of fifty.
עשו — the only Strong's candidate provided is H6215 'Esau,' but the context absolutely demands the imperative of עשה (H6213) 'to do/make.' The consonants are identical.

translation_notes: כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. With prefix ו and followed by עשו (they did), 'and so' is the natural reading. Chose H3651.
עשו: Candidate listed: H6215 'Esau'. As in section 4, this is clearly the 3rd person plural perfect of עשה (H6213) 'to do.' 'And so they did' is coherent; 'and so Esau' is not. Chose H6213.
לקח: Candidates: H3947 'to take', H3948 'instruction'. As a verb following a subject (Yeshua), 'took' is the natural reading. Chose H3947.
ושני (both occurrences): Candidates: H2059 'Vashni', H8145 'two/second', H5204 'lamentation'. Before דגים/הדגים (fish), 'two' is the only coherent reading. Chose H8145.

ובירך: Candidate listed: H3409 'thigh' (ירך). However, the consonants ו-ב-י-ר-ך clearly parse as ו + בירך, the piel of ברך (H1288) 'to bless.' The ב is part of the root, not a prefix. 'And blessed them' fits the context of a meal blessing. Chose H1288.
ובצע: Candidates: H1214 'to cut off/break/finish', H1215 'plunder/gain'. In context of bread, H1214 'to break' (bread) produces a natural image — breaking bread before distributing it. Chose H1214.
הפת: Candidates: H6595 'a bit/morsel (of bread)', H6596 'a hole/hinge'. After 'broke,' H6595 'the bread/morsel' is the coherent reading. Chose H6595.

וצום: Candidates: H6684 'to fast', H6685 'a fast'. However, in context 'and _____ them that they set it before the people,' this must be from צוה (H6680) 'to command' with 3mp suffix — וצום = 'and he commanded them.' The consonants support this reading. Chose H6680.
ההוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/that'. As a demonstrative following העם, 'that people' is standard. Chose H1931.
textual_notes: החמ<ה — damaged character, almost certainly חמשה (five), consistent with previous sections.
ל<מים — damaged character. Most likely לשמים (to the heavens/sky), from שמים H8064. The act of looking upward before a blessing is a coherent physical image.
וצום — the candidates listed are H6684/H6685 (fast/fasting), but the context demands צוה (H6680, to command) with suffix ם. The final מ is the 3mp object suffix, not part of the root.
שיניחוהו — parsed as ש + יניחו + הו = 'that they would place/set it.' From נוח/ינח (H3240) in hiphil 'to cause to rest/set down.'

translation_notes: ושבעו: Candidate listed: H1159 'a request' (בעו). However, the full consonants שבעו clearly parse as the 3mp perfect of שבע (H7646) 'to be satisfied/sated.' After 'they ate,' 'they were satisfied' is the natural continuation. Chose H7646.
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. As a copula verb 'was,' H1961 is the clear reading. Chose H1961.

מלאות: Candidates listed from אות: H225 'to assent', H226 'a sign.' However, מלאות is the feminine plural of מלא (H4392) 'full.' The אות ending is the feminine plural morpheme, not a separate root. Chose H4392.
textual_notes: קופות — no Strong's candidates were provided. This is a post-biblical Hebrew word for 'baskets' (related to קופה). It does not appear in the classical Strong's lexicon, suggesting this text uses later Hebrew vocabulary.

translation_notes: היה: Candidates: H1961 'to be', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. As 'Yeshua was alone,' H1961 is clear. Chose H1961.

שאלם: Candidates listed from אלם: H481 'to be tongue-tied', H482 'silence', H483 'speechless'. However, the full consonants שאלם parse as שאל (H7592 'to ask') + suffix ם (them) = 'he asked them.' The listed candidates only address the אלם portion, missing that ש is part of the root שאל. Chose H7592.
העם: Candidates: H5971 'people', H5973 'with'. As subject of 'saying,' 'the people' is correct. Chose H5971.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. In the question 'who am I?', H589 'I' is the only sensible reading. Chose H589.
textual_notes: ונעשה — could be parsed as niphal of עשה (H6213) 'and it came about/happened' or as 'and we will do.' The 3ms narrative context (followed by שישוע היה) strongly supports the impersonal niphal: 'and it happened that...'

translation_notes: וענו: Candidate listed: H6035 'meek/humble' (ענו as adjective). However, in context before ואמרו ('and said'), this is clearly the 3mp perfect of ענה (H6030) 'to answer.' Chose H6030.

טבול: H2871 'dyed/turbaned.' The consonants טבול relate to טבל 'to dip/immerse.' As a descriptor of Yochanan, 'the immerser/baptizer' — one who dips/immerses — is the coherent reading, describing his practice of ritual immersion.
ומקצת: Candidates: H7117 'a portion/some', H7118 same Aramaic. 'And some [are] saying' fits perfectly. Chose H7117.
אליהו: H453 is listed as 'Elihu.' However, the consonants אליהו also match אליהו/Eliyahu (H452), the prophet Elijah. In context of prophetic figures, Elijah is the coherent identification.
נביא: Candidates: H5029 'prophet (Aramaic)', H5030 'prophet/inspired man'. In a Hebrew context, H5030 is appropriate. Chose H5030.

מן: Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 same Aramaic, H4482 'musical chord'. Before הראשונים ('the former ones'), 'from' is the only coherent preposition. Chose H4480.
חי: Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 same Aramaic. After 'returned,' 'alive' produces a clear image — a prophet who returned to life. Chose H2416.
textual_notes: הי״ב — this appears to be an abbreviation using the Hebrew numeral notation י״ב = 12. 'The twelve' refers to the twelve emissaries/disciples.

שחזר — parsed as ש + חזר 'that returned.' חזר is common in post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew for 'to return' but does not have a classical Strong's number, further indicating this text uses later Hebrew vocabulary.
אליהו — the Strong's candidate given is H453 'Elihu,' but the consonants are identical to Elijah (אליהו, traditionally H452). Context clearly points to the prophet Elijah.

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 Aramaic, H561 'something said', H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer'. As verb before speech, H559. Chose H559.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'them'. Preposition ל + הם = 'to them.' Chose H1992.
ואתם: Candidate listed: H864 'Etham (place)'. However, ו + אתם is clearly 'and you (plural)' from H859. The consonants match the 2mp pronoun perfectly. Chose H859.
ענה: Candidates: H6030 'to answer/respond', H6031 'to afflict', H6032 Aramaic 'to answer', H6034 'Anah (name)'. Before direct speech, 'answered' is the natural reading. Chose H6030.
שמעון: Candidates: H8095 'Shimon', H4583 'dwelling', H5771 'iniquity'. As a proper name followed by כיפא (Kepha/Peter), H8095 'Shimon' is clearly correct. Chose H8095.
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 same, H859 'you'. In the declaration 'you are,' H859 'you' is the only coherent reading. Chose H859.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/the one', H1933 'to be'. As copula/emphatic identifier 'you are [the one],' H1931 fits. Chose H1931.
אל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/Mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Before חי ('living'), 'God/Mighty One' produces the coherent theological title 'son of the living God.' Chose H410.
חי: Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 same Aramaic. As modifier of אל, 'living God' is a well-attested Hebrew expression. Chose H2416.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. In 'who am I?', H589 is obvious. Chose H589.
textual_notes: כיפא — no Strong's number provided. This is an Aramaic word meaning 'rock/stone' (כֵּיפָא), used as the epithet of Shimon (= Greek Petros/Peter). It is not in the classical Hebrew Strong's lexicon.

בדעתכם — parsed as ב + דעת + כם = 'in your knowledge/opinion/understanding.' From דעת (H1847) with 2mp suffix. This phrasing ('in your understanding') asks for their personal assessment, as distinct from public opinion.

אתה הוא ישוע — this could be parsed as 'You are he — Yeshua' (identifying him as the awaited one whose name means 'salvation') or 'You, he is Yeshua' (less natural). The former reading is more coherent.

translation_notes: צום (consonants צ-ו-מ): Candidates: H6684 'to cover over the mouth, to fast', H6685 'a fast'. In context with לבל יגידו (not to tell), the verb here functions as a command to cover the mouth—i.e., to enjoin silence, to command. H6684 chosen because the root meaning 'to cover over the mouth' fits perfectly as issuing a command of silence.

לבל (ל + בל): Candidates: H1077 'not, lest', H1078 'Bel', H1079 'the heart'. With the prefix ל and following a verb of commanding, H1077 'not/lest' produces 'so as not to'—a natural purpose clause. Chose H1077.

לשום (ל + שום): Candidates: H7760 'to put/set', H7761 same, H7762 'garlic'. Here לשום functions as 'to any' (ל + שום in the sense of 'any whatsoever'), a usage attested in later Hebrew. Chose H7760 in the broad sense of 'any/whatsoever'.
אדם: Candidates: H119 'flush/rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'red gem'. In context of 'not tell any ___', H120 'human being/person' is the natural fit.
textual_notes: צום could theoretically be parsed as 'fast' (noun), but the syntactic position before לבל יגידו strongly supports a verbal reading meaning 'commanded/charged' (from the root meaning to cover the mouth, hence to silence/command).

translation_notes: שבן (ש + בן): The ש is the relative particle 'that', and בן is H1121 'son'. Together: 'that the son of'. Chose H1121 as the context demands 'son of man' as a title.
האדם (ה + אדם): Candidates: H119-H124. With the definite article ה and following בן, 'the man/the human' (H120) produces 'Son of the Man'—a well-known Semitic title. Chose H120.

ושרי: The provided candidates are H8297 'Sarai' and H8298 'Sharay'. However, the consonants ש-ר-י naturally parse as the construct plural of שר (chief/prince/official), meaning 'chiefs of'. In context with הכהנים (the priests), 'chiefs of the priests' is the only coherent reading.
חי: Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 same in Aramaic. After ויחזור (and he will return), H2416 'alive' produces the natural image of returning to life. Chose H2416.
ביום (ב + יום): Candidates: H3117 'a day', H3118 same Aramaic. With preposition ב and followed by 'the third', H3117 'on [the] day' is standard. Chose H3117.
textual_notes: שחוייב appears to be a form meaning 'it is obligated/necessary' — possibly a passive participle from חוב/חיב (to be obligated). This is not a standard biblical Hebrew form but fits later Hebrew or a translated text.
ויקללוהו could derive from קלל (to curse/make light of/despise) or קלה (to despise). In context of rejection by religious leaders, 'despise/reject' fits well.
ישישים could be from ישיש (aged/elder) or from ישש (to be old). The meaning 'elders' fits the context of religious authority figures.
The damaged letter in ה<לישי is presumably a שׁ, giving השלישי 'the third'.

translation_notes: אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. After 'he said to all' and before 'a man desires', H518 'if' creates a conditional clause. Chose H518.
איש: Candidates: H376 'a man/person', H377 'to act manly'. As subject of חפץ, H376 'a man' is the natural reading.
חפץ: Candidates: H2654 'to incline/desire/be pleased', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire'. As a verb with איש as subject, H2654 'desires' fits.
אחרי: Candidate H317 'other' is listed, but the consonants אחרי standardly mean 'after me' (אחר + pronominal suffix י). The context 'to come after me' demands 'after me'.

כופר (כ-ו-פ-ר): The listed candidate is H6499 פר 'bullock', but the full consonants כפר point to the root כפר meaning 'to deny/cover/atone'. As a participle 'denying' with בעצמו 'himself', this produces 'denying himself'—a coherent image of self-renunciation.

ושתי: Candidates: H2060 'Vashti', H8358 'intoxication', H8359 'a fixture, the warp in weaving'. In context with וערב, H8359 'warp' pairs with 'woof/weft' to describe a cross-beam structure—the translator's rendering of a cross/stake (שתי וערב = warp and weft, crossing elements). Chose H8359.

וערב: Candidates: H6148 'to braid/intermix', H6149 'to be agreeable', H6150 'to grow dusky', H6151 'to commingle', H6152 'Arabia', H6153 'dusk'. Paired with שתי (warp), H6148 'to braid/intermix' or its nominal sense 'woof/weft' (the crossing thread) is the only coherent pairing. Chose H6148.

שלו: Candidates: H7958 'quail', H7959 'security', H7960 'fault', H7961 'tranquil/careless/his'. Here שלו functions as a possessive pronoun 'his' (של + ו), referring to his cross. Chose H7961 in the possessive sense.
textual_notes: ושתי וערב שלו is a remarkable phrase. In weaving terminology, שתי (warp) and ערב (weft) form a cross pattern. This appears to be a Hebrew translator's rendering of the concept of a cross/execution stake using the imagery of crossed beams. The bracket around יקח suggests a scribal insertion or restoration.

אחרי is listed only as H317 'other', but the standard Hebrew reading of these consonants with the yod suffix is 'after me' (preposition אחר + 1cs suffix). This is the reading that makes contextual sense.
כופר could be parsed as כ + פר (like a bull) but 'denying himself' fits the passage's logic of self-renunciation far better than 'like a bull in himself'.

translation_notes: וזה (ו + זה): Candidates: H2088 'this (demonstrative)', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this or that'. Following a conditional statement about self-denial, H2088 'this one' (pointing to the person who follows the instruction) is the natural reading.
מה: Candidates: H4100 'what?/how?', H4101 same Aramaic. As an interrogative opening a rhetorical question, H4100 is standard.
לאדם (ל + אדם): Candidates: H119-H124. With prefix ל (to/for) and in context of a universal rhetorical question about profit, H120 'a human being/person' is the natural reading.
אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if'. As a conditional particle introducing the protasis, H518 'if' is the clear choice.

כעפר (כ + עפר): Candidates: H6080 'to be dust', H6081 'Epher', H6082 'a fawn', H6083 'dust/earth'. With prefix כ (like/as), H6083 'dust' produces the vivid simile 'like dust'—heaping up silver as abundantly as dust.

כסף: Candidates: H3700 'to become pale/pine after', H3701 'silver/money', H3702 Aramaic same, H5592 'vestibule/dish', H5593 'Saph'. As the object of heaping up, H3701 'silver/money' is the obvious reading.
textual_notes: יצבור appears to be from the root צבר 'to heap up/accumulate'. Combined with כעפר כסף, the image is of accumulating silver like dust—an intensifying simile for vast wealth.

translation_notes: ודברי: The listed candidate H1704 'Dibri, an Israelite' is a proper name. However, the consonants דברי naturally parse as דבר + י (my words), the construct plural of דבר with 1cs suffix. In context following 'those who despise me and ___', 'my words' is the coherent reading.
בן: Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben', H1123 same. As a title 'son of the father', H1121 is the natural reading.
האב (ה + אב): Candidates: H1 'father', H2 same, H3 'green plant', H4 same. Following בן and with the article, 'the Father' (H1) produces the theologically coherent title 'Son of the Father'.

בידו: The listed candidate H3035 'Jiddo' is a proper name. However, the consonants בידו more naturally parse as a word that in context should mean 'in his glory/splendor'. This may be a form related to הוד (splendor) or may be ביד + ו (in his hand/power). Given the surrounding text about coming with the Father and angels, 'in his glory' or 'in his power' fits.
והאב: Same analysis as האב above — H1 'father' with conjunction and article.
textual_notes: בידו is genuinely ambiguous. It could be ב + יד + ו (in his hand/power) from יד H3027, or it could represent 'in his glory' if the scribe used an unusual form. The context of coming with the Father and angels suggests a theophanic appearance, making 'in his glory/power' the most likely intended sense.
כשיבואו could be parsed as כש + יבואו (when they come, 3mp) or כש + יבוא + ו (when he comes + and). The singular reading 'when he comes' fits better with בן האב as the subject.

The syntax is challenging: 'those who despise me and my words' could be the object of יבזם (the Son of the Father will despise them) or could be a separate clause. The reading where בן האב is the subject of יבזם is more coherent.

translation_notes: אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. As subject pronoun following ואומר (and I say), H589 'I' is the only coherent reading.
שמקצת (ש + מקצת): Candidates: H7117 'a termination/portion', H7118 same Aramaic. With relative ש prefix, 'that some of/a portion of' fits perfectly as the partitive expression.
אלו: Candidates: H431 'lo!/behold', H432 'if'. Here אלו functions as a demonstrative pronoun 'those/these' (common in later Hebrew). H431 in its demonstrative sense is the closest fit.
פה: Candidates: H6310 'mouth', H6311 'here (this place)'. After שהיום (who today), H6311 'here' produces 'who are here today'—a coherent locative expression.
מות: Candidates: H4191 'to die', H4192 title, H4193 'death (Aramaic)', H4194 'death'. As object of יטעמו (will taste), the noun H4194 'death' is required.

עד: Candidates: H5703 'perpetuity', H5704 'until/as far as', H5705 same Aramaic, H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'menstrual flux'. Before שיראו (that they see), H5704 'until' is the only coherent temporal conjunction.
מלכות: Candidates: H4438 'a rule/dominion', H3575 'Cuth'. As the object of seeing, paired with יהוה, H4438 'kingdom/dominion' is the clear reading.
יהוה: Candidates: H3068 'the self-Existent/Eternal', H3069 same. The divine name. Chose H3068.
textual_notes: אלו as a demonstrative pronoun ('those') is a later Hebrew usage not common in biblical texts. This may indicate the manuscript's linguistic register or date.

translation_notes: ושמנה: Candidates: H8083 'eight', H4487-H4490 (from מנה). With ימים following, H8083 'eight' produces 'eight days'—a standard temporal expression.
אחר: Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'after', H311 'after (Aramaic)', H312 'other/next', H313 'Acher'. Before אלה הדברים, H310 'after' creates the temporal phrase 'after these words'. Chose H310.

אלה: Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. However, the consonants אלה also represent the common demonstrative pronoun 'these' (not listed among candidates but the standard reading). In context 'these words', the demonstrative 'these' is required. Noting H426 as closest available but functioning as the demonstrative.
לקח: Candidates: H3947 'to take', H3948 'instruction'. As a verb with Yeshua as subject and persons as objects, H3947 'took' is the clear reading.

ועלה: Candidates: H5927 'to ascend', H5928 'holocaust', H5929 'leaf', H5930 'burnt offering', H5931 'pretext'. With אל ההר following, H5927 'to ascend/go up' produces 'went up to the mountain'. Chose H5927.
אל: Candidates: H408 'not', H409 same, H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H412 same, H413 'to/near'. Before ההר, H413 'to' is the directional preposition needed.
ההר: Candidates: H2022 'a mountain', H2023 'Hor'. With the article ה, H2022 'the mountain' is the natural reading.
textual_notes: אלה is listed with candidates that do not include the common demonstrative pronoun 'these'. The consonants אלה unambiguously function as 'these' in the phrase 'these words'. I have assigned H426 as the closest available Strong's number, but the intended word is the demonstrative pronoun.
כיפא has no Strong's number—this is an Aramaic name (Peter/Cephas), indicating this manuscript uses Aramaic names alongside Hebrew text.

translation_notes: לבן: Candidates: H3835 'to be/become white', H3836 'white', H3837 'Laban', H1121-H1123 (from בן, 'son'). Following ומלבושיו (and his garments), the adjective H3836 'white' describes the garments' appearance. Choosing H3836 because 'his garments white and shining' is a coherent, vivid image of transformation.
textual_notes: ונשתנו is a hitpael/nishtapel form from שנה (to change), meaning 'were changed/transformed'. The plural verb could govern both פניו and ומלבושיו together, or פניו alone with the garments described separately. The most natural reading is that both face and garments were transformed.

translation_notes: והנה (ו + הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. As a presentative particle introducing a sudden visual scene ('and behold, two men...'), H2009 is the natural reading.
שני: Candidates: H8144 'crimson', H8145 'second/double/two', H5204 'lamentation'. Before אנשים (men), H8145 'two' produces 'two men'. H8144 'crimson men' would be bizarre. Chose H8145.
והם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. As a pronoun identifying the two men, H1992 'they' is the clear reading.
משה: Candidates: H4871 'to pull out', H4872 'Mosheh/Moses', H4873 same, H4874 'a debt', H7716 'sheep'. As a proper name paired with Eliyahu, H4872 'Moses' is unambiguous.

ואליהו: Candidate H453 'Elihu'. The consonants אליהו typically represent Elijah (אליהו), though the Strong's entry given is for Elihu. In context with Moses on a mountain during a transformation scene, this is Elijah the prophet.
textual_notes: ואליהו: The Strong's candidate H453 is listed as 'Elihu' (Job's friend and others), but the consonants אליהו also represent Elijah the prophet (typically H452 in some systems). Given the pairing with Moses in a theophanic mountain scene, Elijah is the intended identification.

translation_notes: ואמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 because the context is direct speech introduction.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon (proper name)'. Chose H113 because the speaker is addressing Yeshua with a title of authority.
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because it functions as a noun ('a thing') modified by טוב.
טוב: Candidates: H2895 'to be good', H2896 'good (adj.)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness (noun)'. Chose H2896 because it serves as an adjective modifying דבר.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as a copular pronoun completing 'a good thing [it is]'.
פה: Candidates: H6310 'mouth', H6311 'here'. Chose H6311 because making tents 'here' fits the spatial context of being at a location.

שלשה: The candidates listed (H8030 Shilshah, H8031 Shalishah, H7716 sheep) do not match; this is clearly the number 'three' (שלשה from שלוש), a standard Hebrew numeral not always separately listed. Context of 'three tents' confirms.
אהלים: H174 lists 'aloe wood sticks' but the consonants אהלים equally represent the plural of אהל (H168) 'tent/tabernacle'. Context of making shelters for three people demands 'tents'.
ומדבר: Candidates: H4057 'wilderness/speech', or from דבר H1696 'to speak'. With prefix ו + participle מדבר, 'and speaking' fits the narrative description of ongoing action.
אומר: H201 lists 'Omar (proper name)' but the consonants are also the active participle of אמר H559 'saying'. Context requires 'saying' as a participle.
textual_notes: אהלים: The Strong's candidate provided (H174 'aloe wood') does not match the context. The consonants equally spell the plural of אהל (H168 'tent'). I read it as 'tents/shelters'.

ולאליהו: The candidate given is H453 Elihu; however, the consonants אליהו also spell Eliyahu (Elijah, H452). The narrative context of Moshe and a prophet appearing together strongly favors Eliyahu/Elijah.

translation_notes: אלו: Candidates: H431 'lo!/these', H432 'if/nay'. Chose H431 because 'these words' is coherent — a demonstrative pronoun modifying דברים.
באה: H872 'an entrance to a building'. However consonantally באה is the feminine 3fs perfect of בוא 'to come/enter'. Since the subject is עב (cloud, feminine), 'came' fits perfectly.
עב: Candidates: H5645 'cloud/darkness', H5646 'architrave'. Chose H5645 because a cloud coming and casting shadow is a coherent image, while an architrave appearing suddenly is not.

לבנה: Candidates: H3839 'whitish tree', H3840 'whiteness/transparency', H3841 'Libnah (place)', H3842 'the moon', H3843 'brick', H1129 'to build'. Chose H3840 because 'white/luminous' as an adjective describing a cloud produces the most natural image.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 because 'for them' (ל + הם) makes sense — the cloud cast shadow over them.
פחד: Candidates: H6342 'to fear', H6343 'fear (noun)', H6344 'testicle'. Chose H6343 as the noun 'fear' forming a cognate accusative with the verb ופחדו.
textual_notes: באה: The only Strong's candidate given is H872 'entrance to a building', but the consonants clearly parse as the 3fs perfect of בוא 'to come'. I read it as the verb.

translation_notes: ובת: Candidates: H1323 'daughter', H1324 'bath (measure)', H1325 'bath (Aramaic)'. Chose H1323 because 'daughter of voice' is a well-known Hebrew idiom for a heavenly or echoing voice.

בני: Candidates: H1137 'Bani (name)', H1138 'Bunni (name)', H5204 'lamentation'. None fit; the consonants בני naturally parse as בן + י (my son, 1cs suffix). Context of a heavenly declaration demands 'my son'.
מאד: Candidates: H3966 'vehemence/greatly', H108 'fog'. Chose H3966 because 'beloved to me greatly' is coherent, while 'fog' makes no sense here.

והערב: Candidates: H6148 'to braid/intermix/give security', H6149 'to be agreeable/pleasing', H6150 'to grow dusky', H6151 'to commingle', H6152 'Arabia', H6153 'dusk'. Chose H6149 because 'the pleasing/agreeable one' parallels 'the beloved' and describes the son.
textual_notes: מ<מים: The text appears partially damaged (< marker). The consonants suggest מן + שמים (from the heavens), which fits the context of a heavenly voice. The < may indicate a damaged or uncertain letter.

ושמעו אותו: This could be parsed as 'and hear him' (imperative + object) or 'and they heard him' (3mp perfect). The imperative reading fits better as part of the heavenly declaration commanding the listeners.

והערב: Multiple readings possible. H6149 'agreeable/pleasing' gives the most coherent parallel to 'beloved'. H6148 'surety/pledge' would be theologically interesting but forced. H6150 'dusk' makes no sense.

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'step'. Chose H834 because כ + אשר = 'when/as', a temporal conjunction introducing the clause.
את: Candidates: H852 'portent', H853 'object marker', H854 'with/near', H855 'hoe'. Chose H853 as direct object marker before הקול.
משיח: Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'shrubbery'. Chose H4899 because 'Yeshua Messiah' is a coherent title, while 'Yeshua shrubbery' is absurd.
רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because 'they saw only Yeshua' is the natural reading.
לבד: Root בד candidates: H905 'separation/alone', H906 'linen', H907 'a lie'. Chose H905 because ל + בד = 'alone/by himself', fitting the context of seeing only Yeshua.

כשלם (שלם): Candidates: H7999 'to be safe/complete', H8000 'to restore', H8001 'prosperity', H8002 'peace offering', H8003 'complete/friendly', H8004 'Shalem'. Chose H8003 because כ + שלם + suffix = 'in their completeness/safely', describing their descent from the mountain.
מן: Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 'from (Aramaic)', H4482 'musical chord'. Chose H4480 because 'from the mountain' is the natural spatial preposition.
אל: Candidates: H408 'do not (deprecative negation)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/near'. Chose H408 because it introduces a negative command before תגידו 'tell'.
לאדם (אדם): Candidates: H119 'flush', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'do not tell any person' is coherent.
עד: Candidates: H5703 'duration/perpetuity', H5704 'until/as far as', H5707 'witness'. Chose H5704 because 'until the son rises' is a temporal clause.
שהבן (בן): Candidates: H1894 'ebony', H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 because 'the son rises alive' is the coherent reading in context.
יקום: H3351 'standing/living thing'. The consonants also parse as the 3ms imperfect of קום 'to stand/rise'. Chose the verbal sense 'rises/will rise' since it governs the clause.
חי: Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 'alive (Aramaic)'. Chose H2416 as the predicate 'alive' describing the son after rising.
אחרי: H317 'other'. However אחרי commonly functions as a preposition 'after'. Context 'after his death' requires the prepositional sense.
textual_notes: צ וה: The text appears to have a space or damage in the word צוה (commanded). I read this as a single word צוה from the root צוה 'to command'.
<ראיתם: The < marker suggests textual damage. Reading as ראיתם '(what) you saw' (2mp perfect of ראה).
כשלם: Could be read as 'when they were complete/safe' or 'as [they were] whole/at peace'. The basic sense is 'in wholeness/safely'.
מותו: No standard Strong's candidate was provided matching well. The consonants מות + ו parse as 'his death' (מות H4194 'death' + 3ms suffix). H8420 'mark/signature' for תו does not fit.
אחרי: H317 'other' is the only candidate given, but the consonants אחרי also function as the preposition 'after' (related to אחר H310). Context demands 'after'.

translation_notes: האחר (אחר): Candidates: H309 'to loiter/delay', H310 'after/behind', H311 'after (Aramaic)', H312 'next/other', H313 'Acher'. Chose H312 because 'the next day' is a natural temporal phrase.
עם: Candidates: H5971 'people/crowd', H5972 'people (Aramaic)', H5973 'with', H5974 'with (Aramaic)'. Chose H5971 because 'a great people/crowd' is the subject that 'came to meet them'.
רב: Candidates: H7227 'abundant/great', H7228 'archer', H7229 'abundant (Aramaic)', H7230 'abundance'. Chose H7227 because it modifies עם as 'a great crowd'.
ירד: Candidates: H3381 'to descend', H3382 'Jered (name)'. Chose H3381 because descending from the mountain fits the narrative of coming down.
מן: Chose H4480 'from' as the preposition before 'the mountain'.
textual_notes: The ' mark in the text likely indicates a textual lacuna or abbreviation. It may represent a subject (possibly Yeshua) that has been abbreviated or damaged. The sentence structure suggests someone descended from the mountain and a crowd came to meet them.

The syntax is slightly ambiguous: it could be 'a great crowd — he descended from the mountain — came to meet them' (with the crowd meeting someone descending), or 'on the next day a great crowd descended from the mountain [and] came to meet them.' I read it as the latter but flag the ambiguity.

translation_notes: אדם: Candidates: H119 'flush', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'one man' calling out in a crowd is the natural image.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one'. Chose H259 because 'one man' is a straightforward quantifier.
קורא: H6981 'Kore (proper name)' is the only candidate. However consonantally this is the active participle of קרא 'to call/cry out'. Context demands 'calling out' as a participle.
ואומר: H201 'Omar (name)' is the only candidate. However this is clearly the active participle of אמר with ו conjunction: 'and saying'. Context requires this reading.
על: Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'upon/over/against', H5922 'upon (Aramaic)', H5923 'yoke'. Chose H5921 because 'eyes opened upon my son' means looking at/attending to him.
בני: Candidates: H1137 'Bani', H1138 'Bunni', H5204 'lamentation'. None fit; parsing as בן + י (my son) is required by context — a father pleading for his child.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'because/for'. Chose H3588 as a causal conjunction: 'for I have none besides him'.
אין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 because 'there is not to me besides him' = 'I have no other'.

והרוח (רוח): Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room', H7306 'to blow/smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 'spirit (Aramaic)'. Chose H7307 because 'the spirit seizes him' describes a possessing force, consistent with the surrounding narrative of affliction.
ומיד: Root יד candidates: H3027 'hand', H3028 'hand (Aramaic)'. The phrase מיד commonly means 'from hand' = 'immediately/at once'. Chose this adverbial sense.

ורוק: H7324 'to pour out/empty'. The consonants רוק also relate to רק 'spittle/saliva' (H7536). In context, 'spit/saliva goes out from his mouth' describes a symptom of the seizure. Reading as a noun 'spit/foam'.
עד: Candidates: H5703 'perpetuity', H5704 'until', H5707 'witness'. Chose H5704 because 'until it distresses him' is temporal.
textual_notes: ורוק: Could be the verb H7324 'to pour out' or the noun 'spittle/saliva'. Both produce a coherent image. I read it as the noun since יוצא ('going out') already serves as the verb of the clause.
ומיד: Literally 'and from hand' but idiomatically 'immediately'. Could theoretically mean 'and from [his] hand' but 'immediately he cries out' is far more natural.

translation_notes: הרוח (רוח): Chose H7307 'spirit' as in the previous section — the evil spirit possessing the boy.

רעה: Candidates: H7462 'to tend/pasture', H7463 'male companion', H7464 'female associate', H7465 'breakage/evil'. Chose H7465 because 'evil spirit' (רוח רעה) is the coherent description of a malevolent possessing force. H7462 would produce 'shepherding spirit' which is incongruous with the context of affliction.
ולא: Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation.
textual_notes: רעה: While H7465 'breakage/evil' fits best, the consonants could also theoretically be read as a feminine adjective from רע (H7451 'bad/evil'), which is not listed among the candidates but shares the semantic field. Either way the meaning is 'evil/wicked'.

translation_notes: ענה: Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6034 'Anah (name)'. Chose H6030 because 'Yeshua answered them' introduces a responsive speech act.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'them'. Chose H1992 because ל + הם = 'to them'.
ואמר: Chose H559 'to say' — introducing direct speech.

משפחה: Candidates: H4940 'family/clan/circle of relatives', H8198 'female slave', H6346 'prefect'. Chose H4940 because 'family/generation refusing' describes the people collectively. This word is used in the sense of 'generation' or 'kind/class'.
כמה: Candidates: H3642 'to pine after', H4100 'what?/how?'. The compound כ + מה yields 'how much/how long'. Chose the interrogative sense because 'how much of the time' is a rhetorical question.
מן: Chose H4480 'from/of' — partitive: 'how much of the time'.
הזמן: Candidates: H2163 'to fix a time', H2164 'to agree', H2165 'an appointed occasion/time', H2166 'occasion (Aramaic)'. Chose H2165 because 'the time' (with article ה) is a noun.
נא: Candidates: H4994 'now/please/I pray', H4995 'raw/uncooked', H4996 'No (Thebes)'. Chose H4994 because 'bring now your son' is a command with an urgency particle.
textual_notes: משפחה: Typically means 'family/clan' but here seems to function as 'generation' (a broader collective). This may be a Hebrew rendering of a concept meaning 'this kind/generation' — the people as a group.
לאכול: 'to eat' — this phrase 'I gave to you to eat' could be literal (nourishment) or metaphorical (spiritual sustenance). The text simply says 'to eat' without clarification.
להם vs. לו: Yeshua 'answered them' (the crowd) but 'said to him' (the father individually). This shift in addressee is noteworthy but appears intentional.

translation_notes: וכאשר: Chose H834 'when/as' — temporal conjunction introducing the approach scene.

קרב: Candidates: H7126 'to approach', H7127 'to approach (Aramaic)', H7128 'hostile encounter', H7129 'hostile encounter (Aramaic)', H7130 'center/midst', H7131 'near'. Chose H7126 because 'the boy drew near to Yeshua' is the natural verbal reading.
הנער: Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble', H5288 'boy/youth', H5289 'wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because 'the boy' is the afflicted child from the previous sections.

השטן: Candidates: H7853 'to attack/accuse', H7854 'opponent/Satan'. Chose H7854 because with the article ה, 'the Satan/Adversary' is a specific entity that struck the boy — consistent with the evil spirit narrative.

קלל: Candidates: H7043 'to make light/curse/diminish', H7044 'brightened/sharpened'. Chose H7043 because 'Yeshua cursed/rebuked the evil spirit' describes an authoritative rebuke causing the spirit to depart.
רעה: Chose H7465 'evil/breakage' as in section 8 — 'evil spirit'.
שלו: Candidates: H7958 'quail', H7959 'security', H7960 'fault', H7961 'tranquil/at peace'. Chose H7961 because 'tranquil and quiet' describes the boy's restored state after the spirit departed.
ושקט: Candidates: H8252 'to repose/be quiet', H8253 'tranquility', H6985 'a little/merely'. Chose H8252 because 'quiet/at rest' pairs naturally with 'tranquil' to describe the healed boy.
textual_notes: הכהו: No Strong's candidates were meaningfully provided (H1930 'oh!' for הו). The consonants parse as הכה + הו = 'struck him' from נכה (H5221 'to strike'). This is the standard reading.

קלל: Could mean 'cursed' or 'made light of/diminished'. In context, both senses work — Yeshua either cursed the spirit or diminished its power. The effect is the same: authoritative dismissal of the evil spirit.
וחזרו: Parses as 'and returned him' (hiphil or verbal form of חזר 'to return'). This could mean Yeshua returned the boy, or the boy returned. Context of 'to his father' suggests Yeshua returned him.

translation_notes: המה: Candidates: H1993 'to make a loud sound/be in commotion', H1992 (from הם) 'they (emphatic)'. In context 'they saw thus were astonished' — the pronoun 'they' resuming the subject of 'the ones walking after him' is the natural reading.
כן: Candidates: H3651 'thus/so', H3652 'so', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. 'Thus they were astonished' is the coherent reading — an adverb linking seeing to astonishment.
ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. With ישוע as subject and לתלמידיו as indirect object, this is clearly the verb 'and he said'.
textual_notes: המה could theoretically be read as H1993 (they were in commotion/tumult) rather than the pronoun, which would give 'they were in tumult, thus were astonished.' Both are grammatically possible, but the pronoun reading is more natural as a resumptive subject.

translation_notes: אלה: Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'an imprecation', H424 'an oak', H425 'Elah (proper name)', H426 'God'. Following 'your hearts' and preceding 'the words,' the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (standard Hebrew אלה) is the only coherent reading — it has no Strong's entry listed but is the common demonstrative.
בן: Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (proper name)', H1123 'a son'. With האדם following, 'son of the man' is the clear construct reading.

האדם (first): Candidates: H119 'to turn rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. With the article ה and preceded by בן, 'the man/human' (H120) is the natural reading — 'Son of the Man' is a known title.
אדם (second): Same candidates. Without the article, 'man/humanity' in generic sense (H120) fits — 'into hands of man.'
textual_notes: אלה has no demonstrative pronoun listed among the Strong's candidates provided. The consonants אלה are identical to H421-H426. However, the demonstrative 'these' is the only grammatically coherent reading before הדברים. This may indicate a gap in the provided lexicon entries.
האדם could be read as 'Adam' (H121) — 'Son of Adam' — which overlaps semantically with 'Son of Man' but carries different theological weight.

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction because/for/that'. As a conjunction introducing the reason they didn't understand, H3588 is clearly correct.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', H1992 (from הם) 'them'. As prepositional ל + pronoun הם = 'to/from them,' the pronominal reading is correct.

לשאול: Candidates: H7585 'Sheol/world of the dead', H7586 'Shaul (proper name)', H193 'body/powerful'. However, the root שאל 'to ask/inquire' is the standard verb here. With the infinitive ל prefix and the context 'they feared to _____ it,' 'to ask' is the only coherent reading. The candidates listed appear to be for שאול rather than the verb שאל, but the consonants לשאול clearly represent the infinitive of שאל.
textual_notes: The text appears fragmented: 'וי ר או' seems to be a broken form. Reading these three fragments together as וייראו (and they feared) makes contextual sense — 'they feared to ask about it.' The spacing may reflect manuscript damage or scribal convention. This is my reconstruction.

יהוה here is striking — the text says 'the word of YHWH' rather than what one might expect. This could indicate the speaker equates the utterance with divine speech, or מלת יהוה could be a scribal convention. I translate as found.

לשאול: The candidates given do not include the verb שאל 'to ask,' but the consonantal form לשאול is the standard infinitive construct of שאל with ל prefix. The candidates H7585/H7586 share consonants but produce nonsense in context ('they feared toward Sheol her').

translation_notes: מהם: From הם H1992 'them' with preposition מ 'from' — 'from among them.' The other candidates (H1990 'Ham region', H1991 'abundance') produce incoherent readings.
textual_notes: ונשאו ונתנו is a Hebrew idiom meaning 'they debated/discussed' (literally 'they lifted and gave' i.e. exchanged words back and forth). This is a well-known Rabbinic Hebrew expression.

translation_notes: לקח: Candidates: H3947 'to take', H3948 'instruction/something received'. As a verb with נער אחד as object, 'took' (H3947) is the clear reading.

נער: Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Following the verb 'took' and modified by 'one,' 'a boy/child' (H5288) produces the only coherent image.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/united'. As a numeral modifying נער, 'one' (H259) is the correct reading.
ואמר: H559 'to say' — verb with Yeshua as implied subject and להם as indirect object.
להם: H1992 (הם 'them') with preposition ל — 'to them.' H3859 'to rankle' makes no sense here.

המקבל: Candidates: H6901 'to admit/take/receive', H6902 'to acquire', H6903 'in front of', H6904 'battering-ram', H6905 'presence'. The participle with article ה 'the one receiving' (H6901) is the only reading that fits the sentence structure.
נער: H5288 'a boy/child' — same reasoning as section 5.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Demonstrative 'this' modifying נער is the natural reading. H2089 'a sheep' would produce 'boy sheep' — incoherent.
בשמי: The candidates list H8060 'Shammai' and H4310 'who'. But בשמי is naturally ב + שם + י = 'in my name' (שם H8034 with 1cs pronominal suffix). The candidates seem incomplete.

והקטן: Candidates: H6994 'to diminish', H6995 'little finger', H6996 'small/diminutive', H6997 'Katan (name)'. With article ה and in context of comparing rank, 'the small/least one' (H6996) is correct.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. As a pronoun in a nominal clause 'he [is] great,' H1931 is the standard reading.
textual_notes: ש<לחני appears to have a scribal mark or damage indicated by <. The root שלח 'to send' (H7971) with 1cs suffix ני = 'sent me' is the clear reading. The < may indicate a letter that was damaged or uncertain in the manuscript.

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say' — Yochanan as subject, introducing direct speech.
אדם: Candidates: H119-H124. 'A man/human being' (H120) is the only coherent reading — they saw a person casting out demons.
אחד: H259 'one' — used as an indefinite article 'a certain [man].'

מגרש: Candidates: H4054 'a suburb/open country', H1643 'grain', H1644 'to drive out/expel', H1645 'produce'. As a participle describing what the man was doing to demons, 'driving out/expelling' (H1644) is the only coherent reading.
בידו: The candidate H3035 'Jiddo (proper name)' is irrelevant. This is ב + יד + ו = 'by his hand / against him.' In context of rebuking, it means 'we protested against him.'
כאשר: Candidates for אשר: H833-H838. With כ prefix, כאשר = 'as/when/because' — H834 'who/which/that/because' is the correct base. 'Because he is not walking after you with us.'
textual_notes: ה<דים has a scribal mark or damage (<). The expected word is השדים 'the demons' (from שד). The < likely represents a damaged or uncertain letter.
ומחינו could derive from מחה 'to protest/object' or מחא 'to strike/clap.' In context of rebuking someone, 'we protested/objected' fits best. The suffix נו = 'we.'
בידו could mean 'by his hand' (i.e., we physically stopped him) or be an idiom for 'against him.' Both readings are plausible; I chose the idiomatic sense of opposing him.

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say' — Yeshua as subject.
להם: H1992 (הם 'them') with ל — 'to them.'
אל: Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative negation)', H410 'strength/God', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. Before an imperfect verb תמנעו, H408 'do not' is the standard negative imperative particle.
כי: H3588 'for/because' — introducing the reason for the command.
הוא: H1931 'he' — pronoun in nominal clause 'he is for us.'
וכאשר: אשר candidates: H833-H838. With כ and ו prefix, וכאשר = 'and as/when' — H834 as the relative/conjunction is the correct base.
דברי: The candidate H1704 'Dibri (proper name)' shares consonants, but דברי is clearly the construct plural of דבר 'word' — 'words of.' The proper name makes no sense before ישוע.

משיח: Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder/converse', H7879 'contemplation/utterance', H7880 'a shoot/shrubbery'. As a title following the proper name Yeshua, 'Messiah/Anointed One' (H4899) is the only coherent reading.
textual_notes: This appears to be an incomplete sentence — a temporal clause ('and when... were completed') that expects a main clause to follow. The text as given ends here, suggesting it continues in a subsequent section.

translation_notes: אדם (consonants א-ד-ם): Candidates: H119-H124. A person approaching and speaking — H120 'human being/man'.
אחד (consonants א-ח-ד): Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. Modifying אדם as 'one man / a certain man' — H259.
ואמר (consonants א-מ-ר): H559 'to say' — standard verb of speech in narrative.
משיח (consonants מ-ש-י-ח): H4899 'anointed/Messiah' — title following Yeshua as in all prior sections.
למקום (consonants מ-ק-ו-ם): Candidates: H4725 'place/standing', H6965 'to rise'. With ל prefix before a relative clause 'that you go' — H4725 'to the place' is correct.
אמר (consonants א-מ-ר): H559 'to say' — verb of speech in narrative context.
יש (consonants י-ש): H3426 'there is/are' — existential particle indicating possession 'they have'.
להם (consonants ל-ה-ם): H3859 'to rankle' vs H1992 'them'. As prepositional ל + הם 'to them' (expressing possession) — H1992.
ובן (consonants ב-ן): H1121 'son' — in the title 'son of the man'.
האדם (consonants א-ד-ם): H120 'human being' with definite article — completing 'Son of Man'.
אין (consonants א-י-ן): Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Negating existence — H369 'there is not'.
מקום (consonants מ-ק-ו-ם): H4725 'place' vs H6965 'to rise'. Before a relative clause 'that he bend his head' — a noun 'place' is required — H4725.
textual_notes: ה<ועלים has a damaged/unclear consonant (<). Context of animals with dens strongly suggests השועלים 'the foxes' (from שועל). The missing consonant is likely ש.

שיכוף is not in the candidate list. The root כ-ו-ף / כ-פ-ף means 'to bend/bow'. With the relative ש prefix, it reads 'that he may bend/lay [his head]'. This is an unusual word choice compared to more standard biblical Hebrew but fits the later linguistic register of this manuscript.

translation_notes: אמר (consonants א-מ-ר): H559 'to say' — standard speech verb.
לאיש (consonants א-י-ש): Candidates: H376 'a man/individual', H377 'to act manly'. With ל prefix 'to a man' — H376.
אחר (consonants א-ח-ר): Candidates: H309-H313. Modifying 'man' as an adjective — H312 'another/other'.
וענה (consonants ע-נ-ה): Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to afflict', H6034 'Anah (name)'. In dialogue context after being spoken to — H6030 'answered'.

הנח: The candidate H5146 'Noah' does not fit. This is clearly the Hiphil imperative of נ-ו-ח 'to rest/leave/allow' — meaning 'permit/leave [me]'. The Strong's entry for the root is not among the candidates provided for נח.
את (consonants א-ת): H853 'object marker' before 'my father' — the direct object of burying.
אבי: H21 'Abi (proper name)' is the only candidate, but contextually this is אב + י 'my father' with 1st person possessive suffix.
textual_notes: הנח could theoretically be parsed as ה + נח 'the Noah' (H5146), but this makes no sense in context. It is the Hiphil imperative הנח from root נ-ו-ח meaning 'allow/leave/permit'.
אחרי: H317 'other' is given, but this is more naturally the prepositional form אחרי 'after me' (from אחר + 1cs suffix). The instruction 'go after me' = 'follow me'.

translation_notes: אמר (consonants א-מ-ר): H559 'to say' — speech verb.
הנח: Same as section 7 — Hiphil imperative 'leave/allow'. Not H5146 'Noah'.

אבל (consonants א-ב-ל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. As a conjunction contrasting 'leave them to bury' with 'but you come' — H61 'but/yet' is the correct adversative conjunction.
אתה (consonants א-ת-ה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H859 'you'. As the subject of the imperative 'come' — H859 'you'.
מלכות (consonants מ-ל-כ-ו-ת): Candidates: H4438 'kingdom/dominion', H3575 'Cuth'. In 'kingdom of God' — H4438.
האל (consonants א-ל with ה): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. With definite article before אל in the phrase 'kingdom of ___' — H410 'God/the Almighty'.
textual_notes: הישמעאלים ('the Ishmaelites') is a striking and unusual reading. In parallel traditions, the expected word is 'the dead' (המתים). 'Ishmaelites' here may be a theological substitution or a scribal interpretation meaning 'outsiders/gentiles/those not of the covenant.' This is a significant textual variant that deserves attention.

The phrase 'leave the Ishmaelites to bury' is syntactically incomplete — 'to bury [whom/what]' is implied but not stated. The understood object is likely 'their dead' or 'your father' from the preceding verse.

translation_notes: ואדם (consonants א-ד-ם): H120 'human being/man' — a person speaking in narrative.
אחר (consonants א-ח-ר): H312 'another/other' — modifying 'man' as in previous sections.
אמר (consonants א-מ-ר): H559 'to say' — speech verb.
אדון (consonants א-ד-ו-ן): H113 'sovereign/lord' — form of address.
אני (consonants א-נ-י): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. As subject pronoun before 'will go' — H589 'I'.
אלך: H479 'these' is given, but contextually this is clearly 1cs imperfect of הלך 'I will go/walk'. The Strong's candidate does not match the verbal use.
רק (consonants ר-ק): Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely', H7536 'spittle'. As a restrictive adverb — H7535 'only'.
הנח: Same as sections 7-8, Hiphil imperative 'allow/permit'.
עד (consonants ע-ד): Candidates: H5703 'perpetuity', H5704 'until', H5707 'witness'. Before a temporal clause 'that I do' — H5704 'until'.

באופן (consonants א-ו-פ-ן): H212 'a wheel'. In post-biblical Hebrew, אופן developed the meaning 'manner/way' (from the idea of a wheel/mechanism). With ב prefix 'in a manner/way' — H212 used in its extended sense.
שידע (consonants י-ד-ע): Candidates: H3045 'to know', H3046 (Aramaic), H3047 'Jada (name)'. As a verb 'that [someone] knows' — H3045.
הכל (consonants כ-ל with ה): H3605 'the whole/all' with definite article — 'everyone/everything'.
textual_notes: באופן שידע הכל is ambiguous: it could mean 'in a way that everyone knows [about my departure]' or 'in a way that everything is known/arranged.' The first reading implies the man wants to inform his household; the second implies he wants to settle his affairs. Both are plausible.
אלך: The only candidate provided (H479 'these') does not match the context. This is clearly the 1st person singular imperfect of הלך 'to walk/go' — a very common verbal form.

translation_notes: וישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua/Yeshua', H3443 'Jeshua'. Proper name, H3442.
אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560-H564 (other readings). Introducing speech, H559.
האיש: Candidates: H376 'a man/individual', H377 'to be manly'. With the article ה, 'the man' (H376) — generic/categorical use referring to anyone who does this.

ידו: The candidate H3035 'Jiddo (proper name)' is listed, but in context this is clearly יד (H3027, hand) with 3ms suffix ו — 'his hand.' The consonants ידו match the inflected form of יד perfectly. H3035 as a proper name makes no sense in 'the one placing Jiddo on the plow.'
יהוה: Candidates: H3068 'YHWH', H3069 'YHWH (variant)'. The divine name. H3068.
כן (from section 4): H3651 'thus/likewise.' Already addressed above.
textual_notes: המשים — parsed as the hiphil participle of שים (to put/place), with article ה: 'the one placing.' This is a standard participial construction. No Strong's candidates were provided for this form.
במחרישה — from חרש (to plow), the noun מחרשה means 'plow/plowshare.' The ב prefix means 'on/in.' No Strong's candidates were provided.
ומביט — hiphil participle of נבט (to look/gaze), with waw: 'and looking.' Standard form.
אחריו — 'behind him,' from אחר (behind/after) with 3ms suffix.
אינו — negative existential אין with 3ms suffix: 'he is not.'
ראוי — 'fit/worthy/suitable.' This is a post-biblical Hebrew adjective. No Strong's number applies directly.

[] — empty brackets at the end suggest a lacuna or missing text in the manuscript. The sentence appears grammatically complete without it, though something may have followed (e.g., a qualifying phrase about the kingdom).

במלכות יהוה — the preposition ב could mean 'in' or 'for.' Both readings are viable: 'is not worthy in the kingdom of YHWH' or 'is not fit for the kingdom of YHWH.' The latter is more natural in English.

translation_notes: ואחר (אחר): Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'after', H311 'after (Aramaic)', H312 'other/next', H313 'Acher'. Chose H310 because it functions as a temporal adverb 'and after/afterward' connecting to the next narrative event.

הראה (ראה): Candidates: H7200 'to see/show', H7201 'bird of prey', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. The ה prefix with causative sense gives 'he showed/revealed'. Chose H7200 as the verb 'to show' in hiphil-like usage.
אל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'mighty/God', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Chose H413 because the directional preposition 'to the others' is the only coherent reading here.
עתיד: Candidates: H6263 'prepared', H6264 'prepared/the future'. Chose H6264 because 'prepared/about to' fits the sense of future intention before the infinitive 'to come'.
textual_notes: ש(ים — the text has a damaged/parenthetical character. The reading שבעים (seventy) is reconstructed from context (sending disciples in pairs). The parenthetical mark suggests textual damage at this point.
הראה could be parsed as 'the seeing/vision' (noun) or as a hiphil verb 'he showed/caused to see'. The narrative context with Yeshua as subject favors the verbal reading.

translation_notes: ואמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because this is clearly a narrative verb 'and he said'.
רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because 'but/only' serves as a contrastive conjunction between 'many yields' and 'few reapers'.
להם: The ל prefix + הם. Candidates for הם: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 'to them' as the indirect object of 'he said'.
הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'behold' naturally introduces a dramatic declaration ('I am sending you...').
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the first person pronoun is required by the verb 'sending you'.
בין: Candidates: H995 'to understand', H996 'between/among', H997 'between (Aramaic)'. Chose H996 because 'among wolves' creates the coherent image of lambs surrounded by predators.

תן: The candidate H8565 'a monster/sea-serpent/jackal' is listed, but the consonants תן here clearly function as the imperative of נתן (H5414 'to give'). The Strong's entry H8565 refers to the noun תנין. Chose the imperative of H5414 as this begins a prayer petition 'give to us'.
לחם: Candidates: H3898 'to feed on/to battle', H3899 'bread/food', H3900 'bread (Aramaic)', H3901 'battle'. Chose H3899 because 'bread' is the natural object of 'give to us' in a prayer context.
textual_notes: לכו — the candidate listed is H3551 כו 'a window', but the consonants לכו are the standard imperative plural of הלך (H3212) 'go/walk'. The Strong's entry for כו is irrelevant here.
