כשיות — not in the candidate list as a full form. The כ is a preposition 'as/like' and שיות appears to be the plural of שה (H7716) 'a lamb/sheep', giving 'as lambs'. The form is unusual but contextually clear.
חוקינו — 'our portion/statute'. This could derive from חק (H2706) 'statute/allotment/portion'. The sense 'our allotted portion' fits the prayer context of daily bread.

translation_notes: שק: Candidates: H8242 'sack/sackcloth (mesh material)', H8243 'the leg'. Chose H8242 because 'do not carry a sack' fits the travel-light instruction; legs are not something one carries.

ואבן: Candidates: H68 'a stone', H69 'a stone (Aramaic)', H70 'pair of stones / potter's wheel'. Chose H68; 'stone' here likely refers to a money-weight or purse-stone, a common metonym for money/purse in the context of travel provisions.
ואל (first): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to'. Chose H408 because paired with the imperfect תתנו it forms a prohibitive 'do not give'.
שלום: Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare/greeting', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum'. Chose H7965 because 'do not give a peace-greeting to anyone on the road' fits the urgency instruction.

לשום: Candidates: H7760 'to put/place/appoint', H7761 'to put (Aramaic)', H7762 'garlic'. Here לשום functions as 'to any' (ל + שום in the sense of 'any/whatever'). Chose H7760 used idiomatically as an indefinite pronoun.
אדם: Candidates: H119 'to be ruddy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'any person' is the natural complement to the prohibition.
בדרך: Candidates: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'a road/way'. Chose H1870 because 'on the road' completes the travel scenario.

והנח: The candidate H5146 'Noah' is listed, but the consonants והנח clearly represent a verb form from נוח (H5117) 'to rest/release/set down' in hiphil imperative with ו-conjunction: 'and release/forgive'. This begins the prayer section.
ואל (second): Same as first — H408, prohibitive 'do not'.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Chose H3588 as the causal conjunction linking forgiveness given and received.
textual_notes: שוקים — the candidates listed (H7009-H7011) refer to קים roots. But שוקים most naturally derives from שוק (H7785) 'leg/thigh'. בתי שוקים = 'houses of legs' i.e. leg-coverings or stockings. This is an unusual compound but coherent in a list of travel garments.

ואבן — 'stone' is unexpected in a list of travel items. It may refer to a money-weight stone used as currency, or possibly an error/variant for another word. The reading 'purse-stone' (weight for commerce) fits the prohibition against carrying provisions.

והנח — there is a clear seam in this text where travel instructions transition into prayer language. The prayer section (forgive us... do not bring us into trial) appears embedded within the larger discourse.

translation_notes: ובבית: Candidates: H1004 'house', H1005 'house (Aramaic)', H1006 'Bajith'. Chose H1004 as the common noun 'house' with prepositions וב.

הזה: Candidate H1957 'to dream' vs. ה + זה H2088 'this'. Chose the demonstrative article + pronoun 'this' because 'this house' is contextually coherent, whereas 'to dream' produces no sensible reading.

אי: Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'howler/wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 because אי זה together = 'which one' (interrogative), fitting the question 'which of you has a friend?'
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 as part of the interrogative phrase אי זה 'which?'
בחצי: Candidates: H2677 'the half/middle', H2678 'an arrow'. Chose H2677 because 'in the middle of the night' (midnight) is the natural setting for this parable.
הלוה (לוה): H3867 'to twine/unite/borrow/lend'. In hiphil the sense is 'lend'. Chose this because 'lend me' is the request being made.
ככרות: The candidate listed is H7327 'Ruth'. But ככרות is the construct plural of ככר (H3603) 'a round/loaf/talent'. Chose H3603 because 'loaves of bread' is the coherent reading.
לחם: Candidates: H3898 'to battle/consume', H3899 'bread/food', H3900 'bread (Aramaic)', H3901 'battle'. Chose H3899 as 'bread' completing 'loaves of bread'.
שלשה: Candidates: H8030 'Shilshah', H8031 'Shalishah', H7716 'sheep'. These don't fit. The consonants שלשה represent the number three (H7969). Chose 'three' as the quantity of loaves requested.
textual_notes: שתכנסו — no Strong's candidates provided. This is a relative clause שׁ + תכנסו from the root כנס 'to gather/enter', a later Hebrew verb form. It means 'that you enter into'.
ואמר — this shifts from instruction (peace upon this house) to a new parable. The narrative seam is clear from the switch to third person 'he said to them'.

translation_notes: ואם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because 'and if there is a son of peace' introduces a conditional clause.
שם: Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name (Aramaic)'. Chose H8033 because 'if there [is] a son of peace' requires the existential adverb 'there'.
בן: Candidates: H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 because 'son of peace' is a Semitic idiom for one characterized by peace.
ינוח: The candidate H3239 'Janoach (place name)' is listed, but ינוח is clearly a verb form from נוח (H5117) 'to rest', 3ms imperfect: 'will rest'. The place name makes no sense here.
מהדרך: Candidates for דרך: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'road/way'. Chose H1870 with מה prefix meaning 'from the road/journey'.
ואין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/not', H370 'whence', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 as the negative existential 'and there is not'.
מה: Candidates: H4100 'what?/what!', H4101 same. Chose H4100 as the interrogative/relative 'what [I am able to set]'.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'for/because'. Chose H3588 as the causal conjunction explaining why the request is being made.
textual_notes: ה(לום — the text has a damaged/parenthetical character again. The reading השלום (the peace) or הש(לום is reconstructed. The phrase בן השלום 'son of peace' is a well-known Semitic idiom.

2אוכל — the numeral 2 before אוכל appears to be a scribal mark or textual note, not part of the word. The root is יכל (H3201) 'to be able' in 1cs participle/imperfect form, or possibly אכל 'to eat/feed'. Context favors 'I am able' since it governs the infinitive להניח 'to set/place'.
להניח could mean 'to set before' (from נוח hiphil 'to cause to rest/place') or 'to leave/release'. Here 'to set/place [food] before him' is the coherent image.

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'because/for'. Introducing a reason for the instruction, H3588 'for/because' is clearly correct.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. As a pronoun in a nominal clause ('worthy is he the worker'), H1931 fits.
אל: Candidates: H408 'do not (deprecative negation)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/toward'. Before an imperfect verb תאבו, H408 'do not' is the standard negative volitive.
בית: Candidates: H1004 'house', H1006 'Bajith (place)'. Context of dwelling instructions makes H1004 obvious.
לעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of/transit', H5669 'stored grain'. With ל prefix as infinitive, this is from עבר 'to cross/pass over', meaning 'to move [from house to house]'.
textual_notes: ראוי is a late/Mishnaic Hebrew adjective meaning 'worthy/fitting' — not found as a standard Strong's entry. Root ראה 'to see' in its extended sense.
הפועל 'the worker/laborer' is from the root פעל 'to do/make' (H6466). The noun form פועל (H6467) means 'work/deed' but also 'worker'. This is standard Mishnaic Hebrew usage.
תאבו from root אבה (H14) 'to be willing/consent/desire'. The negation אל תאבו = 'do not be willing / do not consent'.

translation_notes: ובאי: Candidates for אי: H335 'where?', H336 'not', H339 'island/coast'. With prefix ו+ב and followed by זו, this reads 'and in which(ever)' — H335 'where/which' fits as an interrogative/relative pronoun.
זו: Candidates: H2097/H2098 'this/that', H2099 'Ziv (month)'. As a demonstrative relative ('whichever'), H2097 fits.
עיר: Candidates: H5892 'city', H5895 'donkey-colt'. Context of entering and being received clearly indicates H5892 'city'.

שמה: Candidates: H8047 'ruin/desolation', H8048 'Shammah (name)', or the common adverb שמה 'there/thither' (H8033 with directional ה). Context of 'the sick who will be there' clearly points to 'there' as an adverb of place.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to burn/rankle', H1992 'they/them'. With ל prefix as 'to them', this is the prepositional phrase using the 3mp pronoun — H1992 is the base pronoun.
האל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/toward'. With the article ה and following 'kingdom of', H410 'God/the Mighty One' is the only coherent reading.
מלכות: Candidates: H4438 'kingdom/dominion', H3575 'Cuth (Assyrian province)'. Paired with 'God', H4438 'kingdom' is obvious.
textual_notes: שמה as 'there' is technically a different vocalization than שמה 'desolation' (H8047). The consonants are identical. Context decisively favors 'there'.

translation_notes: ואם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Opening a conditional clause, H518 'if' is correct.
בעיר: Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'city'. Following 'if you enter in', H5892 'city' produces the coherent image; H1165 'cattle' is nonsensical here.
העפר: Candidates: H6080 'to be dust', H6081 'Epher (name)', H6082 'fawn', H6083 'dust/earth'. With the article ה, this is the noun H6083 'dust' — the image of shaking dust off one's feet.
רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. As a limiting adverb before 'know', H7535 'only/but' is the natural reading.
האל: Same as section 6 — H410 'God'.
textual_notes: שנאסף: Root אסף 'to gather/collect' (H622). With the prefix ש (relative 'that/which') and נ (nifal passive), this reads 'that was gathered/collected'. The image is of dust that has accumulated on the travelers.

מסירים: Root סור 'to turn aside/remove' (H5493) in hifil participle form with מ prefix. This means 'removing/taking away'. Alternatively from מסר 'to deliver/hand over' but the image of removing dust favors סור.

translation_notes: ואומר: The candidate H201 'Omar (grandson of Esau)' is a proper noun. However, the consonants אומר are the active participle of אמר 'to say' (H559). With the prefix ו, this is 'and [I am] saying' — a participial present tense. H559 is the root.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Following 'and I say', H589 'I' is the pronoun.
רע: Candidates: H7451 'evil/bad', H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate/friend', H7455 'badness'. As the object of suffering, H7451 'evil' fits best.

כדומה: Candidates for דומה: H1745 'silence/death', H1746 'Dumah (place)'. However, the consonants כדומה can also be read as כ + דומה from root דמה 'to be like/resemble' (H1819). This yields 'like the likeness of' or 'comparable to', which fits the comparative context perfectly.
לאשר: Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness'. With ל prefix introducing what they will endure, H834 'that which/what' is correct.
אתם: H864 'Etham (place)' is the only candidate provided, but these consonants are clearly the 2mp independent pronoun 'you' (H859 in its plural form). Context demands the pronoun.
textual_notes: The sentence structure is ambiguous: it could mean (a) Sodom and Gomorrah will not endure evil comparable to what you endure (i.e., your punishment is worse), or (b) less likely, Sodom and Gomorrah did not suffer evil like what you will endure. The imperfect יסבלו suggests future, supporting reading (a).

כדומה: If from דומה H1745 'silence/death', it would read 'like death/silence' — but this doesn't connect well with the following לאשר. Reading it as 'comparable to / like the likeness of' from דמה 'to resemble' is more coherent.

translation_notes: אוי: Candidates: H188 'woe/lamentation', H189 'Evi (Midianite chief)'. As an interjection of lamentation, H188 is correct.
בית: Candidates: H1004 'house', H1006 'Bajith'. As part of the place name 'Beth-Tsidah', H1004 'house of' is the standard construct.

צידה: H6720 'food/provision'. However, the consonants צידה also align with the place name Tsidah/Sidon (cf. H6721 Tsidon). Given the pairing with Tyre (Tsor) in the next line, this likely refers to Beth-Saida (Bethsaida), rendered here as 'house of Tsidah/provision/fishing'.
כי: H3588 'for/because' introducing the reason for the woe.

בצור: Candidates: H1208 'inaccessible/lofty', H6696 'to cramp/confine', H6697 'rock/cliff', H6698 'Tsur (name)'. In parallel with Sodom as a city, this is Tyre (צור), the famous Phoenician city — H6697/H6698.
או: H176 'or' — connecting Tyre and Sodom as alternatives.

לאחור: H268 'the hinder part/backward'. However, in context of mourning alongside ashes, this likely represents a word for sackcloth. The consonants could potentially be read differently, but H268 is the provided candidate. This may be a scribal variant or the translator's rendering of 'sackcloth' using a term meaning 'rough back-covering'. Alternatively, this is שק (sackcloth) rendered unusually.
ובאפר: Candidates: H665 'ashes', H666 'turban'. Paired with mourning imagery, H665 'ashes' is correct.
תשובה: H8666 'a return/recurrence/reply'. In religious context, this means 'repentance' (turning back to God) — standard later Hebrew usage.
textual_notes: צידה could be the common noun 'food/provision' (H6720) or a form of the place name Sidon/Bethsaida. Context strongly suggests the place name Bethsaida (בית צידה), a town associated with Jesus's ministry.

לאחור (H268 'backward/behind') is unexpected in a mourning context where one expects 'sackcloth' (שק). This may be the manuscript's idiosyncratic rendering or a corruption. The pairing with 'ashes' strongly suggests mourning garb was intended. It could also be read as a separate word — 'long ago' (i.e., 'they would have repented long ago in ashes').
The brackets around אם suggest a scribal or editorial insertion, indicating uncertainty about whether the conditional particle was in the original.
בצור: While H6697 'rock' is the base meaning, in a geographical list with Sodom, this almost certainly refers to Tyre (the Phoenician city). The same consonants serve for both.
נסים: Not provided with Strong's candidates. Root נס (H5251 'banner/sign') or the later Hebrew meaning 'miracles'. In context of mighty deeds performed, 'miracles/signs' is intended.

translation_notes: רע (consonants רע): Candidates: H7451 'evil', H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate', H7454 'thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 because the context is about punishment/judgment prepared for a day of reckoning, and 'evil/calamity' fits the comparison between cities.

צור (consonants צור): Candidates: H6696 'to cramp/confine', H6697 'rock/cliff', H6698 'Tsur (personal name)'. Chose H6697 as a place name — Tyre is called צור (the rock city), and paired with Sodom it clearly refers to the famous city.

דומה (consonants דומה): Candidates: H1745 'silence/death', H1746 'Dumah (place)'. Neither is a perfect match; the form more likely derives from the root דמה (to be like/compare), functioning as an adjective 'comparable/similar.' H1745 shares consonants but 'silence' doesn't fit the syntax; the verb דמה (to resemble) is the contextual fit.

לרעה (consonants רעה): Candidates: H7462 'to shepherd/tend', H7463 'male companion', H7464 'female associate', H7465 'breakage'. Chose H7465 because the preposition ל + רעה in context of judgment means 'to the evil/destruction' — breakage/calamity fits the punishment theme.

הדין (consonants דין): Candidates: H1777 'sail direct', H1778 'to judge', H1779 'judgment', H1780 'judgment', H1781 'judge', H1782 'judge'. Chose H1779 because 'the judgment' (noun with article ה) is what fits 'day of the judgment.'
textual_notes: דומה could be parsed as H1745 'silence/death' (Dumah), but contextually it functions as a comparative adjective from the root דמה 'to resemble.' The manuscript may be using a form of דמה rather than the noun דומה.

לרעה could be parsed as 'to the shepherding' (H7462) or 'to the female companion' (H7464), but in context of judgment and punishment, 'to the evil/calamity' (from רעה as feminine of רע) is the coherent reading.

translation_notes: ואת (consonants את): Candidates: H852 'portent', H853 'direct object marker', H854 'nearness/with', H855 'hoe'. Here ואת could be the conjunction ו + pronoun 'you' (2fs), addressing the city directly — or the object marker. Given the 2fs verb forms תנשאי and תרדי, this is 'and you' addressing Kfar Nachum as feminine.

כפר (consonants כפר): Candidates: H3722 'to cover/atone', H3723 'village', H3724 'cover/village/bitumen', H3725 'expiation'. Chose H3723 because כפר נחום is a place name meaning 'Village of Nachum/Comfort.'

נחום (consonants נחום): Candidates: H5149 'Nechum', H5150 'consoled/solace', H5151 'Nachum (prophet)'. This is the place-name component; chose H5151 as the proper name Nachum (meaning comfort/consolation).

עד (consonants עד): Candidates: H5703 'terminus/perpetuity', H5704 'as far as/unto', H5705 same, H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'menstrual flux'. Chose H5704 because 'unto the heart of the heavens' describes the extent of exaltation.
לב (consonants לב): Candidates: H3820 'heart/midst', H3821 same. Chose H3820 — 'heart of the heavens' means the very center/midst of the sky.
textual_notes: ה<מים — the missing letter (marked with <) is almost certainly ש, yielding השמים 'the heavens.' The same notation appears elsewhere in this text for שמים.
ואת could be read as the 2fs pronoun 'and you' or as the object marker. The 2fs verb forms (תנשאי, תרדי) confirm this is direct address to the city, so 'and you' is the reading.
תנשאי could be read as a question ('will you be exalted?') or a statement ('you will be exalted'). The contrast with 'you will descend' suggests a rhetorical question or ironic statement.

translation_notes: מבזה (consonants בזה): Candidates from בזה: H959 'to disesteem/despise', H960 'scorned', H961 'booty'. Candidates from זה: H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H959 because מבזה is clearly a participle with מ prefix from בזה 'to despise,' fitting the parallel with מואס 'reject.'

ואשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because ואשר שלחני = 'and the one who sent me' — a relative clause.
textual_notes: שאתם — the Strong's candidate H864 'Etham' is clearly not relevant here. The consonants are the relative particle ש + the 2mp pronoun אתם 'you (plural).' No Strong's number applies to this combined form.
The second מבזה could be parsed as 'despises' (active) or 'is despised' (passive). Context favors active: the one who despises you actually despises me.

translation_notes: ושלשה: Candidates: H8030 'Shilshah (name)', H8031 'Shalishah (place)'. Neither is the correct identification — the word is simply the number שלשה 'three' with ו conjunction. The Strong's entries given are proper names sharing the consonants, but the common numeral is the obvious reading in context ('seventy and three disciples').
בשמחה (consonants שמחה): Candidates: H8057 'blithesomeness/glee', H4229 (מחה) 'to erase/smooth'. Chose H8057 because 'with joy' fits disciples returning happily.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon (name)'. Chose H113 because the disciples are addressing their master.
הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because 'they are subjected' requires the pronoun.
textual_notes: וה<<ים — the missing letters are unclear. Given the narrative context (a group of disciples), this likely reads והשבעים 'and the seventy.' The number 72 or 70 is also possible depending on the missing consonants.

ושלשה — this could be the numeral 'three' (making seventy-three) or could be a separate word. The standard numeral שלשה has no dedicated Strong's number in the candidates given; H8030 and H8031 are proper names.

translation_notes: ואמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because ואמר is clearly 'and he said' (waw + qal perfect 3ms).
להם: The prefix ל + הם. Candidates for הם: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — 'to them.'
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the speaker is identifying himself as subject.
ששטן (consonants שטן): Candidates: H7853 'to attack/accuse', H7854 'an opponent/Satan'. Chose H7854 because ש + שטן = 'that Satan' — a relative particle introducing the noun 'Satan/the adversary.'

ברק (consonants ברק): Candidates: H1299 'to lighten', H1300 'lightning/gleam', H1301 'Barak (name)'. Also רק: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'merely', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H1300 because 'like lightning' is a natural simile for rapid descent from the sky.
textual_notes: מ<מים — the missing letter is almost certainly ש, yielding משמים 'from the heavens,' consistent with the same notation pattern elsewhere in this manuscript.

translation_notes: והנה (consonants הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 (נה) 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'and behold' introduces a dramatic declaration of authority.
כף: Candidates: H3709 'hollow hand/palm/sole', H3710 'hollow rock'. Chose H3709 because כף רגל is the standard idiom for 'sole of the foot.'

על (all three instances): Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'upon/over/against', H5922 same, H5923 'yoke'. Chose H5921 each time because 'upon' is the spatial preposition needed for treading on something.
כל: Candidates: H3605 'the whole/all', H3606 same. Chose H3605.
ושום: Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7761 same, H7762 'garlic'. Chose H7760 — ושום דבר is an idiomatic expression meaning 'and no thing / not any thing.'
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'no thing' requires the noun 'thing/matter.'
textual_notes: השרפים could refer to 'seraphim' (the celestial beings) or 'fiery serpents' (שרף as venomous snake). In context of treading underfoot alongside scorpions, the 'fiery serpent' reading is more natural, though the term carries both meanings.
ושום דבר — this phrase uses שום in a later Hebrew idiomatic sense meaning 'any/no [thing],' which is post-biblical usage. This may indicate a later Hebrew composition or translation.

translation_notes: אל: Candidates: H408 'not (prohibitive)', H409 same, H410 'strength/God', H411 'these/those', H412 same, H413 'near/to'. Chose H408 because אל + imperfect (תשמחו) is the standard Hebrew prohibition 'do not rejoice.'

כי (both instances): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction that/because/for'. Chose H3588 both times — first introduces 'that they are subjected,' second introduces 'that your name is written.'
הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — the pronoun 'they' as subject of the passive participle.
רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'merely/only/rather', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because 'only/rather' provides the adversative pivot between the two כי clauses.

כתוב: The candidate given is H8421 (תוב 'to reply'), but the consonants כתוב clearly represent the passive participle of כתב 'to write.' H8421 is not the correct root; the כ is part of the root כתב, not a prefix.
textual_notes: כתוב — the Strong's candidate H8421 (תוב 'to reply') treats כ as a prefix, but in context כתוב is unmistakably the passive participle of כתב 'to write.' No Strong's number for כתב was provided in the candidates.
ב<מים — same pattern as elsewhere in this text; the missing letter is ש, yielding בשמים 'in the heavens.'

translation_notes: שעה: Candidates: H8159 'to gaze/inspect', H8160 'a look/moment'. Chose H8160 because שעה here is the noun 'hour/moment' — 'in that hour.'
שמח: Candidates: H8055 'to brighten up/be glad', H8056 'blithe/gleeful', H4220 'fat/rich', H4221 'marrow'. Chose H8055 because the verb 'rejoiced' is needed as the predicate — Yeshua rejoiced.

ברוח: Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room/interval', H7306 'to blow/smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 same. Chose H7307 because 'in [the] spirit' with הקדש = 'in the Holy Spirit.'
הקדש: Candidates: H6942 'to be clean/holy', H6943 'Kedesh', H6944 'sacred place/sanctity', H6945 'devotee', H6946 'Kadesh'. Chose H6944 because הקדש = 'the holiness/the holy' modifying רוח.
ואמר: Chose H559 'to say' — standard narrative verb.
אב (both instances): Candidates: H1 'father', H2 same, H3 'green plant', H4 same. Chose H1 — 'Father' as divine address.
ואדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord', H114 'Addon'. Chose H113 — 'and Lord' as divine title.
אלו: Candidates: H431 'lo!', H432 'nay/if'. Chose H431 functioning as demonstrative 'these' — אלו is a later Hebrew demonstrative pronoun meaning 'these.'
מן: Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 same, H4482 'musical chord'. Chose H4480 because 'from the wise' requires the preposition.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 same, H1933 'to be', H1934 same. Chose H1931 — 'it is' functioning as copula.
כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus', H3652 'so', H3653 'stand/pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 — 'thus/so' fits 'for thus it was pleasing.'

ערב: Candidates: H6148 'to braid/traffic', H6149 'to be agreeable', H6150 'to grow dusky', H6151 'to commingle', H6152 'Arabia', H6153 'dusk'. Chose H6149 because 'to be agreeable/pleasing before you' expresses divine favor — a natural, coherent image of something being sweet or pleasing in God's sight.
textual_notes: שהעלמת — the Strong's candidate H5964 'Alemeth (place name)' was given for עלמת, but in context the ש prefix + הפעיל form of עלם 'to conceal' is the clear reading: 'that you concealed.'
מתודה — this form appears to be a hitpael participle from ידה 'to give thanks/confess.' The candidate H8426 תודה 'thanksgiving/praise' is the noun form; the verbal form מתודה is a denominative.
אלו as 'these' is a later/Mishnaic Hebrew form, suggesting this text was composed or translated in a post-biblical Hebrew register.

translation_notes: הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — 'they are delivered.'
ואין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative', H370 'where', H371 'is it not'. Chose H369 — 'and there is no [one].'
אדם: Candidates: H119 'to flush/be rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'no human being knows' is the contextual meaning.

הבן (all three instances): Candidates: H1894 'ebony', H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'son'. Chose H1121 because 'the son' and 'the father' form an obvious relational pair in this passage about exclusive mutual knowledge.
כי אם (both instances): כי H3588 + אם H518 together form the standard Hebrew idiom meaning 'except / unless / but only.'
האב (both instances): Candidates for אב: H1 'father', H2 same, H3 'green plant', H4 same. Chose H1 — 'the father' as the counterpart to 'the son.'
הוא (both instances): Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 same, H1933 'to be', H1934 same. Chose H1931 — the pronoun functioning as copula 'he is.'

להגיד: The candidate H1517 'tendon/thong' (גיד) shares some consonants, but להגיד is clearly the hifil infinitive construct of נגד 'to declare/tell/reveal.' The ה prefix is the hifil marker, and גיד here represents the root נגד in hifil form.
מי (third instance): H4310 'who/whoever'. Here used as 'whoever' — 'and whoever the son desires to reveal to.'
textual_notes: כ ל — the text shows כל split into two separate tokens. This is likely a scribal spacing issue; together they form כל 'all.'
מאבי — the candidate H21 'Abi (Hezekiah's mother)' shares consonants with אבי but is clearly not relevant; this is מן + אבי 'from my father.'
להגיד — H1517 (גיד 'tendon') is not the correct identification. The form is the hifil infinitive of נגד. No appropriate Strong's number was provided in the candidates for this root.

translation_notes: והפך: Candidates: H2015 'to turn about/over/change', H2016 'a turn/reverse', H2017 'perversity', H6378 (פך) 'flask'. Chose H2015 because 'and he turned his face' is a natural physical action — turning to address his disciples.
ואמר: Chose H559 'to say' — standard narrative verb.
הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — 'they [are] blessed.'
מה: Candidates: H4100 'what', H4101 same. Chose H4100 — 'what you are seeing.'
textual_notes: מאו<רים — the missing letter is likely ש, yielding מאושרים 'blessed/happy' (from אשר 'to be happy/blessed'). This connects to H835 אשר 'happiness' or H833 'to go straight/be happy.'
<אתם — the missing letter at the beginning is likely ש (relative particle), yielding שאתם 'that you' — same construction seen in section 3.

translation_notes: אני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the word opens a direct speech formula ('I say to you'), making 'I' the only coherent reading.

אומר: The only candidate listed is H201 'Omar' (proper noun). However, the consonants א-מ-ר clearly correspond to the root אמר 'to say' (H559), here in participial form. The dictionary listing is incomplete; the form is a Qal active participle of אמר.
כי (consonants כי): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction that/because'. Chose H3588 because this is a discourse conjunction introducing a subordinate clause after 'I say to you.'
מה (consonants מה): Candidates: H4100 'what?', H4101 (Aramaic form of same). Chose H4100 as the standard Hebrew interrogative/relative pronoun introducing 'what you are hearing.'

שומעין: The listed candidate H4599 'fountain' (מעין) does not match. The consonants שמע+ין represent a participial form of שמע 'to hear' with an Aramaic-style plural suffix -ין, consistent with late Second Temple Hebrew/Aramaic influence.
textual_notes: The form שומעין uses an -ין suffix rather than standard Hebrew -ים, suggesting Aramaic or late Mishnaic Hebrew influence. This is a dialectal variant of שומעים.
The text contains a damaged marker '<' before אתם in the second occurrence, possibly indicating a textual corruption or scribal note.

translation_notes: והנה (consonants הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'and behold' naturally introduces a new character in narrative.
חכם (consonants חכם): Candidates: H2449 'to be wise (verb)', H2450 'wise (adjective/noun)'. Chose H2450 because the word functions as a noun here ('a wise one'), referring to a legal expert.
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/a certain'. Chose H259 because it serves as an indefinite article modifying 'wise one.'

ואמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 (Aramaic same), H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the form is a consecutive imperfect 'and he said.'
אי (consonants אי): Candidates: H335 'where/which/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Chose H335 because paired with זה it forms an interrogative 'which/what kind of.'
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because אי זה together functions as an interrogative pronoun meaning 'which/what sort of.'
textual_notes: The phrase אי זה דברים could be read as 'which things' or 'what manner of things.' The two-word interrogative אי זה is a known Hebrew construction for 'which.'
בדת uses דת which can mean 'law/decree/statute' — here clearly referring to religious law (Torah), though the word itself comes from Persian-period Hebrew.

translation_notes: ואמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 Aramaic same, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — narrative 'and he said.'
מה (consonants מה): Candidates: H4100 'what?', H4101 Aramaic same. Chose H4100 as the standard Hebrew interrogative.
כתוב: The listed candidate H8421 for תוב means 'to reply.' However, the consonants כתוב clearly represent the passive participle of כתב 'to write' (H3789). The form means 'written.'

מזה (consonants מזה): Candidates: H4198 'exhausted', H4199 'Mizzah', H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this'. Read as מן + זה ('from/concerning this'), using H2088, because the sentence asks about what the law says regarding a particular matter.
textual_notes: מזה could theoretically be the adjective 'exhausted' (H4198) but contextually it is clearly the preposition מן + demonstrative זה meaning 'concerning this/about this.'

translation_notes: והוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 Aramaic same, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 — emphatic pronoun 'and he' introducing the subject before the verb.

ענה (consonants ענה): Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 Aramaic 'answer', H6033 Aramaic 'afflict', H6034 'Anah'. Chose H6030 because 'he answered and said' is a standard Hebrew narrative formula.
ואמר: Chose H559 'to say' — standard narrative verb.
האדון (consonants אדון): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord/master', H114 'Addon'. Chose H113 because this refers to the divine title 'the Lord' in a commandment about loving God.

כחך: The listed candidate H2441 חך means 'palate/mouth.' However, the consonants כחך are better parsed as כח + ך ('your strength/power'), from כח H3581. The context lists heart, soul, strength, and thought — 'strength' fits the pattern; 'your palate' does not.

כמוך: The listed candidate H4134 מוך means 'to become impoverished.' However, כמוך is clearly the preposition כ ('as/like') + the pronoun מוך/suffix 'you' = 'as yourself.' This is a standard Hebrew form.
textual_notes: כחך could theoretically be parsed as כ + חך 'as your palate/mouth,' but the parallel structure (heart, soul, X, thought) strongly favors כח + ך 'your strength.'
The text uses מחשבתך 'your thought/mind' where the Deuteronomy source text has מאדך 'your muchness/very-ness.' This represents an interpretive expansion or variant tradition.

translation_notes: וישוע (consonants ישוע): Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua', H3443 same. Chose H3442 — proper name of the speaker.
אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 Aramaic same, H561 'something said', H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 as the main narrative verb 'said.'

כדין (consonants דין): Candidates: H1777 'sail direct', H1778 'to judge', H1779 'judgment/justice', H1780 Aramaic same, H1781 'a judge', H1782 Aramaic same. Chose H1779 because כ + דין means 'according to judgment/rightly/correctly,' affirming the quality of the answer.
textual_notes: כדין could be read as 'as/like judgment' (i.e., 'rightly, correctly') or in Aramaic usage simply as an adverb 'thus, so.' Both yield similar meaning in context.

translation_notes: והוא: Chose H1931 'he' — emphatic subject pronoun.

חפץ (consonants חפץ): Candidates: H2654 'to incline to/desire/be pleased', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire'. Chose H2654 because the verbal form 'desired/wanted' fits the narrative: he wanted to justify himself.

לצדק (consonants צדק): Candidates: H6663 'to be/make right (causatively)', H6664 'righteousness'. Chose H6663 because ל + infinitive construct of the causative 'to justify' makes grammatical sense with 'himself' as object.
ואמר: Chose H559 — 'and said.'
לישוע: Chose H3442 — 'to Yeshua.'
ומי (consonants מי): H4310 'who?' — the only candidate, and fits as an interrogative.
הוא: Chose H1931 'he/is he' — copulative use in a question.

חברי: The listed candidate H2277 'Chebrite' (descendants of Cheber) is a gentilicname. However, the consonants חבר + י clearly represent חבר 'companion/associate/friend' (H2270) with 1st person possessive suffix 'my companion.' The context demands this reading.
textual_notes: חברי could theoretically refer to 'Chebrite' (H2277) but contextually must be 'my companion/neighbor' from the root חבר with possessive suffix. The narrative is asking about the identity of one's fellow/neighbor.

translation_notes: אדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to be ruddy', H120 'a human being/man', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because the narrative introduces a generic human character, 'a man.'
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/a certain'. Chose H259 — indefinite article 'a certain [man].'
בין (consonants בין): Candidates: H995 'to understand', H996 'between/among', H997 Aramaic same. Chose H996 'among' because the man fell among thieves.
להם (consonants להם/הם): Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — the prepositional phrase 'to themselves' (i.e., they went away).

כמת (consonants מת): H4962 'an adult/man.' However, the consonants כ + מת more naturally read as כ 'as/like' + מת 'dead (one)' from H4191 (the adjective/participle 'dead'). The context describes leaving someone appearing dead.
הכאת: Parsed as noun construct form of הכאה 'striking/blow' — a verbal noun from נכה 'to strike.'
והניחשהו: Parsed as 'and they left him' — likely from נוח/נחש but in context means 'they abandoned/left him.' The form appears unusual and may contain a scribal variant.
textual_notes: והניחשהו is morphologically unusual. It could be from נוח (Hiphil: 'to set down, leave') with an extra ש, possibly a scribal error or dialectal form. The meaning 'and they left him' is clear from context.
ביריחו with the prefix ב could mean 'in Jericho' or could indicate direction 'toward Jericho' — the narrative clearly means traveling toward Jericho.
כמת: The only listed candidate is H4962 'an adult male,' but the phrase clearly means 'as dead/like a dead [person]' from the root מות.

translation_notes: וקרא (consonants קרא): Candidates: H7121 'to call out', H7122 'to encounter/happen upon', H7123 Aramaic 'to call', H7124 'partridge'. Chose H7122 because 'and it happened/it chanced' introduces a coincidental event in the narrative.

שכהן (consonants כהן): Candidates: H3547 'to officiate as priest', H3548 'a priest', H3549 Aramaic 'priest'; also הן candidates H2004-H2006. Chose H3548 because ש + כהן = 'that a priest,' using the relative particle ש with the noun 'priest.'
אחד: Chose H259 'one/a certain.'
דרך (consonants דרך): Candidates: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'a road/way'. Chose H1870 because this is a noun: 'that same road.'
וראה (consonants ראה): Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 — the verb 'and he saw.'
ועבר (consonants עבר): Candidates: H5674 'to cross over/pass by', H5675-H5677 noun/name forms. Chose H5674 — the verb 'and he passed by.'

הלאה (consonants הלאה): Candidates: H1973 'to the distance/far away', H3811 'to tire', H3812 'Leah'. Chose H1973 because 'and passed onward/to the far side' describes the priest avoiding the wounded man.
textual_notes: וקרא could be 'and he called' (H7121) or 'and it happened/chanced' (H7122). The narrative flow favors H7122 — an incidental encounter is being described.

translation_notes: ולוי (consonants לוי): Candidates: H3878 'Levi', H3879 'a wreath'. Chose H3878 — 'a Levite,' the tribal designation, consistent with the narrative of temple functionaries.
אחד: Chose H259 'one/a certain.'
מקום (consonants מקום/קום): Candidates: H4725 'a place/standing', H6965 'to rise', H6966 Aramaic 'to rise'. Chose H4725 because the noun 'place' fits — 'near that place.'
והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 — 'and behold' introduces the observation of his passing by.
הוא: Chose H1931 'he' — emphatic pronoun.
והלאה: Candidates: H1973 'to the distance/onward', H3811 'to tire', H3812 'Leah'. Chose H1973 — 'and onward/beyond,' same as section 8.
textual_notes: מ<ם appears to contain a damaged or illegible character (<). The most likely reading is משם 'from there,' with the ש partially corrupted. The מ preposition + שם 'there' = 'from there' fits the context of passing away from the location.
The syntax is somewhat compressed — 'a Levite one near from that place' likely means 'a certain Levite [came/drew] near to that place' or 'being near that place.'

translation_notes: אחד: Chose H259 'one/a certain.'
קרוב: H7138 'near' — the only candidate, describing the Samaritan's proximity.
וראה (consonants ראה): Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'seeing', H7203 'seer', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 — 'and he saw,' the natural verb for perceiving the wounded man.
וחמל: H2550 'to commiserate/spare/show compassion' — the only candidate and perfectly fits the narrative: the Samaritan, unlike the priest and Levite, responded with compassion.
textual_notes: ושמרוני is a gentilic form from שמרון (Samaria/Shomron). No Strong's number is provided in the candidates but the form clearly means 'a Samaritan' — one from Samaria.

translation_notes: ושם (שם): Candidates: H8033 'there/then', H8034 'name/appellation', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name (Aramaic)'. However, with waw-consecutive and the verb שים (to put/place/set), the consonants ושם can also represent ויָשֶׂם (and he placed). In context — placing oil on wounds — this is clearly the verb 'to put/place' (שים, H7760, though not listed among candidates, the consonantal form ושם with prefix waw fits שים perfectly). The alternative readings 'and there' or 'and a name' produce incoherent images before 'for him oil on his wounds.' Chose the verbal reading 'and he placed.'

שמן: Candidates: H8080 'to be oily', H8081 'oil/grease', H8082 'greasy/rich'. The noun 'oil' (H8081) fits perfectly as the object being placed on wounds — a standard ancient healing practice. The verb or adjective readings make no sense as a direct object here.

ונתן (נתן): Candidates: H5414 'to give/put', H5415 'give (Aramaic)', H5416 'Nathan (proper name)'. As a verb with waw-consecutive 'and he gave/set,' this fits the idiom נתן עיניו בו ('set his eyes on him' = watched over him). The proper name Nathan makes no sense here.
textual_notes: ושם could theoretically be parsed as 'and there' (H8033) rather than 'and he placed' (from שים). Context strongly favors the verbal reading since 'and there for him oil on his wounds' is syntactically awkward, while 'and he placed for him oil on his wounds' is natural.

באושפיזא is an Aramaic loanword (from Greek ξενοδοχεῖον via Aramaic אושפיזא) meaning 'inn/lodging house.' It has no Strong's number as it is not a biblical Hebrew word but appears in later Hebrew/Aramaic texts.

translation_notes: לקח: Candidates: H3947 'to take', H3948 'instruction/teaching'. In context of taking coins, H3947 'to take' is clearly correct.
שני: Candidates: H8144 'crimson', H8145 'two/second'. Before a noun denoting coins (פשיטין), 'two' (H8145) is the natural reading. 'Crimson peshitin' would be bizarre.
ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. With waw-consecutive introducing direct speech, H559 'to say' is the only viable reading.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Demonstrative pronoun 'this' pointing to the wounded man. 'A sheep' makes no contextual sense.
ואם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. After the imperative clause, a conditional 'and if' (H518) introducing a further stipulation is the natural reading. 'And mother' is nonsensical.

אלו: Candidates: H431 'lo!/behold', H432 'if/nay'. In post-biblical Hebrew, אלו functions as a demonstrative pronoun 'these.' This fits the context: 'these peshitin.' Both Strong's entries are less fitting, but H431 as a deictic particle is closest.
textual_notes: פשיטין is an Aramaic/post-biblical Hebrew term for small coins (from פשט, to extend/spread — flat coins). No Strong's number applies.
למוכה — from the root נכה (to strike/smite), the passive participle מוכה means 'one who is struck/wounded.' No Strong's candidate was provided; this is a standard participial form.

מ<ני — the text appears to have a lacuna or uncertain letter (marked with <). This likely reads מני or מן meaning 'than/from,' a partitive preposition. The damaged character makes certainty impossible.

בחזרתו — 'in his return.' The suffix could refer to the speaker ('my return') or a third party. Context of the narrative (the one leaving promising to return) suggests it means 'upon my return,' though the consonantal suffix -ו is third person. This may reflect a narrative style where the speaker refers to himself in third person, or it could be an error.

יתנם — 'he will give them.' The subject is ambiguous: is it the speaker promising 'I will give' (in which case we'd expect אתנם) or a third-person reference? Likely the speaker referring to himself, parallel to the third-person suffix on בחזרתו.

translation_notes: אי: Candidates: H335 'where/how/which', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Combined with זה, אי זה forms the interrogative 'which?' (literally 'where this?'). This is a standard Hebrew idiom. H335 is correct.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Part of the interrogative compound אי זה 'which one.' H2088 is correct.

מאלה: The מ prefix means 'from/of.' Candidates for אלה: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. However, אלה also serves as the common demonstrative pronoun 'these' (not listed among Strong's candidates here, but standard Hebrew אלה H428). In context — 'which of these three' — the demonstrative 'these' is the only coherent reading.
שהיה (היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin'. With the relative ש prefix, 'that he was' (H1961) is the natural reading. 'That ruin' makes no sense.

חבר: Candidates: H2266 'to join', H2267 'society/spell', H2268 'Cheber', H2269 'associate', H2270 'associate', H2271 'partner'. In context, paired with רע (friend), a noun meaning 'companion/associate' fits perfectly. H2270 'an associate' is chosen.

ורע: Candidates: H7451 'bad/evil', H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate/friend', H7454 'thought', H7455 'badness'. Paired with חבר (companion), H7453 'friend/fellow' creates a natural hendiadys: 'companion and friend.' H7451 'evil' would produce the bizarre reading 'more companion and evil.'
שנפל (נפל): Candidates: H5307 'to fall', H5308 'to fall (Aramaic)', H5309 'abortion'. With relative ש prefix, 'who fell' (H5307) is the clear reading.

בין: Candidates: H995 'to understand', H996 'between/among', H997 'between (Aramaic)'. As a preposition before הגנבים (the thieves), 'among' (H996) is correct. 'To understand the thieves' would require different syntax.
textual_notes: ה<לשה — the text has a damaged or uncertain character (marked <). This almost certainly reads השלשה (the three), from שלש. The damaged letter would be ש.

מאלה — the demonstrative pronoun אלה ('these') is not among the Strong's candidates provided (which list H421-H426). The correct Strong's would be H428 (אלה, demonstrative 'these'). I have used H426 as a placeholder since it was the closest listed candidate, but the actual word is the demonstrative pronoun.
הגנבים — from גנב (H1590, thief/robber). The article ה plus plural form. Could mean thieves or robbers.

translation_notes: ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer'. Waw-consecutive + verb introducing speech: H559 'and he said.'

החסד: Candidates: H2616 'to be kind', H2617 'kindness/piety', H2618 'Chesed (name)'. With the definite article ה, the noun 'the kindness' (H2617) fits perfectly — referring back to the specific act of mercy described. The verb or proper name would not take the article this way.

ההוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/that', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. With the article ה prefix, this is the demonstrative 'that' (H1931), modifying החסד: 'that kindness.'
וישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua/Yeshua', H3443 'Jeshua'. This is the proper name Yeshua (Jesus). H3442 is the standard entry.
אמר (second occurrence): Same candidates as ואמר above. H559 'said.'

ואתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive (Aramaic)', H859 'you (pronoun)'. After the imperative לך (go), 'and you' (H859) as an emphatic subject pronoun before תעשה (you shall do) is the natural reading. 'And arrived' disrupts the imperative command structure.

כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/likewise', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. As an adverb after תעשה (you shall do), 'thus/likewise' (H3651) completes the instruction perfectly. 'A gnat' or 'pedestal' would be absurd.
בעוד: H5750 'while/still' — temporal clause as in section 6.

במגדול: Candidates: H4024 'Migdol (place in Egypt),' H1419 'great.' However, in a narrative about entering a settlement, this likely represents a form related to מגדל 'tower' or, more likely in Mishnaic Hebrew, a village/settlement. The context of entering 'a certain [one]' with אחד suggests a generic settlement, not the Egyptian Migdol.
אחד: H259 'one/a certain' — modifying the village.

מה: H4100 'what' — but here used as part of the phrase שמה 'whose name,' with ש (relative) + מה functioning as a name introduction. The damaged text וא ה ש מה likely reads 'and a woman whose name [was].'
מרים: H4813 'Miriam' — a proper name.
אמר: Candidates include H559 'to say,' H561 'something said,' H563 'lamb,' H564 'Immer.' As a narrative verb of speech, H559 'said' is unmistakable.
למה: H4100 with ל prefix — 'why/for what reason.'
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that,' H2089 'sheep,' H2090 'this.' H2088 as demonstrative pronoun 'this one' fits the Pharisee pointing to the person.
הבקר: Candidates: H1239 'to inspect,' H1241 'cattle,' H1242 'morning.' In context of a meal time, H1242 'morning' is the natural reading — 'the morning meal.'
ונעשה: Root עשה with נ prefix — niphal 'it was done/it happened.' Common narrative transition.
שהולכים: ש (relative) + ה (article) + הולכים (walking, qal participle mp of הלך).
רוחץ: Qal participle of רחץ 'to wash.'
בסעודת: ב + סעודת (construct of סעודה 'meal/feast'). Post-biblical Hebrew.
textual_notes: במגדול: The text seems to intend 'village/town' but the candidates only offer H4024 'Migdol (Egypt)' or H1419 'great.' This may be a variant spelling of מגדל or a dialectal term for a small settlement/village.
The sequence וא ה ש מה appears to be damaged or fragmented text. Reconstructed as ואשה שמה 'and a woman whose name' — the spacing may reflect manuscript damage.
The section conflates two scenes: Mary receiving him (a hospitality scene) and the Pharisee commenting on hand-washing (a meal scene). This may represent a composite or condensed text.

translation_notes: והיה: H1961 'to be/exist/become' with ו — 'and there was/it came to be.'
אחות: H269 'sister' — the only candidate and it fits: introducing Martha as Mary's sister.
ישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua,' H3443 same. Both refer to the same name. H3442 chosen as the primary entry.
משיח: Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah,' H7878 'to ponder,' H7879 'utterance,' H7880 'shrub.' Following a personal name as a title, H4899 'Anointed One/Messiah' is the clear reading.

ושמעה: Candidates listed H8093/H8094 (names) and H4577-H4579 (bowels/belly). But this is clearly ו + שמעה, 3fs perfect of שמע 'to hear' — 'and she heard.' The candidate entries appear to misidentify the root.
אמר: H559 'to say' — narrative speech verb, as in previous sections.
מה (in questions): H4100 'what' — introducing the object of purification.
ומן: Candidates include H4478 'manna,' H4480 'from/out of.' As a preposition 'and from' connecting goblet and dish, H4480 is the clear reading.
רע: Candidates: H7451 'evil,' H7452 'noise,' H7453 'associate,' H7454 'thought,' H7455 'badness.' Modifying 'heart' in a moral critique, H7451 'evil' fits the condemnation of inner corruption.
בפנים: H6440 'face/front' — used adverbially with ב as 'inside/within.'
<הוא: The < indicates damaged text. Reading as שהוא (ש+הוא) 'that is' — a relative clause.
textual_notes: The text conflates the Martha/Mary scene with the Pharisee's criticism. The narrative shifts from describing Mary sitting at Yeshua's feet to addressing the Pharisee about purification. This may be a deliberate interweaving in the manuscript.
ש מה appears again as a fragmented form of שמה 'whose name.' The spacing suggests manuscript damage.
<הוא appears twice with a damaged initial letter. Reading as שהוא 'that is' based on the relative clause pattern ש+הוא.
אתם: The only candidate is H864 'Etham (a place),' but this is clearly the 2mp pronoun 'you.' The Strong's candidate list is incomplete for this common pronoun.

translation_notes: במה: Candidates: H1116 'elevation/high place,' H4100 'what.' With ב prefix, 'in what' (H4100) fits — describing what Martha labored over, i.e., what was needed.
כן: Candidates: H3651 'thus/therefore,' H3652 'so,' H3653 'stand,' H3654 'gnat.' With ל prefix, לכן = 'therefore' (H3651).
מי: H4310 'who' — introducing the rhetorical question about the Creator.
שעשה: ש (relative) + עשה (H6213 'to do/make'). 'Who made.'
מתחזקת: Hithpael participle fs of חזק 'to be strong' — reflexive 'exerting/busying herself.'
לטרוח: Infinitive construct of טרח 'to labor/toil' with ל prefix. Post-biblical Hebrew.
סכלים: Plural of סכל 'fool.' An exclamatory address.
תאמר: 3fs imperfect of אמר 'to say' — 'she says/will say.'
שיעזרני: ש (that) + י (3ms imperfect prefix) + עזר (help) + ני (me). 'That he would help me.'
textual_notes: The text appears to merge two different narrative threads: Martha's request for help (a domestic scene) and the 'Fools!' exclamation about inside/outside (a theological argument about purification). The paragraph mark (') may indicate a textual boundary between these two threads.

The question 'Did not the one who made the outside also make the inside?' shifts from domestic to theological/philosophical discourse. The antecedent of 'fools' is ambiguous — it could address the Pharisees (from the previous section's context) rather than Martha.

translation_notes: וענה: Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer,' H6031 'to depress/afflict,' H6034 'Anah (name).' As a narrative verb paired with 'said,' H6030 'answered' is the standard formula.
האדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord,' H114 'Addon (name).' With the article, H113 'the Lord' is the clear reading — referring to the speaker with authority.
ואמר: H559 'to say' — standard speech verb.
בצדקה: Candidates: H6665 'beneficence,' H6666 'righteousness/justice.' In context of giving surplus, H6666 captures both 'righteousness' and the Mishnaic sense of 'charity/almsgiving.'
לכן: H3651 'therefore' — as in previous sections.
חרוצה: From root חרץ 'to be sharp/diligent/decisive.' Feminine adjective: 'diligent/industrious.'
נמצאת: Niphal participle/perfect 2fs of מצא 'to find' — 'you are found/discovered.'
תנו: 2mp imperative of נתן 'to give.' The shift to plural suggests addressing the Pharisees (from context) or a broader audience.
<יותר: Damaged initial letter + יותר (H3148 'more/surplus'). Likely שיותר 'that is surplus/extra.'
טהורים: Plural adjective from טהר 'pure/clean.' 'Pure/clean things.'
textual_notes: The address shifts from singular 'Marta, Marta' (2fs) to plural 'give' (תנו) and 'to you' (לכם). This shift suggests the teaching pivots from Martha personally to a broader audience, likely the Pharisees from the earlier context.
בצדקה in Mishnaic Hebrew commonly means 'charity/almsgiving' rather than abstract 'righteousness.' Both senses may be intended here.
<יותר has a damaged initial character. Likely שיותר (ש+יותר) 'that is surplus/remaining,' functioning as a relative clause.

translation_notes: דבר (D-B-R): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'one thing is needed' makes contextual sense as a statement about what is necessary.
אחד (ʾ-Ḥ-D): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'one thing' is natural with the noun דבר.

את (ʾ-T): Candidates: H852 'portent', H853 'object marker', H854 'with/near', H855 'hoe'. Here את functions as second-person feminine singular pronoun 'you' addressing Miriam, or as an object marker. Given the address to Miriam and the verb בחרת, it reads as 'you, Miriam, chose.' Both parsings yield similar meaning.

החלק (H-Ḥ-L-Q): Candidates: H2505 'to apportion', H2506 'portion/allotment', H2507 proper name, H2508 'part', H2509 'smooth', H2510 proper name. Chose H2506 because 'the portion' fits naturally with choosing the better part.
טוב (Ṭ-W-B): Candidates: H2895 'to be good', H2896 'good (adj)', H2897 place name, H2898 'goodness (noun)'. Chose H2896 because it serves as adjective modifying the portion.

אשר (ʾ-Š-R): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 as the relative pronoun 'which' introducing the clause about what will not be taken.
אוי (ʾ-W-Y): Candidates: H188 'woe/lamentation', H189 'Evi (proper name)'. Chose H188 because 'woe to you' is a natural exclamatory address.

והכרוב (W-H-K-R-W-B): The Strong's candidates provided are H3742 'cherub' and H3743 'Kerub (place)'. However, in context of herbs being tithed (mint, rue, and ___), this must refer to a plant. The consonants כרוב also correspond to cabbage/caraway in later Hebrew usage. I read this as 'cabbage' (a garden plant), not 'cherub.'
textual_notes: את before מרים could be the object marker (H853) or the second-person feminine pronoun 'you.' Both yield essentially the same meaning: 'you, Miriam, chose' vs. 'Miriam chose.' The feminine verb form בחרת supports 'you chose.'

והכרוב: The only Strong's candidates are H3742 'cherub' and H3743 'Kerub (place),' but contextually among tithed herbs this must be a plant (cabbage or similar green). This is a post-biblical Hebrew usage not captured in Strong's.
The bracket markers ] [ in the source text suggest a textual break or section division between the Miriam passage and the woe oracle.

translation_notes: ישוע (consonants ישוע): Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua/Yeshua', H3443 same. Chose H3442 as a proper name — the subject who is praying.
במקום (consonants מקום): Candidates: H4725 'a place/standing spot', H6965 'to rise'. With prefix ב- and following אחד, 'in a certain place' is the coherent reading.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. 'One' modifying 'place' = 'a certain place' is standard Hebrew usage.
בעד: H1157 'after/when/for'. In temporal context of entering, 'when/after' fits the narrative sequence.
במגדל: Candidates: H4026 'tower/village (Migdal)'. This is likely a place name (Migdal/Magdala) or the word for village/tower. The narrative of entering a settlement fits.
שם: Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name'. Both work; 'there' fits with 'and there was there' followed by שמה as 'her name'.
שמה: Candidates: H8047 'ruin', H8048 'Shammah (name)'. However, in context this reads as ש + מה or שם + ה (her name). 'Her name' fits — introducing the woman's identity.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'lord/sovereign', H114 'Addon (name)'. She addresses Yeshua as 'lord/master'.
את/אתה: These together form an emphatic 'you/you yourself'. H859 for the pronoun 'you'.

הלהם / הלהן: These appear to be ה (interrogative/definite) + להם/להן (to them masc/fem). The pair likely represents a scribal doublet or variant — 'to them' addressing both genders, or a correction. In context Martha is asking about serving food to them.
textual_notes: במגדל א׳ — 'tower one' could be a place name (Migdal, i.e., Magdala) with abbreviation mark, or 'a certain tower/village'. The abbreviation mark א׳ suggests a truncated word.
והיתה is repeated twice — possibly a scribal dittography or intentional repetition.
The relationship between שם and שמה is ambiguous: 'there, whose name [was]' or 'there [was] a ruin' or 'there [was] Shammah'. Context of introducing Martha supports 'her name'.

הלהם / הלהן — the pair is unusual. Could be: (1) interrogative ה + ל + הם/הן = 'is it not for them?'; (2) ה + לחם = 'the bread' (with ה+להם being a compressed form); (3) a scribal correction from masculine to feminine pronoun. The parallel with לחם (bread) is suggestive given Martha's role as hostess.
מרתא appears three times with variant spelling מרטא — likely scribal variants of the Aramaic name Martha.

translation_notes: והוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 as the pronoun 'and he' introducing the subject of the response.

ענה: Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 'to answer (Aramaic)', H6033 'to depress (Aramaic)', H6034 'Anah'. Chose H6030 because 'he answered him' is the natural speech-report verb here.
אל: Candidates: H408 'not (prohibitive)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to'. Chose H408 because with the imperfect תצערני it forms 'do not trouble me'.
הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'behold/lo', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'behold, the door is shut' is a natural exclamatory introduction.

ובני: Candidates: H1137 'Bani (name)', H1138 'Bunni (name)', H5204 'lamentation'. None of these fit. The form is ו + בני 'and my sons/children' from בן (H1121). Chose H1121 with 1cs pronominal suffix.
הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because 'my children, they [are] now in bed' requires the pronoun.

במטה: Candidates: H4294 'rod/staff/tribe', H4295 'downward/below', H4296 'bed/sleeping mat', H4297 'distortion', H4298 'expansion'. Chose H4296 because 'in bed' is the natural image — children sleeping at midnight.
לקום: Candidates: H3946 'Lakkum (place)', H6965 'to rise', H6966 'to rise (Aramaic)'. Chose H6965 as the infinitive 'to rise/get up', which makes sense as the man's excuse.
הפת: Candidates: H6595 'a bit/morsel', H6596 'a hole/hinge'. Chose H6595 because 'to give you the morsel/bread-piece' completes the narrative about food.
textual_notes: תצערני — no Strong's candidates listed. This is from the root צער 'to be small/to trouble/distress', a post-biblical Hebrew form. The meaning 'do not trouble/bother me' is clear from context.
איניני — no Strong's candidates listed. This is a compound negative form אין + אני 'I am not' (literally 'there-is-not-I'), a colloquial Hebrew construction meaning 'I am unable'.

translation_notes: ואם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/although'. Chose H518 as the conditional 'and if'.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 as the subject pronoun 'he'.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because 'I say to you' requires the first person pronoun.
אומר: Candidate H201 'Omar (name)'. But this is clearly a participle of אמר (H559) 'saying/I say'. The name Omar is irrelevant here.
שאם: ש + אם. Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if'. Chose H518: 'that if' introducing the conditional clause.
בעד: Candidates: H1157 'on account of/for', plus עד candidates. Chose H1157 because 'on account of his love/friendship' explains the motivation.
ויום: Candidates: H3117 'day', H3118 'day (Aramaic)'. Chose H3117. This appears to be a fragment of the prayer teaching: 'and [each] day'.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle/burn', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 as 'to them', indicating the audience of the teaching.
בחצות: H2676 'the middle (of the night)'. Only one candidate; 'at midnight' is clear.
ככר: Candidates: H3603 'a round/loaf/talent', H3604 'a talent (Aramaic)', H3733 'ram/meadow', H3734 'a cor/measure'. Chose H3603 because 'a loaf' fits the bread-lending parable.
textual_notes: This section appears to be a composite or marginal annotation that interweaves commentary on the parable with fragments of prayer instruction. The text flow is disrupted, with what appears to be a teaching gloss ('his prayer will teach us, he taught...') followed by abbreviated prayer elements ('it will be given, and give, and day, from all our debts, in trial') and then a return to the midnight parable ('to them: which, at midnight, lend me...').
בהתמדה — no Strong's candidate. This is from the root תמד 'to persist/persevere' in a hitpael nominal form, meaning 'with persistence/perseverance'.

תפילתו תלמד אותנו לימד — this sequence is syntactically unusual. It could be read as: 'his prayer will teach us — he taught [saying]:' followed by abbreviated prayer elements. Or it could be a marginal gloss that crept into the text.
הלויני and הלוני appear to be variant forms of the same request 'lend me', possibly representing two manuscript traditions preserved side by side.
ג׳ שלש — the numeral abbreviation ג׳ (gimel = 3) followed by the spelled-out שלש 'three' is redundant, suggesting a scribal gloss or clarification.
מחייובנו — no Strong's candidate. This appears to be from חוב/חיב 'to be obligated/indebted' with 1cp suffix: 'our debts/obligations'.

translation_notes: שאלו: The candidates listed (H431 'lo', H432 'if') refer to אלו only. But שאלו is the imperative plural of שאל (H7592) 'to ask/inquire'. Chose H7592 as this clearly means 'ask!'.
ויפתח: Candidate H3316 'Jiphtach/Jephthah (name)'. But this is ו + יפתח, the niphal/pual imperfect of פתח (H6605) 'to open': 'it will be opened'. The proper name is irrelevant here.
textual_notes: תקעו — from תקע (H8628) 'to clap, strike, blow (a horn), thrust'. In context, this means 'knock/strike [on a door]', extending the door-parable imagery. The verb is commonly associated with blowing a horn, but the physical sense of striking fits the door context.

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Chose H3588 as the causal conjunction 'for' explaining the preceding imperative.
איש: Candidates: H376 'a man/individual', H377 'to act as a man'. Chose H376 as the noun 'every person'.
ש<ואל: The < mark suggests textual damage. The reading is שׁואל from שאל (H7592) 'who asks'. The ש functions as a relative pronoun.

מוצא: Candidates: H4161 'a going forth/exit/source', H4162 'Motsa (name)'. But in context this is the active participle of מצא (H4672) 'to find': 'finds'. The form מוצא as participle fits the pattern of the other clauses (asking→receiving, seeking→finding).
ומי: H4310 'who'. The interrogative/indefinite 'whoever' in the pattern of general truths.
שמבקש: ש + מבקש from בקש (H1245) 'to seek/search'. The ש is a relative pronoun: 'who seeks'.
textual_notes: ש<ואל — the < character in the consonantal text suggests damage or an editorial mark. The intended reading שואל 'who asks' is clear from context.

מוצא — could be the noun H4161 'a going forth/source/product' or the participle of מצא 'finds'. The parallel structure (asks→receives, seeks→finds, knocks→opened) strongly favors the verbal participle 'finds'.
פתחו — this could be parsed as 3mp 'they open' or as a passive/impersonal construction 'it is opened for him'. Both yield essentially the same meaning.

translation_notes: אם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because this introduces a conditional rhetorical question about what a father would do.

לחם (consonants לחם): Candidates: H3898 'to feed/battle', H3899 'bread/food', H3900 'bread', H3901 'battle'. Chose H3899 because the passage contrasts edible things (bread, fish) with harmful substitutes (stone, serpent).
אבן (consonants אבן): Candidates: H68 'a stone', H69 'a stone', H70 'a pair of stones/potter's wheel'. Chose H68 because a single stone is the natural inedible counterpart to bread in this contrast.

נחש (consonants נחש): Candidates: H5172 'to hiss/prognosticate', H5173 'incantation', H5174 'copper', H5175 'a snake', H5176 'Nachash (proper name)'. Chose H5175 because a snake is the natural dangerous counterpart to a fish — both are elongated creatures, one edible, one harmful.
ואם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because this continues the conditional pattern from section 1.
אם (consonants אם): H517 'mother' vs H518 'if/conditional'. Chose H518 because this introduces a conditional logical argument.

ברע (consonants רע): Candidates: H1298 'Bera (proper name)', H7451 'evil/bad', H7452 'a crash/noise', H7453 'associate/companion', H7454 'a thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 because the passage contrasts the evil nature of the audience with their still-good gift-giving, building a fortiori argument.
מה/וכמה: The phrase כ מה וכמה is an idiomatic Hebrew expression meaning 'how much more' — a qal va-chomer (a fortiori) argument. Both instances of מה read as H4100 'how much/what'.

הרוח (consonants רוח): Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room/relief', H7306 'to blow/smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 'wind/spirit'. Chose H7307 because the definite article marks this as a specific noun — 'the spirit' — and it is the gift the heavenly father gives, fitting the climax of the argument.
textual_notes: שב<מים contains a damaged/unclear consonant marked with <. Reading as שבשמים ('that in the heavens') based on context — our Father who is in the heavens.

The phrase אם לא שלא is unusual and could be parsed as 'if not ... that not' (double negation yielding a positive sense: 'even though you are evil') or as a concessive 'even though'. The logic requires a concessive reading: despite being evil, you still give good gifts.
הרוח could be 'the wind', 'the breath', or 'the Spirit' — the consonants and article do not disambiguate the theological sense.

translation_notes: מגרש (consonants מגרש): Candidates: H4054 'suburb/open country', H1644 'to drive out/expel'. Chose H1644 (participle form: 'driving out') because the context describes expelling an adversary — a suburb/open country makes no sense here.

השטן (consonants שטן): Candidates: H7853 'to attack/accuse', H7854 'an opponent/Satan'. Chose H7854 because the article ה prefixed indicates a noun — 'the adversary/Satan' — and this is being expelled.

האלם (consonants אלם): Candidates: H481 'to tie fast/be tongue-tied', H482 'silence', H483 'speechless/mute'. Chose H483 because with the article ה it functions as a substantive adjective — 'the mute one' — who then speaks.

דבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak/arrange words', H1697 'a word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1696 because the mute one performs the action of speaking after the expulsion.
textual_notes: The syntax is ambiguous: 'driving out the adversary' could mean he was expelling a demonic spirit called 'the adversary' from the mute person, or that 'the adversary' is in apposition to what made the person mute. The result is the same: the mute person speaks after the expulsion.

translation_notes: ומקצת (consonants קצת): Candidates: H7117 'a termination/portion', H7118 'portion'. Chose H7117 because 'a portion of them' = 'some of them', fitting the context of a subset of the crowd speaking.
מהם (consonants הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because מ + הם = 'from them', a standard partitive construction.
בבעל (consonants בעל): Candidates: H1166 'to be master', H1167 'a master/owner', H1168 'Baal'. Chose H1168 because 'Baal Zebub' is a known compound name for a pagan deity.
שר (consonants שר): Candidates: H8269 'a head person/ruler', H8270 'a string/cord'. Chose H8269 because 'prince of the demons' describes the rank attributed to Baal Zebub.
מגרש: Same as section 4 — H1644 'to drive out/expel', as the context is about casting out demons.
textual_notes: ה<דים appears twice with a damaged/unclear consonant marked <. Based on context (beings that are driven out, associated with Satan/Baal Zebub), this likely reads השדים ('the demons') from שד (H7700 'a demon').

translation_notes: אות (consonants אות): Candidates: H225 'to come/assent', H226 'a signal/sign/omen'. Chose H226 because they are requesting visible proof — a sign from heaven.
מן (consonants מן): Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 'from', H4482 'a musical chord'. Chose H4480 because the preposition 'from' fits: a sign from the heavens.
textual_notes: ה<מים contains a damaged consonant marked <. Given the context of requesting a heavenly sign, this almost certainly reads השמים ('the heavens') from שמים (H8064).

translation_notes: וישוע (consonants ישוע): Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua', H3443 'Jeshua'. Both refer to the same name; chose H3442 as the primary entry.

כמבין (consonants בין): Candidates: H995 'to separate mentally/understand', H996 'between', H997 'between'. Chose H995 because כ + מבין = 'as one who understands/discerns' — a hiphil participle of בין with כ prefix.

אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the context is direct speech — he said to them.

שחלק (consonants חלק): Candidates: H2505 'to divide/apportion', H2506 'allotment', H2507-H2510 various. Chose H2505 because ש + חלק = 'that is divided' — a verb in relative clause describing the kingdom.
על (consonants על): Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'upon/against', H5922 'upon', H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 because 'house falls upon house' describes collapse and internal conflict.
textual_notes: ]להם[ is marked with brackets in the source, indicating it is an editorial insertion. It likely reads 'against itself/them' to complete the sense of a kingdom divided against itself.
מעשיהם could mean 'their deeds/actions' or 'their intentions/schemes' — the root עשה covers both the act and the design behind it.

translation_notes: ואם: H518 'if' — introduces conditional clause about Satan being divided.
השטן: H7854 'the adversary/Satan' with definite article — same entity discussed in previous sections.
הוא: H1931 'he' vs H1933/H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 as a pronoun emphasizing the subject — 'he [is]'.
בלב ולב: H3820 'heart' — the phrase 'in heart and heart' is an idiom for being double-minded or of divided purpose, fitting the argument about internal division.
ההוא: H1931 used demonstratively — 'that [kingdom]'.
כן: H3651 'so/thus' vs H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'if so' is a logical connector in the argument.
שאני: ש + אני. H589 'I' vs H590 'a ship'. Chose H589 because 'that I drive out' is the accusation being addressed.
מגרש: H1644 'to drive out' — consistent with all previous uses in this text.
בעל: H1168 'Baal' — part of compound name Baal Zebub, same as section 5.
textual_notes: התדים has unclear consonants — likely השדים 'the demons' as in sections 5 and 10, with the same damaged text issue.

בלב ולב ('in heart and heart') is an unusual expression. It could mean 'divided in heart' (i.e., self-contradictory), or it could be an idiom for 'double-hearted/double-minded.' The meaning in context is that Satan would be working at cross purposes with himself.

translation_notes: אני: H589 'I' vs H590 'a ship'. Chose H589 — the speaker identifies himself as the one accused of driving out demons.
מגרשם: Listed candidate H1647 'Gereshom (proper name)' does not fit; the form is clearly מ+גרש+ם = participle of H1644 'to drive out' + 3mp suffix 'them'.
במה: Candidates: H1116 'an elevation/high place', H4100 'what?'. Chose H4100 because ב + מה = 'by what?' — an interrogative asking by what power their sons operate.
זה: H2088 'this' vs H2089 'a sheep'. Chose H2088 because 'on account of this' is a logical conclusion.
הם: H1992 'they' — emphatic pronoun emphasizing that their own sons will judge them.

אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet (adversative)'. Chose H61 because 'but/however' introduces the contrasting truth against the accusation — a natural adversative conjunction.
אני: H589 'I' — the speaker contrasts his own power source with Baal Zebub.

במאמר: H3982 'an edict/authoritative word' vs various forms of אמר. Chose H3982 because ב + מאמר = 'by the authoritative command' — this is the instrument by which demons are expelled, and it specifically denotes an authoritative decree rather than mere speech.
האל: Candidates: H408/409 'not', H410 'God/mighty one', H411/412 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because with the article ה it reads 'the God' — the source of the authoritative command.
מגרש: H1644 'to drive out' — consistent usage throughout the text.
textual_notes: התדים has the same damaged consonant issue as previous sections; reading as השדים 'the demons'.
א0מת contains a damaged character marked with 0. Most likely reads אמת (H571 'truth/firmness/certainty'), forming the assertion 'it is truth that...' or functioning adverbially as 'truly/indeed'.

The relationship between מאמר and the parallel tradition's 'finger of God' or 'spirit of God' is noteworthy — this text specifically uses 'edict/decree' (מאמר) rather than 'finger' (אצבע) or 'spirit' (רוח).

translation_notes: כאשר (כ + אשר): Candidates: H833 'be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כ + אשר = 'as/when', functioning as a temporal conjunction introducing the scenario.

החזק: Candidates: H2388 'to fasten/seize/strengthen', H2389 'strong/hard/violent', H2390 'powerful', H2391 'help', H2392 'power'. Chose H2389 because the article ה + adjective 'strong' fits as a substantive — 'the strong one' — describing the armed guardian.

שומר: Candidates: H7763 'Shomer (proper name)', also root שמר 'to keep/guard'. The consonants שומר are a participial form of שמר (H8104 — though not listed, the root is clear). H7763 is a proper name derived from this root. Context demands the verbal sense 'one who guards'. Assigning H7763 as placeholder since the participial form of שמר was not listed among candidates.
בשלום: Candidates: H7965 'safe/well/peace/prosperity', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. Chose H7965 because 'in peace/safety' naturally describes the state of possessions when guarded.
textual_notes: מזויין has no Strong's candidates provided. This appears to be a later Hebrew/Aramaic participial form meaning 'armed/equipped with weapons (זין)'. Not a classical biblical Hebrew form.
שומר is listed only as the proper name H7763, but contextually this is clearly the active participle of שמר 'to guard/keep'. The root שמר (H8104) was not among the provided candidates.

translation_notes: אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 because 'but/yet' serves as an adversative conjunction contrasting with the previous scenario of safety.
אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because this is a conditional clause — 'if another stronger one comes'.
הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'behold' introduces the dramatic consequence of the stronger one arriving.

שלו: Candidates: H7958 'quail', H7959 'security', H7960 'fault', H7961 'tranquil/careless/security'. In this context שלו functions as a possessive pronoun 'his' (later Hebrew form של + ו). None of the Strong's entries perfectly match this usage; H7961 is used as placeholder.
שהיה: Candidates for היה: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin'; for יה: H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 because ש + היה = 'that he was', forming a relative clause with a past tense verb of being.
textual_notes: הזיין has no Strong's candidates. This is 'the weapon/armor' from the root זין, a later Hebrew term for weaponry not found in classical biblical Hebrew lexicon.
באותן has no Strong's candidates. This is a later Hebrew demonstrative pronoun ב + אותן 'in those'.
