translation_notes: מן (MN): Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 'from', H4482 'musical chord'. Chose H4480 because 'from the wedding' is the only coherent reading with the verb 'returns'.
כי (KY): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: that/when/because'. Chose H3588 because a conjunction is required after למען to form the purpose clause.

ויגע (WYGʿ): Candidates: H3021 'to gasp/be exhausted/toil', H3022 'earnings', H3023 'tired'. The consonants י-ג-ע here in post-biblical Hebrew carry the sense of 'touch/strike/knock'. In context with 'at the door', knocking is the only coherent image — not exhaustion or earnings.
מיד (MYD): From H3027 'hand' — the prepositional phrase מיד means 'from [the] hand', i.e. immediately/at once.
textual_notes: המחכים: The root חכה (to wait/expect) is not listed in the candidates; only H2445 חכים (wise/Magian) appears. The participial form 'the ones waiting' fits the context perfectly (people waiting for their master), while 'wise men/Magians' would not cohere with the parable structure. This likely reflects a root not captured in the provided Strong's entries.

ויגע: Standard biblical Hebrew יגע means 'to toil/be weary', but in post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew נגע can mean 'to touch/knock'. The context 'at the door' demands 'knock'. This may reflect a later Hebrew usage not perfectly captured by the biblical lexicon entries provided.

translation_notes: הם (HM): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (region)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. Chose H1992 because 'they are the servants' forms a coherent emphatic identification.
אני (ʾNY): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because 'I say to you' is a coherent speech formula; 'a ship says to you' is nonsensical.

אומר (ʾWMR): The candidate provided is H201 'Omar (proper name)'. However, these consonants are clearly the participle of אמר (H559) 'to say'. The form אומר is the active participle 'saying/one who says'. Assigning H559.
בבוא (BBWʾ): H935 with prefix ב — 'at the coming of', an infinitive construct with preposition.
textual_notes: ומיד יברכם: 'Immediately he will bless them' — the subject of 'bless' is ambiguous; contextually it refers to the master blessing the watchful servants.

וישרתם: Could be parsed as 'and he will serve them' (3ms + 3mp suffix) or 'and they will serve him' — but the radical reversal of master serving servants is the point of the parable, so 'he will serve them' is the more striking and contextually coherent reading.

translation_notes: ואם (WʾM): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because 'and if he comes' forms a conditional clause, which is the only coherent reading.

במשמר (BMŠMR): Candidates: H4929 'guard/watch (the post or period)', H8104 'to guard', H8105 'wine sediment', H8106 'Shemer', H8107 'observance'. Chose H4929 because 'in the watch' (night watch period) fits perfectly with the temporal context of second or third watch.
שני (ŠNY): Candidates: H8144 'crimson', H8145 'second', H5204 'lamentation'. Chose H8145 because 'second watch' is the obvious temporal reference.
כן (KN): Candidates: H3651 'thus/so', H3652 'so', H3653 'stand/pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'finds them thus' (i.e., in this manner, still watching) is the coherent reading.
הם (HM): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — 'they are the servants' is a predication.
ההם (HHM): The article ה + H1992 הם = 'those' (demonstrative), referring to 'those servants'.
textual_notes: מאו<רים: The consonants appear damaged (indicated by angle bracket). The likely reading is מאושרים (blessed/fortunate) from אשר, or possibly מאורים (illuminated/radiant) from אור. Context — describing the state of the faithful servants — supports either 'blessed' or 'radiant'. I read it as 'blessed/fortunate' since it parallels the blessing in section 2.

translation_notes: אבל (ʾBL): Candidates: H56 'bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet' (adversative). Chose H61 because 'but/however' introduces a contrast with the preceding parable, which is the natural discourse function here.
זה (ZH): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'this you shall know' is coherent; 'a sheep you shall know' is not.
שאם (Š + ʾM): Candidates for אם: H517 'mother', H518 'if/conditional'. Chose H518 — 'that if the father knew' forms a conditional clause.

האב (HʾB): Candidates: H1 'father', H2 'father (Aramaic)', H3 'green plant', H4 'green plant'. Chose H1 because 'the father/householder' is the subject who would guard against a thief; a green plant would be nonsensical.

באי (BʾY): Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 because 'in which' (באי זו שעה = 'in which hour') is the interrogative required by context.
זו (ZW): Candidates: H2097 'this/that', H2098 'this/that', H2099 'Ziv (month)'. Chose H2097 — the demonstrative/relative 'which' completing 'in which hour'.
שעה (ŠʿH): Candidates: H8159 'to gaze/inspect', H8160 'a moment/hour'. Chose H8160 because 'hour/moment' fits with 'in which hour the thief comes'.
הגנב (HGNB): Candidates: H1589 'to steal', H1590 'a thief'. Chose H1590 because the article ה marks this as a noun 'the thief', not a verb.
עתיד (ʿTYD): Candidates: H6263 'prepared', H6264 'prepared/future/destined'. Chose H6264 because 'destined/about to come' captures the future intention of the thief.
ולא (WLʾ): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Chose H3808 — standard Hebrew negation.
textual_notes: האב: Literally 'the father' but in this context likely functions as 'the master of the house / householder' (a common usage). The parable compares the householder to someone who should stay vigilant.

אמת שיהיה ניעור: This could be read as 'truly he would have been awake' (apodosis of the conditional) or as an independent assertion 'it is certain that he would have been awake'. The former reading is more natural as the consequence of the 'if he had known' clause.

חפור: This appears to be the infinitive construct of חפר 'to dig', referring to the ancient method of breaking into mud-brick houses by digging through walls. 'Digging through of his house' = 'breaking into his house'.

translation_notes: כי (KY): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction'. Chose H3588 because 'for/because' introduces the reason for the command to stay awake.
בשעה (BŠʿH): H8160 'hour/moment' with prefix ב — 'in the hour'. This is the temporal expression matching section 4.
שלא (Š + Lʾ): H3808 'not' with prefix ש (relative particle) — 'that not', forming 'in the hour that you do not expect'.
בן (BN): Candidates: H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 because 'son of the human' is a coherent title/designation.

האדם (HʾDM): Candidates: H119 'to be ruddy', H120 'human being/mankind', H121 'Adam (name)', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'son of the human' (בן האדם) is a recognized designation meaning 'human one / mortal / representative human'.
textual_notes: ואתם: The provided candidate H864 'Etham (place name)' does not fit; this is clearly the 2mp pronoun 'and you' (ואתם). No Strong's number applies to the basic pronoun form here in the same way.

בן האדם: Could theoretically be 'son of Adam' (H121) reading it as a proper name, or 'son of the human' (H120) as a generic/titular designation. Context — an eschatological coming figure — supports the titular reading 'the Son of Humanity'.

translation_notes: אמר (ʾMR): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because 'said' as a verb of speech is the only coherent reading.
אדון (ʾDWN): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/master', H114 'Addon (name)'. Chose H113 because Kepha is addressing his master, not calling him by the name 'Addon'.
זה (ZH): Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'this matter/word' is coherent.

הדבר (HDBR): Candidates: H1907 'vizier', H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'this word/matter' (i.e., this parable/teaching) is what Kepha is asking about.
לכל (LKL): H3605 'all/every' with prefix ל — 'to all/everyone'.
textual_notes: אמור לנו זה הדבר או לכל: The syntax is ambiguous — it could be an imperative 'Say to us: [is] this matter [for us] or for all?' or it could be a question 'Are you saying this matter to us or to all?' Both yield essentially the same meaning.

translation_notes: אמר (ʾMR): Chose H559 'to say' — speech verb introducing discourse.
לכל (LKL): H3605 with prefix ל — 'for every/to all'. Context requires 'for every person who is faithful'.
האיש (HʾYŠ): H376 'man/person' — 'the man/person who is faithful' is the subject being described.
בחכמה (BḤKMH): Candidates: H2451 'wisdom', H2452 'wisdom (Aramaic)'. Chose H2451 — standard Hebrew 'in wisdom'.

משים (MŚYM): The root שים 'to set/place/appoint'. The candidates listed (H3220 'sea', H3221 'sea', H3222 'warm spring') are for the suffix ים, but here the whole word is a hiphil/qal participle of שים — 'the one who sets/appoints'. The ים suffix candidates are irrelevant.
האדון (HʾDWN): H113 'sovereign/master' — 'the master appoints over his house'.
על (ʿL): Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'over/upon', H5922 'over (Aramaic)', H5923 'yoke'. Chose H5921 — 'over his house' is the natural prepositional usage.

לבני (LBNY): Candidates: H3845 'Libni', H3846 'Libnite', H1137 'Bani', H1138 'Bunni', H5204 'lamentation'. All are proper names or unrelated. This is clearly ל + בני (construct of בנים 'sons') from H1121. 'To the sons of his house' = household members.
להם (LHM): Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'they'. This is ל + הם = 'to them'. Chose H1992.
textual_notes: The structure of this verse is complex. It appears to combine two sayings: (1) 'Let your loins be girded and your lamps [burning]' — a command to readiness, and (2) a question or statement about 'who then is the faithful and wise steward whom the master appoints over his household.' The transition between these two parts is abrupt in the Hebrew.
ועששיות: This word (lamps/lanterns) has no Strong's candidate provided. It appears to be a post-biblical Hebrew word for oil lamps or lanterns, from the root עשש.
משים: The candidates listed are for ים (sea/spring), but the word is clearly the participle of שים (to set/appoint). No exact Strong's match is provided for this parsing.
החטה: H2406 'wheat' — this could be literal (wheat rations) or figurative (provisions/sustenance). The parable context suggests provisions/food distribution.

translation_notes: הוא (HWʾ): Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 — the emphatic pronoun 'he is' in a predication 'blessed is he'.

עבד (ʿBD): Candidates: H5647 'to work/serve', H5648 'to do (Aramaic)', H5649 'servant (Aramaic)', H5650 'servant', H5651 'Ebed (name)', H5652 'deed'. Chose H5650 'servant' because the passage is about a servant/steward.

שרבו (ŠRBW): The ש is relative particle 'that/whose', רבו from רב meaning 'his master/great one'. Candidates for רבו: H7238 'increase of dignity', H7239 'myriad', H7240 'myriad (Aramaic)'. The word here means 'his master' — רב as a title of authority. H7238 (dignity/greatness) is closest to this usage.
כן (KN): Candidates: H3651 'thus/so', H3652 'so', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 — 'thus doing' means 'doing in this manner / faithfully carrying out his duties'.
textual_notes: מאו<ר: Damaged text (angle bracket). Same word as in section 3. Could be מאושר 'blessed/happy' or מאור 'light/radiant'. Both yield a positive exclamation about the servant. I read 'blessed/fortunate'.
שרבו: Could be parsed as ש + רבו 'that his master' or ש + רב + ו 'that his great-one'. Both yield the same meaning contextually.

translation_notes: אני (ʾNY): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 — 'I say' is the speech formula.
אומר (ʾWMR): H201 'Omar' is the only listed candidate, but this is clearly the participle of H559 אמר 'to say'. Assigning H559.

שעל (ŠʿL): Candidates: H8168 'palm/handful', or ש + על (H5921 'over/upon'). Chose ש + H5921 because 'that over all the things' is the coherent construction — the relative particle ש plus the preposition על. 'A handful of all the things' does not fit the context of granting authority.
כל (KL): Candidates: H3605 'all/whole', H3606 'all (Aramaic)'. Chose H3605.
textual_notes: שעל: This could theoretically be the single word H8168 שעל 'handful', but parsing as ש + על 'that over' is far more coherent with the following 'all the things that he holds, he will give him rule'.

translation_notes: אבל (ʾBL): Candidates: H56 'bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel', H60 'lamentation', H61 'but/yet/truly'. Chose H61 because 'but if that servant says' introduces the contrasting negative scenario after the positive one.
אם (ʾM): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/conditional'. Chose H518 — conditional 'if' introducing the hypothetical scenario.
עבד (ʿBD): Candidates: H5647 'to work', H5648 'to do', H5649 'servant (Aram.)', H5650 'servant', H5651 'Ebed', H5652 'deed'. Chose H5650 'servant' — continuing the parable about a servant.
לבוא (LBWʾ): H935 with prefix ל — infinitive 'to come'.

להכות (LHKWT): The candidate H3575 'Cuth/Cuthah' does not fit. This is clearly ל + הכות, the hiphil infinitive construct of נכה 'to strike/beat'. The provided candidate is irrelevant; the form means 'to strike/beat'.
textual_notes: וה<פחות: Damaged text. The likely reading is השפחות 'the maidservants' (from שפחה). The angle bracket indicates textual damage or uncertainty in the consonants.

להכות: The only Strong's candidate provided (H3575 'Cuthah') is a place name and clearly wrong for this context. The word is the hiphil infinitive of נכה (to strike), a common biblical Hebrew verb. No appropriate Strong's entry was provided among the candidates.

translation_notes: שעה (consonants שעה): Candidates: H8159 'to gaze/inspect', H8160 'a look, a moment'. Chose H8160 because the context pairs it with 'day' as a temporal marker — 'in a day… and in a moment/hour' — making a time-unit reading far more natural than 'gazing'.
textual_notes: אדוניו is not listed in the provided candidates; it is parsed as אדון + 3ms suffix, 'his lord/master'.
יקווהו appears to be a form of קוה (to wait, expect, hope) with 3ms suffix — 'he expects/awaits him'. No candidates were provided.
ידעה could be parsed as ידע + 3fs suffix (he knows her/it) or as 3ms imperfect of ידע. Context suggests 'he does not know [it]' referring to the hour.

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay, truly, yet'. Chose H61 because the passage introduces a contrasting case ('but that servant who…'), making the adversative/affirmative particle the natural fit.

עבד (consonants עבד): Candidates: H5647 'to work/serve', H5648 'to do/make', H5649 'a servant', H5650 'a servant', H5651 'Ebed (name)', H5652 'a deed'. Chose H5650 because the context describes 'that servant who knew' — a noun is required.
שידע (consonants ש+ידע): Candidates: H3045 'to know', H3046 'to know (Aramaic)', H3047 'Jada (name)'. Chose H3045 because ש + ידע = 'who knew', a standard Hebrew relative clause.
textual_notes: מוכה is parsed as a passive participle of נכה (to strike/smite) — 'struck/beaten'. The provided candidates under כה (H3541/H3542) are not relevant here; מוכה derives from the root נכה (H5221).
מזמין is a hiphil participle of זמן (to prepare/appoint), a post-biblical Hebrew form not in the standard Strong's list. The meaning 'preparing/readying' fits the context perfectly.
בעליו is parsed as בעל + 3ms suffix, 'his master/owner' (cf. H1167). No candidates were provided.

translation_notes: אדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because the context discusses 'a person to whom much is given' — a generic human referent.

דבר (consonants דבר) — all instances: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 throughout because the context speaks of things entrusted or given — 'a matter/thing' fits naturally.
רב (consonants רב): Candidates: H7227 'abundant', H7228 'archer', H7229 'abundant (Aramaic)', H7230 'abundance'. Chose H7227 because it modifies דבר as an adjective — 'an abundant/great matter'.
textual_notes: הגונים is a post-biblical Hebrew term meaning 'fitting, proper, worthy'. It has no standard Strong's entry. In context it means 'things deserving [of punishment]' — i.e., blameworthy deeds done in ignorance.
מועטים is a post-biblical Hebrew term meaning 'few, small in number'. No Strong's entry provided.

שדבר could be parsed as ש + דבר (noun: 'to whom a thing') or ש + דבר (verb: 'who spoke'). The passive ינתן ('is given') that follows favors reading דבר as a noun — 'a thing/matter [that] is given to him'.

translation_notes: אש (consonants אש): Candidates: H784 'fire', H785 'fire (Aramaic)', H786 'entity/there is', H787 'a foundation'. Chose H784 because the phrase 'to place ___ in the land' combined with the desire for it to be 'kindled' produces a coherent image of casting fire on the earth.
שום (consonants שום): Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7761 'to put (Aramaic)', H7762 'garlic'. Chose H7760 because 'to place fire' is a natural verbal construction.
חפץ (consonants חפץ): Candidates: H2654 'to desire/be pleased', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire'. Chose H2654 as the verbal form — 'I desire' — fitting the first-person statement.

מורד (consonants מורד): H4174 'a descent'. In context, this likely renders a concept of the fire being 'brought down' or 'descended/kindled'. The root ירד (to descend) in the hoph'al/muph'al participle yields מורד — 'brought down, caused to descend'.

The final phrase בשבתות ('on Sabbaths') seems somewhat redundant after 'on the coming Sabbath'. It may serve to specify that this was his custom on Sabbaths, or it may indicate 'on one of the Sabbaths' as a temporal marker.

שנים (consonants שנים): H8147 'two/twofold' — but here contextually this is שנים meaning 'years' (from שנה H8141), the plural form; the candidate list only shows H8147 but the word clearly functions as 'years' in context of a time duration following 'eighteen'.

למעלה (consonants למעלה): Candidates: H4608 'elevation/upward', H5927 'to ascend', H5929 'leaf'. Chose H4608 because 'to look upward' is a coherent physical image of someone bent over who cannot straighten up.
textual_notes: The word כלם could be read as כֻּלָּם 'all of them' (referring to the eighteen years) or from H3637 meaning 'humiliation/wounding'. The context of illness duration favors 'all of them' but a reading of 'humiliation' (a disease of humiliation for eighteen years) is also plausible.

היבוסי 'the Jebusite' is puzzling in a medical context. It may be a textual corruption or a colloquial/coded term for a particular type of affliction. The Jebusite identification (H2983) is the only consonantal match provided.
The % markers and numerical notation הי״ח suggest scribal annotations or damaged text. הי״ח appears to be an abbreviation for 'the eighteen' using Hebrew numerals יח.

translation_notes: ישוע (consonants ישוע): H3442 and H3443 both refer to Jeshua/Yeshua. Chose H3442 as the primary entry for the proper name.
ואמר (consonants אמר): Candidates include H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 because this is clearly a speech verb introducing direct discourse.

סרה (consonants סרה): H5626 'Sirah, a cistern' vs H5627 'apostasy/remission/turning aside'. Chose H5627 because the sense of 'departure/remission' fits perfectly: 'your illness has departed.' The root סור means to turn aside/depart, and סרה as a noun means removal or turning away.
textual_notes: The < symbol in א<ה suggests a damaged or uncertain letter. The word likely reads אשה (woman/wife) based on context — Yeshua addressing the ill woman.

translation_notes: עליה (consonants עליה): H5944 'upper room/lofty place'. However, in context this is clearly עָלֶיהָ 'upon her' (preposition על + 3fs suffix). The candidate H5944 shares consonants but the prepositional reading is the obvious contextual fit.
ומיד (consonants ומיד): Contains יד H3027 'hand'. However, ומיד here functions as the adverb 'immediately' (literally 'from hand' = 'at once'), a well-known Hebrew idiom.
עמדה (consonants עמדה): H5979 'a station/domicile'. However, this is clearly the verb עמד 'to stand' in 3fs perfect form. She stood up in her full height.

האל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/Mighty One', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because with the definite article ה, האל means 'the God/the Mighty One' — she praised God after being healed.

וענו (consonants ענו): H6035 'humble/depressed'. However, this is clearly the verb ענה 'to answer' in 3mp perfect with vav consecutive. The consonantal form ענו matches both, but in narrative context 'and they answered' is the correct reading.
בבית (consonants בית): H1004 'house' vs H3487 'sign of object'. Chose H1004 because בבית הכנסת is 'in the house of the assembly' — a synagogue.
ששת (consonants שת): H8351 'tumult', H8352 'Seth', H8353 'six'. Chose H8353 because ששת ימים 'six days' is the clear contextual meaning preceding 'days'.
הם (consonants הם): H1992 'they' fits as the copula: 'six days they are in the week'.
שבהן (consonants שבהן): The ש is the relative particle 'that/which', ב is 'in', and הן (H2004) is 'them (f.)' referring to the days. Together: 'in which'.
לעשות: The candidates H6219 'polished' and H6220 'Ashvath' are for עשות, but this is clearly the infinitive construct of עשה (H6213) 'to do/make' with ל prefix.
ולא (consonants לא): H3808 'not'. Simple negation: 'and not on the Sabbath'.
textual_notes: The < symbols in ב<בוע and ב<בת likely represent damaged or illegible letters. Based on context, ב<בוע is likely בשבוע 'in the week' and ב<בת is likely בשבת 'on the Sabbath'.
מלאים could theoretically connect to H366 'frightful' (אים), but contextually it is clearly מלאים 'full (of)' from מלא.

translation_notes: וענה (consonants ענה): H6030 'to heed/respond/answer' vs H6031 'to depress/afflict'. Chose H6030 because Yeshua is responding in dialogue.
ישוע: H3442 Jeshua/Yeshua — proper name, same as section 2.
הם: H1992 'them' — Yeshua answered 'them'.
ואמר: H559 'to say' — introducing direct speech.
כל: H3605 'every/all' — 'every one of you'.
אחד: H259 'one' vs H258 'to unify'. Chose H259 because 'each one of you' is the natural reading.
קשר: H7194 'to tie', H7195 'alliance/bond', H7196 'girdle'. Chose H7195 as the noun 'bond/tying/tether' — the thing that ties the animal, which is being untied.
החמור: H2543 'a male donkey' vs H2544 'Chamor (person)'. Chose H2543 — a donkey in a stall is a coherent domestic image.

הרפת: H7517 'a stall for cattle' — perfectly fits the image of untying an animal.
למים: H4325 'water' vs H3220 'sea'. Chose H4325 because leading a domestic animal to water (not to the sea) is the natural image.
textual_notes: ה<ור likely reads השור 'the ox' with the damaged letter being שׁ. The consonantal pattern שור (H7794) means 'ox/bull'.
רמאים 'deceivers' — this is the Hebrew word used where other traditions might say 'hypocrites'. The root רמה means to deceive/beguile.

translation_notes: אם: H517 'mother' vs H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because 'if so' (אם כן) is a logical connector introducing the a fortiori argument.
כן: H3651 'so/thus/right' vs H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 — אם כן 'if so/therefore' is a standard Hebrew phrase.
בת: H1323 'daughter' vs H1324 'bath (measure)'. Chose H1323 — 'daughter of Abraham' is the clear meaning.
כמה/וכמה: H3642 'to pine after' vs H4100 'how much/what'. Chose H4100 — כמה וכמה 'how much and how much' is a well-known Hebrew intensifying idiom meaning 'how much more so'.
שהשטן: H7853 'to accuse' vs H7854 'Satan/adversary'. Chose H7854 as the noun with the article: 'the Satan/the Adversary'.
קשר (second occurrence): H7194 'to tie', H7195 'bond/alliance', H7196 'girdle'. Chose H7195 as the noun 'bond' — 'from that bond'.

את: H852 'portent', H853 'object marker', H854 'with/near'. The sentence structure suggests either the object marker or possibly 'you (fs)'. Given the following word וראתה 'and you saw her', את here may be an emphatic 'you' addressing the audience, or it could be an object marker. Context slightly favors reading it in conjunction with what follows.
textual_notes: The final phrase בכריעה את וראתה is syntactically ambiguous. It could mean 'in bowing — you saw her' (addressing the audience, reminding them they witnessed her condition), or it could be parsed differently. The את could be 'you' (2fs/2ms) or the object marker.
ב<בת again has a damaged letter, almost certainly בשבת 'on the Sabbath'.
מאותו could mean 'from that' (מ + אותו) referring to the type of bond, or could be temporal 'from that [time]'.

translation_notes: וכאשר: H834 'who/which/when' — with כ and ו prefix: 'and when/as'. Chose H834 because כאשר 'when/as' is the standard temporal conjunction.
אמר: H559 'to say' — he spoke these words. Standard speech verb.

אלה: Candidates include H421 'bewail', H422 'imprecate', H424 'oak', H426 'God'. However, the consonants אלה also represent the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (H428, not listed but the standard reading). In context 'all these words' is the obvious meaning.
והעם: H5971 'people/nation' vs H5973 'with'. Chose H5971 — 'and the people rejoiced' is coherent.
שעשה: H6213 'to do/make' — 'that he did/made'.
textual_notes: אלה: The candidate list provided does not include H428 (the demonstrative 'these'), but the consonants אלה clearly function as 'these' in this context. The provided candidates (H421-H426) do not fit the syntax 'all these the words'.

translation_notes: ואז: H227 'then/at that time' — temporal transition.
אמר: H559 'to say' — introducing speech.
להם: The candidate H3859 'to rankle' does not fit. This is ל + הם (H1992 'them'): 'to them'.
למה: H4100 'what?' with ל prefix: 'to what?' — introducing the comparison question.
הוא: H1931 'he/it' — 'it is comparable'. Chose H1931 as the pronoun referring to the kingdom.

דומה: H1745 'silence/death' vs H1746 'Dumah (place)'. However, the consonants דומה also represent the adjective/participle from דמה 'to be like/comparable' (H1819, not listed). In context 'to what is it comparable' requires the meaning 'similar/comparable'. The provided candidates don't match but the consonantal reading is clear.
מלכות: H4438 'kingdom/dominion' — 'kingdom of heaven'.
שמים: H8064 'heaven/sky' vs H4325 'water'. Chose H8064 because 'kingdom of heaven' is the coherent phrase.
ומי: H4310 'who?' — 'and who can estimate it?'
אי: H335 'where?/which?' vs others. Chose H335 in the sense of 'which' — אי זה = 'which [one]'.
זה: H2088 'this/that' — אי זה דבר = 'which thing'.
דבר: H1697 'word/thing/matter' vs H1698 'pestilence'. Chose H1697 — 'to which thing shall it be likened' is coherent.
textual_notes: דומה: The provided candidates (H1745 'silence', H1746 'Dumah') do not include the common adjective meaning 'similar/comparable' from the root דמה. The consonantal text clearly intends 'comparable/resembling'.
משערו could be from שער 'to estimate/reckon/measure' with מ prefix (participle) and 3ms suffix: 'can estimate/measure it'. This fits the rhetorical question structure.

translation_notes: הנה: H2009 'lo!/behold' vs H2007 'themselves' vs H2008 'hither'. Chose H2009 because 'Behold, it is like...' introduces the parable naturally.
הוא: H1931 'it' — the subject pronoun referring to the kingdom.
של: H7944 'a fault' vs H7945 'on account of/of'. Chose H7945 — של חרדל 'of mustard' is a possessive/genitive particle.
שהאדם: H120 'a human being/mankind' — 'that the person sows'. Chose H120 over H121 'Adam (proper name)' because this is a generic parable about any person.
וגדל: H1431 'to grow/become large' vs H1434 'thread/tassel'. Chose H1431 — a seed that grows into a tree.
אילן: H363 'a tree' — the Aramaic/late Hebrew word for tree.
גדול: H1419 'great/large'.
עד: H5704 'until/as far as' — 'until the birds rest'. Temporal limit.

נחים could be from נוח 'to rest/settle' (participle plural) — birds resting/settling in the branches. This is the most natural reading.

translation_notes: ופעם: H6470 'to tap/beat' vs H6471 'a stroke/time/instance'. Chose H6471 — פעם אחרת 'another time/occasion' is a standard temporal phrase.
אמר: H559 'to say'. Speech verb introducing discourse.
משל: H4910 'to rule', H4911 'to use figurative language/liken', H4912 'a parable/proverb'. Chose H4912 as the noun 'parable/comparison' — the object of what he will set forth.
מלכות: H4438 'kingdom/dominion'.
יהוה: H3068 'YHWH/the Eternal'. Note that section 8 used שמים 'heaven' while this section uses יהוה directly — the same concept expressed differently.
הוא: H1931 'it' — pronoun for the kingdom.
דומה: As in section 8, the consonants mean 'comparable/similar' from the root דמה, though the candidates listed (H1745/H1746) don't include this common meaning.
textual_notes: אמשול could be parsed as 1cs imperfect of H4911 'I will liken/compare' — meaning 'I will set a parable'. This is the most natural reading.
דומה: Same issue as section 8 — the listed candidates don't include the participial/adjectival meaning 'comparable' from דמה, but the context demands it.

translation_notes: לשאור (consonants ל+שאור): The prefix ל is 'to/for'. The root שאור is not listed among the אור candidates (H215-H218), which all relate to light/flame/Ur. The consonants שאור correspond to H7603 (leaven/sourdough), which is the correct identification. The context of flour, hiding, and leavening confirms this decisively — a light-related reading would make no sense with flour becoming leavened.

עד: Candidates include H5703 'duration', H5704 'until', H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'menstrual flux'. Chose H5704 because the temporal conjunction 'until' fits the clause 'until it becomes leavened' perfectly.
textual_notes: The word שהא<ה appears to contain a scribal mark or damage at the < symbol. Reading as שהאשה ('that the woman'), which is a relative clause 'that a woman...' The ה before אשה would be the definite article, or this is simply the relative ש + אשה.

translation_notes: והלך: Candidates H1980 'to walk', H1981 'to walk (Aramaic)', H1982 'a journey/wayfarer', H1983 'a journey/toll'. Chose H1980 because the ו prefix + verb form indicates 'and he walked/went', a narrative action verb.

נגד: Candidates H5046 'to front/declare', H5047 'to flow', H5048 'opposite/in front of/toward', H5049 'opposite'. Chose H5048 because as a preposition 'toward/in the direction of' it fits the spatial sense of traveling toward Jerusalem.

והלשכו: This word is difficult. It could be parsed as ו+ה+לשכ+ו. The root may relate to teaching/instructing (a later Hebrew usage). The context of journeying and arriving at Jerusalem suggests an activity done along the way.
textual_notes: והלשכו is morphologically unusual. It might be parsed as a form related to לשכה (chamber, H3957) but that makes little contextual sense with the journey narrative. More likely it reflects a later Hebrew verbal form meaning 'teaching them' or 'instructing,' consistent with the broader narrative of a teacher traveling toward Jerusalem.

translation_notes: ואמר: Candidates H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because ו+אמר is a standard narrative form 'and he said'.

אדם: Candidates include H119 'flush/rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'a human being / a person' fits the context of someone addressing a question — a man asked him.
אחד: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts' or H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'one man' = 'a certain man' is a standard Hebrew construction.
אדון: H113 'sovereign/lord/master' or H114 'Addon (proper name)'. Chose H113 because this is clearly an address — a person calling someone 'Master/Lord'.
הם: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because the clause structure requires a pronoun: 'are they few?'
מן: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 'from (Aramaic)', H4482 'a musical chord'. Chose H4480 because 'from those' fits the response structure.
textual_notes: The ending 'מן אותם אותם' is puzzling — the doubled אותם may indicate emphasis ('from those very ones') or could reflect a scribal repetition/dittography. Alternatively, the phrase could be an incomplete sentence, with the second אותם beginning a new thought that continues in the next section. The translation attempts to read it as emphatic repetition.

translation_notes: בפתח: Candidates H6605 'to open wide', H6606 'to open', H6607 'an opening/door/entrance way', H6608 'opening (figurative)/disclosure'. Chose H6607 because the prefix ב ('in/through') + noun = 'through the doorway/entrance'. A verb form would not take the preposition ב this way in context.

הצר: Candidates H6862 'narrow/tight place/trouble', H6863 'Tser (place)', H6864 'a stone/knife', H6865 'Tsor/Tyre'. Chose H6862 because 'the narrow' as an adjective modifying 'opening/doorway' produces a coherent physical image of a narrow entrance.
אני: H589 'I' or H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because 'I say to you' is a coherent speech formula; 'a ship says to you' is nonsensical.
כי: H3587 'a brand or scar' or H3588 'conjunction: that/because'. Chose H3588 because a conjunction introducing the clause 'that many will desire...' is syntactically required.

אומר: The only listed candidate is H201 'Omar (proper name)', but the consonants אומר clearly represent the qal active participle of H559 (אמר 'to say'), i.e., 'saying/am saying'. The participial form אומר is standard Hebrew.
textual_notes: ואתם: The only Strong's candidate listed is H864 'Etham, a place in the Desert,' but the consonants אתם universally function as the second-person plural pronoun 'you' in Hebrew. No Strong's number is assigned to this pronoun in the provided candidates, but the reading is unambiguous from context.

translation_notes: וכאשר: The כ prefix + אשר. Candidates for אשר include H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כאשר = 'when/as' is a standard temporal conjunction, fitting the narrative structure perfectly.

אב: H1 'father', H2 'father (Aramaic)', H3 'green plant', H4 'green plant (Aramaic)'. Chose H1 because 'the father of the company/household' = the master of the house, which fits the door-shutting scenario. A 'green plant of the company' makes no sense.
אל: Candidates include H408 'not', H410 'mighty/God', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/toward'. Chose H413 because 'call toward the entrance' produces a coherent image of people calling out at a door.
הפתח: H6605 'to open', H6606 'to open', H6607 'entrance/doorway', H6608 'disclosure'. Chose H6607 because with the article ה this is a noun 'the entrance', the place where they call out.
פתח: Same consonants as above. Here chose H6605 'to open' because this is an imperative: 'Open for us!' — a verb command directed at the master.
והוא: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 because 'and he will answer' requires a pronoun subject.

יענה: The only listed candidate is H3284 'ostrich', but the consonants ענה (H6030 'to answer/respond') in imperfect 3ms form = יענה. The ostrich reading is absurd in context. This is clearly the verb 'he will answer'.

מכיר: H4353 'Makir (proper name)' or H3600 'cooking range' (from כיר). Neither fits. The consonants מכיר represent the hiphil participle of נכר (H5234 'to recognize/acknowledge'). In context 'I do not recognize you' is the only coherent reading.
textual_notes: הסיעה: Not in the provided candidates. This appears to be a post-biblical Hebrew term meaning 'the group/company/party.' It could alternatively relate to the root נסע (to journey/travel), but 'father of the company/household' fits the parable context of a householder.
איני: This is a compound negative form (אין + suffix י = 'I am not / I do not'), standard in later Hebrew. No Strong's candidates were provided.

מכיר: Neither provided candidate (H4353 Makir, H3600 cooking range) fits. This is almost certainly the hiphil participle of נכר (H5234), meaning 'recognizing.' The phrase 'I do not recognize you' is contextually demanded.

translation_notes: לאמר: Candidates for אמר include H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because ל+אמר = the infinitive construct 'to say', a standard Hebrew construction after verbs of beginning.
ואתה: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive (Aramaic)', H859 'you (singular)'. Chose H859 because 'and you taught us' requires a pronoun subject. 'And arrived taught us' makes no sense.
והוא: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 as the pronoun 'and he' introducing the speech.
לא: H3808 'not' or H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Chose H3808 as this is standard Hebrew negation.
מאין: The מ prefix + אין. Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where? (whence)', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H370 because מ+אין = 'from where' fits 'I did not know from where you are.'

און: H202 'ability/power/wealth', H203 'On (Israelite)', H204 'On (city)', H205 'nothingness/trouble/vanity/wickedness', H206 'Aven (places)'. Chose H205 because 'workers of wickedness/iniquity' is a coherent moral condemnation in this context of rejection.
ברוע: H7321 'to mar/break; to shout'. The noun form רוע can mean 'evil/badness' (related to רע). In context 'in evil of heart' = 'with wicked heart' fits the condemnation.
לב: H3820 'the heart' or H3821 'the heart (Aramaic)'. Chose H3820 as this is standard Hebrew.
textual_notes: ממני: The provided candidates (H4507 'Fate idol', H4508 'Minni province', H5204 'lamentation') do not match the obvious reading. ממני is simply the preposition מן + first person singular suffix = 'from me'. This is standard Hebrew morphology.

ברוע לב: This phrase could be parsed as 'in the evil of heart' or 'in the breaking of heart'. The root רוע (H7321) has both senses — marring/breaking and shouting. Reading as 'evil/wickedness of heart' seems most natural as part of the condemnation, though 'with broken heart' (i.e., gnashing/anguish) is also possible given the weeping context in the next section.

translation_notes: ושם: H8033 'there', H8034 'name/appellation', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name (Aramaic)'. Chose H8033 because 'and there will be weeping' establishes a location/state. 'And a name will be weeping' is incoherent.
בכי: H1065 'weeping' or כי H3587 'brand/scar' / H3588 'conjunction'. Chose H1065 because 'weeping' paired with 'gnashing of teeth' produces the expected image of anguish and distress.
כאשר: H834 'when/that'. Chose H834 because כ+אשר = 'when' introduces the temporal clause 'when you see Abraham...'

האל: Candidates H408 'not', H410 'mighty/God', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/toward'. None of these fit well. However, the consonants here likely represent a defective or unusual spelling. In context, after 'shaking/gnashing of,' a body part is expected. This likely reads as a form meaning 'the teeth' (cf. later Hebrew). The word may be a corruption or variant form. None of the Strong's candidates for אל apply naturally here.
textual_notes: האל: This is the most problematic word in the section. The Strong's candidates (not, mighty/God, these, to) do not produce a coherent image after 'shaking/gnashing of.' The expected word would be שנים (teeth). האל may be a scribal variant, a later Hebrew form, or a textual corruption. I have tentatively read it as 'the teeth' based on contextual demand (weeping + gnashing of teeth is a well-known Hebrew idiom for distress), but this reading requires a form not attested in the provided dictionary entries.
והרעשת: Likely from the root רעש (to shake/quake, H7493) in a causative or nominal form + construct ending ת. 'The shaking/quaking of' = gnashing/grinding, describing teeth.

translation_notes: ממזרח: Candidates — H4217 'sunrise/the east' vs. H2224 'to irradiate/rise', H2225 'rising of light', H2226 'Zerach (name)'. Chose H4217 because מ+מזרח = 'from the east' as a directional noun with the preposition מן is the natural geographic reading, paired with west, north, and south.
וממערב: H4627 'traffic/mercantile goods' or H4628 'the west'. Chose H4628 because the geographic pairing with east, north, and south demands 'from the west.'
textual_notes: ומ]צפון[ and ומ]תימן[: These words appear to have damage or editorial marks (brackets in the source text). The consonants צפון and תימן are standard Hebrew for 'north' and 'south' respectively, with the מ prefix indicating 'from.'

ויסובו: From the root סבב (to turn, surround, go around). In this context it likely means 'recline' (at a banquet) or 'take their seats' — i.e., join the feast in the kingdom. The root can convey gathering around or taking one's place at a table.

translation_notes: והנה: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold!', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'and behold' is a standard attention-calling interjection that fits the declarative tone of this pronouncement.
textual_notes: This section appears to be the first half of a well-known reversal saying. The text as given ends abruptly at 'first' — the expected continuation (something like 'will be last, and those who were last will be first') is absent from this section. Either the manuscript is fragmentary here, or the second half belongs to a subsequent section not provided.

translation_notes: שעה (שעה): Candidates: H8159 'to gaze/inspect', H8160 'a moment'. Chose H8160 because 'in that moment' is the natural temporal phrase introducing a narrative event.
ומקצת (קצת): Candidates: H7117 'a portion', H7118 'a portion (Aramaic)'. Both mean the same; chose H7117 as the Hebrew form. 'And some of the Pharisees' fits the context of a subset approaching.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: for/because'. Chose H3588 because this is clearly a causal conjunction introducing the reason for the warning.

ישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua/Yeshua (name)', H3443 same. Chose H3442 as the standard entry for the personal name.

אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because a finite verb 'said' is required by the narrative syntax.
להם: The prefix ל + הם. Candidates for הם: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — 'to them' is the natural indirect object here.

שועל: Candidates: H7776 'a jackal/fox', H7777 'Shual (name)'. Also על candidates but שועל as a whole word is clearly H7776 'fox/jackal' — Yeshua is calling Herod a fox, which fits the warning about Herod in the prior section.

מגרש: Candidates: H4054 'suburb/open country', H1643 'grain', H1644 'to drive out/expel', H1645 'produce'. Chose H1644 because 'driving out demons' is the coherent action described here — a participle form of גרש 'to drive out'.
תם: Candidates: H8535 'complete/pious/gentle', H8536 'there', H8537 'completeness/innocence'. Chose H8535 because 'I will be complete' paired with 'and ended' describes the conclusion of his work.
ואפס: Candidates: H656 'to disappear/cease', H657 'cessation/end'. Chose H656 as a verb form paralleling 'I will be complete' — 'and I will cease/come to an end'.
textual_notes: ה<דים and ה<לישי have damaged/missing consonants (marked with <). From context, ה<דים is almost certainly השדים (demons/shedim) and ה<לישי is השלישי (the third). These reconstructions are based on narrative logic but the actual consonants are incomplete.

תם ואפס could be read as two nouns ('completion and cessation') or as adjective + verb. The phrase 'I will be תם ואפס' likely means 'I will be finished and done' — describing the completion of his mission.

translation_notes: רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/although', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because 'only/nevertheless' is the natural adverbial conjunction opening a qualifying statement.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because'. Chose H3588 — causal conjunction introducing the reason.
אין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 because 'there is not fitting' = 'it is not fitting' is the natural construction.
שנביא: Candidates: H5029 'a prophet (Aramaic)', H5030 'a prophet/inspired man'. Chose H5030 as the Hebrew form. The ש prefix is the relative particle 'that'.

יראה: The consonants ירא + ה could be from ראה 'to see' (niphal: 'be seen') or from H3374 'fear/reverence'. In context, 'a prophet should perish' is the expected meaning (paralleling Luke 13:33 tradition), but the consonants יראה most naturally read as a niphal of ראה — 'should be seen/should appear'. However, this could also be a scribal form meaning 'should perish' from a different root. I've assigned H3374 as the listed candidate but the reading 'be seen/appear' from ראה is more likely.
textual_notes: למחףרת has a damaged consonant (marked with ף). This is almost certainly למחרת 'for the morrow/next day'.

יראה is genuinely ambiguous: the consonants could be niphal of ראה 'to be seen/appear' or could relate to H3374 'fear'. The expected meaning in this context of prophets and Jerusalem is 'should perish' (from אבד), but that root is not present. 'Should be seen/should appear outside of Jerusalem' makes reasonable sense — it is not fitting for a prophet to appear/meet his end outside Jerusalem. The Strong's candidate H3374 is the only one listed, but the consonants more naturally parse as a niphal form of ראה (H7200).

translation_notes: כמה: Candidates: H3642 'to pine after', or כ + מה where H4100 'what/how'. Chose H4100 with prefix כ — 'how many' is the natural reading before 'times' (פעמים).
תחת: Candidates: H8478 'underneath/below', H8479 same (Aramaic), H8480 'Tachath (name)'. Chose H8478 because 'under her wings' is the coherent physical image of a hen sheltering chicks.
ולא: Chose H3808 'not' — simple negation 'and not'.
textual_notes: יכולתי — the consonants appear to be a first-person form ('I was able'), but contextually the meaning seems to be 'you (Jerusalem) were not willing' (second person). This may reflect a textual variant where the final word is ולא אביתם/יכלתם (you were not willing/able) condensed. The manuscript reads as first person 'I was not able' which is also a valid reading: 'and I was not able [to gather them]'.

translation_notes: והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', or from נה H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'and behold' is the natural exclamatory introduction to a prophetic declaration.
מאין: From מ + אין. Candidates for אין: H369 'non-entity/negative', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 — 'from without' = 'without' or 'devoid of', modifying 'one inhabiting'.
ואני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 — 'and I' is the obvious reading as subject of 'say'.
שזה: ש + זה. Candidates for זה: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'that this' introduces the declaration.
לא: H3808 'not' — simple negation.
textual_notes: The phrase 'שזה לא יהיה' is ambiguous: it could mean 'that this will not happen' (i.e., you will not see me) or could be an incomplete sentence trailing into a following section. The text as it stands reads as a self-contained prophetic warning.

14.summary: Phase 1 consonantal translation — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided. Literal and amplified readings produced independently from consonantal Hebrew.

translation_notes: בבית (consonants בית): Candidates: H1004 'a house', H1005 (same), H1006 'Bajith (place name)', H3487 'sign of object'. Chose H1004 because the context describes entering a physical dwelling for a meal.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because it functions as a numeral modifying 'rulers' — one of the rulers.

משר (consonants שר): Candidates: H8269 'a head person/ruler', H8270 'a string/cord'. Chose H8269 because the passage describes a social setting — entering the house of a prominent person among the Pharisees.
פת: Candidates: H6595 'a bit/morsel (of bread)', H6596 'a hole/hinge'. Chose H6595 because the context is eating — 'to eat bread/a morsel' is a standard Hebrew idiom for dining.

והנם: The only Strong's candidate is H2011 'Hinnom (a Jebusite name)' which makes no sense here. This is clearly a pronominal form וְהֵנָּם / וְהִנָּם meaning 'and they/and behold they,' a common Mishnaic Hebrew demonstrative pronoun not well represented in Strong's. Translated as 'and they [were].'
textual_notes: ונעשת — This form does not appear in Strong's candidates. It appears to be a Mishnaic/late Hebrew form meaning 'and it happened/came to pass,' possibly from עשה in a reflexive stem or a variant of ויהי. No Strong's number assigned.
כשנכנס — A compound form (כש + נכנס) meaning 'when he entered,' using the late Hebrew verb נכנס. No Strong's candidates provided.
הפרושים — 'the Pharisees' — a post-biblical term for the sect, derived from פרש (to separate). No Strong's candidates given.
ב&בת — Appears to be בשבת 'on the Sabbath' with the shin corrupted or marked. The ampersand likely indicates a damaged or uncertain letter.
והנם — The Strong's candidate H2011 (Hinnom) is clearly wrong for this context. This must be a pronominal/demonstrative form.

translation_notes: והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because this is a narrative introduction drawing attention to a new character — 'and behold' fits perfectly.
איש: Candidates: H376 'a man/individual', H377 'to act manly'. Chose H376 because a noun is needed as the subject of the clause.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 — 'one man' meaning 'a certain man.'
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 because the context requires a copula — the man 'was' before him.
textual_notes: משוקה — No Strong's candidates provided. The consonants שקה relate to drinking/watering (H8248 שקה 'to give drink') but in a passive/nominal form could indicate being 'waterlogged' or swollen, i.e., suffering from dropsy (edema). This is consistent with the Mishnaic Hebrew medical term. The root could also relate to שוק (H7785 'leg/thigh') but 'swollen with fluid' fits the narrative better, as the passage sets up a healing scenario.
לפניו — Compound form: ל + פני + ו = 'before him / to his face.' פנים (H6440) with preposition and suffix. No ambiguity in meaning.

translation_notes: וישוע: Candidates: H3442 and H3443, both 'Jeshua/Yeshua.' Chose H3442 as the standard entry for this proper name.

ענה: Candidates: H6030 'to heed/respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 (Aramaic 'respond'), H6033 (Aramaic 'depress'), H6034 'Anah (name)'. Chose H6030 because 'answered and said' is the classic Hebrew narrative formula for responding in speech.

ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 (Aramaic 'to say'), H561 'something said', H562 (same), H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because the verb 'said' following 'answered' is the standard Hebrew speech formula.
הדת: Candidates: H1881 'a royal edict/statute/law', H1882 (same, Aramaic). Chose H1881 because 'wise ones of the law' describes Torah scholars, the standard designation for legal experts.
textual_notes: לחכמי — No Strong's candidates given. From חכם (H2450 'wise') in construct plural with ל preposition: 'to the wise ones of.' This is a term for Torah scholars/legal experts, equivalent to 'lawyers' or 'scribes' in other traditions.

לעשות — The candidates H6219 'shining/polished' and H6220 'Ashvath (name)' do not fit. This is clearly the infinitive construct of עשה (H6213 'to do/make') with ל preposition, a standard Hebrew construction meaning 'to do/perform.' The provided Strong's candidates match different consonantal roots.

הראוי — No Strong's candidates provided. This appears to be from ראה (to see) in a passive participial form meaning 'seen as fitting/proper/permitted' — a standard Mishnaic Hebrew term for legal permissibility.
רפואה — No Strong's candidates provided. From רפא (H7495 'to heal') — the noun form meaning 'healing/remedy/cure.'
ב&בת — Same as section 1, likely בשבת 'on the Sabbath' with damaged/marked shin.

translation_notes: והוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/self', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because 'and he healed' requires the personal pronoun.

האדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to be ruddy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. Chose H120 because 'the man' (the sick person just described) is the coherent referent of healing.
textual_notes: ועזבו could mean 'and he left him' or 'and he released/sent him away'. Both are plausible from the root עזב (to leave/forsake/release). In a healing context, 'released him' or 'let him go' is the more natural reading.

translation_notes: וענה (consonants ענה): Candidates: H6030 'to answer', H6031 'to afflict'. Chose H6030 as the dialogue continuation.
להם: ל + הם. Chose H1992 'them' as the prepositional object.
ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559.

אי (consonants אי): Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Chose H335 because 'which' (interrogative) paired with זה = 'which one' makes sense in a rhetorical question.
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because אי זה = 'which one' is a standard interrogative construction.
אם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'a mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because 'if his ox falls' is the conditional clause.
בבור (consonants בור): Candidates: H952 'to bore/examine', H953 'a pit/cistern'. Chose H953 because 'falling into a pit' is the coherent physical image.
textual_notes: שורו: The provided candidate for רו is H7299 'aspect', which does not fit. The consonants שור clearly point to 'ox' (from שור, an ox/bull), with the possessive suffix ו. This is a standard Hebrew word not adequately covered by the candidate list.

The phrase שלא יעלהו could be parsed as 'that not he-will-raise-it' (rhetorical question expecting the answer 'of course he would') or as a statement. The rhetorical question reading is more coherent.

translation_notes: ולא (consonants לא): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 same. Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation.

לענות: The provided candidate H6039 'affliction' (noun) does not fit the infinitive construct context. This is ל + ענות, the infinitive of ענה (H6030 'to answer'). The ל prefix marks purpose/infinitive: 'to answer'.
textual_notes: לענות could theoretically derive from H6031 'to afflict' (infinitive: 'to afflict him') but context of a debate clearly favors 'to answer him' from H6030.

translation_notes: ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559.

דבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'a pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'a word/matter' = a teaching/parable fits the context of telling a story to guests.
כאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness'. Chose H834 with כ prefix = 'as/when', because 'when they chose' introduces the observed action.
מושבות: The candidate H7622 'exile/captivity' does not fit. The consonants מושבות point to the plural of מושב (a seat/dwelling, from ישב 'to sit'). Context of a banquet clearly favors 'seats'.
וכסא (consonants כסא): Candidates: H3677 'full moon/festival', H3678 'throne/seat'. Chose H3678 because 'seat of honor' at a banquet is the coherent image.
textual_notes: נשמע is ambiguous: it could be a niphal participle of שמע 'to hear' (meaning 'heard' or 'a thing heard', i.e. a parable/teaching), or it could be parsed differently. In this context it seems to function as a descriptor of דבר — 'a word heard' meaning a parable or teaching.
דבר נשמע together could mean 'a parable' (literally 'a word/matter [to be] heard') or could be two separate clauses. The parable reading fits since what follows is clearly a teaching story.

translation_notes: אשר: Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness'. Chose H834 as the conjunction 'when' paired with כ.
אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative negation)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/near'. Chose H408 because אל + imperfect תשב = 'do not sit', the standard prohibitive construction.

בראש (consonants ראש): Candidates: H7217 'head/sum', H7218 'head (most applications)', H7219 'poison plant', H7220 'Rosh'. Chose H7218 because 'at the head [place]' of a banquet table is the coherent image.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'because/for'. Chose H3588 as the causal conjunction.
באולי: Candidates: H194 'perhaps', H195 'Ulai river', H196 'foolish/impious'. Chose H194 because 'perhaps someone more honored' is the natural reasoning in a banquet context.
שם (consonants שם): Candidates: H8033 'there/then', H8034 'a name/honor', H8035 'Shem'. Chose H8033 'there' because 'has been called there' = invited to that same seat.
תן: The candidate H8565 'a sea-serpent/jackal' does not fit. This is the imperative of נתן 'to give'. Context demands 'give [your] place'.
מקום (consonants מקום/קום): Candidates: H4725 'a place/standing spot', H6965 'to rise'. Chose H4725 because 'give place' = yield your spot.
לזה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'to this one' = to this person.
ואז: H227 'then/therefore'. Straightforward temporal conjunction.

מטה (first, consonants מטה): Candidates: H4294 'a branch/rod/tribe', H4295 'downward/below', H4296 'a bed', H4297 'distortion', H4298 'expansion'. Chose H4295 because 'you will go down lower' is the coherent image of descending to a lower seat.
מטה (second): Same candidates. Chose H4295 again. The repetition מטה מטה emphasizes 'lower and lower' or 'to the very lowest place'.
textual_notes: שזמנך contains the root זמן (to appoint/invite) with a relative prefix ש and 2ms suffix ך — 'the one who invited you'. This is a post-biblical Hebrew construction.
תן is clearly the imperative of נתן despite the candidate H8565 being unrelated.

translation_notes: רק (consonants רק): Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because 'but/rather' introduces the contrasting instruction after the negative example.
כאשר: Chose H834 'when' with כ prefix, same as previous sections.
במקום: Candidates: H4725 'a place', H6965 'to rise'. Chose H4725 'in the place'.
היותר: H3148 'more/most'. The ה prefix makes it superlative: 'the most'.
אחרון: H314 'last/hinder/western'. 'The most last' = the lowest/last place.

במעלה (consonants מעלה/עלה): Candidates: H4608 'elevation/platform', H4609 'elevation/rank/ascent', H5927 'to ascend'. Chose H4609 because 'in rank/elevation' qualifies 'the most last' — the lowest in rank.
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 as the purpose conjunction.

עלה (consonants עלה): Candidates: H5927 'to ascend', H5928 'a holocaust', H5929 'a leaf', H5930 'a step/stairs', H5931 'a pretext'. Chose H5927 because 'come up!' is the imperative invitation to ascend to a higher seat.
הנה (consonants הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/here', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2008 because 'come up here/hither' is the directional adverb matching the invitation.
מעלה (second instance): Candidates: H4608 'elevation', H4609 'elevation/rank'. Chose H4609 because 'you will gain elevation/honor' before the guests is the culminating reward image.
לפני: H3942 'anterior/before'. Straightforward prepositional usage.
textual_notes: שכשיבוא is a compound: ש + כש + יבוא ('that when he comes'). This is a post-biblical Hebrew construction using multiple relative/temporal particles.
אהוב could be parsed as a passive participle 'beloved/loved one' or as an adjective used as a term of address 'friend/dear one'. Both yield essentially the same meaning in this context.
במעלה in both occurrences could be H4608 or H4609; both mean 'elevation'. H4609 is chosen for both as it better captures the figurative sense of rank/status in a banquet setting.

translation_notes: כי (consonants כי): Candidates: H3587 'a brand or scar', H3588 'conjunction: for, because, that'. Chose H3588 because the word introduces a causal or explanatory clause linking the two halves of the saying.
שפלות (consonants שפלות): Only candidate H8220 'remissness/lowliness'. Fits the context of being brought low as a consequence of self-exaltation.
textual_notes: להתנשאות: The hitpael infinitive construct of נשא could mean 'to exalt oneself' or 'to be exalted.' In this antithetical parallelism (the one who lowers himself → exaltation), the passive sense 'to be exalted' fits best as the reward for humility.

translation_notes: אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates include H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 because this is clearly a speech-introduction verb ('and he said').

לאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness'. Chose H834 as the relative pronoun 'to the one who' — it introduces the person who invited him.
בקר (consonants בקר): Candidates: H1239 'to plough/inspect', H1241 'cattle', H1242 'morning'. Chose H1242 'morning' because it pairs with ערב 'evening' to describe two types of meals.

ערב (consonants ערב): Candidates: H6148 'to intermix/traffic', H6149 'to be agreeable', H6150 'to grow dusky', H6153 'dusk/evening'. Chose H6153 'evening' as it pairs with בקר 'morning' for morning meal vs. evening meal.
אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/near'. Chose H408 as the negative particle with the imperfect תרצה — 'do not desire.'

תרצה: The candidates list H8656 (Tirtsah, a place name). However, the consonants ת-ר-צ-ה clearly match the verb רצה (H7521, 'to desire/be pleased') in 2ms imperfect form. The place name Tirtsah does not fit a verbal context following אל. Chose to read as verb form of רצה.

באולי (consonants אולי): Candidates: H194 'perhaps', H195 'Ulai river', H196 'foolish/impious'. Chose H194 'perhaps' with prefix ב — the clause warns against inviting those who might reciprocate, making it a transactional exchange.
שאתה (consonants אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H859 'you (pronoun)'. Chose H859 — 'that you' as the subject of 'are calling.'

גמול (consonants גמול): Candidates: H1576 'recompense/requital', H1577 'Gamul (name)'. Chose H1576 — the sentence warns against inviting people who will repay you, i.e., making hospitality transactional.
ה<כנים: The damaged letter < likely represents שׁ, yielding השכנים 'the neighbors' (from H7934 שכן). This fits the list of people not to invite: friends, brothers, relatives, wealthy neighbors.
textual_notes: תרצה: The only Strong's candidate provided is H8656 (Tirtsah, a place name), but the grammatical context requires a 2ms imperfect verb. The consonants match רצה (H7521) perfectly. This is almost certainly the verb 'to desire/wish.'

ה<כנים: The damaged letter makes this word uncertain. Reading as השכנים (neighbors) fits the context of a list of social contacts. Alternatively, it could be a form of הכנים (those prepared/established).
קורא: The only candidate given is H6981 (Kore, a proper name), but the context demands a participle of קרא (H7121) 'calling/inviting.' The consonants are identical.

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 as an adversative conjunction 'but/rather' — it contrasts with the previous instruction about who NOT to invite.
קרא (consonants קרא): Candidates: H7121 'to call out/address by name', H7122 'to encounter', H7124 'partridge'. Chose H7121 'call/summon' — the imperative to invite guests.
textual_notes: והנטולים: No Strong's candidates were provided. The root נטל can mean 'to lift/carry' or 'to be taken away' — suggesting those whose limbs have been taken from them (i.e., the crippled/maimed). This is post-biblical Hebrew vocabulary.

translation_notes: וברוך: The candidate H1263 is the proper name Baruk. However, the consonants ברוך are the standard passive participle of ברך (H1288) meaning 'blessed.' The sentence 'and blessed you will be' is coherent; the proper name is not.
אין (consonants אין): Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 — 'there is not to them' = they do not have.

והשכר (consonants שכר): Candidates: H7936 'to hire', H7937 'to become tipsy', H7938 'wages', H7939 'payment/salary/compensation', H7941 'intoxicant'. Chose H7939 'reward/payment' — the noun with definite article, referring to divine recompense.
<יגמלוך: The damaged letter is likely ש, yielding שיגמלוך 'that they will repay you' (from גמל H1580). This continues the theme from section 2 about reciprocal repayment.
textual_notes: בתחיית: This noun form (תחייה) from the root חיה does not have a direct Strong's entry as a noun. It is a post-biblical Hebrew formation meaning 'resurrection/revival.' The concept 'resurrection of the righteous' is clear from context.
<יגמלוך: The damaged first letter is most likely ש (yielding שיגמלוך, 'that they will repay you'), though it could theoretically be another letter.

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness'. Chose H834 — with prefix כ it forms כאשר 'when/as,' a temporal conjunction.
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 'one' — 'one of his disciples.'
שמע (consonants שמע): Candidates: H8085 'to hear', H8087-8090 proper names/nouns. Chose H8085 — 'heard' as the completed action verb.

אלה (consonants אלה): Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H426 'God'. None of these match. The demonstrative pronoun אלה 'these' (H428) shares these consonants and fits perfectly: 'these words.'
אמר: Chose H559 'to say' — speech introduction verb.
מאו<ר: The damaged letter suggests מאושר 'happy/blessed' (from the root אשר H833/H835). The ש is the missing letter. This exclamation 'blessed/happy will be...' fits the context.
פת (consonants פת): Candidates: H6595 'a bit/morsel (of bread)', H6596 'a hole/hinge'. Chose H6595 — eating bread/a morsel in the kingdom makes perfect sense.
מי (consonants מי): Only candidate H4310 'who/whoever'. Fits as the indefinite 'whoever will eat.'
textual_notes: אלה: The provided candidates do not include the demonstrative pronoun אלה (H428, 'these'), but the consonants are identical and the context ('these words') demands it. The candidates listed (bewail, adjure, oak, God) do not fit.

מאו<ר: With the damaged letter, this most likely reads מאושר (blessed/happy). The אשר root (H833/H835) supports this. An alternative reading מאור (H3974, 'light/luminary') is possible if the damaged letter is different, but 'happy/blessed will be' fits the exclamatory context better.

translation_notes: אדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam (name)', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom'. Chose H120 — 'a man/person,' the subject of the parable.
אחד: Chose H259 'one' — used idiomatically as 'a certain [man].'
אמר: Chose H559 'to say.'

translation_notes: אמר: Chose H559 'to say' — narrative verb of speech.

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction for/because/that'. Introducing a declaration; chose H3588.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. First person pronoun before a verb of speech; chose H589.

שום: Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7762 'garlic'. In post-biblical Hebrew שום functions as 'any/no' (as in שום אדם = no person/any person). Chose H7760 as the closest root.
אדם: Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. 'Man/person' fits; chose H120.

textual_notes: The text shows כ and י as separate words, which together form כי (for/because/that). This may be a scribal separation or a textual peculiarity. I read them together as the conjunction כי.
בזימוני appears to be ב + זימון + י (at my invitation/banquet). זימון is a post-biblical term for an invitation to a meal, from the root זמן. No Strong's entry covers this specific noun.
שום אדם in later Hebrew idiom means 'no person at all' — this is a post-biblical usage of שום as a quantifier.

translation_notes: ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Verb of speech; chose H559.
textual_notes: ועמים could be from עם (people/nation) in plural, or עמים could be an intensified form. Context of crowds following suggests 'peoples/crowds'.
ונהפך is the nifal (reflexive/passive) of הפך — 'he turned himself' toward them.

translation_notes: אם: Candidates: H517 'a mother', H518 'if/whether'. Opens a conditional clause; chose H518.

אי זה: Candidates for אי: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Combined with זה (H2088 'this'), the phrase אי זה forms the interrogative/indefinite 'which one' or 'any'. Chose H335 for אי and H2088 for זה.
איש: Candidates: H376 'a man', H377 'to act manly'. Subject of the conditional; chose H376.
ילך: H3212 'to walk'. The sense here is complex — 'does not walk [away from]' his family, meaning does not distance himself from them.

ואחיו: Only candidate H283 'Achio (proper name)'. However, the consonants are clearly אח (brother) + יו (his, plural suffix). This is 'his brothers'. The Strong's entry is a proper noun that doesn't fit.
ועוד: Candidates: H5749 'to testify', H5750 'again/still/also'. Adverbial 'and also/even'; chose H5750.
לא: H3808 'not'. Simple negation.
textual_notes: The phrase ולא ילך עמי is difficult. It seems to mean something like 'and does not depart from' or 'does not renounce.' The Hebrew literally says 'does not walk with me his father...' which is syntactically awkward. One possibility: ולא ילך עמי should be read as introducing a list — 'and does not leave behind his father...' — where ילך functions as 'go away from' or the עמי is 'from with' (i.e., away from the company of). Another reading: the second עמי is actually part of the construction 'walk from with' (leave) his father etc. The text may be a Hebrew rendering where the idiom 'hate' or 'leave behind' is rendered as a form of departure.
נשמתו: From נשמה (breath/soul/life). 'Even his own life' — the intensification with ועוד (and also) emphasizes this is the ultimate demand.
תלמידי is a post-biblical Hebrew term for 'my disciple/student', from the root למד (to learn).

translation_notes: ומי: H4310 'who'. Introduces a relative clause 'whoever'; chose H4310.
שתי: Candidates: H8358 'intoxication', H8359 'warp (in weaving)'. Combined with וערב (woof), this is a weaving metaphor — warp and woof form a cross-pattern. Chose H8359.

וערב: Candidates: H6148 'to braid/intermix', H6149 'to be agreeable', H6150 'to grow dusky', H6151 'to commingle', H6152 'Arabia', H6153 'dusk'. Paired with שתי (warp), the woof/weft of weaving is meant — the cross-threads. Chose H6148 as the root for the weaving term.

שלו: Candidates: H7958 'quail', H7959 'security', H7960 'a fault', H7961 'tranquil/careless'. Here שלו functions as the possessive 'his own' (a post-biblical usage of של + ו). None of the Strong's entries perfectly match, but H7961 is closest consonantally. The actual function is possessive pronoun.
אחרי: Only candidate H317 'other'. However, אחרי commonly means 'after/behind' (from אחר). In context 'coming after me' is the clear reading.
textual_notes: שתי וערב (warp and woof) is a remarkable Hebrew rendering. In weaving, the שתי (warp threads) cross with the ערב (woof/weft threads), forming a cross-pattern. This appears to be a Hebrew idiom for the cross/execution stake, using the image of crossed beams. This is a distinctive Hebrew translation choice.
שלו as a possessive ('his') is post-biblical Hebrew (של + ו). The Strong's candidates don't cover this usage.
אחרי: The sole candidate H317 'other' doesn't fit. This is clearly the preposition אחרי 'after/behind me', a standard biblical Hebrew word (related to אחר H310).

translation_notes: כי: H3588 — conjunction introducing the parable; chose H3588.
אי זה: Same as section 6. H335 + H2088 = 'which one'. Interrogative pronoun.
שחפץ: Candidates: H2654 'to incline/be pleased/desire', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire'. With ש prefix as relative pronoun, 'who desires'; chose H2654 as the verbal form.

אם: H518 'if/whether' — introducing the question of sufficiency; chose H518.

כח: H3581 'vigor/strength/capacity/means'. Resources to complete the project; chose H3581.
textual_notes: ימנה: The Strong's listing only offers H3232 (a proper name), but contextually this must be the imperfect of מנה 'to count/reckon' (H4487). The verb fits perfectly: counting the cost before building.
ההוצאה and הצריכה are post-biblical Hebrew forms: 'the expenditure' and 'the necessary/required'. No Strong's candidates were provided.
בידו: The Strong's entry is a proper name, but this is transparently the prepositional phrase 'in his hand' meaning 'at his disposal'.

translation_notes: ואם: H518 'if/whether' — conditional clause; chose H518.
יבנה: Only candidate H2996 'Jabneh (place name)'. However, this is clearly the imperfect of בנה 'to build' (H1129) with י prefix: 'he will build'. The proper noun is irrelevant here.
ולא: H3808 'not' — negation.
כל: H3605 'all/every' — modifying 'the ones seeing'; chose H3605.
textual_notes: יבנה: Strong's only offers the place name Jabneh (H2996), but this is unmistakably the imperfect verb 'he builds/will build' from בנה (H1129).
היסודות, הבניין, ילעיגו are post-biblical or unlisted forms: 'the foundations', 'the building/construction', 'they will mock'.

translation_notes: האיש: Candidates: H376 'a man', H377 'to act manly'. With the article, 'the man'; chose H376.

translation_notes: אם (first occurrence, consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether/conditional'. Chose H518 because the sentence introduces a hypothetical scenario about a king going to war, requiring a conditional particle.

נגד (first occurrence): Candidates: H5046 'to front/declare', H5047 'to flow', H5048 'opposite/against', H5049 'opposite'. Chose H5048 because it functions as a preposition meaning 'against/opposite' before 'kings,' producing a coherent military image.
אם (second occurrence): Chose H518 again — introduces the embedded question 'whether with ten thousand he is able.'
עם (first occurrence): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with (preposition)'. Chose H5973 because 'with ten thousand' describes the force accompanying the king, not a separate people.

אלף (first occurrence): Candidates: H502 'to learn', H503 'to multiply', H504 'family/ox', H505 'thousand', H506 'thousand (Aramaic)', H507 'Eleph (place)'. Chose H505 because 'ten thousand' is a numerical expression describing troop strength.
נגד (second occurrence): Same reasoning as above — H5048, 'against/opposite,' functioning as a preposition before the relative clause.
מי: H4310 'who' — interrogative/relative pronoun identifying the opposing king.

שעם: This is ש (relative particle 'that/who') + עם. Candidates for עם: H5971 'people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5973 'with' because 'the one who with twenty thousand comes' describes the opposing force, parallel to 'with ten thousand.'
אלף (second occurrence): Chose H505 'thousand' for the same reason — 'twenty thousand' is the opposing army's count.
textual_notes: The word שעם is parsed as the relative particle ש prefixed to עם. This is a later Hebrew construction (not classical biblical Hebrew), consistent with a post-biblical or Mishnaic-era text.
מלכים could theoretically be read as plural of H4432 'Molek' (foreign deities), but the military context strongly favors H4428 plural 'kings.'

translation_notes: זה: Candidates: H2088 'this (masc. demonstrative)', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'apart from this' is a demonstrative reference to the scenario just described; 'a sheep' is contextually absurd here.

הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he (pronoun)', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 because it serves as the emphatic subject pronoun 'he' for the participle 'standing/sends.'
עם: Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with (preposition)'. Chose H5973 because 'with words of peace' describes the content/manner of negotiation — the preposition 'with' is required.

דברי: The candidate H1704 'Dibri (name)' is contextually impossible. This is clearly the construct plural of דבר (H1697 'word/matter'), which was not listed among candidates but is the only plausible reading: 'words of peace.'

שלום: Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare/prosperity', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. Chose H7965 because 'words of peace' describes the diplomatic content of the envoy's message — seeking peace terms.
textual_notes: וזולת is a post-biblical Hebrew term (from the root זולת meaning 'except/apart from'). No Strong's number is provided; this word is not part of the classical biblical lexicon but is well-attested in Mishnaic/Medieval Hebrew.
להשתדל is a hitpa'el infinitive meaning 'to endeavor / to negotiate / to seek terms.' This is a later Hebrew form not found in the biblical corpus, confirming the post-biblical character of the text.

דברי — the only Strong's candidate offered (H1704 Dibri, a proper name) does not fit. The reading is unambiguously the construct plural of דבר 'word' (H1697), which simply was not listed among candidates.

translation_notes: כן (k-n): Candidates: H3651 'thus/so/upright', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'stand/pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. As an adverb introducing a concluding statement, 'thus/so' (H3651) is the clear choice.
כל (k-l): H3605 and H3606 are Hebrew and Aramaic forms of the same word 'all/every'. Chose H3605 for both occurrences as this is a Hebrew text.
איש (ʾ-y-sh): Candidates: H376 'man/person', H377 'to act manly'. As a noun following כל, 'every man/person' is the natural reading. Chose H376.
textual_notes: שאינו, מתיאש, שמחזיק, אינו, יכול, להיות, תלמידי are all later Hebrew (Mishnaic/Rabbinic) constructions without Strong's entries. מתיאש is from the hitpael of יאש (to despair/give up hope), here meaning 'renounce' or 'let go.' שמחזיק is from חזק in the hiphil (to hold onto/grasp). תלמידי = 'my disciple' from תלמיד, a post-biblical term.

The phrase מתיאש מכל הדברים שמחזיק could mean either 'despairs of all the things he holds' or 'renounces all the things he possesses.' The root יאש carries both senses of hopelessness and relinquishment.

translation_notes: המלח (h-m-l-ḥ): Candidates: H4414 'to pulverize/salt', H4415 'to eat salt', H4416 'salt', H4417 'powder/salt', H4418 'rag', H4419 'sailor', H3892 'fresh', H3893 'vigor'. In a statement about seasoning and taste, 'the salt' (H4417 with definite article) is the clear reading.
