אי: Candidates: H335 'where?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'howler', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H336 'not' because אי + איפשר = 'not possible' = 'impossible.' This is a standard post-biblical Hebrew construction.
שיש: Candidates: H7893 'marble/white', H3426 'there is/are'. Chose H3426 because ש + יש = 'that there is' — 'those that have' is coherent; 'those that marble' is not.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — ל + הם = 'to them,' completing 'that there is to them' = 'who have.'
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as copular pronoun 'it is.'
textual_notes: עצבונו: From עצבון (H6093 'toil/pain/sorrow') + 3ms suffix = 'his grief/sorrow.' Not separately listed in candidates.
ממון is a post-biblical Hebrew/Aramaic loanword meaning 'wealth/riches/mammon,' not in Strong's biblical lexicon.
שיכנסו: ש + יכנסו = 'that they will enter,' from post-biblical כנס 'to enter/gather.'
שאותן: ש + אותן = 'that those' (feminine/generic accusative demonstrative in post-biblical Hebrew).

translation_notes: הגמל: Candidates: H1580 'to treat/ripen/requite/wean', H1581 'a camel'. Chose H1581 because 'a camel passing through the hole of a needle' produces a vivid, coherent image of impossibility. 'A requital passing through a needle hole' does not.

בנקב: Candidates: H5344 'to puncture/perforate', H5345 'a bezel (for a gem)', H5346 'Nekeb (place)'. Chose H5345 because a bezel is a setting/hole, and 'in the hole of the needle' = 'through the eye of a needle' is the coherent physical image. A place name or abstract verb of puncturing is less natural as the noun here.

מאדם: Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby/garnet'. The מ prefix is comparative 'than.' Chose H120 because 'than a human [who is] rich' is the natural comparison; 'than Edom rich' or 'than a ruby rich' lacks coherence.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as copular pronoun 'it [is]' in the predicate 'more easy it is.'
textual_notes: נקל: This appears to be from קלל (H7043 'to be light/easy') in niphal or a related form. 'Easy/light' is the contextual meaning. Not in the provided candidates.
המחט: From מחט (not in Strong's biblical lexicon as a standalone), meaning 'needle' — a well-known post-biblical Hebrew word. The ה is the definite article.
שיעבור: ש + יעבור = 'that will pass through,' from עבר (H5674 'to cross over/pass through').
בנקב could also be read as the verbal noun 'in the piercing/perforation' (from H5344) rather than the noun 'bezel' (H5345). Both yield essentially the same image: the hole/eye of the needle.

translation_notes: אלה (consonants א-ל-ה): Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'an imprecation', H424 'an oak', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. However, in context 'these the-words' demands a demonstrative pronoun; the consonants אלה also correspond to H428 (אֵלֶּה, 'these'), which is the standard demonstrative. None of the listed candidates fit as well as the demonstrative pronoun reading. Chose H428 (unlisted but consonantally identical) because 'these words' is the only coherent reading.

יוכל (consonants י-ו-כ-ל): Candidate: H3116 'Jukal, an Israelite name'. However, in context 'and who Jukal to be saved' is nonsensical. The consonants י-כ-ל correspond to the verb H3201 'to be able, to prevail', with יוכל being a standard imperfect form. Chose H3201 because 'who is able to be saved' is the only coherent reading.
נושע (consonants נ-ו-ש-ע): This is a nifal participle from ישע (H3467, 'to save/deliver'). The passive form means 'saved/delivered'.
textual_notes: אלה: The provided candidates do not include the demonstrative pronoun H428, but the consonants are identical. Context demands the demonstrative reading.
יוכל: The only provided candidate is the proper name Jukal (H3116), but the consonants clearly support the common verb יכל (H3201, 'to be able') in imperfect form.

translation_notes: אמר (consonants א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Context demands a speech verb introducing a quote. Chose H559.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', or ל + הם H1992 'they/them'. Context 'said to them' requires the prepositional phrase ל + הם. Chose H1992.

לאדם (consonants א-ד-ם): Candidates: H119 'flush', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. The phrase 'the impossible for a human being' demands the generic noun for humanity. Chose H120.

לאל (consonants א-ל): Candidates: H3815 'Lael', H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Context contrasts what is impossible for humans with what is possible for God. Chose ל + H410 'God'.
אשר (consonants א-ש-ר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Used as relative pronoun 'that/which'. Chose H834.
textual_notes: The text appears to combine two separate teachings: one about impossibility/possibility with God, and commandments about coveting and loving one's neighbor. The ellipsis after תחמד suggests missing text.
ואהבתלרעךכמוך appears to be written as a single string, representing 'and-you-shall-love-your-neighbor-as-yourself' — a well-known compound phrase from Leviticus 19:18.

translation_notes: אמר: Same analysis as before. Speech verb in narrative context. Chose H559.
הנה (consonants ה-נ-ה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. The interjection 'behold' fits a declarative statement opening. Chose H2009.
כל (consonants כ-ל): H3605 'the whole/all' vs H3606 (Aramaic equivalent). Hebrew context. Chose H3605.
textual_notes: וכיפא is not in the Strong's dictionary; this is an Aramaic proper name (Kepha/Cephas/Peter), indicating the text uses later Hebrew or is a translation from Aramaic.

translation_notes: שום (consonants ש-ו-ם): Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7761 (Aramaic), H7762 'garlic'. In later Hebrew שום functions as an indefinite determiner ('any/some'); combined with לא it means 'no' (no human). Chose H7760 as the base form that evolved into this usage.
אדם: Same as section 2. Generic human being. Chose H120.
אני (consonants א-נ-י): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Context 'truth I am saying' requires first person pronoun. Chose H589.
אומר: The listed candidate H201 'Omar' is a proper name. However, consonants א-מ-ר are clearly a participle of H559 'to say'. Chose H559 (participle form).

אחיו: Listed candidate H283 'Achio (proper name)'. However, consonants א-ח-י-ו clearly read as אָחִיו 'his brother(s)' from H251 (אָח, 'brother') with 3ms suffix. Chose H251 because the list of family members demands 'his brothers'.
בעד (consonants ב-ע-ד): H1157 'for, on behalf of, behind'. Context 'for the sake of the kingdom' fits perfectly. Chose H1157.
מלכות: H4438 'a rule/dominion/kingdom' vs כות H3575 'Cuth'. Context demands 'kingdom'. Chose H4438.
יהוה: H3068 vs H3069, both refer to the divine name. Chose H3068 as the primary entry.
textual_notes: יניח appears to be hifil imperfect of נוח (H3240, 'to cause to rest, to leave, to set down'). This is not listed among candidates but is the clear verbal form.

בתי דירתו ('houses of his dwelling') is an unusual phrase. דירתו does not appear in the Strong's lexicon directly; it appears to be a noun דירה ('dwelling/residence') with 3ms suffix, suggesting a later Hebrew or medieval Hebrew term.
The sentence beginning 'no human will leave... for the sake of the kingdom of YHWH' appears to continue into the next section, suggesting this is an incomplete clause (protasis of a conditional).

translation_notes: שלא: ש (relative particle 'who/that') + לא H3808 ('not'). Together: 'who not' or 'that not'. Contextually this completes the conditional from section 4: 'no one who leaves... who will not receive more.'
ממה: מן ('from') + מה H4100 ('what'). 'From what' = 'than what'.
בזמן: Candidates: H2163 'to fix a time', H2164 'to agree on a time', H2165 'an appointed occasion', H2166 (Aramaic). Chose H2165 as the noun 'time/appointed occasion' fits with the prepositional ב.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. 'In time this' = 'in this time'. Chose H2088.
חיים: Not listed with candidates but consonants ח-י-י-ם clearly correspond to H2416 'life/alive'. The ים suffix here is intensifying — 'life in its fullness' — as indicated by the singular concept.
נצחיים: Root נצח (H5331, 'perpetuity/everlasting') with adjectival ים suffix. 'Everlasting/eternal'.
textual_notes: The < before הניח likely indicates a textual note or uncertain letter. The verb appears to be hifil perfect of נוח (H3240), 'he left/set aside', continuing from section 4.

שלא could be parsed as ש + לא ('who not') creating a double negative with the preceding section's לא, yielding 'no one... who will not receive' = 'everyone will receive'. This is the most natural reading.

translation_notes: לקח: Candidates: H3947 'to take', H3948 'instruction'. Verb fits the narrative action of taking aside disciples. Chose H3947.
שנים: H8147 'two/twofold'. Combined with עשר = 'twelve'.

עשר: Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6236 'ten (Aramaic)', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth', H6240 'ten (in combination, -teen)'. With שנים, this forms 'twelve'. Chose H6240 which is the combining form used for numbers 11-19.
הנה: Same as section 3. Interjection 'behold'. Chose H2009.
בעד: H1157 'for, behind, concerning'. In context 'written by/concerning the prophets'. Chose H1157.
שבן: ש (relative 'that') + בן H1121 'son'. Together 'that the son of'. Chose H1121.
האדם: Candidates same as before. 'The human/the man' — forming the title 'Son of Man'. Chose H120.
ואמר: H559 'to say'. Narrative speech verb. Chose H559.
textual_notes: בעד הנביאים could mean 'by the prophets' (agency) or 'concerning the prophets' or 'through the prophets'. The most natural reading in context of 'things written' is 'by/through the prophets'.

שבן האדם: The placement at the end is ambiguous — it could be the subject of 'will be completed' (all the things written by the prophets about the Son of Man will be completed) or could begin a new clause. The former reading is more coherent.
תלמידיו is a post-biblical Hebrew word (from למד 'to learn') not found in the Strong's lexicon, indicating a later Hebrew text.

translation_notes: לעג (consonants ל-ע-ג): Candidates: H3932 'to deride/mock', H3933 'derision/scoffing', H3934 'a buffoon/foreigner'. Context 'they will bring out mockery upon him' requires a noun. Chose H3933 'derision/scoffing'.

נגש (consonants נ-ג-ש): Candidates: H5065 'to drive/oppress/tyrannize', H5066 'to come near/approach'. In context of suffering and affliction, 'oppressed/driven' fits the parallel with 'afflicted'. Chose H5065.
textual_notes: ונענה could be from ענה H6031 ('to afflict/humble') in nifal ('he will be afflicted') or from ענה H6030 ('to answer/respond'). The suffering context strongly favors 'afflicted'.
וירוקו could be from רקק H7556 ('to spit') or from ירק H3417 ('to spit'). Both yield the same meaning. The waw-consecutive + imperfect form suggests 'and they will spit'.

translation_notes: וכאשר: Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. With prefix וכ, this reads 'and as/when'. Chose H834.
וביום: H3117 'a day' vs H3118 'a day (Aramaic)'. Hebrew context. Chose H3117.
חי: Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 'alive (Aramaic)'. Hebrew context. Chose H2416.
textual_notes: נגוש appears to be a passive participle from נגש H5065 ('oppressed/driven'). It could also be parsed as a noun form, but the passive participle reading is most natural with יהיה.
ה<לישי: The < suggests a textual uncertainty or damaged letter. The word clearly reads השלישי ('the third') from H7992.
יחזור is not a standard biblical Hebrew form but is common in later Hebrew, from חזר ('to return'). This confirms the text is in a later stratum of Hebrew.

translation_notes: והם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Context demands pronoun 'they'. Chose H1992.
שום: Same as section 4. Used as indefinite determiner 'any'; with negative אינם = 'not any' = 'no'. Chose H7760.
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. As a noun following שום, 'any thing/word'. Chose H1697.

מאלו: מן + אלו. Candidates: H431 'lo!', H432 'if'. However, אלו in later Hebrew functions as a demonstrative pronoun 'these'. Chose H431 loosely, but the actual function is demonstrative 'from these'.
זה: H2088 'this/that' vs H2089 'sheep' vs H2090 'this/that'. Demonstrative pronoun in context. Chose H2088.
הדבר: Candidates: H1907 'vizier', H1697 'word/matter'. 'This the-matter' requires the common noun. Chose H1697.
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to be/become', H1962 'ruin'. 'Was hidden' requires the copula. Chose H1961.
מהם: מן + הם H1992 'them'. 'From them'.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 (Aramaic), H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Pronoun 'it' completing 'what it [was]'. Chose H1931.
מבינים: Listed candidate H3241 'Janim (place)' matches only ינים, not the full מבינים. The word is clearly a hifil participle of בין H995 ('to discern/understand'). Chose H995.
textual_notes: The ' mark between נעלם and מהם may indicate a textual break, damaged section, or scribal notation.
מאלו uses a demonstrative form (אלו 'these') typical of later/Mishnaic Hebrew rather than biblical Hebrew אלה.
אינם is a negative existential particle + 3mp suffix ('they are not'), common in later Hebrew but not listed in the Strong's system.

translation_notes: כאשר: Same as section 8. כ + אשר H834 'when/as'. Chose H834.
ישוע: H3442 vs H3443, both 'Jeshua'. Chose H3442 as primary entry.
קרב: Candidates: H7126 'to approach/draw near', H7127 (Aramaic), H7128 'hostile encounter', H7129 (Aramaic), H7130 'the center/midst', H7131 'near'. As a verb 'drew near', chose H7126.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. As a numeral/indefinite article modifying 'blind man', chose H259.
לדרך: Candidates: H1869 'to tread/walk', H1870 'a road/path'. With preposition ל, the noun reading 'to/near the road' is natural. Chose H1870.

שואל: The candidate list for אל gives H408-H413 (various), but שואל is clearly a participle from שאל H7592 ('to ask/request/beg'). The consonants ש-א-ל point to the verb, not to the preposition אל with prefix.
עיור: Not directly in candidates but consonants ע-ו-ר correspond to H5787 (עִוֵּר, 'blind'). The י may be a mater lectionis.
textual_notes: ונעשה could be parsed as nifal of עשה H6213 ('and it was done/happened') or as 'and we will do' (1cp cohortative). The narrative third-person context strongly favors 'and it happened'.
שואל could theoretically be parsed as ש + אל ('that to'), but the participial reading 'asking/begging' is far more natural in the scene of a blind beggar by the road.

The sentence structure suggests the blind man was both sitting and begging — asking passers-by to give to him. The verb יתנו (imperfect 3mp of נתן) functions as a subjunctive: '[that] they would give'.

translation_notes: העור (consonants ע-ו-ר): Candidates: H5782 'to wake', H5783 'to be bare', H5784 'chaff', H5785 'skin', H5786 'to blind', H5787 'blind'. Chose H5787 because with the article ה this is a substantive adjective 'the blind one' — a person who hears a crowd passing and asks about it, which fits blindness perfectly.
עם (consonants ע-מ): Candidates: H5971 'a people/crowd', H5973 'with'. Chose H5971 because it pairs with רב to form 'great crowd' — a blind person hearing a large group passing by.

רב (consonants ר-ב): Candidates: H7227 'abundant/great', H7228 'archer', H7229 'abundant', H7230 'abundance'. Chose H7227 because 'great people/crowd' is the natural description of what the blind man hears passing.
textual_notes: שעובר appears to be the relative particle ש + עובר (participle of עבר, to pass over/through). No Strong's candidates were provided for this compound form.

translation_notes: והעור (consonants ע-ו-ר): Same as section 1. Chose H5787 'blind' — the blind man from the narrative is now crying out.
קרא: Candidates: H7121 'to call out/address by name', H7122 'to encounter', H7123 'to call out', H7124 'partridge'. Chose H7121 because the blind man is calling out/crying aloud to Yeshua by name.
דוד: Candidates: H1730 'love/uncle', H1731 'pot/basket', H1732 'David'. Chose H1732 because 'son of David' is a title directed at Yeshua.

עלי: Candidates: H5940 'pestle', H5941 'Eli', H5942 'high', H5943 'supreme'. However, the consonants על + pronominal suffix י naturally read 'upon me'. This is a prepositional phrase, not one of the listed nouns.
textual_notes: רחמנות is a later Hebrew abstract noun form (from root ר-ח-מ 'to have compassion') not directly listed in the Strong's candidates. It clearly means 'compassion/mercy'.
עלי could theoretically be a proper noun (Eli) or the preposition 'upon me'. Context demands 'upon me' as part of the plea for mercy.

translation_notes: והוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because 'and he, the blind one' is a contrastive subject pronoun introducing the blind man's defiant response.
עור: Same consonants as before. Chose H5787 'blind' — continuing the narrative about the blind man.

חמול: The sole candidate H2538 is 'Chamul, an Israelite' (proper name). However, the root ח-מ-ל means 'to have compassion/spare' (cf. H2550 חמל). In context this is an imperative 'have compassion!' directed at the son of David. The consonants support the verb חמול as an imperative of חמל.
עלי: As in section 3, this reads as the preposition 'upon me' rather than any of the listed noun candidates.
textual_notes: חמול: The only Strong's candidate provided is H2538 (proper name Chamul). But the root חמל (H2550, 'to spare/have compassion') produces the imperative form חמול. This is clearly the intended reading contextually — a plea for mercy — though the specific Strong's number for the verb was not among the candidates.
מקללין could derive from קלל 'to curse' or in later usage 'to rebuke/scold'. In this narrative context, 'rebuking' or 'scolding' him to be silent is the most natural sense.

translation_notes: עמד: Candidates: H5975 'to stand', H5976 'to shake', H5977 'a spot', H5978 'along with'. Chose H5975 because Yeshua stopping and standing still before issuing a command is the natural narrative action.
וכאשר: The כ prefix + אשר. Candidates for אשר include H834 'who/which/when'. Chose H834 as temporal conjunction 'and when' — introducing the next action in sequence.

שאלו: The consonants could include שאל (H7592 'to ask') + suffix ו. Chose this reading because Yeshua asks the blind man a question (section 6 provides the question). The listed candidates H431/H432 for אלו do not fit.
textual_notes: הץביאוהו appears to be a scribal variant or error for הביאוהו ('they brought him'). The צ may be a copying artifact. The hiphil form of בוא with 3ms suffix is the intended reading.
שאלו could be parsed as ש + אלו ('that those') or as שאל + ו ('he asked him'). Context strongly favors 'he asked him' since section 6 immediately gives the content of the question.

translation_notes: אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because 'what do you desire' requires a second person pronoun as subject.
חפץ: Candidates: H2654 'to incline/be pleased/desire', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire'. Chose H2654 because this is a verb form — 'what do you desire that I do for you?'
אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because 'he said' is the standard dialogue marker.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon'. Chose H113 because the blind man addresses Yeshua as 'lord/master'.
textual_notes: שאעץשה appears to be a scribal variant for שאעשה ('that I do'), with an extra צ possibly a copying error. The intended form is the 1cs imperfect of עשה with relative ש prefix.

translation_notes: ראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'bird of prey', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 as an imperative 'see!' — both a command and profoundly fitting since the blind man is being granted sight. The double meaning (imperative 'see!' and the actual granting of sight) is striking.
אמר: Chose H559 'to say' — standard dialogue introduction.
textual_notes: אץמונתך appears to be a scribal variant for אמונתך ('your faith/faithfulness'), with an extra צ as a copying artifact. The root is א-מ-נ (H530 אמונה 'faithfulness/faith') with 2ms possessive suffix.

תושיע is a hiphil imperfect 3fs of ישע ('to save/deliver'), with 'your faithfulness' as the subject. It could also be read as 2fs — but the subject 'your faithfulness' taking a feminine verb makes better grammatical sense.

translation_notes: ומיד: The מ prefix + יד (H3027 'hand'). The idiom מיד means 'from hand' i.e. 'immediately/at once'. This is the standard Hebrew expression for immediacy.

ראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'experiencing', H7203 'seer', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 because the blind man, having been told 'see!', now actually sees — the narrative fulfillment.
והלך: Candidates: H1980 'to walk', H1981 'to walk', H1982 'a journey/wayfarer', H1983 'a journey/toll'. Chose H1980 because 'he walked after Yeshua' describes the man following him.
משבח: Candidates: H7623 'to address in a loud tone/praise', H7624 'to adulate/adore'. Chose H7623 because 'praising YHWH' in a loud voice fits the joyous response of a man just healed of blindness.
ליהוה: Candidates: H3068 'YHWH', H3069 'YHWH'. Chose H3068 as the primary form of the divine name.
textual_notes: אחרי: The sole candidate provided is H317 'other'. However, the consonants אחרי naturally read as the preposition 'after/behind' (typically identified as H310 אחרי). Context demands 'after Yeshua' — he followed behind him.

19.summary: Phase 1 consonantal translation — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided. Literal and amplified readings produced independently from consonantal Hebrew.

translation_notes: והנה (הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2009 because the particle introduces a new character appearing on the scene, a classic use of the presentative 'behold'.

שר: Candidates: H8269 'a head person (of any rank or class)', H8270 'a string/umbilical cord'. Chose H8269 because in context this man holds authority over tax-collectors, making 'head person/chief' the coherent reading.

שהיה (היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because the ש prefix functions as a relative pronoun 'who' and היה as 'was', giving 'who was' — a natural description of the man's role.
textual_notes: העולמיים has no Strong's candidate provided. The consonants עולם typically mean 'eternity/world' (H5769), but in this context 'chief of the world-people' makes no sense. This appears to be a medieval Hebrew coinage for 'tax-collectors' or 'publicans' — possibly derived from a concept of worldly/fiscal affairs. The term is not standard biblical Hebrew and may reflect a later compositional layer.

translation_notes: חפץ: Candidates: H2654 'to incline to/be pleased/desire', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire/valuable thing'. Chose H2654 as the verbal form because the sentence structure (והיה חפץ) indicates an active state of desiring, not a noun.

משיח: Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder/converse', H7879 'contemplation/utterance', H7880 'a shoot/shrubbery'. Chose H4899 because it follows the proper name Yeshua as a title — 'Yeshua the Anointed One' is the natural reading.

אי: Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'howler/wild creature', H339 'habitable spot/island'. Chose H335 as an interrogative 'which/what kind of' because the phrase 'אי זה איש הוא' reads as an embedded question: 'what sort of man he was.'
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that (demonstrative)', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this or that'. Chose H2088 because אי זה together form the interrogative 'which/what kind of', a known Hebrew construction.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/self/the same', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as the pronoun completing the embedded question 'what man he [was].'
העם: Candidates: H5971 'a people/tribe', H5973 'with/among'. Chose H5971 because 'the people' is the coherent object after 'multitude of' — referring to the crowd.
textual_notes: The consonants ק טן appear to be a single word קטן (H6996, 'small/young/insignificant') split across a word boundary, possibly due to scribal practice or manuscript damage. Reading them together as קטן makes full sense: 'small of form/stature.'
הצורה (H6699) means 'form' or 'figure' — here it functions as 'stature/physical form,' describing Zakkai's short physical build.
אותו could be parsed as the accusative marker + 3ms suffix ('him') or as a demonstrative. In context it seems to function as a connector: 'for that [same] Zakkai was small of stature.'

translation_notes: ועלה: Candidates: H5927 'to ascend/mount', H5928 'a holocaust', H5929 'a leaf', H5930 'a step/holocaust', H5931 'a pretext'. Chose H5927 because the narrative describes physical action — running and then climbing up into a tree.

שקמה: Candidates: H8256 'a sycamore (tree)', H7054 'something that rises/stalk of grain'. Chose H8256 because the context identifies it as the name of the type of tree (אילן) he climbed — a sycamore tree fits perfectly.

שם: Candidates: H8033 'there/then', H8034 'name/appellation', H8035 'Shem'. Chose H8033 'there' because the sentence describes the location where Yeshua was about to pass — 'for there he was to pass.'

יוכל: The only Strong's candidate is H3116 'Jukal, an Israelite' (a proper name). However, the consonants י-כ-ל clearly represent the imperfect form of יכל 'to be able' (from the root כול/יכל). In context 'in order that he would be able to see' is the only coherent reading. The Strong's number for the verb 'to be able' is H3201.

לעבור: Candidates: H5668 'transit/on account of', H5669 'stored grain'. The root עבר (H5674) means 'to pass over/through.' Here the infinitive לעבור means 'to pass by,' describing Yeshua's anticipated route.
textual_notes: ורץ is listed only under H7518 'a fragment', but the consonants רץ also represent the participle or past form of רוץ (H7323, 'to run'). In context, 'he ran' is the only coherent reading. The narrative describes physical urgency: running ahead and climbing a tree.

יוכל: The Strong's candidate H3116 is a proper name 'Jukal'. In this context it must be the imperfect of יכל 'to be able' (H3201). The consonants are identical but the narrative demands the verbal reading.

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when/where', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כאשר is a standard temporal conjunction meaning 'when/as' — introducing the moment Yeshua arrived at the spot.
אל: Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'strength/God', H411 'these/those', H413 'near/to/among'. Chose H413 because 'came to the place' is the natural directional reading.
המקום: Candidates: H4725 'a standing/place/locality', H6965 'to rise'. Chose H4725 because the narrative describes Yeshua arriving at a specific location — 'the place' where Zakkai was in the tree.
וראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'a vulture', H7203 'a seer/vision'. Chose H7200 because the verb 'and he saw' continues the narrative action of looking up and perceiving.
ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the context introduces direct speech — 'and said to him.'

מהר: Candidates: H4116 'to hurry', H4117 'to bargain for a wife', H4118 'in a hurry', H4119 'a price for a wife', H2022 'a mountain'. Chose H4116/H4118 because the command 'come down quickly' demands urgency, not marriage or mountains.

וחושה: The only candidate is H2364 'Chushah, an Israelite (proper name)'. However, the consonants חוש represent the root חוש (H2363, 'to hurry/hasten'). The ה suffix is the cohortative/imperative ending. In context, 'and hurry!' is the only coherent reading paired with 'come down quickly.'
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because 'compelled am I' requires the first person pronoun.
textual_notes: The subject of הביט and וראה is ambiguous. The text reads 'Zakkai looked up and saw Yeshua the Anointed One' — but it could also be parsed as 'Yeshua looked up and saw Zakkai.' The word order (ישוע בא אל המקום ... הביט וראה) could attach the verbs to either party. However, the phrase order suggests Yeshua came to the place, then [he] looked up — since Zakkai was above in the tree, looking 'up' more naturally describes the one on the ground (Yeshua) looking upward. But the traditional narrative has Yeshua looking up at Zakkai. Either parsing is syntactically possible.

מוכרח has no Strong's candidate provided. The root כרח implies compulsion/necessity. This appears to be a later Hebrew formation (hophal/pual participle of כרח) meaning 'compelled/necessitated.' It is not standard biblical Hebrew vocabulary.
וחושה: H2364 is a proper name, but the consonants clearly function here as an imperative of חוש 'to hurry.' The Strong's number for the verbal root would be H2363.

translation_notes: ירד: Candidates: H3381 'to descend/go down', H3382 'Jered (name)'. Zakkai was up in a tree and was told to come down — 'descended' is the clear reading. Chose H3381.
מהרה: Candidates: H4120 'a hurry/promptly', H2029 'to become pregnant', H2030 'pregnant'. As an adverb describing the speed of descent, 'quickly' is obvious. Chose H4120.

וקבל: Candidates: H6901 'to admit/take/receive', H6902 'to acquire', H6903 'in front of/on account of', H6904 'battering-ram', H6905 'presence/in front of'. Describing welcoming a guest, 'received/welcomed' fits perfectly. Chose H6901.
בשמחה: Candidates: H8057 'blithesomeness/glee/joy', H4229 'to stroke/erase'. With ב prefix meaning 'with/in,' the reading 'with joy' is the natural one. Chose H8057.
וכאשר: כאשר = 'when/as' (H834 as conjunction). Chose H834.
העם: Candidates: H5971 'a people/crowd', H5972 same, H5973 'with', H5974 'with'. Subject of the verb 'saw' — 'the people.' Chose H5971.
ההוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/that', H1932 same, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. As a demonstrative modifying העם — 'that people/those people.' Chose H1931.
ראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'seeing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. As main verb 'saw,' chose H7200.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Object of seeing — 'this [thing].' Chose H2088.
שבבית: ש (that/in) + ב (in) + בית. Candidates for בית: H1004 'house', H1005 same, H1006 'Bajith (place)'. 'In the house of' — chose H1004.
אדם: Candidates: H119 'turn rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Describing the householder as a sinner — 'a man/person.' Chose H120.
textual_notes: התלוננו — hitpolel perfect of לון/לין (to murmur/grumble, H3885), 3mp + 'they murmured.' This is a post-biblical form but clearly contextual.
כולם — כל (all, H3605) + suffix הם (them) = 'all of them.'
בקרבם — ב + קרב (midst, H7130) + suffix הם = 'in their midst/among themselves.'
חוטא — qal participle of חטא (to sin, H2398) = 'sinning/a sinner.'
נכנס — niphal perfect of כנס (to gather/enter) — a post-biblical Hebrew form meaning 'he entered.' Not in classical biblical Hebrew Strong's.

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer'. As main verb of speech, chose H559.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord/controller', H114 'Addon (name)'. As a form of address to Yeshua, 'Lord/Master' is the clear reading. Chose H113.
אני (both): H589 'I' or H590 'ship/fleet'. First person pronoun in self-referential speech. Chose H589.
חפץ (both): Candidates: H2654 'to desire/be pleased with', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire/matter'. As a verb expressing intention ('I desire to give/restore'), chose H2654.
חצי: Candidates: H2677 'the half/middle', H2678 'an arrow'. Before 'my possessions,' 'half' is the coherent reading. Chose H2677.
ואם: H517 'mother' or H518 'if/although'. Introducing a conditional clause ('and if I defrauded'), chose H518.
שום: Candidates: H7760 'to put/set (any)', H7761 same, H7762 'garlic'. Before אדם ('person'), שום functions as 'any' — a Mishnaic usage meaning 'any/some.' Chose H7760 for the functional range.
אדם: H120 'a human being.' Object of defrauding — 'any person.' Chose H120.
הדבר: Candidates: H1907 'a vizier', H1697 'a word/matter/thing'. With article ה, 'the thing/matter' that was taken. Chose H1697.
ההוא: H1931 'he/that.' Demonstrative modifying הדבר — 'that thing.' Chose H1931.

להשיב: The candidates given (H7867-7869) relate to aging/growing gray, but להשיב is clearly the hiphil infinitive of שוב (H7725, to return/restore). 'To restore/give back' is the obvious meaning in context of restitution.
textual_notes: עומד — qal participle of עמד (to stand, H5975). 'Standing' — no candidates provided but form is standard.
לתת — infinitive construct of נתן (to give, H5414) with ל prefix. Standard form.
נכסי — נכסים (possessions/property) + suffix י (my). This is a post-biblical Hebrew/Aramaic term (related to H5233 נכס). 'My possessions.'
לעניים — ל + עניים (poor ones), plural of עני (H6041, poor/afflicted). 'To the poor.'
רימיתי — appears to be a piel perfect 1cs of רמה (H7411, to deceive/defraud) = 'I have defrauded/cheated.' The spelling with י is a later Hebrew orthographic convention.
בארבעה — ב + ארבעה (four, H702). 'In four [measures].'
כפלים — plural/dual of כפל (H3718, double/fold). 'Folds/doublings.' Combined with בארבעה: 'fourfold.'

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say.' Speech verb. Chose H559.
היום: H3117 'a day/today' or H3118 'a day'. With article, 'today.' Chose H3117.

שלום: Candidates: H7965 'safe/well/peace/welfare/prosperity', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. After 'was made,' 'peace/salvation/wholeness' produces the most meaningful image. Chose H7965.

בזה: Candidates: H959 'to despise', H960 'scorned', H961 'booty', H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this'. Parsing as ב (in) + זה (this) = 'in this.' A preposition + demonstrative before הבית ('the house') is natural. Chose H2088 for זה.
הבית: Candidates: H1004 'house', H1005 same, H1006 'Bajith (place)', H3487 'object marker'. With article, 'the house.' Chose H1004.
בעבור: H5668 'on account of/because' or H5669 'stored grain'. Introducing causal clause. Chose H5668.
שזה: ש (that/because) + זה. H2088 'this.' 'Because this [one]...' Chose H2088.
בן: Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'a son'. Describing lineage — 'a son of Abraham.' Chose H1121.
textual_notes: נעשה — niphal perfect of עשה (to do/make, H6213) = 'was made/has been made.' Standard form.
שלום could carry its full semantic range here: peace, wholeness, salvation, well-being. The Hebrew concept is broader than any single English word.
The word בזה could theoretically be parsed as the verb 'to despise' (H959), but in context before הבית it clearly functions as preposition + demonstrative.

translation_notes: לבקש: Candidates: H1245 'to search out/seek/strive after', H7179 'straw'. The infinitive 'to seek' after 'came' is the clear reading — purpose of coming. Chose H1245.
בן: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben', H1123 'a son'. In the phrase 'son of the man/human,' this is a well-known Hebraic title. Chose H1121.
האדם: Candidates: H119 'turn rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. With the article ה, 'the human/the man' — forming the title 'Son of Man.' Chose H120.
מה: H4100 'what?/that which' or H4101 same. As a relative pronoun 'what/that which [was lost],' chose H4100.
textual_notes: The word order is unusual: 'came to seek son of the man to save what was lost.' It could be parsed as 'the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost' — where בן האדם is the subject and בא is the main verb. The word order (verb first, then purpose infinitives, then subject) is possible in Hebrew but awkward; alternatively בן האדם could be the object of לבקש ('came to seek the Son of Man, to save what was lost'), though the former reading is more natural given the broader narrative.
<היה — the < symbol appears to be a manuscript mark or damage. Reading as שהיה or simply היה (was, H1961). Combined with אבוד, it means 'was lost.'
אבוד — passive participle of אבד (to perish/be lost, H6). 'Lost/perishing.' No candidates were provided.
להושיע — hiphil infinitive of ישע (to save/deliver, H3467) with ל prefix. 'To save.' The root relates to the name ישוע itself.

translation_notes: וזה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'and this' fits naturally as introducing what he said.
אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the context requires a verb of speech — 'he said.'
שהיה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because 'that he was a prophet' is coherent; 'ruin' makes no sense here.
שמים (consonants שמים): Candidates: H8064 'sky/heaven', H4325 'water', H3220 'sea'. Chose H8064 because 'kingdom of heaven' is a coherent phrase in this context about prophetic expectation.

שמיד: The ש is the relative particle 'that', and מיד means 'from hand' i.e. 'immediately/at once' (from H3027 יד 'hand' with prefix מ). Chose this reading because the sentence speaks about their expectation of an imminent revelation.
textual_notes: שמיד is parsed as ש + מיד ('that immediately'). The word מיד derives from יד (H3027 'hand') with the prepositional prefix מ, yielding the adverbial sense 'from the hand' = 'immediately.' This is a common Hebrew idiom but not explicitly listed as a separate Strong's entry.

translation_notes: אדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'flush/turn rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'a man/person' fits the parable context of introducing a character.
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'one man' = 'a certain man' is natural narrative introduction.
הלך (consonants הלך): Candidates: H1980 'to walk/go', H1981 'to walk', H1982 'a journey', H1983 'toll'. Chose H1980 because the context requires a verb of motion — 'he went.'
מאד (consonants מאד): Candidates: H3966 'vehemently/very', H108 'fog'. Chose H3966 because 'very far' is the natural adverbial modifier for רחוק.
בעבור (consonants עבור): Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because the purpose clause 'in order to receive kingship' fits the narrative.
textual_notes: מעולה has no Strong's candidates provided. It appears to be a passive participle from עלה ('to go up'), meaning 'exalted, noble, of high rank.' This is a post-biblical Hebrew form.
ושיחזור has no Strong's candidates. It is ו + ש + יחזור (and + that + he would return), from חזר 'to return,' a common post-biblical Hebrew verb not represented in the Strong's lexicon.

translation_notes: וקרא (consonants קרא): Candidates: H7121 'to call out/summon', H7122 'to encounter', H7123 'to call', H7124 'partridge'. Chose H7121 because summoning servants fits the narrative action perfectly.

שלו (consonants שלו): Candidates: H7958 'quail', H7959 'security', H7960 'a fault', H7961 'tranquil/careless'. In context, שלו functions as the possessive pronoun 'his' (ש + לו = 'that [belong] to him'). None of the Strong's entries apply directly; this is a syntactic construction rather than a lexical entry.
ונתן (consonants נתן): Candidates: H5414 'to give', H5415 'give', H5416 'Nathan'. Chose H5414 because the verb 'gave' fits the action of distributing money.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 as the 3rd person plural pronoun 'to them' with the preposition ל.
עשר (consonants עשר): Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth'. Chose H6235 because 'ten minas' matches 'ten servants' in the parable.

עשו: The only Strong's candidate is H6215 'Esau.' However, in context this is clearly the imperative plural of עשה 'to do/make' — a basic verb form not matched to the proper noun. The consonants עשו serve as the command 'do/make.'
עד (consonants עד): Candidates: H5703 'duration', H5704 'until/as far as', H5707 'witness'. Chose H5704 because 'until I come' is the temporal clause.
textual_notes: עשו could consonantally match H6215 'Esau,' but context demands the imperative plural of עשה 'to do/make.' No Strong's entry for the verb עשה was listed among the candidates.
שלו is parsed as ש + לו ('that [belong] to him' = 'his'), a common relative possessive construction in post-biblical Hebrew, rather than any of the lexical entries provided.
מנים (no candidates provided) — parsed as plural of מנה (mina, H4488), a unit of weight/currency.
הוצאותיכם (no candidates provided) — plural noun with 2mp suffix, from יצא in the causative, meaning 'your expenditures' or 'your business dealings.'

translation_notes: כבר (consonants כבר): Candidates: H3527 'to augment/multiply', H3528 'long ago/formerly/already', H3529 'Kebar river'. Chose H3528 because 'already' fits temporally — the citizens had already been hostile.
שזה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'that this one should reign' is the coherent protest of the citizens.
לא: Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not'. Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation.
textual_notes: ע appears to be a truncated or abbreviated form. It may be a scribal abbreviation or a fragment of a longer word. Possibly עם ('with') or the abbreviation of a word. The text may be corrupt at this point.

ירוניו has no candidates provided. It appears to be a plural noun with 3ms suffix, possibly from עיר ('city') yielding 'his city-dwellers/citizens,' though the consonantal form is unusual — perhaps a variant of עירוניו.

והקציפוהו has no candidates. It parses as a Hiphil perfect 3cp of קצף ('to be angry') with 3ms object suffix — 'they made him angry' or 'they angered him.' Alternatively it could mean 'they were angry at him.'
The bracket around מלאכים in the source text suggests it may be a scribal insertion or gloss.

translation_notes: כאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כ + אשר = 'when/as' — a temporal conjunction introducing the return.
מן: Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 'from', H4482 'musical chord'. Chose H4480 because 'from the kingdom' is the natural spatial preposition.
שנתן (consonants נתן): Candidates: H5414 'to give', H5415 'give', H5416 'Nathan'. Chose H5414 because 'that he had given to them' describes the prior distribution of money.
שידע (consonants ידע): Candidates: H3045 'to know/ascertain', H3046 'to know', H3047 'Jada'. Chose H3045 because 'that he would know' fits the purpose clause.
כמה: Candidates: H3642 'to pine after', H4100 'what/how much'. Parsed as כ + מה or simply כמה = 'how much.' Chose H4100 because 'how much each one earned' is the coherent purpose.
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because this introduces the purpose clause.
textual_notes: הוציא (no candidates provided) — Hiphil perfect 3ms of יצא 'to go out,' in causative = 'to bring out, spend, produce.' In commercial context it could mean either 'spent' or 'produced/earned.' The ambiguity is genuine.
כמה could be parsed as the single word H3642 'to pine after' or as כ + מה 'how much.' The commercial context strongly favors 'how much.'

translation_notes: אומר: The only candidate listed is H201 'Omar, grandson of Esau.' However, in context this is clearly the active participle of אמר (H559 'to say'), meaning 'saying.' The participle form was not separately listed.
אדון (consonants אדון): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon'. Chose H113 because the servant is addressing his master.
עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5973 because 'with your mina' describes the instrument of profit.

המנה (consonants מנה): Candidates: H4487 'to weigh out', H4488 'a mina', H4489 'a portion of time', H4490 'a portion/ration', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H4488 because the mina is the unit of money given to the servants.
שלך (consonants שלך): Candidates: H7993 'to throw away', H7994 'pelican'. In context, שלך is the 2ms possessive pronoun 'yours' (ש + לך = 'that [belongs] to you'), not a verb or bird name.
textual_notes: הרוחתי has no candidates provided. It appears to be a 1cs perfect of a verb רוח in Hiphil, meaning 'I profited/gained.' This is a post-biblical Hebrew commercial term.
שלך is a possessive construction (ש + לך) rather than the verb H7993 'to throw' or H7994 'pelican.'

translation_notes: שמח (consonants שמח): Candidates: H8055 'to brighten up/be glad', H8056 'blithe/gleeful', H4220 'fat/rich', H4221 'marrow'. Chose H8055 because the imperative 'rejoice!' or 'be glad!' fits the master's commendation of the servant.
עבד (consonants עבד): Candidates: H5647 'to work', H5650 'a servant', H5652 'a deed'. Chose H5650 because 'good servant' is the vocative address.
טוב (consonants טוב): Candidates: H2895 'to be good', H2896 'good (adj)', H2897 'Tob', H2898 'goodness'. Chose H2896 because the adjective 'good' modifies 'servant.'
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'because/that'. Chose H3588 because 'because in a small matter you were faithful' gives the reason for the reward.
בדבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'in a matter/thing small' is coherent.
קטן (consonants קטן): Candidates: H6994 'to diminish', H6995 'little finger', H6996 'small/diminutive', H6997 'Katan'. Chose H6996 because 'small' modifies 'matter.'
ממשלה: Candidates: H4475 'rule/realm', and שלה variants. Chose H4475 because 'rule/authority over a hundred towns' is the reward.
על: Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'over/upon', H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 because 'over a hundred towns' specifies the domain of rule.
מאה: Candidates: H3967 'a hundred', H3968 'Meah tower'. Chose H3967 because 'a hundred towns' is the numerical reward.
textual_notes: עיירות has no Strong's candidates provided. It is the plural of עיירה/עיר 'town/city,' a common post-biblical Hebrew form.
נאמן has no candidates provided. It is the Niphal participle of אמן 'to be firm/faithful/trustworthy.'

translation_notes: והאחר (consonants אחר): Candidates: H309 'to loiter/delay', H310 'after/behind', H311 'after', H312 'other/another', H313 'Acher'. Chose H312 because 'the other [servant]' introduces the next character in the parable sequence.
ואמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because 'and said' is the speech verb.

המנה (consonants מנה): Candidates: H4487 'to weigh out', H4488 'a mina', H4489 'portion of time', H4490 'portion/ration', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H4488 because this is the same unit of money from the parable.
שלך (consonants שלך): Same as section 6 — possessive construction ש + לך = 'yours', not the verb 'to throw' (H7993).
textual_notes: בנעלם has no candidates provided. It appears to be ב + נעלם, where נעלם is a Niphal participle of עלם 'to be hidden/concealed,' thus 'in a hidden place' or 'in concealment.' Alternatively it could relate to נעל 'shoe/sandal' + ם, but the context of hiding money strongly favors 'in concealment.'

שמרתיה and והצנעתיה have no candidates. שמרתיה = 'I guarded it' (1cs perfect of שמר + 3fs suffix). והצנעתיה = 'and I hid/concealed it' (1cs Hiphil perfect of צנע + 3fs suffix). Both are post-biblical Hebrew forms.

translation_notes: כי (both occurrences): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'because/that'. Chose H3588 both times because 'because I feared' and 'for you are' are causal conjunctions.
אתה (both occurrences): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because 'you are a cruel man' and 'you take' require the pronoun 'you.'
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/self/same', H1932 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 as the emphatic copula — 'you, he [= you are]' is a Hebrew construction for emphasis.
איש: Candidates: H376 'a man', H377 'to act manly'. Chose H376 because 'a man cruel' = 'a cruel man.'
מה (both occurrences): Candidates: H4100 'what', H4101 'what'. Chose H4100 as the relative/interrogative 'what.'

הנחת (consonants נחת): Candidates: H5181 'to descend/press down/deposit', H5182 'to descend/deposit', H5183 'descent/rest', H5184 'Nachath', H5185 'descending'. Chose H5181 because 'you deposited/laid down' fits the financial context — taking what was not deposited.
textual_notes: הנחת could alternatively be parsed as a Hiphil form of נוח 'to rest/place,' meaning 'you placed/set down.' Both readings yield essentially the same meaning in this financial context: 'what you did not deposit/place.'
The < symbol before לא in the source may indicate a textual marker or variant reading indicator in the manuscript.

translation_notes: רע (consonants רע): Candidates: H7451 'bad/evil', H7452 'a crash/noise', H7453 'an associate/friend', H7454 'a thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 because 'evil/wicked servant' is the master's condemnation, contrasting with 'good servant' in section 7.
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because 'you knew' requires the pronoun.
שאני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because ש + אני = 'that I [am]' introducing the self-description.
איש: Candidates: H376 'a man', H377 'to act manly'. Chose H376 because 'a cruel man' is the same construction as section 9.

מלקט (consonants לקט): Candidates: H3950 'to pick up/glean/gather', H3951 'the gleaning', H6985 'a little/merely'. Chose H3950 because 'gathering what I did not sow' parallels 'taking what I did not deposit.'
textual_notes: The ו standing alone between הנחתי and מלקט appears to be the conjunction 'and.' It may have been separated from the following word in the manuscript.

מלקט could be a Piel participle of לקט (H3950 'to glean/gather') with the prefix מ, or possibly a noun form. The participial reading 'gathering/gleaning' fits the parallel structure with לוקח ('taking').

Note the shift from section 9 where the servant says וקוצר ('and reaping') to the master's version here using מלקט ('and gleaning/gathering'). This may represent a deliberate distinction in the narrative — the master corrects or restates the servant's characterization.

translation_notes: ואני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. The speaker is addressing someone about money, so 'I' is the only coherent reading.
מבקש: Candidates: H1245 'to search out/seek/demand', H7179 'straw'. In context of collecting money with interest, 'seeking/demanding' makes sense; 'straw' is incoherent.
עם: Candidates: H5971 'people', H5973 'with'. 'With the increase' fits the financial context; 'people of the increase' does not.

ברבית: The consonants רבית match H7245 (Rabbith, a place name), but contextually this is clearly the common noun רבית meaning 'interest/usury' (not given a Strong's entry in the candidates but well-attested in Mishnaic Hebrew). The place name makes no sense here.
textual_notes: ברבית: The only Strong's candidate provided is H7245 (a place name), but the consonants clearly function here as the noun 'interest/usury' in this financial context.
המדות: No Strong's candidates provided. Could derive from מדה 'measure/portion' or מדות 'measures/profits.' Given the financial context, 'the measured returns / the increase' is most fitting.

translation_notes: ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. The ו prefix + narrative context clearly yields 'and he said.'
שם: Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name', H8035 'Shem'. 'Standing there' is the natural spatial reading.
המנה: Candidates: H4487 'to weigh out', H4488 'a mina', H4489 'a portion of time', H4490 'a portion', H5089 'lamentation'. In a financial parable about money, 'the mina' (H4488) is the clear fit.
שיש: Candidates: H7893 'marble', H3426 'there is/has'. 'Who has to him ten minas' is coherent; 'who marble to him' is not. The ש is the relative pronoun prefixed to יש.
textual_notes: גזלו: No Strong's candidates provided. The root גזל means 'to seize/rob/take by force.' In context this is an imperative plural 'seize [from] him' — though the form could also be parsed as 3ms perfect 'he seized from him.' The imperative reading fits the dialogue better.

translation_notes: לאדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller/lord', H114 'Addon (a person)'. They are speaking to a master figure in the narrative, so H113 is clearly correct.

כבר: Candidates: H3527 'to augment', H3528 'already/long ago', H3529 'Kebar river', H1247-H1252 (various 'בר' meanings). 'Already there is to him ten minas' makes perfect sense as a protest; all other readings are forced.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. The speaker is making a pronouncement — 'I say to you' — so H589 is obvious.

אומר: The only candidate listed is H201 'Omar (a person)'. However the consonants אומר are clearly the qal participle of אמר (H559) 'saying/say.' The identification as a proper name makes no sense in this syntax.
אדם: Candidates: H119 'turn rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. After 'to every' the noun 'person/human' (H120) is the natural reading.
שיש: Candidates: H7893 'marble', H3426 'there is/has'. Same as section 2 — the ש is relative prefix + יש 'has.'
שאין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. ש + אין = 'who does not have' — H369 is the straightforward negative.
מה: Candidates: H4100 'what?', H4101 same. 'What there is to him will be seized' — the interrogative/relative 'what' functioning as a relative pronoun.
textual_notes: ויושפע: No candidates provided. The root שפע means 'to overflow/abound.' The הופעל/causative passive form ויושפע = 'and he will be caused to overflow/abound.' This is a rare form but contextually clear.
<יש: The < mark in the manuscript may indicate a textual note or lacuna. Reading יש as H3426 'there is.'

translation_notes: שאין: H369 'negative particle' — 'who do not desire' is the clear reading in context.
פה: Candidates: H6310 'mouth', H6311 'here/this place'. 'Bring them here' makes perfect sense as a command; 'bring them mouth' does not.

ואלו: Candidates: H431 'lo!/behold', H432 'if'. However ואלו in Mishnaic Hebrew commonly means 'and these.' The demonstrative usage fits perfectly: 'and these words being said.' H431 as an interjection would also work ('and behold, the words being said') but the demonstrative is more natural with the definite noun הדברים.
textual_notes: ואלו: Could be parsed as the demonstrative 'and these' (common in post-biblical Hebrew) or as H431 'and behold.' Both produce coherent readings. Chose 'and these' as it pairs naturally with הדברים.

translation_notes: לבית: Candidates: H1004 'house', H1005 'house (Aramaic)', H1006 'Bajith', H3487 'object marker'. 'To the house of Pagei' = Bethphage, a known place name. H1004 is correct.
בהר: Candidates: H2022 'mountain', H2023 'Hor'. 'At the mountain' fits the well-known Mount of Olives location.
ושלח: Candidates: H7971 'to send', H7972-H7975 (various). 'And he sent two disciples' — H7971 is the standard verb.
שני: Candidates: H8144 'crimson', H8145 'second/two', H5204 'lamentation'. 'Two disciples' is the obvious reading.
textual_notes: פגי: No Strong's candidates. This is a transliterated place name (Bethphage).
תלמידים: No Strong's candidates. This is a post-biblical Hebrew term for 'disciples/students.'

translation_notes: מגדול: Candidates: H4024 'Migdol (a place in Egypt)', H1419 'great/large'. The consonants מגדול could also represent מגדל 'tower' (H4026) which in post-biblical usage can mean a fortified village. H4024 as the Egyptian place name makes no contextual sense. H1419 'great' with the prefix would read 'to the great one' which is awkward. Reading as 'tower/village' is most coherent.
שהוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932-H1934 variants. 'That it is near to us' — H1931 as the pronoun is standard.

עיר: Candidates: H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'young ass/colt'. Context describes finding an animal tied up that no one has ridden, a son of a she-donkey — H5895 'colt/young donkey' is the only coherent reading. 'City' would be absurd with 'tied up' and 'son of a she-donkey.'
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. 'One colt' — H259.
אתון: Candidates: H860 'she-donkey', H861 'furnace'. 'Son of a she-donkey' is coherent; 'son of a furnace' is not.
רכב: Candidates: H7392 'to ride', H7393 'vehicle', H7394 'Rekab', H7395 'charioteer'. 'No person has ridden upon it' — H7392 as the verb.
אדם: Candidates include H120 'human being'. 'No person rode upon it' — H120.
textual_notes: מגדול: The Strong's candidates provided don't include the common noun מגדל 'tower' (H4026). The consonants could represent a variant spelling. In context it likely means a small fortified settlement or village.
לכו: The candidates list only H3551 'window' for כו, but לכו is clearly the imperative plural of הלך 'to go.' The Strong's mapping here is a mismatch.

translation_notes: ואם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. 'And if any man asks' — conditional H518.

אי: Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Combined with זה, אי זה = 'which/any' — a standard Hebrew construction meaning 'whichever/some.' H335 in its indefinite sense.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. With אי forming 'any/some' — H2088.
איש: Candidates: H376 'man', H377 'to act manly'. 'Any man' — H376.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'because/that'. 'You shall say because...' — H3588.
חפץ: Candidates: H2654 'to desire/be pleased with', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire/matter'. As a verb 'desires' — H2654.
textual_notes: שואל: The candidates listed are for אל (various), but שואל is clearly the participle of שאל 'to ask/inquire' (H7592). The Strong's mapping provided does not include the correct root.
אתם (both occurrences): The only candidate listed is H864 'Etham (a place)'. However אתם is obviously the 2nd person plural pronoun 'you.' The Strong's mapping is incomplete.
פעולתו: No candidates provided. From the root פעל 'to do/make' — פעולה = 'deed/work/purpose' + 3ms suffix 'his.'

translation_notes: שם: Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name', H8035 'Shem'. 'They went there' — spatial adverb H8033.

העיר: Candidates: H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir', H5894 'watcher', H5895 'young donkey/colt'. Following the previous section where they were sent to find a colt, and the colt is described as 'standing' — H5895 'colt' is the coherent reading. A city does not 'stand' in this manner.
שאמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560-H564 (various). 'Just as he said' — H559 with the relative prefix ש.
textual_notes: וה<לוחים: The < mark suggests a textual note or possible lacuna. The consonants suggest שלוחים 'sent ones/emissaries' (from שלח H7971) with the article ה. The initial letter(s) before לוחים may be damaged.
הלכו: The candidates list only H3551 'window' for כו, but הלכו is the 3rd person plural perfect of הלך 'to walk/go' (H1980). The Strong's mapping is a mismatch.

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because with the prefix כ and conjunction ו, this forms 'and when', a temporal clause introducing a narrative event.

העיר (עיר): Candidates: H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'young ass/colt'. Testing H5892: 'they came to untie the city' — untying a city makes no coherent physical sense. Testing H5895: 'they came to untie the young ass' — untying a tethered animal is a natural, coherent action. The verb להתיר (to loosen/untie) combined with אדון (owner/master) demanding why they are doing it creates a perfectly logical scene of people untying someone's donkey. Chose H5895.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller/owner', H114 'Addon (name)'. Chose H113 because the context describes the owner of the animal confronting those untying it.
להם: The ל is a preposition 'to' + הם H1992 'them'. This is a standard prepositional phrase meaning 'to them'.
באו: This is the verb בוא (H935 'to come/enter') in 3mp perfect form. The candidate listed (H176 'or') is for the root או alone; here ב is not a prefix but part of the root באו from בוא.
אתם: Though H864 'Etham' is listed, in context this is clearly the 2mp pronoun 'you' (standard Hebrew אתם), functioning as subject of the participial clause.
textual_notes: להתיר and מתירים have no Strong's candidates listed. The root נתר/תיר in hiphil/hitpael means 'to loosen, untie, release'. These are post-biblical Hebrew forms consistent with later manuscript language.
העיר is genuinely ambiguous between H5892 'city' and H5895 'young ass'. The verb 'untie' decisively favors 'young ass' — one unties an animal, not a city.

translation_notes: והם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because the context requires a pronoun subject 'and they said'.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction that/because'. Chose H3588 because it introduces reported speech.
האדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord', H114 'Addon'. Chose H113 because the context describes a master who has authority and need of the animal.
textual_notes: רבינו has no Strong's candidates listed. It appears to be רב + suffix ינו meaning 'our master/teacher/rabbi'. This is a post-biblical Hebrew form.
צריך has no Strong's candidates listed. It is a post-biblical Hebrew adjective meaning 'needing/in need of'.
לו could mean 'to him' or 'for it' — the referent is ambiguous but contextually refers to the animal.

translation_notes: לישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua/Yeshua', H3443 same. Both refer to the same name. Chose H3442 as the primary entry for this proper name.
textual_notes: ונהגו has no Strong's candidates listed. Root נהג means 'to lead, drive, conduct' — here in 3mp perfect with waw-consecutive.
ומניחים and והניחו derive from the root נוח (to rest/place/set down). ומניחים is a participial form 'placing', והניחו is 3mp perfect 'they placed'.
מלבושיהם has no Strong's candidates. Root לבש with מ prefix = 'garment/clothing' + 3mp possessive suffix.
עליו is ambiguous: 'upon it' (the animal) or 'upon him' (Yeshua). First occurrence refers to the animal (garments placed on it); second also refers to the animal (Yeshua seated on it).

translation_notes: הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 same (Aramaic), H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because it functions as the pronoun subject 'he' with the participle הולך.
בדרך: Candidates: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'a road/path'. Chose H1870 because the ב prefix + noun 'road' = 'on the road', which fits the image of garments being spread on the path.
textual_notes: משימים has no Strong's candidates listed. Root שים means 'to put, place, set'. This is a masculine plural participle — the subject (people/crowds) is implied.
הולך is parsed as a qal active participle of הלך (H1980), depicting ongoing action: 'going/walking'.

translation_notes: קרב: Candidates: H7126 'to approach', H7127 same (Aramaic), H7128 'hostile encounter', H7129 same, H7130 'the center', H7131 'near'. Chose H7126 because the sentence describes someone drawing near to a location — a verb of approach fits naturally.
הר: Candidates: H2022 'mountain', H2023 'Hor'. Chose H2022 because it is followed by 'the olives', forming the well-known toponym 'Mount of Olives'.

לשמח: Candidates for שמח: H8055 'to brighten up/rejoice', H8056 'gleeful'. Candidates for מח: H4220 'fat', H4221 'marrow'. Chose H8055 because the ל prefix + infinitive 'to rejoice' fits the sentence structure 'began to rejoice and praise'.
ושבח: Candidates: H7623 'to address in a loud tone/praise', H7624 'to adulate/adore'. Chose H7623 because it pairs naturally with rejoicing and a 'great voice'.

האל: Candidates: H408/409 'not', H410 'strength/Mighty One/God', H411/412 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because the context describes praising the divine — 'praise the Mighty One' is the coherent reading.
מן: Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 same, H4482 'musical chord'. Chose H4480 because 'descending from the mountain' is the natural spatial image.
על: Candidates: H5920 'the top/Most High', H5921 'over/upon/concerning', H5922 same, H5923 'yoke'. Chose H5921 because 'concerning all the wonders' fits the reason for praising.
textual_notes: לירידת has no Strong's candidates. Root ירד 'to descend' + noun form ירידה 'descent' + construct ת. This is a post-biblical form meaning 'the descent of'.
הזתים has no Strong's candidates listed. This is הזיתים 'the olives' (from זית H2132). The spelling without yod is a variant.
התחילו has no Strong's candidates. Root חלל in hiphil can mean 'to begin' (cf. H2490). This is a 3mp perfect form 'they began'.
היורדים: Qal active participle plural of ירד 'to descend' with the article ה.
הנפלאות: Niphal participle feminine plural of פלא 'to be wonderful' — 'the wonders/marvelous things'.
שראו: ש (relative 'that/which') + ראו (3mp perfect of ראה H7200 'to see') = 'that they saw'.

translation_notes: הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 same, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 as the pronoun 'he', forming 'blessed is he'.

זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Testing H2089: 'blessed is he a sheep who came in the name of God' — while symbolically possible, it breaks the natural syntax. Chose H2088 as the demonstrative 'this [one]'.

בשם: Candidates for בשם: H1313 'balsam plant', H1314 'fragrance/spicery'. Candidates for שם: H8033 'there', H8034 'name/authority', H8035 'Shem', H8036 same. Testing H1313/1314: 'who came in the balsam of God' — possible but strained. Testing H8034: 'who came in the name of God' — this is a natural, recognizable liturgical formula. Chose H8034.
האל: Same as section 5. Chose H410 'Mighty One/God' because the phrase 'in the name of God' is the coherent reading in a praise context.

שלם: Candidates: H7999 'to be safe/complete', H8000 'to complete/restore', H8001 'prosperity', H8002 'requital/sacrifice', H8003 'complete/friendly', H8004 'Shalem (Jerusalem)'. Chose H7999/H8001 as 'peace/wholeness' because the sentence declares a blessing — 'peace will be in the heavens' forms a coherent proclamation.

שבא: The listed candidate H7614 'Sheba' is the proper noun. However, the consonants ש+בא clearly parse as the relative particle ש + בא (perfect of בוא H935 'to come'). The compound שבא = 'who came'. This is the contextually correct reading.
textual_notes: ברוך: H1263 'Baruk (proper name)' is listed, but the consonants ברוך are also the passive participle of ברך (H1288 'to bless'), meaning 'blessed'. In this liturgical context, 'blessed' is the clear reading.
ל<מים: The text appears corrupted (< symbol). This likely represents לשמים 'to the heavens/skies' (שמים H8064). The < may be a scribal gap or damage where ש was lost.
ועלוי: No Strong's candidates listed. This appears to be a noun form from the root עלה 'to go up' — meaning 'exaltation, elevation, glory'.
לעליונים: No Strong's candidates listed. Root עליון (H5945 'highest, Most High') + plural suffix + ל prefix = 'to the highest ones' or 'in the highest [places]'.
יהיה: No candidates listed. Standard 3ms imperfect of היה (H1961) 'to be' = 'will be/shall be'.

translation_notes: העם: Candidates: H5971 'people/nation', H5972 same (Aramaic), H5973 'with', H5974 same. Chose H5971 because 'Pharisees of the people' describes their social origin — a coherent image.
textual_notes: ואותן: No Strong's candidates. This appears to be 'and certain/some of' — possibly אותן functioning as a demonstrative or from a form meaning 'certain ones'.
פרושי: No Strong's candidates. Root פרש 'to separate' — פרושים are 'the separated ones / Pharisees'. The construct form פרושי = 'Pharisees of'.
רבי: No Strong's candidates. This is a title רבי 'my master / my teacher / Rabbi'.
מקללים: No Strong's candidates. Root קלל (H7043 'to be light, to curse'). Piel participle plural = 'cursing/blaspheming'. The Pharisees accuse the disciples of speaking blasphemously in their praise.
תלמידיך: No Strong's candidates. Post-biblical Hebrew תלמיד 'student/disciple' + 2ms suffix ך = 'your disciples'.

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the sentence requires a verb 'he said'.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the context is first-person speech 'I say'.

אומר: H201 'Omar (proper name)' is listed. However, the consonants אומר also serve as the qal active participle of אמר (H559) meaning 'saying/I say'. The participial form 'I am saying' is the obvious reading after אני.
שאם: ש (relative/conjunction 'that') + אם. Candidates for אם: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because 'that if they are silent' is the logical conditional clause.
הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because 'they are silent' requires a pronoun subject.
ולהם: ו + ל + הם. The ל is a preposition 'to' and הם H1992 = 'them'. Together 'and to them'.
textual_notes: ישתוקו: No Strong's candidates. Root שתק 'to be quiet, be silent' — a well-attested Hebrew verb. This is 3mp imperfect = 'they will be silent / they fall silent'.
האבנים: No Strong's candidates listed. ה (article) + אבנים, plural of אבן (H68 'stone') = 'the stones'.
ידברו: No Strong's candidates listed. Root דבר (H1696 'to speak') in 3mp imperfect = 'they will speak'.

translation_notes: אל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Chose H413 because 'he approached to the city' requires a directional preposition.

העיר (first, second occurrences): Candidates: H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir', H5894 'watcher', H5895 'young ass'. In section 1, the context of untying favored 'young ass'. Here, the context is approaching, seeing, and weeping over — one weeps over a city (lament for its fate), making H5892 the coherent choice.
ראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'bird of prey', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 because 'he saw her' is a natural verbal action.

ובכה: Candidates for בכה: H1058 'to weep', H1059 'a weeping'. Candidates for כה: H3541 'thus/here', H3542 same. The ו prefix + בכה as 'and he wept' creates the coherent image of weeping over the city. Chose H1058.

עליה: H5944 'upper room/stair-way' is listed. However, עליה also parses as the preposition על (H5921 'over/upon') + 3fs suffix ה = 'over her/over it'. Since he is weeping over the city (feminine noun), this prepositional reading is correct.
קרב (both): Chose H7126 'to approach' for the same reasons as section 5.
הלך: Candidates: H1980 'to walk/go', H1981 same, H1982 'journey/wayfarer', H1983 'toll'. Chose H1980 as the verb 'he went'.
textual_notes: This section appears to contain significant textual corruption or conflation. The phrase 'וכאשר ובאו לו על העיר הנחוי הניחו הלך כברמתקרב קרב לשמוח ושבחו בכל שאנורואים' is difficult to parse coherently and may represent a marginal gloss, duplicated text, or scribal error merging two variant readings.
כברמתקרב appears to be a compound or run-together phrase: כבר (already) + מת/מתקרב (approaching/drawing near). This is unusual orthography.
שאנורואים appears to be ש (that) + אנו (we) + רואים (seeing, participle of ראה) = 'that we are seeing'. This is distinctly post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew.
הנחוי: Possibly a passive participle of נחה 'to guide/lead' = 'the guided one(s)' or a nominal form.
הניחו: Root נוח in hiphil 'they placed/set down'.
ובאו: ו + באו, 3mp perfect of בוא (H935) = 'and they came'. The candidate H176 for או is for the standalone particle; here ב is part of the root.
The entire second half of this section is likely a corrupted or alternative reading and should be treated with great caution.

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560-564 various. Chose H559 as the verb introducing speech.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction'. Chose H3588 as the discourse particle introducing the content of speech.
אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because כי אם together form 'if only / would that' — an optative or conditional expression.

הכרת: H3772 'to cut off/covenant' is listed. However, the consonants הכרת can also be parsed as hiphil perfect 2ms of נכר (H5234 'to recognize, discern, know'). Testing H3772: 'if you had cut off the things' — this doesn't produce a coherent continuation with 'and believed'. Testing H5234: 'if you had recognized and believed the things' — this creates a natural parallel of perception and faith. Chose the reading from נכר (H5234) despite only H3772 being listed.

שהם: Candidates: H7718 'beryl gem', H7719 'Shoham'. Also: ש + הם where הם = H1992 'they'. Testing H7718: 'the things beryl yours' — incoherent. Testing ש + H1992: 'the things that are yours' — perfectly coherent. Chose ש + H1992.

שלך: Candidates: H7993 'to throw out/cast away', H7994 'pelican'. However, שלך also parses as ש + ל + ך = a possessive 'that [belong] to you / yours'. Testing H7993: 'the things that they cast away' — possible but strained given following context. Testing possessive: 'the things that are yours' — natural. Chose possessive reading.
כזה: ב/כ prefix + זה. Candidates for זה: H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this'. Chose H2088: כ + זה = 'like this' or 'on this [day]'.
היום: Candidates: H3117 'day', H3118 same. Chose H3117 as 'the day'.
לשלום: Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare', H7966 'requital', H7967 'Shallum'. Chose H7965 because 'the things for your peace' is the coherent reading in a lament context.
הן: Candidates: H2004 'they (fem.)', H2005 'lo!/behold', H2006 'lo/whether'. Chose H2004 because the feminine pronoun matches נעלמות (feminine plural) as its subject: 'hidden they are'.
textual_notes: הכרת: The only listed candidate H3772 means 'to cut off', but the consonants equally support the hiphil of נכר (H5234) 'to recognize/discern'. The latter fits the context far better — lamenting that the city failed to recognize the things belonging to its peace. This is a significant consonantal ambiguity.
והאמנת: No Strong's candidates listed. Root אמן in hiphil = 'to believe, trust' (H539). 2fs/2ms perfect + ו = 'and you believed/trusted'.
הדברים: No candidates listed. Plural of דבר (H1697 'word, thing, matter') with article = 'the words/things'.
נעלמות: No candidates listed. Niphal participle feminine plural of עלם (H5956 'to hide, conceal') = 'hidden things / things that are hidden'.
לעיניך: ל + עינים (H5869 'eyes') + 2ms suffix. The ל here functions as מן 'from' — 'from your eyes'. This use of ל for מן is attested in later Hebrew.
שלך as possessive vs. H7993 'to cast away' is a genuine ambiguity. The possessive reading produces the more natural sentence.

translation_notes: כי (KY): Candidates: H3587 'a brand or scar', H3588 'conjunction: because/that/when'. Chose H3588 because this word introduces a causal clause explaining what will happen.
מכל (MKL): Candidates: H3605 'the whole, all', H3606 (Aramaic equivalent). Chose H3605 as the standard Hebrew form with preposition מן, meaning 'from all'.
צדדין: This appears to be an Aramaic-influenced plural of צד (H6654, 'side'), with the -ין plural ending typical of Aramaic/late Hebrew.
textual_notes: שאויביך appears to be a relative particle ש + אויביך ('your enemies'), a construction common in late/Mishnaic Hebrew rather than the classical אשר.
ויצורו could derive from צור (H6696 'to besiege/press') or from יצר (H3334 'to be narrow/distressed'). The siege context with surrounding and encircling strongly favors צור 'to besiege'.
צדדין uses an Aramaic-style plural ending (-ין), suggesting this text has late Hebrew or Aramaic linguistic features.

translation_notes: ולא (WLA): H3808 'not' — standard negation. H3809 is Aramaic equivalent. Chose H3808 for Hebrew context.
אבן (ABN): Candidates: H68 'a stone', H69 (Aramaic 'a stone'), H70 'a pair of stones/potter's wheel'. Chose H68 because the context describes demolition of a structure, stone by stone.
על (ʿL): Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'upon/over', H5922 (Aramaic), H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 'upon' — stone upon stone is a coherent physical image of building construction.
בעבור (BʿBWR): Candidates: H5668 'on account of, in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because this introduces the reason for destruction.

הכרת (HKRT): H3772 'to cut/destroy/covenant'. The consonants also support נכר (H5234) 'to recognize/discern' in hifil — הכרת would be 'you recognized/discerned'. In context 'you did not recognize the time of your visitation' makes far better sense than 'you did not cut'. Reading as hifil of נכר (H5234).
שלא: Relative particle ש + לא (H3808) = 'that not', a late Hebrew construction.
textual_notes: הכרת is the key ambiguity: consonantally it could be from כרת (H3772 'to cut off/covenant') or from נכר (H5234 'to recognize/discern') in the hifil. The context 'you did not ___ the time of your visitation' strongly favors 'recognize/discern' (hifil of נכר), as 'cut off the time' is incoherent. The candidate list only provides H3772, but the consonants HKRT perfectly match hifil 2fs perfect of NKR.
פקודתך is not listed in candidates but clearly derives from פקד (H6485/H6486) meaning 'visitation, appointed reckoning, accounting'.

translation_notes: וכאשר (WKʾŠR): Candidates include H834 'who/which/when', H833 'to be straight', H835 'happiness', etc. Chose H834 because כאשר means 'when/as' — temporal conjunction introducing the narrative sequence.
במקדש: Candidates: H4720 'sanctuary/consecrated place', or roots of קדש. Chose H4720 as the noun 'sanctuary' with prefix ב 'in', since this is a location being entered.

לגרש (LGRŠ): Candidates: H1643 'grain/kernel', H1644 'to drive out/expel', H1645 'produce'. Chose H1644 because the infinitive construct with ל ('to drive out') followed by people (the buyers) demands the verb meaning 'to expel/drive out'.
textual_notes: נכנס does not appear in the provided Strong's candidates. It is a well-known late/Mishnaic Hebrew verb (root כנס) meaning 'to enter/gather in'. This confirms the text's late Hebrew register.
מ<ם appears to have a textual corruption or scribal abbreviation — the < likely represents a missing letter (ה). Reading as מהם 'from them'.
התחיל is not provided with Strong's candidates. It derives from חלל (H2490) in the hifil, meaning 'to begin' — a common late Hebrew usage.
הקונים derives from קנה (H7069) 'to buy/acquire' — the participle with article: 'the ones buying'.

translation_notes: והוא (WHWʾ): Candidates: H1931 'he/she/it', H1932 (Aramaic), H1933/H1934 'to be/exist'. Chose H1931 — the pronoun 'he' as subject of the sentence.
