נסע: H5265 'to pull up tent-pins / start a journey / move away'. This fits perfectly — he moved a distance away from them.
מהם: Preposition מן + הם (H1992). 'From them'.
אבן: Candidates: H68 'a stone', H69 'a stone', H70 'pair of stones'. Chose H68 — 'a stone's throw' as a unit of distance.

ותקע: Candidates: H8628 'to clap/drive/thrust', H8629 'a trumpet blast'. Chose H8628 because 'he drove his knees to the ground' creates a vivid image of kneeling forcefully — planting one's knees on the earth.
לארץ: H776 'the earth/ground'. With ל prefix = 'to the ground'.
textual_notes: כזריקת: From זרק 'to throw/sprinkle'. The construct כזריקת אבן אחת 'as the throwing of one stone' is a measure of distance. זריקה as a noun is post-biblical.
הברכים: From ברך 'knee' (H1290). The definite article + plural 'the knees'. Could also relate to ברכה 'blessing' but 'knees' fits the physical action of kneeling.

translation_notes: אומר: Only candidate H201 'Omar'. But clearly this is the participle of אמר (H559) 'saying'. Assigning H559.
אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 — conditional 'if' introducing a request.
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because the sentence addresses God directly: 'if you are willing'.

המות: Candidates: H4191 'to die', H4192 title, H4193 'death', H4194 'death'. Chose H4194 because 'the death' as a noun with definite article fits. This is remarkable — the parallel tradition has 'this cup'; this text reads 'this death'.
הזה: Candidates: H1957 'to dream', H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this'. Chose H2088 as the demonstrative 'this' modifying 'the death'.

מעלי: The preposition מעל + first person suffix = 'from upon me'. The candidates for עלי (H5940 'pestle', H5941 'Eli', H5942 'high', H5943 'supreme') are the root עלה/על; here it's simply the compound preposition.
רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/although', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 as the limiting conjunction 'only/but rather'.
textual_notes: המות הזה: 'This death' is the plain reading. The parallel tradition has 'this cup' (כוס). This text explicitly says 'death' — either the translator rendered the metaphor literally, or this represents a different textual tradition.
תחפוץ: From חפץ 'to desire/delight in/be willing'. Not in the provided candidates but the root is clear from the consonants.
הסר: This is an imperative of סור 'to turn aside/remove' (hiphil). The candidate H5620 'peevish' for סר does not apply; this is clearly a verbal imperative.
רצוני / רצונך: From רצון 'will/desire/pleasure'. Post-biblical nominal forms with possessive suffixes.

translation_notes: והנה: Candidates: H2009 'lo!/behold', H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither'. Chose H2009 because 'and behold' introduces a sudden visionary event — the appearance of an angel.
מלאך: Candidates: H4397 'messenger/angel', H4398 'angel (Aramaic)', H389 'surely'. Chose H4397 as 'messenger/angel of the heavens'.
ה<מים: The < likely indicates textual damage or an abbreviation. The consonants suggest השמים 'the heavens' with the ש damaged or abbreviated. Reading as 'the heavens'.

מחזק: Root חזק. Candidates: H2388 'to fasten/seize/strengthen', H2389 'strong', H2390 'powerful', H2391 'help', H2392 'power'. Chose H2388 as a piel participle 'strengthening' — the angel was strengthening him.
textual_notes: ה<מים: The damaged character (<) almost certainly conceals a ש, giving השמים 'the heavens'. However, if the missing letter were different, other readings might be possible. The context of 'angel of the ___' strongly supports 'heavens'.
The ים suffix on שמים is intensifying (the fullness of sky/heaven), not pluralizing, consistent with the translation principle for this suffix.

translation_notes: בצרה (consonants ב+צרה): Candidates: H1223 'sheep fold', H1224 'Botsrah (place in Edom)', H6869 'tightness/trouble/distress'. In the context of someone praying in fear with sweat like blood, 'distress' (H6869) is the only reading that produces a coherent image — praying in a sheep fold or in Edom makes no contextual sense here.
textual_notes: The word ב]פחד[ appears with editorial brackets in the source, suggesting the consonants are partially reconstructed or uncertain.

translation_notes: מהתפלה (consonants תפלה): Candidates: H8604 'frivolity', H8605 'intercession/supplication/prayer'. Since the context describes rising from an act of praying (section 1 described prayer in distress), H8605 'prayer/supplication' is the obvious fit.
אל: Candidates: H408/H409 'not', H410 'strength/mighty/God', H411/H412 'these/those', H413 'to/toward'. Following 'came' (ובא), the directional preposition 'to/toward' (H413) is the natural reading.
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. 'On account of' fits the context of explaining why the disciples were sleeping; 'stored grain' makes no sense here.

מהלך: Candidates: H4108 'a walking/access', H4109 'a walk/passage/distance', or from root הלך H1980 'to walk'. The word appears before הולך המלך ('going the king'). As a noun H4108/H4109 it could mean 'a procession' or 'a passage.' As a participle from H1980 with מ prefix, it could mean 'from walking.' The noun reading 'procession/approach' fits best with the following phrase about the king coming.
המלך: Candidates: H4427 'to reign', H4428 'a king', H4429-H4432 various. With the article ה, 'the king' (H4428) is the most natural nominal reading.
textual_notes: The phrase מהלך הולך המלך is syntactically ambiguous. It could mean: (1) 'a procession — the king was approaching,' (2) 'walking, the king was going,' or (3) the entire clause could be a separate sentence fragment describing the approach of the arresting party (the king referring to the authority behind the arrest). The relationship between the disciples sleeping and the approaching procession is unclear — whether 'on account of anxiety' modifies only the sleeping or also introduces the approach.

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. With the ו prefix (narrative consecutive) and context of speech, H559 'to say' is clearly correct.
textual_notes: The word לפתוי does not appear in the Strong's candidates provided. It appears to derive from a root פתה meaning 'to entice/seduce' — the form פתוי would be a verbal noun meaning 'enticement/temptation.' No Strong's number is assigned since the exact form is not listed among candidates.

translation_notes: עוד: Candidates: H5749 'to duplicate/testify', H5750 'iteration/continuance/still/again', H5751 same. In context of 'still he was speaking,' H5750 'still/yet' is the clear adverbial reading.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 same (Aramaic), H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. As a pronoun subject before מדבר, H1931 'he' fits naturally.

מדבר: Candidates: H4057 'pasture/desert/speech', H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. As a participle following הוא ('he was speaking'), H1696 as a participle form is the correct reading.
כן: Candidates: H3651 'thus/so', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. After 'speaking,' the adverb 'thus/so' (H3651) makes natural sense.

והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold!', H5089 'lamentation'. With ו prefix introducing a sudden scene, H2009 'behold!' is the standard dramatic interjection.
אחד: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. As a numeral ('one of the twelve'), H259 is correct.

עשר: Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6236 'ten (Aramaic)', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth', H6240 '-teen'. Combined with the preceding damaged word (מ<נים = שנים 'two'?), this likely reads 'twelve,' so H6240 '-teen' combining with 'two' makes sense, though H6235 'ten' is also possible if the preceding word supplies 'two.'
בעבור: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. 'In order that he might kiss him' — H5668 as purpose clause is the clear reading.
לישוע: H3442 and H3443 are essentially the same name. H3442 is the standard entry for Yeshua.
textual_notes: The word מ<נים contains a damaged character (<). It likely reads משנים (from שנים = 'two'), making 'שנים עשר' = 'twelve.' However, the damage makes this partially reconstructed.
The word שי<קהו also contains a damaged character. It likely reads שינשקהו or שיקהו from the root נשק 'to kiss,' with a 3ms suffix — 'that he might kiss him.'

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say' fits the speech-introducing context. H563 'lamb' and H564 'Immer' are contextually irrelevant.
בן: Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'a son (Aramaic)'. As a common noun in the construct phrase 'son of the man,' H1121 is correct.

האדם: Candidates: H119 'to flush/turn rosy', H120 'a human being/mankind', H121 'Adam (name)', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. With the article ה, 'the man/the human' (H120) fits the well-known Semitic expression 'son of man' meaning a human being.
textual_notes: The word תבגוד (root בגד 'to deal treacherously/betray') is not among the provided Strong's candidates, but the root is clear from context. It is a 2ms imperfect form — 'you betray' or 'you are betraying.'

translation_notes: מה: H4100 'what?/how?' and H4101 are essentially the same. H4100 is the standard Hebrew form. 'What was about to come' = 'what was about to happen.'
אדון: H113 'sovereign/lord/master', H114 'Addon (name)'. As a form of address to a leader, H113 'lord/master' is clearly correct.
אם: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. In context of a question ('shall we strike?'), H518 'if/whether' is correct — it introduces the question.
נכה: H5221 'to strike', H5222 'a smiter', H5223 'smitten/maimed'. As a 1cp imperfect ('shall we strike?'), H5221 is the verbal form that fits.
textual_notes: The word <עתיד contains a damaged character at the beginning. It likely reads העתיד ('the one destined/about to') from the root עתד. This is a post-biblical Hebrew form meaning 'about to/destined to.'
The word בסכין ('with a knife') does not appear in the Strong's lexicon as provided. The noun סכין is a later Hebrew word for 'knife/blade.'

translation_notes: מהם: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they/them'. With the preposition מ ('from'), H1992 'them' gives 'from them' — the natural partitive reading.

הכה: The consonants הכה with context of striking. Although the candidates listed are for כה (H3541 'thus', H3542 same), this is actually the hifil perfect 3ms of נכה (H5221 'to strike'). The form הכה = 'he struck.'

עבד: Candidates: H5647 'to work/serve', H5648 'to do (Aramaic)', H5649 'servant (Aramaic)', H5650 'a servant', H5651 'Ebed (name)', H5652 'a deed'. As the direct object ('struck a servant'), H5650 'a servant' is correct.
אחד: H258 'to unify', H259 'one'. As an adjective/numeral 'one of the chiefs,' H259 is correct.

משרי: Candidates listed are H8297 'Sarai' and H8298 'Sharay.' However, the consonants שרי naturally parse as the construct plural of שר (H8269 'chief/prince/official') — 'chiefs of.' This is not among the provided candidates but is the obvious reading in context ('chiefs of the priests').
האזן: H238 'to listen', H239 'to weigh', H240 'a spade/paddle', H241 'the ear'. With the article ה and in context of cutting off a body part, H241 'the ear' is unmistakably correct.
textual_notes: The word משרי: The provided candidates (Sarai, Sharay) do not match the contextual meaning. The consonants שרי are the construct plural of שר 'chief/prince/official' (H8269), which was not listed among candidates but is the clearly intended reading.

translation_notes: וענה: Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 same (Aramaic), H6033 same (Aramaic), H6034 'Anah (name)'. In a speech context ('answered Yeshua'), H6030 'to respond/answer' is correct.

עד: Candidates: H5703 'perpetuity', H5704 'until/as far as', H5705 same (Aramaic), H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'menstrual flux'. In the phrase 'until here' (עד כאן), H5704 'until/as far as' is correct.
כאן: The candidate listed is H575 אן 'where?/whither?' However, כאן in post-biblical Hebrew means 'here' (כ + אן). This is a common Mishnaic Hebrew term meaning 'here/this point.'
וכאשר: H834 'who/which/what/that/when'. With the prefix כ and ו, 'and when' (H834 used as conjunction of time) is the correct reading.
נגע: H5060 'to touch', H5061 'a blow/plague'. As a verb ('he touched'), H5060 is correct — he touched the ear to heal it.
באזן: H241 'the ear' with preposition ב. Same reasoning as section 7.
textual_notes: The phrase הניחו עד כאן could be parsed as 'let it be, up to here' (meaning 'stop/enough') or 'leave him alone until now.' The imperative הניחו from root נוח 'to rest/leave' with 3ms suffix could mean 'leave him' or could be a plural imperative 'leave off!' Both yield a similar sense of 'stop this.'

translation_notes: לאשר: H834 'who/which/that' is the relative pronoun. 'To those who' — H834 used as a relative introducing 'those who came to him.'
ולשרי: Same as section 7 — the consonants שרי are the construct plural of שר 'chief/official,' not Sarai (H8297).
המקדש: H4720 'a consecrated place/sanctuary/temple'. The other candidates (H6942 'to be clean', H6943 'Kedesh', etc.) do not fit as nouns with the article. H4720 'the sanctuary/temple' is correct.
כגנב: H1589 'to thieve', H1590 'a stealer/thief'. With the preposition כ ('like'), H1590 'a thief' as a noun gives 'like a thief,' which fits the accusatory context.
textual_notes: The word ולרבני does not appear in the Strong's candidates. It appears to be the construct plural of רבן or רב with a suffix meaning 'leaders/masters/rabbis of.' This is a post-biblical Hebrew term.
The word ובעצים could derive from עץ (H6086 'tree/wood/stick') in the plural — 'sticks/clubs.' This is not among provided candidates but is the clear contextual reading.

translation_notes: כל: H3605 'the whole/all/every', H3606 same (Aramaic). H3605 is standard Hebrew — 'every day.'
היום: H3117 'a day', H3118 'a day (Aramaic)'. H3117 is standard Hebrew. With the article, 'the day' — combined with כל: 'every day.'
ולא: H3808 'not', H3809 same (Aramaic). H3808 is the standard Hebrew negation.
יד: H3027 'a hand', H3028 same (Aramaic). H3027 'hand' — the idiom שלח יד means 'to send/stretch out a hand (against someone).'
בי: H994 is glossed 'oh that!/with leave.' However, בי here is simply the preposition ב + 1cs suffix 'in me/against me.' H994 doesn't fit; this is a simple prepositional phrase.
רק: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. As a conjunction introducing a contrast ('but/only'), H7535 is correct.
ועוז: H5756 'to be strong/strengthen.' The noun form עוז means 'strength/power/might.' In construct with the following word, 'the power/strength of the darkness.'

שלחתם: The candidates listed are for חתם (H2856 'to seal'), but the actual root here is שלח 'to send' with 2mp suffix — שלחתם = 'you sent.' The Strong's candidates appear mismatched; the root is שלח (H7971).
textual_notes: The word הע&רפל contains a damaged character (&). It most likely reads הערפל from ערפל (H6205) meaning 'thick darkness/gloom/dark cloud.' The damage makes this partially reconstructed.

The word שעתנו ('your hour') uses the post-biblical Hebrew word שעה 'hour' with a 2mp or 1cp suffix. The suffix כם would be expected for 'your (pl.)'; the נו suffix typically means 'our.' This could read 'our hour' rather than 'your hour.' Context suggests it addresses the adversaries ('your hour'), but the morphology could indicate 'our hour.'
The word בי: H994 is the only candidate provided, but contextually this is the preposition ב + 1cs pronominal suffix ('against me'), not the interjection 'oh that!'

translation_notes: בית (B-Y-T): Candidates: H1004 'house', H1005 same, H1006 'Bajith' a place name. Chose H1004 because context describes being led to a dwelling/compound of the priestly prefect.
סגן (S-G-N): Candidates: H5460 and H5461 both mean 'prefect of a province.' Chose H5461 as the standard form; here it refers to the deputy/chief of the priests.
textual_notes: סגן הכהנים could mean 'prefect of the priests' (a deputy high priest) or could be read as a general authority title over the priestly class.

translation_notes: האש (H-A-Sh): Candidates: H784 'fire', H786 'entity/there is', H787 'foundation'. Chose H784 because they are kindling it and standing around it — clearly fire.
והם (V-H-M): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because it serves as the pronoun subject of 'standing.'
היה (H-Y-H): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because it functions as the past-tense copula 'was' before 'sitting.'

שפחה (Sh-P-Ch-H): Candidates: H8198 'female slave/maidservant', or root פחה H6346 'prefect.' Chose H8198 because the narrative describes a servant girl noticing someone, and the full consonantal form matches 'maidservant' exactly.

באש (B-A-Sh): Candidates: H887 'to smell bad', H784 'fire' (with prefix ב). Context from section 2 establishes a fire scene; 'sitting by the fire' is coherent. 'Sitting in stench' would be bizarre. Chose ב + H784 'by/at the fire.'
זה (Z-H): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep'. Chose H2088 because the maidservant is identifying a person: 'this one was with them.'
היה (H-Y-H): Candidates: H1961 'to be/was', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 as past tense copula in the statement 'this one was with them.'
textual_notes: באש could theoretically be parsed as the verb H887 'to stink' but contextually it is clearly the preposition ב + אש 'fire' continuing the fire scene from the previous section.

translation_notes: כפר (K-P-R): Candidates: H3722 'to cover/expiate/deny', H3723 'village', H3724 'cover/bitumen', H3725 'expiation', H6499 (פר) 'bullock'. Chose H3722 in the sense of 'to deny/cover over' because Kepha is responding to an accusation by concealing the truth.

אומר: The only Strong's candidate listed is H201 'Omar' (proper name). However, these consonants are clearly the participial form of אמר H559 'to say.' The candidate list is incomplete; this is the active participle 'saying.'
textual_notes: א־ה appears twice and is not given dictionary candidates. The dashes suggest interrupted or abbreviated writing. In context these appear to be negative interjections — likely a form of 'no' (perhaps אלה or a dialectal negative). Translated as emphatic denial 'no, no.'
איניני appears to be an emphatic first-person negative form: אין + אני 'I am not' — a doubled/intensified denial form.

translation_notes: ואחר (V-A-Ch-R): Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'after', H311 'after', H312 'other/next'. Chose H310 as adverbial 'after' because 'after a little' makes temporal sense.
מעט (M-'-T): Candidates: H4591 'to lessen', H4592 'a little/few', H4593 'sharp', H5842 (עט) 'stylus'. Chose H4592 'a little' because 'after a little' is a natural temporal phrase.
פעם (P-'-M): Candidates: H6470 'to tap/beat', H6471 'a stroke/time/occurrence'. Chose H6471 'time/occurrence' because 'another time' fits the narrative of repeated encounters.
ואתה (V-A-T-H): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because the maidservant is addressing Kepha directly: 'and you are from them.'

אדם (A-D-M): Candidates: H119 'to flush', H120 'human being/man', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 'man' as an exclamatory address — Kepha saying 'Man, I am not!' as an emphatic denial.
אשה (A-Sh-H): Candidates: H800 'fire', H801 'burnt offering', H802 'woman'. Chose H802 'woman' as it appears in a direct address context.
textual_notes: This section appears heavily corrupted or contains significant scribal errors/glosses. From 'ועצים עמכם שעתנו שעתינו ועז הערפליי ראהו איני היית אשה אתה את' the text is very difficult to parse coherently. The words 'ועצים' (and trees/counsels), 'שעתנו/שעתינו' (our hour, repeated with variant spelling), 'ועז הערפליי' (and the strong/bold foggy one), and 'היית אשה אתה את' (you were a woman, you) do not form a coherent narrative sequence. This may represent marginal glosses, scribal notes, or textual corruption that has been copied into the main text. The core narrative appears to be: 'And after a little while another time she saw him and said: You too are from them! And Kepha said: Man, I am not!' The remainder may be a corrupted parallel or displaced text.
The apostrophe/quotation mark after אדם is unusual and may represent a scribal notation or paragraph marker.

translation_notes: שעה (Sh-'-H): Candidates: H8159 'to gaze/look', H8160 'a look/moment.' Chose H8160 'moment/hour' because 'about one hour' is a natural temporal measurement following 'a little.'
זה (Z-H): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep'. Chose H2088 demonstrative pronoun — the speaker is pointing out a person.
היה (H-Y-H): Candidates: H1961 'to be/was', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 as past copula: 'this one was with them.'
כי (K-Y): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'for/because.' Chose H3588 as causal conjunction introducing the reason for the identification.

גללי: The only listed candidate is H1562 'Gilalai, an Israelite.' However, these consonants (ג-ל-ל-י) closely match the demonym 'Galilean' (גלילי), with a plausible scribal simplification of the double-lamed. In this narrative context — identifying someone by regional origin — 'Galilean' is the clear intended meaning.
הוא (H-V-A): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as the emphatic pronoun completing the identification: 'he is.'
textual_notes: א<ה contains a bracket/corruption marker. This may be אחד ('one/a certain') with a damaged letter, or possibly another word. Context suggests it introduces 'a certain one' who is speaking.

גללי is listed only as H1562 'Gilalai' (a proper name) but contextually must be the gentilic 'Galilean' — the consonants are very close to גלילי. This appears to be a dialectal or scribal variant spelling.

אומרת has feminine participial form, yet the preceding word sequence is ambiguous about the speaker's gender. If א<ה אחת is 'a certain [woman]' (אחת being feminine), then the feminine participle אומרת is consistent.

translation_notes: אמר (A-M-R): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because Kepha is actively speaking.
אדם (A-D-M): Same analysis as section 5 — chose H120 'man' as an exclamatory address in denial.
מה (M-H): Candidates: H4100 'what?', H4101 same. Chose H4100 as interrogative: 'what you are saying.'
אתה (A-T-H): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because the sentence requires a subject pronoun: 'what you are saying.'
קרא (Q-R-A): Candidates: H7121 'to call out', H7122 'to encounter', H7124 'partridge'. Chose H7121 'to call out' because it describes the rooster crowing.
ומיד: Literally 'and from hand' — an idiomatic expression meaning 'immediately.' Based on יד H3027 'hand' with prefixes ו + מ.
textual_notes: התרנגול is not given Strong's candidates — it is a post-biblical Hebrew word for 'rooster/cock' not found in the classical Strong's lexicon. It is well attested in Mishnaic Hebrew.

translation_notes: ישוע (Y-Sh-V-'): Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua', H3443 same. Chose H3442 as the proper name Yeshua.
דבר (D-B-R): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 'word' because Kepha is remembering a spoken utterance.
שאמר: ש (relative particle 'that/which') + אמר H559 'said.' The compound means 'that he said.'
שלש (Sh-L-Sh): Candidates: H8027 'to make triple/three', H8028 'Shelesh', H8029 'third generation.' Chose H8027 in its cardinal sense 'three' modifying 'times.'

כופר: Listed candidate is פר H6499 'bullock.' However, כופר is the active participle of כפר H3722 'to deny/cover' — the same root used in section 4. In context 'denying me' is the clear reading, matching Kepha's repeated denials throughout this narrative.
בי (B-Y): The listed candidate is H994 'oh that!/please.' However, here בי functions as the preposition ב + first person suffix 'in me/me,' the object of the denial: 'denying me.'
textual_notes: בי could theoretically be the interjection H994 'oh that!' but contextually it must be the prepositional phrase 'in me' — the object of כופר 'denying.'
קודם is a post-biblical Hebrew temporal adverb 'before' — not found in the classical Strong's lexicon but well attested in Mishnaic Hebrew.

translation_notes: יצא (Y-Ts-A): Candidates: H3318 'to go out', H3319 same. Chose H3318 as the standard form.

ובכה (V-B-K-H): Candidates: H1058 'to weep', H1059 'a weeping', or כה H3541 'thus.' Chose H1058 'to weep' because the narrative describes an emotional reaction after the rooster's crow and remembering the prophecy.
והעם: Candidates: H5971 'a people/nation', H5973 'with.' Chose H5971 because the article ה indicates a definite noun 'the people,' not a preposition.

מכים: The candidates listed are for the suffix ים (H3220 'sea' etc.) but this is clearly the hiphil participle plural of נכה H5221 'to strike.' The ים here is the masculine plural participial ending 'ones striking.'
textual_notes: התופשים derives from תפש 'to seize/take hold of' — this is a participial form 'the ones seizing/holding' which is not in the provided candidates but is well-established Hebrew (cf. H8610).

translation_notes: נביא (consonants נביא): Candidates: H5029 'a prophet', H5030 'a prophet or inspired man'. In this context the word functions as an imperative command — 'prophesy!' — addressed to the person being struck. Both entries point to the same root meaning. Chose H5030 as the more general entry. Note: the consonants נביא could be parsed as the noun 'prophet' or as an imperative 'prophesy!' The surrounding context (a challenge to identify the striker) strongly supports the imperative reading.

הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 'he/it (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 because this is a Hebrew clause functioning as a pronoun 'he' in the question 'who is he that struck you.'

שהכה: The ש is the relative particle 'that/who'; הכה is from נכה (to strike/smite). The candidates listed under כה (H3541/H3542 'thus/like this') do not apply here — the root is clearly הכה from נכה meaning 'struck', as the entire context describes physical striking.
textual_notes: נביא could be read as the noun 'prophet' (O prophet! who is he...) or as an imperative 'prophesy!' Both make contextual sense — one mocks his prophetic claim as a title, the other commands him to demonstrate prophetic ability. The imperative reading is slightly favored by the interrogative structure that follows.

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher (proper name)', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. With the prefixed וכ (and-as/when), H834 is the only candidate that works as a temporal conjunction: 'and when.' All other options would produce incoherent syntax.

העם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people/tribe', H5972 (Aramaic people), H5973 'with (preposition)', H5974 (Aramaic with). Preceded by זקני ('elders of'), H5971 'the people' is the natural reading — 'elders of the people.'

ושרי (consonants שרי): The listed candidates H8297 'Sarai' and H8298 'Sharay' are proper names that make no sense here. The word is clearly שרי from שר (H8269, 'chief/prince/ruler') in construct plural — 'chiefs of.' The candidates provided do not include H8269 but the consonants שר+י clearly represent the construct plural of שר.

בבית (consonants בית): Candidates: H1004 'a house', H1005 (Aramaic house), H1006 'Bajith (place name)'. With the prefix ב ('in') and followed by עצתם ('their counsel'), H1004 'house' is correct — 'in the house of their counsel' i.e. their council chamber.
textual_notes: עצתם ('their counsel/council') could refer to either the abstract concept of their deliberation or the concrete council body/assembly. Both readings are valid; the phrase 'house of their counsel' likely refers to a council chamber or sanhedrin hall.

translation_notes: אם (first instance): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether/although'. Chose H518 because this introduces a conditional question — 'if you are the Messiah.'
אתה (consonants אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 same, H859 'you (singular)'. Chose H859 because the syntax requires a pronoun — 'if you [are] Messiah.'

משיח (consonants משיח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'shrub'. Chose H4899 because it functions as a title predicate — 'if you are the Anointed One.'
אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the context is direct speech — 'Yeshua said.'

להם (consonants להם/הם): Candidates: H3859 'to burn/rankle', H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 with ל prefix — 'to them' — the standard prepositional phrase for indirect object.
אם (second instance): Same analysis as first — H518 'if' introducing a conditional clause.
אומר: H201 'Omar (name)' was the only candidate offered, but this is clearly a qal active participle of אמר (H559) meaning 'I say/am saying.' The proper noun reading makes no sense in context.
textual_notes: אומר — the only Strong's candidate provided was H201 (Omar, a name), but this is transparently the participle of אמר H559 'saying/I say.' I assign it to H559.
תאמינוני has no candidates provided; it is a hiphil imperfect 2mp of אמן with 1cs suffix — 'you will believe me.'

translation_notes: ואם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because this continues the conditional pattern from the previous section — 'and if I ask you.'
לא (both instances): Candidates: H3808 'not (absolute negation)', H3809 same in Aramaic. Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation particle.
textual_notes: תעזבוני could be from עזב 'to leave/forsake/release' — in this context it could mean 'you will not let me go/release me' or 'you will not leave me alone.' The former fits better with a trial/interrogation setting where the accused might hope for release.
אשאל is 1cs imperfect of שאל (H7592) 'I will ask/question.' No candidates were provided for this inflected form.
תענוני is 2mp imperfect of ענה 'to answer' with 1cs suffix. No candidates were provided.

translation_notes: בעבור (consonants עבור): Candidates: H5668 'crossed/transit — on account of, in order that', H5669 'passed/stored grain'. Chose H5668 because it functions as a temporal/causal adverb — 'on account of this' or 'from this [point forward].'

זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'this' as the demonstrative object of the preposition. 'On account of a sheep the son of man will sit' is incoherent.
בן (consonants בן): Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 same as H1121. Chose H1121 because 'son of the man/Adam' is a well-known title construction.

האדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to be ruddy', H120 'a human being/mankind', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because בן האדם 'son of man/humanity' is the standard construct — it denotes a human being. H121 'Adam' is also possible (son of Adam), but H120 as generic 'man' is the primary reading.
לימין (consonants ימין): Candidates: H3225 'right hand/side', H3226 'Jamin (name)'. Chose H3225 because 'sitting at the right hand of power' describes a position of authority.
כח (consonants כח): H3581 'vigor/force/power' — the only candidate. It describes divine might.
יהוה (consonants יהוה): Candidates: H3068 'YHWH', H3069 same. Chose H3068 as the primary entry for the divine name.
textual_notes: בעבור זה could mean 'on account of this' (causal) or 'from this [time onward]' (temporal). Both readings are grammatically valid. The temporal reading ('from now on') fits better with the future tense יהיה 'will be.'
האדם could be H120 'humanity/a human' or H121 'Adam' — 'son of man' vs. 'son of Adam.' Both produce a meaningful title. H120 is the more standard reading for this construct.

translation_notes: אם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 — introduces the inferential question 'if so, then you are...'
כן (consonants כן): Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/right', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. Chose H3651 because אם כן is a standard idiom meaning 'if so/therefore.'
אתה (consonants אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 same, H859 'you'. Chose H859 — the pronoun 'you' is required as the subject of the implied copula.
בן (consonants בן): Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben', H1123 same. Chose H1121 — 'son of God' as a title.
האלוה (consonants אלוה): H433 'a deity or the Deity.' With the definite article — 'the God.'
אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — Yeshua spoke in response.
שאני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because ש + אני = 'that I' — the relative particle with the first person pronoun. 'That a ship he is' makes no sense.
הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/self/the same', H1932 same Aramaic, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 — the emphatic pronoun 'he' completing the identification: 'that I am he.'
textual_notes: אתם was given only H864 'Etham (a place in the desert)' as a candidate, but this is clearly the 2mp pronoun 'you (plural).' The Strong's lexicon typically doesn't assign a number to this common pronoun separately; it functions here as subject of the participle אומרים.

The phrase שאני הוא ('that I am he') is an emphatic self-identification. הוא could be read as the existential verb H1933 'to be' rather than the pronoun H1931 'he.' Both produce essentially the same meaning: 'that I am [he]' / 'that I exist [as such].' Chose H1931 as the pronoun reading is more direct.

translation_notes: והם (consonants ה-ם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham, a region', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. Chose H1992 because the waw-prefix + pronoun 'and they' is the natural subject of 'said' in this narrative context; a place name or 'wealth' makes no sense here.

למה (consonants ל-מ-ה): Candidates: H4100 'what? how? why?', H4101 (Aramaic equivalent). Chose H4100 because this is Hebrew text and ל + מה = 'for what' = 'why', which fits perfectly as an interrogative introducing the rhetorical question about needing witnesses.

אתם: The only Strong's candidate provided is H864 'Etham, a place in the Desert.' However, אתם is the standard second-person masculine plural pronoun 'you' (not separately listed in Strong's as a standalone lexeme because it is a basic pronoun). Context demands 'you' — the speakers are addressing others directly about their seeking of witnesses. A desert place name is nonsensical here.

עוד (consonants ע-ו-ד): Candidates: H5749 'to testify/repeat', H5750 'still/again/further', H5751 (Aramaic equivalent). Chose H5750 because the adverbial sense 'still/further' fits the rhetorical question 'why are you still seeking witnesses?' — they already have testimony from his own mouth.

והה: H1929 'ah!' expressing grief. However, in this context והה likely functions as a demonstrative particle 'behold' (variant spelling or interjection drawing attention), introducing the declaration 'we ourselves heard him.' The exclamatory function fits well — it marks the shift from question to emphatic assertion.
כל (consonants כ-ל): Candidates: H3605 'the whole/all', H3606 (Aramaic equivalent). Chose H3605 as the Hebrew form; 'all the people' is the natural reading.

העם (consonants ע-ם with article ה): Candidates: H5971 'a people/assembly', H5972 (Aramaic), H5973 'with (preposition)', H5974 (Aramaic). Chose H5971 because the definite article ה + עם = 'the people/assembly', which is the subject of 'rose up.' A preposition 'with' makes no grammatical sense here.
ישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Yeshua', H3443 (variant). Chose H3442 — the proper name Yeshua (Jesus), the object being led to Pilatus.
textual_notes: The brackets ] [ in the manuscript likely indicate a section break, paragraph division, or a lacuna marker between the two scenes (the declaration about witnesses and the leading of Yeshua to Pilatus). Their exact function is uncertain.

והה could be read as the interjection H1929 'ah!' (expressing grief or exclamation) or as a variant demonstrative particle 'behold/here.' In context the demonstrative-emphatic sense fits better ('behold, we ourselves heard'), but the grief reading ('alas, we ourselves heard') is also possible if the speakers express dismay at what they heard.

אתם is listed only as H864 (Etham, a place name) in the provided candidates, but the consonants are identical to the standard 2nd person masculine plural pronoun. Context unambiguously demands the pronoun.

23.summary: Phase 1 consonantal translation — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided. Literal and amplified readings produced independently from consonantal Hebrew.

translation_notes: זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because the context points to a demonstrative pronoun referring to the accused person — 'this one' — not 'a sheep.'

ומהפך (root הפך): Candidates: H2015 'to turn about/overturn/pervert', H2016 'a turn/reverse', H2017 'perversity'. Chose H2015 as a participial form 'overturning/perverting', fitting the accusation pattern alongside מדיח.
מס (consonants מס): Candidates: H4522 'tax/forced labor', H4523 'fainting/disconsolate'. Chose H4522 because the context is explicitly about paying tribute to Caesar.
שהוא (הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 as the standard Hebrew pronoun 'he' used with the relative particle ש.

מלך (consonants מלך): Candidates: H4427 'to reign', H4428 'a king', H4429 'Melek (name)', H4430 'king (Aramaic)', H4431 'advice', H4432 'Molek'. Chose H4428 'a king' because the accusation is that he claims to be king.

המשיח (consonants משיח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', or root שיח H7878-H7880 'ponder/shrub'. Chose H4899 because the prefix ה is the article on משיח, and the context is a messianic claim — 'the Messiah.'
textual_notes: והתחילו, להלשינו, מצינו, מדיח, עמנו, ומונע, לתת, לקיסר, אומר — these are post-biblical/medieval Hebrew forms not in Strong's lexicon. They are translated based on standard Hebrew morphology and meaning.

אומר: The only Strong's candidate given is H201 'Omar' (a proper name). However, the consonants אמר clearly function here as a participle of the common verb 'to say' (from root אמר, H559). The candidate list appears incomplete; this is unambiguously the verb 'says/saying.'

translation_notes: מלך (consonants מלך): Candidates: H4427 'to reign', H4428 'a king', H4429-H4432 various. Chose H4428 'king' because Pilate is asking about a title/status, not an action.
והוא (הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933/H1934 'to be/exist'. Chose H1931 as the standard pronoun with conjunction ו — 'and he.'
אתה (consonants אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you'. Chose H859 'you' because the response 'you say' is a coherent reply to a direct question.
אומר: As in section 1, the consonants אמר here function as a participle 'say/saying' from the root אמר (H559), not the proper name Omar (H201).
textual_notes: שואל: The Strong's candidates listed are for אל only, but the word is clearly the participial form of שאל 'to ask/inquire' (H7592). The candidate list appears to reflect only the final consonants.

אתהו: This appears to be a compound form — אתה + הוא ('are you he') or simply אתה with a pronominal suffix. Not in Strong's as a standalone entry. Translated as 'are you [he]' based on the interrogative context.
ופילאט, היהודים, ענהו: These forms are not covered by Strong's entries provided. Pilate is a loanword; היהודים is 'the Jews/Judeans'; ענהו is 'he answered him' from root ענה.

translation_notes: אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because Pilate is speaking — the verb 'said' fits perfectly.

לשרי (consonants שרי): Candidates: H8297 'Sarai', H8298 'Sharay', H7377 'irrigation/shower'. None of these fit. The word is actually from שר (H8269 'prince/chief/ruler') in construct plural — 'chiefs of.' The candidates provided do not include the correct root.

בזה (consonants בזה): Candidates: H959 'to disesteem', H960 'scorned', H961 'booty'; or ב + זה: H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this'. Chose ב + H2088 'in this' because Pilate is saying 'in this man' — a preposition plus demonstrative pronoun is coherent in the judicial context.

האדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to flush/turn rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 'human being/man' because Pilate is referring to the accused person.

שום (consonants שום): Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7761 same (Aramaic), H7762 'garlic'. In post-biblical Hebrew שום functions as 'any/whatsoever.' Chose H7760 as the closest root — the word has evolved to mean 'any' in later Hebrew usage.

טעם (consonants טעם): Candidates: H2938 'to taste/perceive', H2939 'to taste/feed', H2940 'taste/perception/intelligence', H2941 'judicial sentence', H2942 'flavor/judgment/account'. Chose H2940 'perception/reason/grounds' because Pilate is declaring he finds no basis or reason for condemnation.

מוצא (consonants מוצא): Candidates: H4161 'a going forth/source/product', H4162 'Motsa (name)'. Here מוצא functions as a participle of מצא 'to find.' The noun form H4161 shares consonants but the verbal participle 'finding' is the correct reading in context — 'I am not finding.'
textual_notes: לשרי: The Strong's candidates (Sarai, Sharay, irrigation) do not include the common word שר 'prince/chief/ruler' (H8269). The form is clearly the construct plural of שר with preposition ל — 'to the chiefs/rulers of.'
ולחיילות: Not in Strong's lexicon. This is a later Hebrew word for 'troops/soldiers/forces.' Could also refer to assembled crowds depending on the manuscript tradition.
מוצא: Could be read as the noun H4161 'going forth/exit' or as the participle of מצא 'to find.' Context demands the participial reading 'finding.'

translation_notes: והם (הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (region)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because the subject is clearly the accusers — 'and they.'
הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 same (Aramaic), H1933/H1934 'to be/exist'. Chose H1931 'he' as the subject pronoun referring to the accused.

באופן (אופן): Candidate: H212 'a wheel.' In biblical Hebrew אופן means 'wheel,' but in later Hebrew it evolved to mean 'manner/way' (as a wheel turns). The context demands 'in [such a] manner/way' — describing how he acts.

שהעם (עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people/nation', H5972 same (Aramaic), H5973 'with (preposition)', H5974 same (Aramaic). Chose H5971 because the ה prefix is the article — 'the people' — and they are the ones being turned/subverted.

לאחר (אחר): Candidates: H309 'to loiter/delay', H310 'after/behind', H311 'after (Aramaic)', H312 'another/other/next', H313 'Acher (name)'. Chose H310 'after' — the people are 'turned to [follow] after [him],' meaning led astray. H312 'another' is also possible — 'turned to another [teaching].'

מלמד (consonants מלמד): Candidates: H4451 'an ox-goad', H3925 'to teach/goad', H4055 'measure/garment'. Chose H3925 as a participial form 'teaching' — he is described as teaching throughout Judea, which fits the accusation narrative perfectly. An ox-goad (H4451) makes no sense here.
בכל (כל): Candidates: H3605 'the whole/all/every', H3606 same (Aramaic). Chose H3605 — 'in all [of].'
מגלילה (גלילה): Candidate: H1552 'a circuit/region.' With מ prefix meaning 'from,' this reads 'from the region' — contextually referring to the Galilee district.

עד (consonants עד): Candidates: H5703 'perpetuity', H5704 'as far as/until', H5705 same (Aramaic), H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'menstrual flux'. Chose H5704 'as far as/until' — describing geographic extent from Galilee to here.
כאן (אן): Candidate: H575 'where/whither.' With כ prefix this could mean 'like where,' but כאן in later Hebrew simply means 'here.' The context 'from Galilee and until here' confirms this reading.
textual_notes: לאחר: Could be read as H310 'after' (the people are turned to follow after [him]) or H312 'another' (the people are turned to another [way/teaching]). Both produce coherent readings in the accusation context.
באופן: H212 'wheel' is the only biblical candidate, but in post-biblical Hebrew אופן means 'manner/way.' The text appears to use later Hebrew vocabulary.
נהפך: This is a nif'al (passive) form of הפך — 'is turned/overturned/subverted.' No Strong's entry was provided for this specific form, but it derives from H2015.

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when/because', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כאשר functions as 'when/as' — a temporal conjunction introducing the clause.

שמע (consonants שמע): Candidates: H8085 'to hear intelligently', H8086 same (Aramaic), H8087-H8090 various names/nouns. Chose H8085 because Pilate is hearing/perceiving the mention of Galilee in the accusation.
מגלילה (גלילה): Candidate: H1552 'a circuit/region.' With מ prefix — 'from the region,' contextually the Galilee.
שאל (consonants שאל): Candidates: H7592 'to inquire/request/demand', H7593 same (Aramaic), H7594 'Sheal (name)'. Chose H7592 — Pilate asked/inquired.
האדם (אדם): Candidates: H119 'flush/rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 — 'the man,' referring to the accused.
אם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because Pilate is asking a yes/no question — 'whether he is a Galilean.'
הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 same (Aramaic), H1933/H1934 'to be/exist'. Chose H1931 'he' as the subject pronoun.

גללי: Candidate: H1562 'Gilalai (a name).' However, the consonants גללי in this context clearly denote a gentillic/demonym — 'a Galilean' — derived from גליל/גלילה 'Galilee.' The Strong's entry for the personal name Gilalai shares consonants but does not fit the context of asking about regional origin.
textual_notes: גללי: The only Strong's candidate is H1562 'Gilalai' (a personal name). However, in context this is clearly the demonym 'Galilean' (from גליל/גלילה). The consonants overlap but the function is entirely different — an adjective of origin rather than a proper name.

אותו האדם: The syntax could be parsed as 'he asked him, the man' (with האדם in apposition to אותו) or 'he asked the man about him.' The former reading is more natural — Pilate asked the man [directly] whether he was a Galilean.

translation_notes: והכיר: The listed candidate H3600 כיר 'cooking range' does not fit. The root here is נכר (H5234) in hiphil — 'to recognize/discern'. The hiphil form הכיר means 'he recognized/understood'. This is the correct reading.

כי (both occurrences): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction'. Chose H3588 both times — first as 'that' (introducing the content of recognition), second as 'for/because' (explaining why he sent him to Herod).
ההם (הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — with the article prefix ה, this is the demonstrative 'those' (ההם = 'those').
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 — 'he was' in Jerusalem at that time.
textual_notes: מיכולת is not in the standard Strong's lexicon. It appears to be מ (from) + יכולת (ability/jurisdiction/authority), derived from the root יכל 'to be able'. This is a later Hebrew formation meaning 'authority/jurisdiction'.
נשתלח is a hitpael or nithpael form of שלח 'to send' — 'he was sent'. The reflexive/passive form indicates the action was done to the subject.
The antecedent of 'he was' (היה) at the end is ambiguous — it likely refers to Herod being present in Jerusalem, explaining why Pilate could send the accused to him.

translation_notes: כשראה (ראה): Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7203 'seer/vision'. Chose H7200 — 'when he saw', a straightforward temporal clause.
שמח: Candidates: H8055 'to brighten up/be glad', H8056 'gleeful'. Chose H8055 — the verb form 'he rejoiced'.
מאד: H3966 'vehemently/greatly'. Straightforward intensifier.
כי: H3588 — conjunction 'for/because', introducing the reason for his joy.

כסף: Candidates: H3700 'to become pale/pine after/yearn', H3701 'silver/money'. Chose H3700 because the context describes emotional desire — 'he longed/yearned to see him'. Silver/money makes no sense here with 'to see him' following.
בעבור (עבור): Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'kept over (grain)'. Chose H5668 — 'on account of' introducing the reason for his longing.

ומצפה (צפה): Candidates: H4707 'observatory', H6822 'to peer/observe/await', H6823 'to overlay with metal'. Chose H6822 — the participle 'expecting/watching/awaiting', which fits Herod's anticipation.
מתי: H4970 'when' — interrogative adverb used in indirect question.
אי: Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H339 'island'. Chose H335 — combined with זה it forms 'some kind of' or 'which' (אי זה = 'which/some').
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep'. Chose H2088 — together with אי forms the compound 'some/any' (אי זה אות = 'some sign').
אות: Candidates: H225 'to assent', H226 'a sign/signal/omen'. Chose H226 — 'a sign/wonder/portent', the object of Herod's expectation.
textual_notes: ש<מע contains a textual marker (<). This likely represents שׁמע 'he heard'.
פעמים lacks a listed Strong's candidate but is clearly the plural of פעם (H6471) 'a time/occurrence'. 'Many times' or simply 'times' — indicating repeated occasions of longing.

כסף as H3700 'to yearn/pine' is the less common reading of these consonants (H3701 'silver' being far more frequent), but the verbal sense is required by the syntax — it governs the infinitive לראותו 'to see him'.

translation_notes: ושאל (שאל): Candidates: H7592 'to inquire/request/demand', H7594 'Sheal'. Chose H7592 — 'and he asked/inquired', the natural verb for questioning.
מעולם (עולם): H5769 'time out of mind/perpetuity'. With the prefix מ and followed by לא, this yields 'never' (from everlasting + not = never).
לא: H3808 'not'. Simple negation paired with מעולם to mean 'never'.
על: Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'upon/about/concerning', H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 — 'about/concerning a matter'.
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence'. Chose H1697 — the noun 'a thing/matter', object of his non-response.
textual_notes: ענהו is the verb ענה (H6030 'to answer') with a 3ms pronominal suffix — 'answered him'. Not listed in candidates but unambiguous from the consonants.
אליו is the preposition אל (H413) with 3ms suffix — 'to him'. The candidates list various readings of אל but H413 is the clear preposition here.

translation_notes: ושרי: Same as previous sections — construct plural of שׂר (H8269) 'chief/prince', not the proper names H8297/H8298.
בחוזק: The prefix ב + חוזק (from the root חזק H2388/H2392 'to be strong'). H2392 is 'strength'. This means 'with strength/forcefully/vehemently'.
ומלשינים: A later Hebrew term from the root לשן 'tongue' — a malshin is an informer/slanderer. This is post-biblical vocabulary meaning 'informing against/accusing/slandering'.
textual_notes: ומלשינים is not found in the classical Strong's lexicon. It is a medieval/late Hebrew participial form meaning 'informing against' or 'slandering' — derived from the denominative verb הלשין (from לשון 'tongue'). The word clearly means accusation/denunciation in this legal context.

translation_notes: עם: Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5973 because the phrase 'Herod with his faction' requires a preposition, not a noun meaning 'people'.

לבנה: Candidates: H3839 'whitish tree/storax', H3840 'whiteness/transparency', H3841 'Libnah (place)', H3842 'the moon', H3843 'a brick'. Chose H3840 'whiteness/brilliance' because it modifies the purple garment — a white or brilliant purple robe is a coherent image of mockery through royal clothing.
לעג: Candidates: H3932 'to deride', H3933 'derision/scoffing', H3934 'a buffoon/foreigner'. Chose H3933 as a noun 'mockery' because it follows the verb 'brought out' — they produced mockery upon him.
באופן: H212 'a wheel'. In later Hebrew, אופן developed the meaning 'manner/way' (from the turning of a wheel). In this narrative context, 'in a manner/way that' makes sense as a transition clause.
textual_notes: לבנה could be read as H3840 'whiteness/brilliance' modifying ארגמן (a white-purple, i.e. a brilliant or light purple), or it could be a separate garment description. The combination 'purple white' is unusual — it may mean a white robe (as distinct from purple) or a luminous purple.
באופן שנגשו — the word אופן in biblical Hebrew means 'wheel' but in later Hebrew means 'manner/way'. This suggests the text may be post-biblical or Mishnaic Hebrew.

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand or scar', H3588 'conjunction: for, because, that'. Chose H3588 because the clause introduces a causal explanation for the preceding statement.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this or that'. Chose H2088 because 'before this' is a standard temporal expression; 'before a sheep' makes no sense.
מאד: Candidates: H3966 'vehemently/greatly', H108 'a fog'. Chose H3966 because 'they were enemies greatly' is coherent; 'enemies of fog' is not.

קרא: Candidates: H7121 'to call out/summon', H7122 'to encounter', H7123 'to call (Aramaic)', H7124 'partridge'. Chose H7121 because Pilate is actively summoning people — this is a deliberate act, not an accidental encounter.

שרי: Candidates: H8297 'Sarai (wife of Abraham)', H8298 'Sharay (a name)'. Neither fits. The consonants שרי are the construct plural of שר 'prince/chief/official'. In the phrase 'שרי הכהנים' this is 'chiefs of the priests' — a standard Hebrew construct.
והעם: Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5971 because it appears as the third element in a list (chiefs of priests, rabbis, and the people), requiring a noun.
textual_notes: שרי is not listed under its proper root שר (H8269) in the candidates provided, but the consonants clearly represent the construct plural of 'chief/prince'. The candidates H8297/H8298 are proper nouns that do not fit this context.

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the vav-prefix form indicates a verb 'and he said'.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 (the 3mp pronoun with preposition ל) because 'he said to them' is the natural reading in this context.
זה (first): H2088 'this/that' — demonstrative pronoun modifying 'the man'. H2089 'a sheep' would produce 'you brought to me a sheep the man' which is incoherent.
האדם (first): H120 'a human being/man'. The article ה + אדם = 'the man'. H123 'Edom' with the article would be unusual and contextually unmotivated.
הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2009 because 'behold, I questioned him' is a standard declarative opening.

דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'I did not find a thing/matter' is coherent; 'I did not find a pestilence' or 'pasture' is not.
textual_notes: The second האדם could be read as 'the man' (referring to the accused) or could carry the broader sense of H120 'humanity/the people' — i.e., 'that he drives away this people'. The narrative context (an accusation before a governor) supports either reading.
שיגרש — the root גרש means 'to drive out/expel'. The accusation may be that he 'drives away' (misleads/stirs up) the people, or that he 'expels' in some other sense.
The angle bracket < before אתם may indicate a textual note or damage in the manuscript.

translation_notes: כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/likewise', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'and also so/likewise' is a standard adverbial phrase.
כי: H3588 'for/because' — introducing the reason (Herod sent them back).
הוא: H1931 'he' — emphatic pronoun referring to Herod.

שלח: Candidates: H7971 'to send away', H7973 'a spear/branch', H7974 'Shelach', H7975 'Shiloach'. Chose H7971 because 'he sent you' is a verb form and fits the narrative of Herod sending them back to Pilate.
והנה: H2009 'behold' — introducing the concluding declaration.
שום: Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7762 'garlic'. In later Hebrew, שום functions as 'any/no' (as in 'שום דבר' = 'nothing/anything'). Chose H7760 in its extended sense.
דבר: H1697 'a thing/matter' — 'no thing worthy of death'.
textual_notes: לו at the end could mean 'to him' (nothing worthy of death was done to him) or 'by him' (nothing worthy of death was done by him). The narrative context of a trial suggests 'by him' — no capital offense was committed by the accused.

translation_notes: כאשר: The כ is the preposition 'as/when' and אשר is H834 'who/which/that/when'. Together כאשר = 'as/when/after'. Chose H834 because this creates the temporal clause 'after I discipline him'.
עזב: H5800 'to loosen/relinquish/release'. In context, Pilate is declaring his intention to release the prisoner — 'I will let him go' is the natural reading.
textual_notes: The verb forms עזב and יסרו could be parsed in multiple ways: עזב could be a first-person imperfect (cohortative sense, 'I will release') or a completed action ('he released'). יסרו could be 'I discipline him' or 'they discipline him' or 'he disciplines him'. Context suggests Pilate speaking of his own intended action: 'I will release him after I chastise him.'

translation_notes: והיה: H1961 'to exist/be/become' — 'and it was' introduces a customary practice.
אסיר: Candidates: H615 'a captive/prisoner', H616 'a captive', H617 'Assir (name)'. Chose H615 because the context describes releasing a prisoner, not referencing a proper name.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'one prisoner' is a quantifier modifying the noun.
ביום: H3117 'a day' — with the preposition ב = 'on the day of'.
החג: H2282 'a festival' — 'the feast/festival'.
העם: H5971 'a people' — 'all the people' is the subject of the verb 'cried out'.
צעק: H6817 'to shriek/proclaim' — the people are crying out loudly.
זה: H2088 'this' — referring to the accused; 'remove this one to death'.

והנח: The root is נוח 'to rest/set down' in the causative (hiphil) = 'cause to rest/release/set free'. The candidate H5146 'Noah' is a proper noun that does not fit. The imperative הנח means 'release/leave/let go'.
textual_notes: ברבאן — the spelling here differs slightly from the more common בר־אבא. This appears to be a transliteration of the name Barabbas with a final nun, possibly reflecting an Aramaic or dialectal form.

translation_notes: והוא: H1931 'he' — the emphatic pronoun introducing the description of Barabbas.
היה: H1961 'to be/exist' — 'he was a man'. H1962 'ruin' does not fit as a verb here.
איש: H376 'a man/individual' — straightforward identification.
במאסר: The מ prefix + אסר root. Candidates: H631 'to bind/yoke', H632 'a vow', H633 'an interdict'. The noun form מאסר = 'place of binding' = prison/confinement. Chose H631 as the root.
בעד: H1157 'on account of/for/against' — introducing the cause of imprisonment.
בעיר: Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'a city'. Chose H5892 because 'treachery that he did in the city' is coherent; 'that he did in the cattle' is not.
שעשה: H6213 'to do/make' — 'that he did/committed' in the relative clause.
textual_notes: בגידה — this word is not in the Strong's candidates but its root is בגד 'to deal treacherously'. It could denote treachery, betrayal, or insurrection/sedition depending on context.

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say' — Pilate is speaking.
עוד: Candidates: H5749 'to repeat/testify', H5750 'again/still/yet', H5751 same as H5750 (Aramaic). Chose H5750 as the adverb 'again/yet' modifying 'another time'.
פעם: Candidates: H6470 'to tap/beat/impel', H6471 'a stroke/time/instance'. Chose H6471 as the noun 'time/instance' because 'another time' = 'once more'.
ישוע: H3442 'Jeshua/Yeshua' — the name of the accused.
והם (הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (region)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. Chose H1992 because the context requires a pronoun subject for the verb 'cried out.'
textual_notes: תלהו could derive from תלה (to hang/suspend) — in this context it likely means 'hang him' or 'impale him' referring to execution by suspension on a wooden beam.

translation_notes: והוא (הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because the context requires a pronoun subject 'he' referring to the speaker (Pilate).
פעם: Candidates: H6470 'to beat/agitate', H6471 'a stroke/time/instance'. Chose H6471 because 'a third time' is a natural adverbial phrase indicating repetition.
אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 because the verb 'said' fits the narrative of direct speech.
להם: The prefix ל + הם. Candidates for הם: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 as prepositional 'to them' — the natural indirect object of 'said.'
אי: Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Chose H335 as an interrogative 'what/which' — combined with זה it forms the question 'what is this.'
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — demonstrative pronoun 'this' forming part of the rhetorical question.

רע: Candidates: H7451 'evil/bad', H7452 'a crash/noise', H7453 'an associate', H7454 'a thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 because 'what evil has he done' is the natural question in a judicial context.

טעם: Candidates: H2938 'to taste', H2940 'perception/intelligence/reason', H2941 'judicial sentence', H2942 'judgment/account'. Chose H2940 because 'reason/cause' fits the judicial context of seeking grounds for condemnation.
אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because 'if so' introduces the conditional conclusion.
כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/just', H3652 'so', H3653 'a stand', H3654 'a gnat'. Chose H3651 — 'if so' (אם כן) is a standard conditional conclusion phrase.
textual_notes: איני is a post-biblical Hebrew form meaning 'I am not' (אין + suffix), not found in biblical Strong's lexicon.
מוצא here functions as a participle 'finding' from מצא (H4672) rather than the noun H4161 'a going forth.'
שום here functions as a post-biblical indefinite pronoun 'any' rather than biblical H7760 'to put.'
יהא is a late/Mishnaic Hebrew form of the verb 'to be' (future tense), not standard biblical Hebrew.
חייב is a post-biblical legal term meaning 'liable/guilty/deserving' — not found in biblical Strong's.
מיתה is the post-biblical nominal form for 'death' (cf. biblical מות H4194).
אייסרהו appears to be 'I will chastise him' from יסר (H3256) with first person prefix and 3ms suffix.
ואניחהו from נוח (H5117) 'I will let him rest/release him' with 3ms suffix.

translation_notes: והם (הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — pronoun subject for the participle 'crying out.'

בשתי (שתי): Candidates: H8358 'intoxication', H8359 'warp (in weaving)'. Chose H8359 because paired with ערב (woof/weft), it forms the weaving idiom 'warp and woof' — a term used for the cross-pattern of a crucifixion frame.

וערב (ערב): Candidates: H6148 'to braid/intermix/woof', H6149 'to be agreeable', H6150 'to grow dusky', H6151 'to commingle', H6152 'Arabia', H6153 'dusk'. Chose H6148 because 'woof/weft' (the cross-thread in weaving) pairs naturally with 'warp' to describe the cross-beam structure.
textual_notes: בשתי וערב ('in warp and woof') is a weaving metaphor. In this execution context, it appears to be a Hebrew idiom for crucifixion — the vertical beam (warp/שתי) and horizontal beam (woof/ערב) forming a cross shape. This is a striking and distinctive Hebrew way of describing the instrument of execution.
שיניחהו is a causative form with the relative ש + יניחהו ('that he place/set him') from נוח (H5117).
הולכים וחזקים — 'going and strengthening' is an idiomatic Hebrew construction meaning 'growing ever stronger/more intense.'

translation_notes: שפט: Candidates: H8199 'to judge/pronounce sentence', H8200 'to judge (Aramaic)', H8201 'a sentence/infliction', H8202 'Shaphat (name)'. Chose H8199 because the verb 'judged/decreed' fits the judicial authority of Pilate pronouncing a sentence.
textual_notes: שתעשה is ש + תעשה ('that it be done') from עשה (H6213), functioning as a purpose/result clause.
שאלתם is שאלה ('request/petition,' H7596) + suffix 'their.'

translation_notes: להם (first and second occurrences): Prefix ל + הם. Candidates for הם: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — 'to them' as indirect object.
שבעבור (עבור): Candidates: H5668 'on account of', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 — 'on account of' introducing the cause of imprisonment.

הוסם (סם): The candidate H5561 'aroma' does not fit. This appears to be הושם from שום/שים (H7760 'to put/place') in the passive — 'was placed.' The ו/ש consonant similarity and passive form explain the spelling.
במאסר (אסר): Candidates: H631 'to bind/yoke', H632 'a vow', H633 'an interdict'. Chose H631 — the noun form מאסר means 'place of binding/prison.'
שהם: Candidates for שהם: H7718 'beryl', H7719 'Shoham'. For ש + הם: H1992 'they'. Chose ש + H1992 — relative particle 'that' + 'they' = 'whom they.'
ונתן: Candidates: H5414 'to give', H5416 'Nathan (name)'. Chose H5414 because 'he gave' continues the narrative of Pilate's actions.
ישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua', H3443 'Jeshua'. Chose H3442 — the proper name Yeshua.
textual_notes: רציחה is a nominal form from רצח (H7523 'to murder') — post-biblical form meaning 'murder/homicide.'
ובגידה is a post-biblical nominal form meaning 'treachery/betrayal/sedition' — possibly related to בגד (H898 'to deal treacherously').
הוסם is ambiguous: it could be from סום/שום (to place) in passive, or possibly related to סם (H5561). The prison context strongly favors 'was placed.'
לרצונם — 'to their will/desire' from רצון (H7522) with 3mp suffix.

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 — כאשר means 'when/as' introducing a temporal clause.
אדם: Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being/man', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'a ruby'. Chose H120 because 'a man' fits the narrative of seizing a bystander.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 — 'one' meaning 'a certain' individual.
שמעון: Candidates: H8095 'Shimon', H4583 'an abode', H5771 'perversity'. Chose H8095 — proper name Shimon (Simon) identified by the preceding 'called.'
שבא: The candidate H7614 'Sheba (place name)' does not fit. This is ש (relative) + בא from בוא (H935 'to come') — 'who came.'
מן: Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 'from (Aramaic)', H4482 'a chord'. Chose H4480 — preposition 'from.'
העיר: Candidates: H5892 'a city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'a watcher/angel', H5895 'a young ass'. Chose H5892 — 'the city' with the definite article ה.

וערב: Candidates: H6148 'to braid/woof', H6149 'to be agreeable', H6150 'to grow dusky', H6151 'to commingle', H6152 'Arabia', H6153 'dusk'. Chose H6148 — 'woof/weft,' paired with the preceding word to form 'warp and woof' (the cross-beam).
אחר: Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'after/behind', H311 'after', H312 'other/next', H313 'Acher'. Chose H310 — 'after/behind' describing the position relative to Yeshua.
textual_notes: ה<תי appears to be a damaged/partially illegible word. Given the pairing with וערב and the identical phrase in section 3 (בשתי וערב), this is almost certainly השתי ('the warp') — the vertical beam, paired with ערב ('woof') for the cross-beam structure. The < likely represents a damaged consonant (shin/sin).
שבא is ambiguous between Sheba (H7614) as a place name and ש + בא ('who came'). Context strongly favors the latter since the man is described as coming from the city.
שישאנה — ש + ישא + נה, 'that he carry it' from נשא (H5375), with feminine object suffix referring to the cross (שתי וערב being conceptually feminine).

translation_notes: חיל: Candidates: H2426 'an army/intrenchment', H2427 'a throe (of childbirth)', H2428 'force/army/wealth/strength', H2429 'an army/strength'. Chose H2428 because 'a great force/multitude' of people fits the description of a crowd following the procession.
textual_notes: ואוננים could derive from אנן/און meaning 'to mourn/lament' (cf. H56 'to mourn'). The form suggests an ongoing mourning action.

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — verb 'said' introducing direct speech.

בני: Candidates: H1137 'Bani (name)', H1138 'Bunni (name)', H5204 'lamentation'. None fits perfectly. This is בנות ('daughters') in construct — the text uses בני as a construct form meaning 'daughters of' or 'children of' Jerusalem. The address to women following him confirms 'daughters.'
אל: Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H409 'not', H410 'strength/God', H411 'these', H413 'to/toward'. Chose H408 — negative particle with the jussive/imperative 'do not weep.'

עלי: Candidates: H5940 'a pestle', H5941 'Eli (name)', H5942 'high', H5943 'supreme/God'. These are all noun readings. However, עלי here is simply the preposition על (H5921) + first person suffix 'me' = 'over me.' None of the Strong's noun candidates fit.
רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'merely/only/but', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 — adverb 'only/but' introducing the contrast.
על: Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'over/upon/against', H5922 'over (Aramaic)', H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 — preposition 'over' with 'yourselves.'
ועל: Same as על above, with conjunctive ו — 'and over.'
textual_notes: בני could be read as 'sons of' or 'children of' but the context of women following and weeping strongly suggests 'daughters of' (בנות in construct). The manuscript may use בני as a general construct form.
עלי is parsed as preposition על + 1cs suffix, not as any of the listed Strong's nouns.

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Chose H3588 — conjunction 'for' introducing the reason for the preceding exhortation.
הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2009 — interjection 'behold' introducing a prophetic announcement.
באים: The candidate H366 'frightful' from אים does not fit. This is the participle of בוא (H935 'to come') — 'coming,' modifying 'days.'
שבהם (הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — ש + ב + הם = 'that in them / in which.'
הן: Candidates: H2004 'they (feminine)', H2005 'lo!/behold/if', H2006 'lo/therefore'. Chose H2004 — feminine pronoun 'they [are]' referring to the barren women.
והבטן (בטן): Candidates: H990 'belly/womb', H991 'Beten (place)', H992 'pistachio-nut'. Chose H990 — 'the womb' in the context of childbearing.
שלא (לא): H3808 'not', H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Chose H3808 — standard Hebrew negation.
וולד: Candidates: H2056 'a boy/child', H3850 'Lod (place)'. Chose H2056 — 'a child/offspring' as the object of 'bore.'
textual_notes: מאו<רות appears damaged. Given the context of a blessing/beatitude, this likely reads מאושרות (from אשר H833/835 'blessed/happy') — 'blessed/fortunate [are].'

וה<דים also appears damaged. From context (parallel with womb and nursing), this is almost certainly השדים / הדדים — 'the breasts' (from שד H7699 or דד H1717). The < likely represents a damaged consonant.
הן is ambiguous between 'they (fem.)' and 'behold/lo!' — chose H2004 (feminine 'they') as it functions as the copula: 'blessed are they, the barren ones.'
כסונו is from כסה (H3680 'to cover/conceal') with 1cp suffix 'us' — 'cover us.' The imperative form is clear from context.
נפלו from נפל (H5307 'to fall') — imperative 'fall' addressed to the hills, with possible 1cp suffix or plural imperative form.

translation_notes: כי (KY): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction for/because/if'. Chose H3588 because this introduces a conditional clause with אם following.
אם (AM): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because it pairs with כי to form 'for if' introducing a conditional.
הלח (HLCh): Candidates: H3892 'fresh/moist/unused', H3893 'freshness/vigor'. Chose H3892 because it functions as an adjective modifying the tree, contrasting with 'dry' at the end.
אלו (ALW): Candidates: H431 'lo!/these', H432 'if'. Chose H431 as a demonstrative 'these' pointing to the דברים (things), since the conditional 'if' is already expressed by כי אם.

ביבש (BYBSH): Candidates: H3001 'to dry up/wither', H3002 'dry', H3003 'Jobesh (place name)'. Chose H3002 because it contrasts directly with הלח (moist/green) — green tree vs. dry tree makes a coherent image.

יעשו: The consonants match the verb עשה (to do/make) in imperfect 3mp. The candidate H3299 'Jaasu' (a proper name) does not fit the syntax of a question beginning with מה. Read as imperfect passive/active of עשה.
textual_notes: נעשו and יעשו have no Strong's candidates listed but are clearly forms of עשה (H6213, to do/make). נעשו is niphal perfect 3cp (were done); יעשו is qal/niphal imperfect 3mp (will be done).
דברים has no candidates listed but is clearly from דבר (H1697, word/thing/matter) in plural.

translation_notes: בעבור (BABWR): Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because the context requires a purpose clause — they are being led in order to be executed.
textual_notes: אחרים has no candidates listed but is clearly from אחר (H312, other/another) in masculine plural.
רעים has no candidates listed; consonants רעים could be from רע (H7451 evil/bad) or רע (H7453 friend/companion). Context of being led to execution strongly favors 'evil ones/criminals'.
נוהגים is a participle from נהג (H5090, to drive/lead), masculine plural — being led/driven.
שימיתום appears to be a compound: ש + ימיתו + ם, i.e. 'that they would cause them to die' from מות (H4191) in hiphil — to put to death.

translation_notes: וכאשר: Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because וכאשר = 'and when', introducing a temporal clause.
באו: The candidate listed is או H176 'or/desire', but באו is clearly בא (H935, to come) in qal perfect 3cp — 'they came'. The prefix ב is part of the root, not a preposition here.
אל (AL): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Chose H413 because directional 'to the place' is the natural reading.
המקום: Candidates: H4725 'place/standing', H6965 'to rise'. Chose H4725 — 'the place' — as it is a noun with the article ה prefixed.
שם (ShM): Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name (Aramaic)'. Chose H8033 'there' because it introduces the location where the action of hanging takes place.
האחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 — 'the one' — functioning as a pronoun identifying the first of the two thieves.
לצד: Candidates: H6654 'a side', H6655 'at the side of'. Both are essentially the same meaning; chose H6654 as the base noun with preposition ל.
ימין: Candidates: H3225 'right hand/side', H3226 'Jamin (name)'. Chose H3225 because it describes a spatial position, contrasting with left.
textual_notes: גשלגשלתא appears to be a corrupted or unusual spelling — likely representing גלגלתא (Gulgoleta/Golgotha, 'the skull'). The doubled של may be a scribal error or dialectal variant.
וה<ני appears to have a damaged letter (marked with <). The expected reading is והשני 'and the second/other', from שני (H8145).
תלו has no candidates listed but is from תלה (H8518, to hang/suspend), qal perfect 3cp — 'they hung'.
והגנבים has no candidates listed but is from גנב (H1590, thief) in masculine plural with article and conjunction.

translation_notes: אמר (AMR): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said (Aramaic)', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because the context requires a speech verb introducing Yeshua's words.

אב (AB): Candidates: H1 'father', H2 'father (Aramaic)', H3 'green plant', H4 'green plant (Aramaic)'. Chose H1 'father' because Yeshua is addressing someone in speech and the vocative 'Father' fits the prayer context.

מחול (MChWL): Candidates: H4234 'a round dance', H4235 'Machol (name)', or from root חול H2342 'to twist/whirl/writhe/be in pain' which in certain stems means 'to pardon/forgive', H2343 'Chul (name)', H2344 'sand'. The form מחול could be an imperative from the root חול in a causative sense. 'A round dance' makes no sense in context. 'Forgive' fits Yeshua's prayer for those executing him. Chose the verbal reading from H2342.
להם (LHM): Candidates: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', or ל + הם H1992 'to them'. Chose the prepositional phrase ל + הם 'to them' because it is the indirect object of 'forgive'.
אין (AYN): Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 as it negates the participle 'knowing'.
הם (HM): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 'they' as the subject pronoun of the participial clause.
textual_notes: מחול is genuinely ambiguous: it could be the noun 'dance' (H4234) or a verbal form from חול meaning 'forgive/pardon'. Context decisively favors the verbal reading.
יודעים has no candidates listed; it is from ידע (H3045, to know) as a masculine plural participle.
עושים has no candidates listed; it is from עשה (H6213, to do/make) as a masculine plural participle.
ומחלקים is from חלק (H2505, to divide/apportion) in a participial form with ו conjunction and מ prefix.
מלבושיו is from לבוש (H3830, garment) with 3ms possessive suffix.
ומטילים is a participial form meaning 'casting/throwing', likely from טול/נטל.
גורלות is from גורל (H1486, lot) in feminine plural.

translation_notes: והעם: Candidates for עם: H5971 'people/nation', H5972 'people (Aramaic)', H5973 'with', H5974 'with (Aramaic)'. Chose H5971 because the article ה indicates a definite noun 'the people', not a preposition.
אם (AM): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 'if' because it introduces a conditional clause challenging Yeshua's identity.
הוא (HWA): Candidates: H1931 'he/self', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 as the emphatic pronoun 'he [is]'.

משיח (MShYCh): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', or from שיח H7878 'to ponder', H7879 'utterance', H7880 'shrubbery'. Chose H4899 because the context is a challenge about Yeshua's messianic identity, and 'anointed/Messiah' fits perfectly with 'chosen of YHWH'.
textual_notes: עומד is singular while והעם could be collective singular — the people as a unit stands. עומדים is plural agreeing with השרים (rulers).
