ומביטו: the ו suffix could be 3ms object 'watching him' or simply a conjunctive form. Context favors 'watching him'.
הושיע is hiphil perfect 3ms of ישע (H3467) — 'he saved'. יושיע is hiphil imperfect 3ms — 'he will save / let him save'.
נבחר is niphal participle from בחר (H977, to choose) — 'chosen/elected'.
האחרים could be 'the others' (accusative object of הושיע) or could begin a new clause. Read as object: 'the others he saved'.

translation_notes: לעג (LAG): Candidates: H3932 'to mock/deride', H3933 'derision/scoffing', H3934 'a buffoon/foreigner'. Chose H3933 because the syntax requires a noun — they are bringing out mockery/derision against him.
textual_notes: וה]פרשים[ has editorial brackets suggesting textual damage or reconstruction. The consonants פרשים likely from פרש (H6571, horseman) in plural — soldiers/cavalry.
מתקרבים is a hitpael participle from קרב (H7126, to draw near).
מוציאים is a hiphil participle from יצא (H3318, to go out) — 'bringing out/producing'.
ומתנדבים is a hitpael participle from נדב (H5068, to be willing/offer freely) — 'volunteering/offering willingly'.
חומץ has no candidates listed; it is from חמץ (H2558, vinegar).
לשתות is an infinitive construct from שתה (H8354, to drink).

translation_notes: אם (AM): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if'. Chose H518 because it introduces a conditional challenge.
אתה (ATH): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive (Aramaic)', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because the syntax requires a pronoun — 'if you [are] king'.

מלך (MLK): Candidates: H4427 'to reign', H4428 'a king', H4429 'Melek (name)', H4430 'king (Aramaic)', H4431 'advice', H4432 'Molek'. Chose H4428 'a king' because it serves as a predicate noun — 'if you are king of Israel'.
textual_notes: תושיע is hiphil imperfect 2ms from ישע (H3467, to save) — 'you will save / save [imperative sense]'.
עצמך is from עצם (H6106, bone/self) with 2ms suffix — 'yourself'.

translation_notes: ועל: Candidates for על: H5920 'the top/God/aloft', H5921 'upon/over/against', H5922 'upon (Aramaic)', H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 because 'upon the writing' describes the location of the inscription.

הכתב: Candidates: H3789 'to write/inscribe', H3790 'to write (Aramaic)', H3791 'a writing/record', H3792 'a writing (Aramaic)'. Chose H3791 because with the article ה it functions as the noun 'the writing/inscription'.
כתוב: The listed candidate is H8421 תוב 'to reply'. However, כתוב is far more naturally parsed as the passive participle of כתב (H3789, to write) — 'written'. Chose H3789 as the root.
מלך: Same as section 7 — chose H4428 'king'.
textual_notes: שעליו is a relative clause: ש (that) + עליו (upon him) — 'that [was] upon him'.
מאותיות: the מ prefix could be 'from' or instrumental 'with/in'. In context, 'in letters' (instrumental) makes better sense.
יוניות, ולאטיניות, ועבריות are adjective forms describing the scripts — Greek, Latin, and Hebrew. No Strong's numbers provided; these are post-biblical or loan-word forms.
זהו appears to be זה + הוא contracted — 'this [is] he' or 'this is'.
היהודים is from יהודי (H3064, a Jew) in masculine plural with article.

translation_notes: ואחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'one of the thieves' is the clear reading.
שהיה: Candidates for היה: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin'; for יה: H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 because ש + היה = 'who was', a relative clause describing the thief's state.
ואומר: The listed candidate H201 'Omar (name)' does not fit. This is ו + אומר, a qal active participle of אמר (H559, to say) — 'and saying'. Chose H559.
אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if'. Chose H518 — conditional 'if'.
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive (Aramaic)', H859 'you'. Chose H859 — pronoun 'you'.
משיח: Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', or from שיח H7878 'to ponder', H7879 'utterance', H7880 'shrubbery'. Chose H4899 — the challenge is about messianic identity.
textual_notes: מהגנבים: מן + ה + גנבים — 'from the thieves', from גנב (H1590).
תלוי is a passive participle from תלה (H8518, to hang) — 'hanging/suspended'.
מחרפו is a piel participle from חרף (H2778, to reproach/revile) with 3ms suffix — 'reviling him'.
תושיע is hiphil imperative or imperfect 2ms from ישע (H3467) — 'save!'.
ואנחנו could be read as 'and we' (subject) but in context functions as 'and us' (object of save) — a colloquial or late Hebrew usage.

translation_notes: והאחר: Candidates: H309 'to loiter/delay', H310 'after/behind', H311 'after (Aramaic)', H312 'other/another', H313 'Acher (name)'. Chose H312 because 'the other [thief]' contrasts with 'the one' from section 9.

עונה: The listed candidate H5772 'sexual cohabitation' clearly does not fit. The consonants ענה also match ענה (H6030, to answer/respond). Chose the verbal reading 'answering' — a participle from ענה H6030.
ומגדף: H1442 'to hack with words/revile'. In context, the other thief is rebuking the first thief for his mockery. 'Rebuking/reproving' fits — he reviles the first thief's attitude. Chose H1442.
אומר: The listed candidate H201 'Omar (name)' does not fit. This is a qal participle of אמר (H559) — 'saying'.
ירא: Candidates: H3372 'to fear/revere', H3373 'fearing/reverent'. Chose H3373 as a participle/adjective — 'fearing' — which pairs with אינך to form 'are you not fearing'.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'for/because'. Chose H3588 — causal conjunction 'for/because'.
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive (Aramaic)', H859 'you'. Chose H859 — pronoun 'you'.
textual_notes: עונה: The only listed candidate (H5772) is implausible. The consonants clearly support ענה (H6030, to answer), which is a standard verb form.
ומגדף (H1442 'to revile') could mean the other thief is rebuking/censuring the first thief, or it could be read as a general 'reviling/blaspheming'. Context favors rebuking the first thief.
א5להים has a corrupted character (5 in place of a letter); this is clearly אלהים (H430, God).

בצרתם: ב + צרה (H6869, distress/affliction) + suffix ם (their). The reading is 'in their distress' — i.e., you share the same punishment, so you should fear God. Alternatively, צרתם could be parsed as צר (H6862, adversary/narrow) + suffix, but 'distress' produces a more coherent image.
אינך: אין (H369, not) + suffix ך (you) = 'you are not'. This is a standard negation of a participial predicate.

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 because the context requires an adversative conjunction ('but') contrasting the speakers' guilt with the innocence of 'this one.'
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because it functions as a demonstrative pronoun pointing to a specific person being discussed.

שום (consonants שום): Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7761 'to put (Aramaic)', H7762 'garlic'. Chose H7760 because in later Hebrew שום functions as 'any' (from the sense of 'putting/placing' → 'anything at all'), fitting the negation pattern שום רע לא עשה ('any evil not did').

רע (consonants רע): Candidates: H7451 'evil/bad', H7452 'a crash/noise', H7453 'an associate', H7454 'a thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 because the context is about moral innocence — 'no evil did he do.'

אמתי (consonants אמתי): The only Strong's candidate is H573 'Amittai' (a proper name), but the consonants אמתי also represent the adjective 'true/genuine' (from אמת H571 with adjectival suffix -י). Chose the adjective reading because 'true judgment' is contextually coherent, whereas a proper name makes no sense here.
textual_notes: ובא5מת appears to contain a transcription artifact (the '5'). Reading it as ובאמת ('and in truth'), a common Hebrew phrase composed of ו + ב + אמת (H571).
סובלים has no Strong's candidates listed — it is a later Hebrew participial form from סבל (to bear/carry). No classical Strong's number applies directly.
הראוי has no Strong's candidates listed — it is a later Hebrew form meaning 'the fitting/deserved one.'
אמתי: The only Strong's entry is the proper name Amittai (H573), but contextually this must be the adjective 'true' derived from אמת (H571).

translation_notes: אדון (consonants אדון): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon (proper name)'. Chose H113 because it is used as a form of address ('Lord/Master'), fitting the plea directed at Yeshua.

מהאל (consonants מהאל): The prefix מה + אל yields multiple readings. Candidates for אל: H408 'not', H410 'strength/God', H411 'these/those', H413 'near/to'. Chose H410 because 'from God' makes contextual sense in a theological declaration.

פרש (consonants פרש): Candidates: H6566 'to break apart/disperse', H6567 'to separate/specify', H6568 'to specify', H6569 'excrement', H6570 'Peresh', H6571 'a steed/driver'. The last word פרש most naturally reads as H6567 'to specify/explain' as a verb form completing the phrase.

ואומר (consonants ואומר): The only Strong's candidate is H201 'Omar' (a proper name), but the consonants clearly represent ו + אומר, the participial form of אמר (H559 'to say'). Chose the verbal reading.
textual_notes: The phrase עמהם מהאל פרשים פרושים ו פרשים פרש is extremely difficult and appears garbled or corrupt. It may represent a marginal gloss or scribal note. The words פרשים and פרושים could mean 'horsemen' (H6571), 'separated ones' (from פרש H6567, i.e. Pharisees/Perushim), or 'interpreters/explainers' (H6567). The repetition and the conjunction ו between the two פרשים groups strongly suggests a scribal annotation — possibly explaining that פרשים can be read as either פרושים (Pharisees/separated ones) or פרשים (horsemen/explainers). This section may be a textual apparatus note rather than narrative text.

ממני: No Strong's candidate fits directly. The listed candidates (H4507 'Meni/Fate', H4508 'Minni/Armenia', H5204 'lamentation') do not match. This is simply מן + ני (from me), a standard prepositional phrase with first-person singular suffix.
כשתבוא and במלכותך have no Strong's candidates — they are compound forms: כש + תבוא ('when you come') and ב + מלכות + ך ('in your kingdom').

translation_notes: אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said (Aramaic)', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the verb 'said' fits the narrative — Yeshua is speaking.
אני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the sentence requires a first-person pronoun: 'I am saying to you.'
אומר (consonants אומר): Only Strong's candidate is H201 'Omar'. But this is clearly the participial form of אמר (H559), meaning 'saying/am saying.'

עדן (consonants עדן): Candidates: H5727 'to be soft/pleasant', H5728 'till now', H5729 'Eden (Mesopotamia)', H5730 'pleasure', H5731 'Eden (Adam's home)', H5732 'a set time/year'. Chose H5731 because בגן עדן ('in the garden of Eden') is a fixed phrase referring to paradise, and the preceding word גן (garden) demands a place name or descriptor. H5730 'pleasure/delight' is also valid as the etymological meaning.
textual_notes: עדן could be read as the place name Eden (H5731) or as the noun 'delight/pleasure' (H5730). Both are consonantally identical and both produce coherent readings: 'garden of Eden' or 'garden of delight.' The phrase likely carries both senses simultaneously.

translation_notes: כמעט (consonants כמעט): Candidates for מעט: H4591 'to lessen', H4592 'a little/few', H4593 'sharp'; also עט: H5842 'a stylus'. With prefix כ ('as/about'), כמעט = 'almost/approximately.' Chose H4592 because כמעט is a standard Hebrew adverb meaning 'almost/about.'
שעה (consonants שעה): Candidates: H8159 'to gaze/inspect', H8160 'a look/moment'. Chose H8160 because the context requires a time unit — 'hour/moment' — paired with ordinal numbers (sixth, ninth).
היה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 because 'darkness was in all the land' requires the existential verb.

עד (consonants עד): Candidates: H5703 'perpetuity', H5704 'until/as far as', H5705 same (Aramaic), H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'menstrual flux'. Chose H5704 because a temporal preposition 'until' is needed between two time references.
textual_notes: ש<ית contains a transcription artifact ('<'). Reading as ששית ('sixth'), the ordinal number. No Strong's entry applies directly.
תשיעית ('ninth') has no Strong's candidate listed — it is the feminine ordinal from תשע (nine).

translation_notes: חשך (consonants חשך): Candidates: H2820 'to restrain/spare', H2821 'to be dark/darken', H2822 'darkness', H2823 'dark/obscure'. Chose H2821 because the sun is the subject, and 'the sun darkened' produces a coherent physical image consistent with the preceding darkness over the land.

ומכסה (consonants ומכסה): Candidates: H4372 'a covering/weatherboarding', H4373 'an enumeration/valuation', H4374 'a covering/garment/coverlet/awning/omentum', H3680 'to cover'. Chose H4374 because a 'covering/curtain' of the sanctuary fits the image of the temple veil being torn. H4372 is also possible but H4374 has broader semantic range including fabric coverings.

המקדש (consonants המקדש): Candidates: H4720 'sanctuary/holy place', H6942 'to consecrate', H6943 'Kedesh', H6944 'a sacred place/thing', H6945 'a devotee', H6946 'Kadesh'. Chose H4720 because 'the sanctuary' is the natural noun form with the ה prefix as definite article.
textual_notes: וה<מש contains a transcription artifact ('<'). Reading as והשמש ('and the sun'). The consonants שמש correspond to H8121 (the sun).
ונבקע has no Strong's candidates listed — it is the nifal (passive) form of בקע (H1234, 'to cleave/split/tear'), meaning 'was torn/split.'
באמצעו has no Strong's candidates listed — it is a compound: ב + אמצע + ו ('in its middle'), from a root related to אמצע (middle/center).

translation_notes: אב (consonants אב): Candidates: H1 'father', H2 'father (Aramaic)', H3 'a green plant', H4 'a green plant (Aramaic)'. Chose H1 because Yeshua is addressing God as 'Father' in a dying declaration.

אלה (consonants אלה): Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'an imprecation', H424 'an oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. However, the consonants אלה also represent the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (H428). Chose H428 because 'these words' (אלה הדברים) is a standard Hebrew phrase and the context describes the words just spoken.

שלח (consonants שלח): Candidates: H7971 'to send away/out', H7972 same (Aramaic), H7973 'a spear/branch', H7974 'Shelach', H7975 'Shiloach', H3892 'fresh', H3893 'freshness'. Chose H7971 because 'he sent/released his spirit' is a coherent description of dying — the spirit departing.
textual_notes: The apostrophe (') between רוחי and ובאמרו may represent a section break, a pause mark, or a damaged portion of the manuscript.
אלה is listed with candidates that do not include the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (H428), but the consonants are identical. In context, 'these words' is the only coherent reading.
צועק has no Strong's candidates listed — it is the qal active participle of צעק (H6817, 'to cry out').
אפקיד has no Strong's candidates listed — it is the hifil first-person singular imperfect of פקד (H6485, 'to visit/appoint/deposit'), meaning 'I will deposit/entrust.'

translation_notes: שר (consonants שר): Candidates: H8269 'a head person/chief', H8270 'a string/cord'. Chose H8269 because 'commander of the hundred' (centurion) is a military title that fits the narrative context.

המאה (consonants המאה): Candidates: H3967 'a hundred', H3968 'Meah (tower)', H3969 'a hundred (Aramaic)'. Chose H3967 because 'the hundred' completes the military title 'commander of the hundred' (centurion).
אלה (consonants אלה): Same as section 6 — reading as demonstrative 'these' (H428). 'These things that were done' is coherent.
הלל (consonants הלל): Candidates: H1984 'to shine/praise/boast', H1985 'Hillel'. Chose H1984 because 'praised YHWH' is the natural verbal reading — the centurion glorified God.
ואמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same (Aramaic), H561 'something said', H562 same (Aramaic), H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the narrative requires 'and said.'
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 as the demonstrative pronoun pointing to the man being discussed.
היה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 because 'this man was righteous' requires the existential verb.
textual_notes: צ דיק appears to be a single word צדיק ('righteous', H6662) split by a space — likely a scribal or transcription artifact. The only Strong's candidate for דיק alone is H1785 'a battering-tower,' which makes no sense here. Reading צדיק as one word meaning 'righteous/just.'

בא: This could be from בוא (H935 'to come/enter') or could be a scribal form of ראה ('to see'). Given the narrative — the centurion witnessing the events — 'saw' is contextually apt, but 'came' is also possible. The ambiguity exists because no Strong's candidates were provided for this word in this section.
הדברים has no Strong's entry listed — it is the definite plural of דבר (H1697, 'word/thing/matter').

translation_notes: שהיה (consonants שהיה): ש + היה. Candidates for היה: H1961 'to exist/be', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 because 'the people that was there' requires the existential verb.
שם (consonants שם): Candidates: H8033 'there/then', H8034 'name/honor', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name (Aramaic)'. Chose H8033 because 'was there' is the natural locative reading.

האלה (consonants אלה): Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. But the consonants with ה prefix represent the demonstrative 'these' (H428). Chose demonstrative because 'all these things' is coherent.
עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people/tribe', H5972 same (Aramaic), H5973 'with', H5974 same (Aramaic). Chose H5971 because 'all the people' is the subject of the sentence.
textual_notes: ההשקפה has no Strong's candidates — it derives from שקף (H8259, 'to look out/overlook') with nominal prefix. It means 'the observation/viewing/spectacle.'

להכות: The only listed candidate for כות is H3575 'Cuth (Assyrian province),' which is irrelevant. The form is the hifil infinitive construct of נכה (H5221, 'to strike/smite'), meaning 'to strike/beat.'

חזותיהם has no Strong's candidates listed. This appears to derive from חזה (H2373 'breast/chest'), with plural possessive suffix: 'their chests/breasts.' An alternative reading from חזה H2372 ('vision') giving 'their visions/appearances' is less coherent — people beating their chests is a known expression of grief.
חזרו has no Strong's candidates listed — it means 'they returned' from חזר, a later Hebrew verb for 'to return.'

translation_notes: מגלילה (consonants מגלילה): With prefix מ + גלילה. Candidate: H1552 'a circuit or region.' This is the geographic term for Galilee (the region/circuit). Chose H1552.

אלו (consonants אלו): Candidates: H431 'lo!/behold', H432 'nay/if'. However, אלו also functions as a later Hebrew demonstrative pronoun 'these.' Chose the demonstrative reading because 'these things' parallels אלה הדברים in previous sections.
שבאו (consonants שבאו): The listed candidate for או is H176 'or/if.' But this is ש + באו, from בוא (H935 'to come/enter'), meaning 'that came.' The ש is the relative particle.
textual_notes: שמכירין has no Strong's entry — it is a later Hebrew participial form (הכיר, hifil of נכר H5234 'to recognize/know') with the plural suffix -ין, meaning 'who recognized/knew.'
הנשים has no Strong's entry listed — it is the definite plural of אשה (H802, 'woman').
עמדו has no Strong's entry listed — it is the qal perfect 3mp of עמד (H5975, 'to stand').
רואות has no Strong's entry listed — it is the qal active participle feminine plural of ראה (H7200, 'to see').

translation_notes: והנה (consonants הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'and behold' introduces a new character, which is the standard narrative function of הנה.

אדם (consonants אדם, first occurrence): Candidates: H119 'to flush/turn rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam (name)', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. Chose H120 because 'a man/person' is the natural reading introducing a character.
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'one man' (i.e. 'a certain man') is the standard indefinite usage.
אדם (second occurrence): Same candidates. Chose H120 again because 'who was a man honored and righteous' describes his character.
שהיה: ש + היה. Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 — 'who was' introduces the description of his character.
textual_notes: נכבד has no Strong's entry listed — it is the nifal participle of כבד (H3513, 'to be heavy/honored'), meaning 'honored/esteemed/noble.'
שמו has no Strong's entry listed — it is שם (H8034, 'name') with the 3ms possessive suffix: 'his name.'

הרמתי (H7435): 'Ramathite' — an inhabitant of Ramah. In the broader textual tradition this figure is associated with Arimathea, but working from the Hebrew consonants alone, the text identifies him as from Ramah.

translation_notes: בעצה (consonants עצה): Candidates: H6095 'to close eyes', H6096 'spine', H6097 'timber', H6098 'advice/counsel/plan'. Chose H6098 because the context describes someone not agreeing — the object of agreement is naturally a plan or counsel, not timber or a spine.

עיר (consonants עיר): Candidates: H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'young donkey'. Chose H5892 because it modifies a place name (Ramathaim) and Judah, clearly denoting a geographical location.

ומצפה (consonants מצפה/צפה): Candidates: H4707 'observatory/watchtower', H4708/H4709 'Mitspeh (place names)', H6822 'to lean forward/peer/observe/await', H6823 'to sheet with metal', H6824 'inundation'. Chose H6822 because the following noun 'kingdom of YHWH' requires a verb of expectation — he was watching/awaiting the kingdom. An observatory or place name would break the syntax.
והיה (consonants היה/יה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 because this introduces a description of the person's origin — 'and he was from Ramathaim.'
מלכות (consonants מלכות): Candidates: H4438 'rule/dominion', H3575 'Cuth (Assyrian province)'. Chose H4438 because paired with YHWH it clearly denotes the divine kingdom.
textual_notes: הסכים has no Strong's candidates provided; it appears to be a later Hebrew form meaning 'agreed/consented' (cf. Mishnaic Hebrew הסכים). No biblical Hebrew Strong's number is available.
מהרמתים is a proper noun 'from Ramathaim' (dual form of Ramah); no Strong's candidates were provided. This appears to be the same Ramathaim known from 1 Samuel.

translation_notes: ונגש (consonants נגש): Candidates: H5065 'to drive/tax/harass/tyrannize', H5066 'to come near/approach/bring near'. Chose H5066 because the subject is approaching Pilate to make a request — drawing near is the natural physical action, not driving or harassing.

אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'strength/mighty/deity', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/near/toward'. Chose H413 because it follows the verb of approach and precedes a person — directional 'to Pilate' is the only coherent reading.
ושאל (consonants שאל): Candidates: H7592 'to inquire/request/demand', H7594 'Sheal (name)'. Chose H7592 because the context requires a verb — he asked/requested the body.

גוף (consonants גוף): H1479 is the only candidate ('to hollow/arch/close/shut'), but in post-biblical Hebrew גוף means 'body.' The context clearly demands 'body' — he is requesting the physical remains of Yeshua. The biblical Hebrew root's sense of 'hollowed/arched form' may underlie the later nominal meaning.
textual_notes: גוף has no Strong's entry for 'body' per se; H1479 covers the verbal root. The noun 'body' is a post-biblical Hebrew development from this root. The context unambiguously requires 'body.'

והודה could be parsed as from ידה (to confess/give thanks/acknowledge) in hiphil, or from הודה meaning 'he granted/conceded.' In context, Pilate responding to a request, 'granted' is the most natural reading.
פילאט is a transliteration of a foreign name (Pilate) with no Strong's entry.

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when/because', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because with prefixed כ and ו it forms 'and when/as' — a temporal conjunction introducing a narrative sequence.

זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that (demonstrative)', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Testing: 'a sheep took down the body' is absurd. 'This one took down the body' is coherent — referring to the person described in section 1. Chose H2088.
סלק (consonants סלק): H5559 'to ascend'. In Aramaic/later Hebrew סלק can mean both 'to go up' and 'to remove/take away.' In context — removing a body from a cross — the sense is 'took down/removed.'

וערב (consonants ערב): Candidates: H6148 'to braid/intermix/pledge', H6149 'to be agreeable', H6150 'to grow dusky at sundown', H6151 'to commingle', H6152 'Arabia', H6153 'dusk/evening'. Chose H6153 because the narrative sequence of burial actions naturally places this at evening time.

בבגד (consonants בגד): Candidates: H898 'to cover with a garment/act covertly', H899 'a covering/clothing'. Chose H899 because with the preposition ב it means 'in a garment/cloth' — the wrapping material.
משי (consonants משי): Candidates: H4897 'silk', H7862 'a gift'. Chose H4897 because it modifies the garment — 'a garment of silk' describes the burial cloth material.
בקבר (consonants קבר): Candidates: H6912 'to inter', H6913 'a sepulchre'. Chose H6913 because with preposition ב it denotes a location — 'in a tomb.'
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because it modifies the tomb — 'one tomb' / 'a certain tomb.'
חדש (consonants חדש): Candidates: H2318 'to be new/rebuild', H2319 'new', H2320 'new moon/month', H2321 'Chodesh (name)'. Chose H2319 because it is an adjective modifying the tomb — 'a new tomb.'
היה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 because the syntax requires a past-tense copula — 'not was a man laid.'
textual_notes: מה<תי appears to contain a damaged/uncertain character (<). The most likely reading is מהתלי or מהצלב — given the narrative context of removing a body, this likely means 'from the cross' (possibly מהתליה 'from the hanging/crucifixion'). The damaged consonant prevents certain identification.

מצוייר appears to be a passive participle meaning 'hewn/carved/shaped' — possibly from יצר (to form) or צור (to cut/hew). This describes the tomb as carved from rock. No Strong's candidates were provided.
ש<ם contains a damaged character. Most likely reading is שם 'there/where.'

מונח appears to be a hophal/passive participle from נוח 'to rest/be placed.' Only H5146 'Noah' was offered as a candidate, but contextually this is clearly the passive participle 'laid/placed' — no person had been laid there. The root is נוח (H5117).
עטפו and ושמהו have no candidates provided; they are verbs with 3ms pronominal suffix — 'wrapped it' (from עטף) and 'placed it' (from שים/שום).

translation_notes: והיה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 because the context introduces a temporal setting — 'and it was the eve of Shabbat.'
textual_notes: The brackets around ערב שבת suggest editorial uncertainty or a textual note in the manuscript. The phrase means 'eve of Shabbat' (Friday evening / preparation day).
וה<בת contains a damaged character (<). The most likely reading is והשבת 'and the Shabbat.'
התחיל is a later Hebrew form (hithpael of חלל or a denominative) meaning 'began.' No Strong's candidates were provided.

להאיר is a hiphil infinitive of אור 'to give light/shine/dawn.' This refers to the Shabbat beginning to dawn — the onset of the holy day as light appears. This is a distinctive way of marking the beginning of Shabbat by the appearance of stars or first light.

translation_notes: מגלילה (consonants גלילה): H1552 'a circuit or region.' This is the standard term for the Galilee district. The context of women traveling from a named region fits perfectly.
הקבר (consonants קבר): Candidates: H6912 'to inter', H6913 'a sepulchre'. Chose H6913 because with the definite article ה it is a noun — 'the tomb.'

באי זה אופן: באי from the consonants אי — Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 because באיזה אופן is a standard later Hebrew idiom meaning 'in what manner/way.' Testing H338 'in a wild creature this wheel' produces nonsense.
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 as part of the idiom באי זה — 'in which/what.'

אופן (consonants אופן): H212 'a wheel.' In later Hebrew אופן developed the meaning 'manner/way/mode' (from the idea of how something turns/operates). The context demands 'manner' — they observed in what way the body was laid.

משיח (consonants משיח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder/converse', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'a shoot/shrub'. Chose H4899 because it follows Yeshua as a title — 'Yeshua the Anointed One.'
היה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 — 'was laid' forms the past tense with the participle מונח.
textual_notes: נמשכות (from משך 'to draw/drag') as a feminine plural participle means 'being drawn/following.' No candidates were provided. The form suggests the women were 'drawn along' or 'following' after him.
מונח — same as in section 3: passive participle 'laid/placed' from נוח. Only H5146 'Noah' was offered, but this is clearly the verbal form.
אופן: H212 literally means 'wheel' but in post-biblical Hebrew it came to mean 'manner/way.' The context demands the latter sense.

translation_notes: בבית (consonants בית): Candidates: H1004 'a house', H1005 same, H1006 'Bajith (place)', H3487 'sign of object'. Chose H1004 because with the preposition ב it means 'to/in the house' — the women returned home.
textual_notes: The transition from the women preparing spices to 'Judah and he approached that he might give' is abrupt. יאודה may refer to Judas (Iscariot or another figure) approaching to hand something over, or it could be a textual disruption. The consonants יאודה match 'Judah/Judas.'
וניגש could be from נגש H5066 'to approach/draw near' or H5065 'to drive/press.' The context of giving/handing over suggests H5066 'approached.'
שיתן is a relative-purpose clause: ש + יתן = 'that he might give' (from נתן). No candidates were provided.
סמים appears to be the plural of סם 'spice/aromatic' (cf. H5561). No candidates were provided directly.
חשובים and מעולות are post-biblical Hebrew adjectives meaning 'important/precious' and 'excellent/superior' respectively. No Strong's candidates were provided.
ומשיחות could be parsed as feminine plural of משיחה 'anointing/ointment' (related to משח) or as the feminine plural of משיח. Context with spices clearly indicates 'ointments/anointings.'
This section may conflate two narrative threads: (1) the women preparing burial spices, and (2) Judas approaching to betray. The manuscript transition is unclear.

24.summary: Phase 1 consonantal translation — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided. Literal and amplified readings produced independently from consonantal Hebrew.

translation_notes: בת (consonants ב-ת): Candidates: H1323 'daughter', H1324 'bath (liquid measure)', H1325 same. In context with וב preceding it, this likely represents 'day one' or 'first day' — the phrase וב בת could be a rendering of 'on the first (day)' with בת used in its relational sense (daughter = belonging to). Chose H1323 because it fits the temporal expression for the first day of the week.

בבקר (first instance, consonants ב-ב-ק-ר): Candidates: H1242 'dawn/morning', H1241 'cattle', H1239 'to inspect', H7119 'cool'. The narrative describes women arriving early at a tomb — 'in the morning' is the natural reading. Chose H1242.
בבקר (second instance): Same consonants repeated — an intensifying doubling: 'in the early morning' or 'at the very break of dawn'. Chose H1242.

בקבר (consonants ב-ק-ב-ר): Candidates: H6912 'to inter', H6913 'a sepulchre'. With preposition ב attached, 'to/at the sepulchre' is the coherent reading since they are arriving at a location. Chose H6913.
textual_notes: The phrase וב בת is unusual. It may represent 'and on day one' (first day of the week), with בת functioning as an ordinal marker. The doubling of בבקר בבקר could be emphatic repetition meaning 'very early in the morning' or could reflect a textual duplication.

translation_notes: אבן (consonants א-ב-ן): Candidates: H68 'a stone', H69 same, H70 'a pair of stones / potter's wheel'. A single stone covering a tomb entrance is the natural image. Chose H68.
הקבר (consonants ה-ק-ב-ר): Candidates: H6912 'to inter', H6913 'a sepulchre'. With the definite article ה, this is a noun — 'the sepulchre'. Chose H6913.
לא (consonants ל-א): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 same (Aramaic). Standard Hebrew negation in a narrative clause. Chose H3808.

גוף (consonants ג-ו-פ): Candidate: H1479 'to hollow or arch, to close/shut'. The consonants ג-ו-פ in later Hebrew mean 'body' (a physical form, something enclosed). The context requires a noun — what they did not find — and 'body' fits perfectly. Chose H1479, understanding the semantic development from 'to enclose' to 'an enclosed form / body'.
ישוע (consonants י-ש-ו-ע): Candidates: H3442/H3443 'Yeshua'. A proper name. Chose H3442.

משיח (consonants מ-ש-י-ח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed one / Messiah', H7878 'to ponder/converse', H7879 'utterance', H7880 'a shoot/shrub'. The word follows a proper name as a title — 'the anointed one' is the coherent reading. Chose H4899.
textual_notes: גוף as 'body' reflects post-biblical Hebrew usage. The only Strong's entry (H1479) gives 'to hollow/close/shut' — the noun meaning 'body' is a later semantic development from the same root consonants.

translation_notes: עוד (consonants ע-ו-ד): Candidates: H5749 'to testify/repeat', H5750 'still/yet/while', H5751 same. With preposition ב, 'while still' — a temporal clause. Chose H5750.
הן (consonants ה-ן): Candidates: H2004 'they (fem. emphatic)', H2005 'lo!/if', H2006 'lo/unless'. The subject of 'were alarmed' — feminine plural pronoun referring to the women. Chose H2004.
זה (consonants ז-ה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Demonstrative pronoun following על — 'about this'. Chose H2088.
הנה (consonants ה-נ-ה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Introduces a sudden new element in the narrative — 'behold' is the natural reading. Chose H2009.

ש ני: The word שני ('two') appears split across ש and ני. H5204 'lamentation' for ני alone makes no sense here. The ש is already a relative particle used in this text, but here שני = 'two' preceding 'men'. The split is likely a scribal or tokenization artifact.
להם (consonants ל-ה-ם): Candidates: H3859 'to burn/rankle', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. With preposition ל, this is 'to them' — a prepositional phrase indicating proximity. Chose H1992 as the pronoun.
textual_notes: The word שני ('two') is split across two tokens ש and ני. If ש is the relative particle and ני is standalone, H5204 'lamentation' does not fit. More likely שני is a single word meaning 'two' that was split in tokenization.
לבנים could theoretically parse as ל + בנים (H1143 'space between armies') but the context of garment description makes לבנים = 'white (masc. pl.)' far more natural.

translation_notes: כאשר (consonants כ-א-ש-ר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. With כ prefixed to אשר, this is a temporal conjunction — 'when/as'. Chose H834.
והם (consonants ו-ה-ם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. Third person pronoun introducing a new subject (the two men). Chose H1992.
להם (consonants ל-ה-ם): Same as before — prepositional pronoun 'to them'. Chose H1992.
למה (consonants ל-מ-ה): Candidate: H4100 'what/why/how'. With ל prefix — 'for what reason' = 'why'. Chose H4100.
עם (consonants ע-ם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with/among'. Preposition connecting 'the living' and 'the dead' — 'among/with'. Chose H5973.
textual_notes: תשאלו could derive from שאל 'to ask/inquire' or 'to seek/request'. Both senses work here — 'why do you ask for / seek the living among the dead?'

translation_notes: פה (consonants פ-ה): Candidates: H6310 'mouth', H6311 'here/this place'. The phrase 'he is not ___' requires a locative — 'here'. Chose H6311.
כי (consonants כ-י): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Causal conjunction explaining why he is not here. Chose H3588.
חי (consonants ח-י): Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 same (Aramaic). Predicate describing his state after returning — 'alive'. Chose H2416.

באי (consonants ב-א-י): Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. With preposition ב and followed by זה אופן ('this manner'), this reads 'in what manner' — an interrogative construction. Chose H335.
זה (consonants ז-ה): H2088 'this'. Demonstrative modifying אופן. Chose H2088.

אופן (consonants א-ו-פ-ן): H212 'a wheel'. In later Hebrew, אופן develops the meaning 'manner/way' (as in the turning/mode of something). The context demands 'manner/way' — 'in what manner he spoke'. Chose H212 with the extended semantic sense.
דבר (consonants ד-ב-ר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. A verb is needed — 'he spoke with you'. Chose H1696.
שהיה (consonants ש-ה-י-ה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Relative particle ש + verb היה 'he was' — temporal clause 'that he was [in the Galilee]'. Chose H1961.
בגלילה (consonants ב-ג-ל-י-ל-ה): H1552 'a circuit/region'. With ב prefix and ה suffix — 'in the Galilee (the circuit/region)'. Chose H1552.

ובשבת, שבת, בשבת, שבתאחד, שבת, שבתאחד, שבת: All instances of שבת — Candidates: H7673 'to cease', H7674 'rest/cessation', H7675 'seat/abode', H7676 'Sabbath'. The repeated שבת with אחד appended suggests 'Sabbath-one' = 'the first of the Sabbath/week'. Chose H7676 throughout.
textual_notes: The end of this section (ובשבת שבת בשבת שבתאחד שבת שבתאחד שבת) appears heavily corrupted or contains scribal repetitions. The phrase שבתאחד likely means 'first of the Sabbath/week' but the multiple repetitions are difficult to parse coherently. This may represent a damaged or multiply-copied passage where the scribe repeated phrases. The core meaning appears to be a temporal reference to 'the first day after the Sabbath.'
אופן as 'manner/way' reflects post-biblical Hebrew semantic development from H212 'wheel'.

translation_notes: אמר (consonants א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same (Aramaic), H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. A verb is needed to introduce reported speech. Chose H559.
שבן (consonants ש-ב-ן): ש is the relative particle + בן. Candidates for בן: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 same. 'Son of the man/humanity' is a well-known Semitic title. Chose H1121.

האדם (consonants ה-א-ד-ם): Candidates: H119 'to be ruddy', H120 'a human being/mankind', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. With definite article ה, 'the man / the human' — part of the title 'son of the man'. Chose H120.
חי (consonants ח-י): H2416 'alive'. Describes the state of returning. Chose H2416.
ביום (consonants ב-י-ו-ם): Candidates: H3117 'a day', H3118 same (Aramaic). With preposition ב — 'on the day'. Chose H3117.
textual_notes: ה<לישי appears to have a damaged or missing letter (represented by <). The consonantal skeleton suggests השלישי 'the third', with a shin likely missing.
תלוי could mean 'hung' or 'suspended' — in context this refers to execution by hanging/crucifixion.

translation_notes: מן (consonants מ-ן): Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 same, H4482 'musical chord'. Preposition of origin — 'from the tomb'. Chose H4480.
הקבר (consonants ה-ק-ב-ר): H6912 'to inter', H6913 'sepulchre'. With definite article — a noun. Chose H6913.
כל (consonants כ-ל): H3605 'all/whole', H3606 same. Chose H3605.

אלה (consonants א-ל-ה): Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. None of these fit. The consonants א-ל-ה also function as the common demonstrative pronoun 'these' (not listed in Strong's as a separate entry but a standard Hebrew word). Context demands a demonstrative — 'all these words'. Chose as demonstrative pronoun 'these'.
אחד עשר: H259 'one' + H6240 'teen/ten in combination' = 'eleven'. A compound number. Chose H259 and H6240.
ולכל: ו + ל + כל H3605 'all'. Chose H3605.
textual_notes: אלה as 'these' (demonstrative pronoun) is not represented in the Strong's candidates provided, which list only nouns/verbs. However, אלה as a demonstrative pronoun is standard Hebrew and is the only coherent reading in this context.

translation_notes: והיה (consonants ו-ה-י-ה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Narrative copula introducing a list — 'and it was'. Chose H1961.
שמרים: ש (relative particle) + מרים H4813 'Miriam'. 'That Miriam...' introducing the named subject. Chose H4813.
אם (consonants א-ם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Followed by a personal name (Yaakov) — 'mother of Yaakov'. Chose H517.
יעקב: H3290 'Yaakov/Jacob'. Proper name. Chose H3290.
אלה (consonants א-ל-ה): Same as section 9 — demonstrative pronoun 'these'. Context: 'these words/things'.
textual_notes: ל<לוחים appears to have a missing letter (marked with <). The consonantal skeleton suggests לשלוחים 'to the sent ones / emissaries / apostles', from the root שלח 'to send'.

The text names three women all called מרים (Miriam). The third מרים is followed by שלומית — this could be a separate name (Shlomit/Salome) or an epithet. It is unclear whether שלומית is a surname or identifies a distinct person.
The third ומרים שלומית could alternatively be parsed as 'and Miriam [called] Shlomit' or 'and Miriam, and Shlomit' with an implied conjunction.

translation_notes: להם (both occurrences): Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 because the prepositional ל + הם = 'to them' fits the context of reporting words to people.
אלו: Candidates: H431 'lo!', H432 'if'. In later Hebrew אלו functions as a demonstrative pronoun 'these'. Context requires a demonstrative modifying דברים, so reading as 'these'.
ולא: Candidates: H3808, H3809 (both 'not'). Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation.
textual_notes: מוסכמין is not a biblical Hebrew form but appears to be a later Hebrew (Mishnaic/Medieval) passive participle from the root ס.כ.מ meaning 'agreed upon, credible'. No Strong's number applies.
האמינום appears to be hifil perfect 3mp of א.מ.נ with 3mp object suffix — 'they believed them'. This is a post-biblical morphological form.

translation_notes: הקבר: Candidates: H6912 'to inter', H6913 'a sepulchre'. Chose H6913 because the article ה + noun 'the tomb' fits — one runs to a tomb, not to a verb.
ראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'experiencing', H7203 'seer', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 because the context describes someone looking and seeing cloth — a verb of sight.

לבד: Candidates: H905 'separation/alone', H906 'linen garment', H907 'a lie'. Chose H905 'alone/by themselves' because the point is that only the cloths remained, with no body present. H906 'linen' is tempting alongside 'garments' but would be redundant; the narrative emphasis is on the absence of the body.
והלך: Candidates: H1980 'to walk', H1981 'to walk', H1982 'a wayfarer', H1983 'a journey'. Chose H1980 as the standard verb 'he walked/went away'.
ורץ: H7518 is listed as 'a fragment' but the consonants רץ also correspond to the verb רוץ 'to run'. Context clearly requires 'ran' — he rose and ran to the tomb.
ממה: H4100/H4101 both mean 'what?' — with מ prefix = 'from what'. Chose H4100.
textual_notes: לבד could be read as H906 'linen' (he saw the linen garments) or H905 'alone/by themselves' (he saw the garments alone). Both produce coherent images. I chose 'alone' because the narrative tension concerns the body's absence, making 'the garments by themselves' the more significant observation.
<נעשה has an angle bracket indicating possible textual damage or scribal note. The word appears to be נעשה — nifal of עשה 'was done/made'.
וכורע appears to be a participle of כרע 'to bow/kneel down' — he stooped down to look into the tomb. Not in the Strong's candidates provided but the root is well attested (H3766).

translation_notes: והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'and behold' naturally introduces a new scene.
מהם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — מ + הם = 'from them/of them'.

במגדול: Candidates: H4024 'Migdol, a place in Egypt', H1419 'great'. The consonants מגדול match מגדל 'tower' (H4026) as well. In context, this is a place name for a town — but the sentence says this place 'is called Emmaus,' so במגדול likely means 'in a town/village' (מגדול as a generic term for a fortified settlement). Chose H4024 as the closest Strong's match for the consonants, but understanding it as a common noun 'tower-town/village' rather than the Egyptian place.
שהיה: Candidates: H1961 'to be/exist', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 — ש + היה = relative 'that' + 'was'.
textual_notes: במגדול is puzzling. The known Emmaus road tradition places it much closer to Jerusalem (about 60 stadia ≈ 7 miles). The text says 'forty miles' which is unusual. מגדול could be a common noun 'tower/fortified place' or a proper name. Since the text immediately clarifies the name as Emmaus, I read במגדול as a generic descriptor 'in a tower-town.'
מילין is an Aramaic/late Hebrew plural of מיל 'mile' (a Roman mile). No Strong's number applies.
שנקרא = ש + נקרא, nifal of קרא 'to call' — 'that is called'. Standard later Hebrew construction.
אימאוס is a transliteration of the place name Emmaus. No Strong's number.

translation_notes: והם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — 'and they' as the subject of the participial clause.

מאשר: Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 — מ + אשר = 'from/about that which', a standard relative construction.

וקרה: Candidates: H7135 'coolness', H7136 'to light upon/happen/occur', H7137 'an occurrence'. Chose H7136 because 'happened/occurred' pairs naturally with 'was done' — describing events that took place.
textual_notes: באותן is a later Hebrew demonstrative form 'in those' (ב + אותן). No Strong's number applies directly.
נעשה is nifal of עשה 'to do/make' = 'was done/was made'. No Strong's candidates were provided.

translation_notes: ובעוד: Candidates: H5749 'to testify/repeat', H5750 'still/yet/while', H5751 same as H5750. Chose H5750 — ב + עוד = 'while still', a temporal conjunction meaning 'while they were still...'.

קרב: Candidates: H7126 'to approach/draw near', H7127 same, H7128 'hostile encounter', H7129 same, H7130 'the center/midst', H7131 'near'. Chose H7126 because the verb 'drew near' fits: Yeshua approached them.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — ל + הם = 'to them'.
ישוע: Candidates: H3442, H3443 (both 'Jeshua'). Chose H3442 as the primary entry for this proper name.
textual_notes: The phrase 'ו מצאו עדים' is difficult. The ו stands alone as a separate word, which is unusual. מצאו could be 'they found' or 'finding'. עדים could be 'witnesses' (from עד H5707) or possibly a form related to עוד. The sequence 'and finding witnesses' before Yeshua's arrival is contextually awkward. This may be a scribal corruption or a phrase meaning something like 'and [while] seeking evidence/testimony,' i.e., they were discussing and trying to make sense of witness accounts when Yeshua appeared.
This entire phrase 'ו מצאו עדים' may be corrupt or may reflect an unusual Hebrew rendering of a source text. The separation of ו from the following word is suspicious.

translation_notes: שלא: ש + לא. Candidates for לא: H3808, H3809 (both 'not'). Chose H3808 — standard negation. ש functions as the relative/conjunction 'that/so that'.
textual_notes: עורות could derive from עור 'to blind/be blind' (H5786/H5787) or from עור 'skin/hide' (H5785) in feminine plural. Context strongly favors 'blinded' — their eyes were blinded so they could not recognize him.
מכירים is a hifil participle of נכר 'to recognize' (H5234). A standard later Hebrew participial construction with היו for ongoing past action.

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — 'said', the standard verb of speech.
באי: Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 — ב + אי = 'in what/which', forming an interrogative with זה: 'in what kind of...'
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — the demonstrative. Together באי זה = 'in what kind of / which', a standard later Hebrew interrogative phrase.

וכבר: Candidates: H3527 'to augment', H3528 'long ago/already/hitherto', H3529 'Kebar river', and various entries for בר. Chose H3528 — 'already', fitting the adverbial sense: 'and already you are walking and worrying.'
אתם (both): The only Strong's candidate is H864 'Etham, a place.' But אתם is the standard 2mp pronoun 'you' in Hebrew. No Strong's number for the pronoun was provided; reading as 'you (plural)'.
textual_notes: ודואגים derives from דאג 'to be anxious, worry, grieve' (H1672). This is a participial form = 'and worrying/grieving'. Not listed in candidates but the root is clear.
The phrase באי זה is a compound interrogative 'in what/which' — a standard medieval Hebrew construction.

translation_notes: וענה: Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 same as H6030, H6033 same as H6031, H6034 'Anah'. Chose H6030 — 'answered', the standard response verb in dialogue.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 — 'one of them'.
מהם: H1992 'them' with מ = 'from them'.
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 same, H859 'you'. Chose H859 — 'you', the subject of the clause.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/self', H1932 same, H1933 'to be', H1934 same. Chose H1931 — 'he/the one', forming with אתה: 'you are the one who...'
גר: Candidates: H1615 'lime', H1616 'a guest/foreigner/sojourner'. Chose H1616 — 'a sojourner/stranger', someone recently dwelling in Jerusalem who apparently doesn't know what happened.
ואמר: H559 'to say'.
אי: Candidates: H335 'where?/what?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Chose H335 — interrogative 'what/which', forming with זה the compound 'what kind of'.
זה: H2088 'this/that'. Together אי זה = 'which/what'.
באלו: Candidates: H431 'lo!', H432 'if'. In later Hebrew אלו functions as a demonstrative 'these'. With ב = 'in these'. Chose H431 as the closest consonantal match, reading as demonstrative.
textual_notes: ש<מו has an angle bracket suggesting textual damage. The reading is clearly שמו 'his name' (from שם H8034 + 3ms suffix).
קלאופש is a transliteration of the name Cleopas (Greek Κλεοπᾶς). No Strong's number.
ואינך is a later Hebrew negation form: ו + אין + ך = 'and you are not'. Standard post-biblical construction.
שמקרוב: ש + מ + קרוב = 'who from nearby/recently'. Could mean 'recently' (temporal) or 'from nearby' (spatial). Context suggests temporal — 'who has recently been sojourning.'

translation_notes: ולהם: Candidates for הם: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — ו + ל + הם = 'and to them'.
ענה: Candidates: H6030 'to answer', H6031 'to afflict', H6032-6034. Chose H6030 — 'answered', continuing the dialogue.
מה: H4100/H4101, both 'what?'. Chose H4100.
הן: Candidates: H2004 'they (fem.)', H2005 'lo!/behold', H2006 'if/whether'. Chose H2004 — 'they are', as in 'what are they, the words?' He asks them to explain.
די: Candidates: H1767 'enough', H1768 'that/of' (Aramaic relative). Chose H1768 — 'of', connecting Yeshua to Nazareth: 'Yeshua of Nazareth.'
שהוא: H1931 'he' with ש = 'who he [was]'. The relative clause introducing the description of Yeshua.
חזק: Candidates: H2388 'to be strong', H2389 'strong/powerful', H2390 'powerful', H2391 'help', H2392 'power'. Chose H2389 — adjective 'strong/mighty', modifying the prophet.
נביא: Candidates: H5029, H5030 both 'a prophet'. Chose H5030 as the more standard entry.
העם: Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5972 same, H5973 'with', H5974 same. Chose H5971 — 'the people', as the object before whom he acted.
textual_notes: The structure of this verse is unusual: Yeshua asks 'what are they?' and then the respondents (or the narrative) continues by describing events about Yeshua of Nazareth. The transition from Yeshua's question to the description beginning with מישוע could mean: (a) Yeshua asks 'what?' and they respond with the description, or (b) the sentence flows continuously — 'What are these words concerning Yeshua of Nazareth...' I read it as the latter: the respondents are explaining what matters they were discussing.
נצרת is the place name Nazareth. No Strong's number applies.
בפועל and ובדבור are later Hebrew forms: 'in deed/action' and 'in speech/utterance'. No Strong's candidates provided.

translation_notes: ובאי: Candidates for אי: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Chose H335 — ו + ב + אי = 'and in what/which', continuing the interrogative pattern from previous sections.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — together with באי forms 'in what manner'.
אופן: H212 'a wheel'. In later Hebrew אופן developed the meaning 'manner/way' (as in modern Hebrew). The consonants match H212 and no other candidate is given. Reading as 'manner/way'.
textual_notes: אופן (H212) literally means 'wheel' in biblical Hebrew but is used as 'manner/way' in post-biblical Hebrew. The context clearly requires 'manner.'
מסרוהו is a later Hebrew verbal form: מסר + והו = 'they delivered him / handed him over'. Root מסר (not in Strong's biblical lexicon in this form).
עליוני appears to be an adjective 'upper/chief' modifying הכהנים 'the priests' — 'the chief priests'.
ושריהם = ו + שרי + הם = 'and their officials/rulers'. From שר (H8269).
בעונש = ב + עונש = 'in/to punishment'. Later Hebrew form.
מיתה = 'death' — later Hebrew noun from מות.
ותלוהו = ו + תלו + הו = 'and they hung him'. From תלה (H8518) 'to hang'. In this context likely referring to crucifixion, as 'hanging on a tree/cross' was the Hebrew idiom for crucifixion.

translation_notes: שהוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/she/it', H1932 same in Aramaic, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because the context requires a pronoun 'that he' as the subject of the following verb 'would redeem'.
את: Candidates: H852 'portent', H853 'object marker', H854 'with/near', H855 'hoe'. Chose H853 because it marks the direct object 'Israel' of the verb 'would redeem'.
שלישי: Candidates: H7992 'third', H3448 'Jesse'. Chose H7992 because 'third day' is the coherent reading following 'day day ___'.
אלו: Candidates: H431 'lo!/these', H432 'if'. Chose H431 functioning as a demonstrative 'these' in later Hebrew usage, pointing to the matters just described.
textual_notes: המתינו has no Strong's candidates listed; it appears to be a later Hebrew (Mishnaic) form meaning 'they waited/expected'. The root מתן is not in the classical Strong's lexicon. The subject could be 'we' (first person plural) or 'they'.
יפדה has no Strong's candidates listed; contextually it is clearly from פדה (H6299) 'to redeem' in imperfect 3ms form.
אלו could be the demonstrative 'these' (common in Mishnaic/later Hebrew) or H431 'lo!'. The demonstrative reading fits the syntax.

translation_notes: רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because the adverbial sense 'only/but' introduces a qualifying statement naturally.
מקצת: Candidates: H7117 'portion/end', H7118 same Aramaic. Chose H7117 as 'some of' — a portion, used with the partitive מן prefix.
בקבר: Candidates: H6912 'to inter', H6913 'a sepulchre'. Chose H6913 because the preposition ב + noun = 'at the sepulchre/tomb'.
textual_notes: מנשינו has no Strong's candidates; it is מן + נשינו 'from/of our women'. The root נשה or אשה (woman) is implied.
החרידונו has no Strong's candidates; it appears to be from חרד (H2729 'to tremble/be alarmed') in a causative form with 1pl object suffix: 'they alarmed us'.
שקודם is a relative particle ש + קודם 'before'; קודם is a later Hebrew temporal adverb not in Strong's classical lexicon.
היו is from היה (H1961) 'to be' — 3rd plural perfect: 'they were'.

translation_notes: גוף: Only candidate H1479 'to hollow/arch/close/shut'. However the consonants גוף in later Hebrew mean 'body' (not in classical Strong's). Context clearly demands 'body' — they did not find the body of Yeshua.

מראה: Candidates: H4758 'a view/appearance/vision', H4759 'a vision/mirror', H4760 'craw of a bird'. Also ראה candidates. Chose H4758 because 'they saw a vision/appearance of angels' is the coherent image.
שהוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 same Aramaic, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 — 'that he [is] alive'.
חי: Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 same Aramaic. Chose H2416 for Hebrew context.
textual_notes: גוף in Strong's (H1479) means 'to close/shut', but in Mishnaic/later Hebrew גוף means 'body'. This text uses it as a noun 'body', which is post-biblical usage.
ובאו could parse as וב+או (H176 'or') but contextually it is ובאו from בוא 'to come' — 3pl perfect with waw: 'and they came'.
אומרות is feminine plural participle of אמר — indicating the speakers (the women) are female.
מלאכים has no candidates listed but is clearly from מלאך (H4397) 'messenger/angel' in masculine plural.

translation_notes: לקבר: Candidates: H6912 'to inter', H6913 'sepulchre'. Chose H6913 because the preposition ל + noun = 'to the tomb'.
כמו: Only H3644 'as/thus/so'. Fits perfectly.
כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/right', H3652 'so' (Aramaic), H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 — כמו כן = 'just so / likewise'.
הלכו: The candidate listed (כו H3551 'window') is irrelevant; this is clearly הלך (H1980) 'to walk/go' in 3pl perfect: 'they went'.
textual_notes: ומקצתנו is not in Strong's; it is מקצת + נו (our/us) = 'some of us', using the same מקצת from section 2.
אותו has no candidates listed; it is the accusative pronoun את + הו = 'him'.
הנשים has no candidates listed; it is הנשים from אשה (H802) = 'the women'.

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same Aramaic, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the verb 'said' fits with the subject Yeshua speaking to them.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle/burn in', H1992 'them'. Chose the prepositional use ל + הם (H1992) 'to them', as the context is speech directed at a group.
ישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua', H3443 same. Chose H3442 as the proper name.
textual_notes: סכלים has no candidates listed; from סכל (H5530) 'foolish/fool' in masculine plural.
תועים has no candidates listed; from תעה (H8582) 'to err/go astray' — masculine plural participle.
מלהאמין is a compound: מן + ל + האמין (hiphil infinitive of אמן H539 'to believe'). The מ functions as 'from' — 'from believing'.
תהיו could be parsed as future 'you will be' or present habitual 'you are being'. Context suggests a present rebuke.

translation_notes: משיח: Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder/converse', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'a shoot/shrub'. Chose H4899 because the context speaks of a specific figure who must suffer and enter glory — the Anointed One.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 as the demonstrative 'this' modifying Messiah.

ובזה: The consonants can be read as ו + בזה (H959 'to disesteem/scorn') or ו + ב + זה (H2088 'and in/by this'). Chose ו+ב+זה because 'and through this he would enter his light/glory' produces a coherent theological statement about suffering leading to glory, whereas 'and he was scorned' would require a different sentence structure.
textual_notes: חוייב has no Strong's candidates; it is a passive (pual/derived) form of חיב, a later Hebrew root meaning 'to be obligated/necessary'. Not in classical Strong's.
לסבול has no Strong's candidates; from סבל (H5445) 'to bear a burden/carry/suffer'. The infinitive with ל = 'to suffer/bear'.
יכנס has no Strong's candidates; from כנס (H3664) 'to gather/enter'. Later Hebrew uses it for 'to enter'.
באורו = ב + אור + ו = 'in his light'. אור (H216) means 'light/luminance'. This could also be understood as 'his glory' since light and glory are closely associated in Hebrew imagery.

translation_notes: ממשה: Candidates: H4871 'to pull out', H4872 'Moses', H4873 same, H4874 'a debt', H7716 'sheep/goat'. Chose H4872 because 'beginning from Moses' (the lawgiver) as the first of the prophetic/scriptural sources is the coherent reading.

מפרש: Candidates: H4666 'an expansion', H6566 'to break apart/spread', H6567 'to separate/specify', H6568 'to specify', H6569 'excrement', H6570 'Peresh', H6571 'a steed'. Chose H6567 'to specify/separate/make distinct' because in later Hebrew פרש means 'to explain/interpret', and the context requires an act of interpretation/exposition.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'them'. Chose ל + הם (H1992) 'to them'.
textual_notes: ומתחיל has no Strong's candidates; from the root חלל or תחל — in later Hebrew התחיל means 'to begin'. This is a participle form.
הכתיבות has no Strong's candidates; from כתב (H3789) 'to write' — הכתיבות = 'the writings/scriptures'. This is a later Hebrew feminine plural nominal form.
הנמצאות has no Strong's candidates; from מצא (H4672) 'to find' — niphal feminine plural participle: 'the ones found' i.e. 'that are found/written'.
ממנו could mean 'from him' or 'concerning him'. Both are grammatically possible; 'concerning him' fits the context of scriptures about the Messiah.

translation_notes: למגדול: Candidates: H4024 'Migdol, a place in Egypt', H1419 'great/large'. The consonants מגדול could be מגדל (tower/fortress, H4026) with plene spelling. 'To the tower/village' produces a coherent image of approaching a destination. H4024 Migdol specifically is Egyptian, which seems less likely. The word is probably מגדל 'tower' used as a settlement name or description. Chose H4024 as the closest Strong's match for the consonants, though the meaning is likely 'the tower/fortified village'.
והוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 same Aramaic, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 — 'and he'.
חפץ: Candidates: H2654 'to incline to/be pleased/desire', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire/matter'. Chose H2654 as the verb 'desired/intended'.
עוד: Candidates: H5749 'to testify/repeat', H5750 'again/still/further', H5751 same. Chose H5750 — adverb 'still/further'.
textual_notes: למגדול: The consonants could represent מגדול (Migdol) or a plene spelling of מגדל (tower). In the narrative context this appears to be the name of a village/destination. It likely corresponds to a settlement name.
וקרבו has no candidates listed; from קרב (H7126) 'to draw near' — 3pl perfect with waw.
ללכת has no candidates listed; from הלך (H1980) 'to walk/go' — infinitive with ל.

translation_notes: ובקשש: Candidate H7197 'to forage for straw/assemble'. However the consonants may represent a later Hebrew form of בקש (to seek/request/urge) with intensification. Context demands 'they urged/pressed him'. Using H7197 as closest consonantal match, but the meaning is 'they pressed/urged'.
הו: Candidate H1930 'oh!'. In context this likely serves as an object suffix 'him' (הו = 3ms pronominal suffix). The exclamation reading is less coherent.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord/master', H114 'Addon'. Chose H113 — they address him as 'lord/master'.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'because/for/that'. Chose H3588 — conjunction 'for/because'.

כבר (both occurrences): Candidates: H3527 'to augment', H3528 'long ago/already/hitherto', H3529 'Kebar river'. Chose H3528 'already' — 'it has already become evening' and 'the day has already declined'.

ערב: Candidates: H6148 'to braid/traffic', H6149 'to be agreeable', H6150 'to grow dusky', H6151 'to commingle', H6152 'Arabia', H6153 'dusk/evening'. Chose H6153 'evening/dusk' because 'it has become evening' is the coherent image.
textual_notes: ת<אר appears to have a scribal issue (the < character). The consonants likely represent תשאר from שאר (H7604) 'to remain/stay' — imperative or imperfect 'stay/remain'. The reading 'stay with us' fits the context perfectly.
ובקשש could be from בקש 'to seek/request' with an unusual doubled shin, or from קשש (H7197). The meaning in context is clearly 'they urged/implored'.
הו as a pronoun suffix 'him' vs. exclamation 'oh!' — the pronoun reading makes better syntactic sense as the object of the urging.
ונכנס has no candidates; from כנס (H3664) 'to enter/gather' — later Hebrew 'he entered'.

translation_notes: וכאשר: Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 — כאשר = 'when/as' — temporal conjunction.
לקח: Candidates: H3947 'to take', H3948 'instruction'. Chose H3947 — 'he took'.
הפת: Candidates: H6595 'a bit/morsel [of bread]', H6596 'a hole/hinge'. Chose H6595 — 'the bread/morsel'. פת commonly refers to a piece of bread.
ונתן: Candidates: H5414 'to give', H5415 'give' (Aramaic), H5416 'Nathan'. Chose H5414 — 'and he gave'.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'them'. Chose ל + הם (H1992) 'to them'.
textual_notes: הסב has no candidates listed; from סבב (H5437) 'to turn/go around' — in later Hebrew הסב means 'to recline (at a meal)', the hiphil form. This is a standard term for reclining at table.
וברכו has no candidates listed; from ברך (H1288) 'to bless' — 3ms perfect with waw and 3ms suffix: 'and he blessed it'.
ובצעו has no candidates listed; from בצע (H1214) 'to cut off/break off' — 3ms perfect with waw and suffix: 'and he broke it'. This is the standard term for breaking bread.

translation_notes: הפת (consonants פת): Candidates: H6595 'a bit/morsel (of bread)', H6596 'a hole, hinge, or pudenda'. In the context of 'breaking of the ___', H6595 (a morsel/bit of bread) produces a coherent image of a meal; H6596 is anatomical/mechanical and makes no sense here.

ואחר (consonants אחר): Candidates: H309 'to loiter/delay', H310 'after (adverb/conjunction)', H311 'after', H312 'another/other', H313 'Acher (name)'. The sentence structure 'and ___ he was not seen' calls for a temporal conjunction; H310 'after' fits naturally.
היה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist, be, become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah (sacred name)'. The sentence requires a verb of being ('he was/became not seen'); H1961 is the clear fit.
והם (consonants הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. The context clearly requires the pronoun 'they' as the subject of 'said'.
היה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. The sentence describes their heart 'was burning'; H1961 as copulative verb fits.

שדבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. With the prefix ש (that/when) and the context 'when he ___ with us on the road', the verb 'spoke' (H1696) is the natural fit.
בדרך (consonants דרך): Candidates: H1869 'to tread/walk', H1870 'a road/way'. With the preposition ב, 'on the road' (H1870 as noun) produces the coherent image of traveling companions.
textual_notes: לבינו could be parsed as לב + ינו ('our heart') or as ל + בינו ('to our understanding'). The context of something 'burning within us' strongly favors 'our heart' but 'our understanding' is not impossible.

translation_notes: שעה (consonants שעה): Candidates: H8159 'to gaze at/consider', H8160 'a look, i.e. a moment'. In the phrase 'in that ___', a temporal noun 'hour/moment' (H8160) makes sense; 'to gaze' does not fit the syntax.
עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people/tribe', H5973 'with (preposition)'. The phrase 'and they sat ___ the eleven' requires the preposition 'with' (H5973).
האחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. As part of the numeral 'the eleven', H259 'one' is the correct reading.

עשר (consonants עשר): Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6236 'ten (Aramaic)', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth', H6240 'teen (in combination)'. Combined with 'one' (אחד עשר), H6240 '-teen' is the proper combinatory form yielding 'eleven'.
יחד (consonants יחד): Candidates: H3161 'to become one', H3162 'unitedly/together'. As an adverb modifying how they sat, H3162 'together' fits naturally.

שהאדון (consonants אדון): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller (human or divine)', H114 'Addon (name)'. The context of someone returning alive and appearing calls for a title—'the lord/sovereign' (H113).
חי (consonants חי): Candidates: H2416 'alive, living, raw, fresh', H2417 'alive (Aramaic)'. Both mean essentially the same; H2416 is the Hebrew form and fits naturally.

לשמעון (consonants שמעון): Candidates: H8095 'Shimon (son of Jacob / proper name)', H4583 'an abode', H4584 'Maon (name/place)'. The prefix ל (to) plus a proper name in a context of appearing 'to someone' calls for H8095 'Shimon'.
textual_notes: לשמעון could theoretically contain the root מעון (abode), but with ל prefix and the narrative context of appearing to a person, the proper name Shimon (H8095) is far more natural.

translation_notes: והם (consonants הם): H1992 'they' — pronoun subject of the verb 'recounted'; same reasoning as section 2.
בדרך (consonants דרך): H1870 'road/way' — same context as section 2, a physical road they traveled on.
הפת (consonants פת): H6595 'a bit/morsel of bread' — same context as section 1; breaking of bread at a meal.

עמד (consonants עמד): Candidates: H5975 'to stand', H5976 'to shake', H5977 'a spot', H5978 'along with'. 'Yeshua ___ in their midst' — 'stood' (H5975) produces the natural image of someone appearing and standing among a group.

ואמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. The syntax 'and ___ to them' requires a verb of speech; H559 'said' is the clear choice.
שלום (consonants שלום): Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare/wholeness', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. As a greeting followed by 'to you', H7965 'peace' is the standard greeting formula.
אני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. As a pronoun before הוא ('he'), 'I' (H589) is the obvious reading.
הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/it (pronoun)', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. In 'I am he', the demonstrative pronoun H1931 fits naturally.

אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not (negative particle, deprecative)', H410 'strength/God', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. Before the imperfect תיראו ('you will fear'), H408 as prohibitive 'do not' is the standard Hebrew construction.
להם: This is the preposition ל + 3mp suffix הם. The candidate H3859 'to rankle' does not fit; this is simply 'to them' using the pronoun H1992.
והם (consonants הם): H1992 'they' — pronoun subject, same reasoning as previous sections.

רוח (consonants רוח): Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely/revive', H7305 'room/interval', H7306 'to blow/smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 'wind/spirit (Aramaic)'. People who are terrified and trembling think they are seeing a ___; 'spirit' (H7307) is the coherent reading — they feared they were seeing a ghost/apparition.
textual_notes: רוח (H7307) has a wide semantic range: wind, breath, spirit, ghost. In context of fearful people thinking they see something supernatural, 'spirit/ghost' is the most fitting sense, but 'breath' (i.e. an apparition or phantom) is also possible.

translation_notes: ואמר (consonants אמר): H559 'to say' — same reasoning as section 6.
להם: Preposition ל + 3mp pronoun הם (H1992) = 'to them'. H3859 'to rankle' does not fit.
למה (consonants מה): Candidates: H4100 'what/how/why', H4101 same (Aramaic). With prefix ל, this forms the interrogative 'why' — H4100.
ומה (consonants מה): H4100 'what' with conjunctive ו — 'and what'.
textual_notes: אתם is listed with only H864 'Etham (a place)' as a candidate, but consonantally אתם is universally the 2mp independent pronoun 'you (masculine plural)'. The Strong's candidate list appears incomplete; this is clearly the pronoun.

translation_notes: ורגלי (consonants רגלי): Candidate: H7273 'a footman/foot-soldier'. However, consonantally רגלי is naturally 'my feet' (רגל + 1cs suffix). In context of 'see my hands and my ___', 'my feet' is the coherent bodily parallel. H7273 'footman' would break the symmetry of body parts. The suffix -י indicates 'my', pointing to the noun רגל 'foot' with possessive.
textual_notes: ורגלי: The provided candidate H7273 means 'footman/soldier', but the consonants also straightforwardly yield 'my feet' (רגל + 1cs possessive suffix). The parallel with 'my hands' makes 'my feet' virtually certain.

translation_notes: שמחה (consonants שמחה): Candidates: H8057 'joy/gladness', H4229 'to wipe/erase'. In 'from abundance of ___ great', 'joy' (H8057) produces the coherent image of people overwhelmed by happiness; 'wiping/erasing' makes no sense.
ואמר (consonants אמר): H559 'to say' — same verb of speech as previous sections.

זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that (demonstrative)', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. In 'any ___ thing to eat', the demonstrative 'this' (H2088) functions as part of the indefinite construction 'some/any kind of thing'.
דבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. In 'any ___ to eat', the noun 'thing' (H1697) is the natural reading.
textual_notes: The consonants א י זה appear to be separated in the manuscript. Together they likely form איזה 'which/any kind of', a later Hebrew interrogative/indefinite pronoun. The separation may be a scribal convention or spacing artifact.

translation_notes: והם (הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham, a region', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. Chose H1992 because this is a subject pronoun introducing who performed the action of giving — 'they gave him.'

חלק: Candidates: H2505 'to apportion', H2506 'allotment/portion', H2507 'Chelek (name)', H2508 'a part', H2509 'smooth', H2510 'Chalak (place)'. Chose H2506 because it functions as a noun meaning 'a portion/piece' of fish, which is the natural construct here.
textual_notes: ויערת appears to be a construct form of יער (honeycomb/forest), likely יערת דבש meaning 'honeycomb of honey.' The word is not listed among the candidates but the consonants support this reading from H3293/H3295.
אפוי is a passive participle from אפה (to bake/roast), not listed in candidates but consonantally clear.

translation_notes: אשר (in וכאשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when/because', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כאשר is a temporal conjunction meaning 'when/as,' fitting the narrative sequence.
אכל: Candidates: H398 'to eat', H399 'to eat', H400 'food', H401 'Ucal (name)'. Chose H398 because a verb is needed here — 'when he ate.'
לקח: Candidates: H3947 'to take', H3948 'instruction'. Chose H3947 because the context describes a physical action: taking the remaining food.

להם: Candidates under להם: H3859 'to rankle'; under הם: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 as prepositional ל + הם = 'to them,' which fits giving the remainder to those present.
textual_notes: הנותר is a nifal participle from יתר (to remain/be left over), consonantally clear though not listed in candidates.
ונתנו could be parsed as 'and he gave it' (3ms + 3ms suffix) or 'and they gave' (3mp). Context favors 'and he gave it' since the subject has been singular (he ate, he took).

translation_notes: אמר (in ואמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because a verb of speaking is required by the narrative context.
להם: Candidates under להם: H3859 'to rankle'; under הם: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 as ל + הם = 'to them.'

אלה: Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to imprecate', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. None of these match the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (H428). The consonants אלה clearly function as the demonstrative pronoun 'these' in context, pointing to the words that follow.
הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — functioning as a copula: 'these are they, the words.'
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 'he/it', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 — impersonal 'it' in the clause 'that it was obligated.'

שכל: Candidates under שכל: H7919 'to be circumspect', H7920 'intelligent', H7921 'to miscarry', H7922 'intelligence'; under כל: H3605 'the whole/all', H3606 'all'. Chose H3605: ש + כל = 'that all,' introducing the content clause about what must be fulfilled.
בדת: Candidates: H1881 'a royal edict/statute', H1882 same. Chose H1881 — 'law/statute,' here referring to the Torah of Moses.
משה: Candidates: H4871 'to pull out', H4872 'Moses', H4873 'Moses', H4874 'a debt'; under שה: H7716 'sheep/goat'. Chose H4872 because 'the law of Moses' is the natural referent.

עלי: Candidates: H5940 'pestle', H5941 'Eli', H5942 'high', H5943 'supreme'. None match the preposition על + 1cs suffix 'about me/concerning me' (H5921 + suffix). Context demands 'that were said about me.'
textual_notes: אלה as a demonstrative pronoun 'these' (H428) is not among the listed candidates, but the consonants are identical and context absolutely demands this reading over 'bewail,' 'imprecation,' 'oak,' or 'God.'
עלי as על + suffix 'concerning me' is the natural reading but was not among the listed Strong's candidates. The alternatives (pestle, Eli, high, supreme) produce no coherent reading here.
שחוייב appears to be a later Hebrew/Aramaic passive form meaning 'it was obligated/necessary' — not a classical biblical Hebrew form, suggesting this text has post-biblical linguistic features.
נשלמים is a nifal participle from שלם meaning 'being completed/fulfilled.'

translation_notes: פתח: Candidates: H6605 'to open wide', H6606 'to open', H6607 'door/entrance', H6608 'disclosure'. Chose H6605 because a verb is needed — 'he opened' their understanding.
להם: As before, ל + הם = 'to them' (H1992).
